docs.title: Liquid LSD
docs.text:
Liquid LSD is open-source VJ software for real-time, audio-reactive visuals. It drives generative shaders and procedural geometry from a live audio feed, runs everything through an analog-style modulation matrix, and gives you a fast keyboard-driven performance interface for playing it live.

It's in active beta — the core workflow is solid and usable, and the docs here aim to help you get comfortable with it as quickly as possible.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
Never used Liquid LSD before? Start with Getting Started to get the app running and your audio routed in.

Getting your bearings? Your Workspace explains the layout, the four decks, and how everything connects.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text:
• Your Workspace — The layout explained: four decks, the mixer, signal flow, and the two main modes.
  • Visual Sources — The built-in generators (Mandala, Icosa-Dodeca, Gyroid, and more), the FX chain, feedback loops, and how to load your own ISF shaders.
  • Modulation — How to wire audio, LFOs, sequencers, and MIDI to your visual parameters using the CV grid.
  • Presets & Library — Saving and loading presets, building setlists, the Auto-VJ queue, and MIDI mapping.
  • Output & Recording — Sending video to projectors and other apps, recording your set, and exporting high-quality renders.
  • Performance Controls — MIDI and OSC/TouchOSC hardware control mapping, the trackpad performance surface, custom notes, and tooltips.
  • Hardware Control — which controller path to use: the Midi Fighter Twister, other MIDI controllers, or OSC/TouchOSC, with quick starts.
  • Macro Controls & the Perform View — Assigning targets to macro knobs with Learn Mode, and performing with the 4×4 macro knob matrix and Edit.
  • Web Broadcast — Live-streaming visual parameters to a browser-based visualizer. (Experimental — requires a relay server.)

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Liquid LSD comes with everything it needs bundled in — no separate Java installation required.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
Before downloading or running Liquid LSD, ensure your machine meets the minimum hardware and software requirements. Real-time procedural rendering across 4 visual decks and low-latency audio analysis requires modern 64-bit hardware and hardware-accelerated OpenGL 3.3 Core Profile support.

Component Minimum Specification Recommended Specification Operating System 64-bit OS:• Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 11+, Fedora 36+, Arch)• macOS 11.0+ (Big Sur or newer)• Windows 10 / 11 64-bit OS:• Linux x64 / ARM64 (Wayland or X11)• macOS 13+ (Apple Silicon M-Series)• Windows 11 (x64) GPU / Graphics OpenGL 3.3 Core Profile hardware support:• Intel HD Graphics 3000 / 4000+ (Mesa 20+ on Linux; HD 4000+ on Windows), Iris, UHD, Xe, Arc• AMD Radeon HD 5000+ (TeraScale 2), HD 7000+ (GCN), RX series, RDNA• NVIDIA GeForce 8000/9000/GT 200+ (Tesla 2.0), GeForce GTX 400+ (Fermi/Kepler/Maxwell/Pascal/etc.)• Apple Silicon M1+ or Metal/OpenGL 3.3+ Intel Macs• 512 MB VRAM Dedicated GPU with 2 GB+ VRAM:• NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 / RTX series• AMD Radeon RX 580 / RX 6000+ series• Apple Silicon M-Series Processor (CPU) 64-bit dual-core with SSE4.1/AVX (Intel 2nd-Gen Core 2011+, AMD FX/Ryzen, Apple Silicon, modern 64-bit ARMv8) Quad-core or 6+ core (Intel 8th-Gen+, AMD Ryzen 3000+, Apple Silicon M-Series) Memory (RAM) 4 GB RAM 8 GB – 16 GB RAM Display 1280 × 720 (minimum enforced window limit) 1920 × 1080 (Full HD) or higher Audio • Linux: ALSA / PulseAudio (Java Sound)• macOS / Windows: Default system audio input • Linux: PipeWire (pipewire-jack) or JACK daemon• macOS / Windows: Low-latency audio interface

[!WARNING] Legacy Hardware Incompatibility (Intel Core 2 Duo / Intel GMA Graphics): Legacy systems such as Intel Core 2 Duo / Core 2 Quad laptops and desktops equipped with Intel GMA integrated graphics (GMA 950, 3100, X3100, 4500MHD) or 1st-Gen Intel HD Graphics (Arrandale/Clarkdale) do not support OpenGL 3.3 Core Profile (their hardware caps out at OpenGL 1.4 – 2.1). Running Liquid LSD on these systems will fail at launch with Failed to create GLFW window. 32-bit operating systems are also not supported.

docs.title: 1. Download & Launch
docs.text:
Download the archive for your platform, unzip it, and launch:

  • macOS (Apple Silicon / M-Series): Double-click run-mac-arm.command.
  • macOS (Intel): Double-click run-mac-intel.command. (If macOS blocks it on first launch, right-click the file and select Open instead.)
  • Windows (x64): Double-click run-windows.bat.
  • Linux (x64 / ARM64): Open a terminal in the folder and run:

bash ./run-linux.sh

Optional: run ./install-desktop.sh to add Liquid LSD to your desktop app menu.

Building from source? See the README for Gradle build instructions.

docs.title: 2. Route Your Audio
docs.text:
Liquid LSD needs to hear your music. How you connect it depends on your platform:

  • macOS & Windows: Works straight away. The app picks up whatever your OS default input device is — a mic, an audio interface, or a virtual loopback driver. Just start playing music and check that the app responds.

  • Linux (PipeWire / JACK): Connect your audio source to lsd:input_1 and lsd:input_2 using Helvum, qjackctl, or jack_connect. This gives you sub-millisecond, sample-accurate routing and is the recommended setup on Linux.

  • Linux (fallback): If PipeWire or JACK isn't running, Liquid LSD will capture from your default ALSA/PulseAudio input automatically.

docs.title: 3. Your First 60 Seconds
docs.text:
When the app opens, you'll see the Perform view on the left with the Mixer on the right, and the Library docked below:

+---------------------------------------------+---------------------+
|              PERFORMANCE                    |        MIXER        |
| (4×4 macro knobs)                       | (Decks & Output)    |
+---------------------------------------------+                     |
|              LIBRARY                        |                     |
+---------------------------------------------+---------------------+

Here's what to try first:

  1. Check the audio feed. Open Preferences → Audio Hardware (Ctrl+P) — you should see the AMP, BASS, MID, and HIGH meters pulsing with your music. If nothing moves, check your audio routing (Step 2).

  2. Click anything. Click the gear on a deck's row to open that deck's Edit, then click any cell in its parameter grid — the Modulation column on the right shows the controls for that parameter. Hover over any label to see a tooltip explaining what it does.

  3. Open the Library. Press Space (when not in a text field) to raise the Library panel into view. This is where you browse presets, build playlists, and manage your play queues. Cycle through Full Height, Half Height, and Docked to find the layout that suits what you're doing.

That's it — you're in. Dig into Your Workspace next to understand what you're looking at, or jump straight to Modulation if you want to start wiring audio to visuals.

docs.title: Twister: Queue Knobs, Queueing at a Place, Auto-Preview (ui/browser/QueueKnobs.kt, ui/browser/QueueOps.kt, ui/NavigationSurface.kt, ui/PerformSurface.kt, control/KnobCommands.kt)
docs.text:
• New: knobs 14 and 15 are queue knobs in the Library view while the queues are under the browser. Knob 14 is the tab's main queue (A/B, A/B FX or Transitions), knob 15 its BG queue. Turn to move the highlight, hold down and turn to carry the item up or down, tap to use it now, Shift + tap to remove it. Their columns are outlined on screen, and the rings show where the highlight is.
  • New: Shift + tap on knob 16 queues the item at a place: after the highlight of the queue knob you touched last. Put that highlight on the playing item and the new item plays next. With no queue knob touched, it goes to the end as before.
  • New: knobs 1-8 play a deck in the Library view: the one you last sent to with knobs 9-13, Deck PV until then. A label on the Library's tab line names it.
  • New: auto-preview. Shift + tap on knob 12 (the PV send) makes PV load whatever the cursor rests on; knob 12 blinks while it's on. It turns off when you leave the Library and pauses while PV has unsaved changes.
  • Queue edits can be undone. Moving or removing queue items, by mouse, keyboard or Twister, is undone with Ctrl+Z (items, playing position and shuffle order). Removing shows a message saying what went.
  • Fixed: dragging a BG queue item down placed it one row too far.

docs.title: Queues Under the Browser in the Library View (ui/browser/QueueSplit.kt, ui/browser/QueueDrop.kt, ui/browser/BrowserDock.kt, ui/browser/QueuesPane.kt, the five queue panels)
docs.text:
• New: with the Library maximized, the Sources, FX and Transitions tabs show the five queues under the browser. Audition a source, effect or chain, then drag it straight to the place in a queue it should go. Before, it went to the bottom of the queue and you reordered it on the Queues tab. Drag the line between the halves to share the height (double-click: half and half); the rows-icon button left of Restore hides or shows the queues. On by default; the Perform view's Library and the Queues tab are unchanged.
  • Queues only take their own kind. While you drag, a queue that can't take what you hold dims and won't accept the drop; a drop mixing kinds keeps the right ones and a toast says how many were skipped. Fixed: the FX and Transition queues accepted any dropped file, so a source could end up in an FX queue.
  • A queue's border flashes when items arrive, by drag or by Q / Shift+Q, so you see where they went.
  • Dragging near the top or bottom of a long queue scrolls it (the browser's tree and list too), so you can drop past the rows on screen.
  • A playlist dragged from the tree drops into a queue as its items, at the drop line.
  • The arrow keys and the controller's cursor step from the browser on into the queues under it.
  • Fixed: dropping into the A/B queue above the item that is playing moved the "playing" marker onto the wrong row.

docs.title: Missing Playlist Items Can Be Found Again; Playlist Folders (ui/browser/BrowserPane.kt, ui/browser/BrowseModel.kt, ui/browser/LibraryRefs.kt)
docs.text:
• New: a playlist item whose file is missing is listed under the playlist with a ⚠, instead of only being counted. Find offers files of the same name elsewhere in the library, Locate... lets you pick the file, Remove drops the item, and Find all fixes every item with exactly one match. A found file is fixed in every playlist and queue that used the old path.
  • New: folders for playlists. Right-click Playlists in the tree for New Folder..., drag playlists onto a folder to move them, and rename, delete or nest playlist folders like the saved sections' folders. A moved playlist stays selected.

docs.title: Tags as Crates, Favorites for Saved FX (ui/browser/LibraryTags.kt, ui/browser/TagPopups.kt, ui/browser/BrowseModel.kt, ui/browser/BrowseFavorites.kt)
docs.text:
• New: a Tags group in the Library tree. Every tag used on the tab's saved items gets a row with a count; pick one to list everything tagged with it. An item can have any number of tags, so tags work like crates in a DJ app. The group starts folded.
  • Tag items from the Library: right-click a saved row, or a multi-selection, for Add Tag... (type tags or click existing ones) and Remove Tag, or drag rows onto a tag. Right-click a tag for Rename Tag... or Delete Tag.... This now works for saved FX, chains and transitions too, not only presets. Tags are written into each file, so they travel with it.
  • Saved single FX and chains can be Favorites (★ in the list, listed in the FX Favorites folder). The slot ◀ / ▶ shortlist still steps through starred stock filters only.
  • Fixed: a deck playing a preset whose tags you just edited wrote the old tags back on its next save.

docs.title: Folders in the Library (ui/browser/LibraryFolders.kt, ui/browser/FolderPopups.kt, ui/browser/BrowserPane.kt, ui/SavePresetModal.kt)
docs.text:
• New: manage folders from the Library. The saved sections (Saved presets, Saved single FX, Saved chains, Saved transitions) now take folders made in the app: the folder-plus button above the tree, or New Folder... on a section or folder's right-click menu. The same menu has Rename Folder..., Delete Folder... and Reveal in File Manager. Empty folders show in the tree.
  • Move items between folders: drag rows (or a multi-selection) onto a folder, or use Move to in a row's menu. Drag a folder onto another to move it. If the destination already has an item with that name, you choose Keep both (the moved one gets _2) or Skip. Playlists, queues, Favorites, Recent and loaded decks and chains all follow the move.
  • Save As picks the folder. The save dialog for presets, FX, chains and transitions has a Folder dropdown. It starts in the folder of what you loaded, so a variation lands next to the original, else in the folder selected in the Library, else at the top level. Saving used to always go to the top level.
  • Deleting goes to the system trash where there is one (macOS, Windows, and Linux through gio), for single items and whole folders. The delete confirmation now names the playlists and queues the items are in, and deleting a folder says how many items it holds.

docs.title: Renaming or Deleting a Saved Item Keeps the Library Consistent (ui/browser/LibraryRefs.kt, ui/browser/BrowserPopupHandler.kt, presets/PresetManager.kt, ui/PlaylistManager.kt)
docs.text:
• Fixed: renaming a saved FX single, FX chain or transition broke every playlist entry that pointed at it. Only deck presets had their playlists updated. Now all saved kinds do.
  • A rename now also follows the item into the live queues (A/B, BG, both FX queues, Transitions), Favorites and Recent, the deck or FX chain it is loaded on (so Save still writes back to the renamed file instead of recreating the old name) and, for presets, its thumbnail.
  • Deleting a saved item now also drops it from Favorites and Recent, and a deck or chain loaded from it becomes unsaved (Save asks for a name) instead of silently writing the deleted file back.
  • This is the groundwork for managing folders inside the Library, which is next.

docs.title: Multi-Select in the FX and Transitions Lists (ui/browser/FXBrowserPanel.kt, ui/browser/TransitionBrowserPanel.kt, ui/browser/BrowserPane.kt, ui/LibraryNavigation.kt, FX and transition queue panels)
docs.text:
• The FX and Transitions lists now multi-select like the Sources list. Ctrl/Cmd+click toggles a row, Shift+click selects a range, Ctrl+Shift+click adds a range. Right-click inside the selection for Add N to A/B (FX) Queue, Add N to BG FX Queue, Add N to '' and Delete N...; Q/Shift+Q enqueue the whole selection, Delete deletes it (or removes it from the open playlist), and dragging carries every selected row into a playlist or queue. Stock FX filters are skipped by queue, playlist and delete (they load one at a time); stock transitions queue and go into playlists, only saved ones delete.
  • Ctrl+A (Cmd+A) selects every row the list is showing, in all three lists, while the list has the keyboard.
  • The FX and transition queues take a multi-row drop, in order, like the source queues already did.
  • A list opened to pick for a deck, slot or transition still selects one row at a time, since a click there applies the row.

docs.title: Chain View: All Three FX Slots at Once (macro/FxMacroSync.kt, rendering/FxChain.kt, ui/PerfRows.kt, ui/FxChainHeader.kt, ui/PerformanceMatrixPanel.kt, ui/ParametersState.kt, ui/ChainLoad.kt, ui/BayHeader.kt)
docs.text:
• New: Chain view. One deck's source row on top and one row per FX slot below it, over the Browse list, so all three effects are playable at once. Open it from Chain View in any FX chain's ⋮ menu or with the Chain button on the pair view's Browse header (Master has one too, with Transitions on top). Load next to it swaps the source row for a load row: the effect highlighted in the list and three targets, → FX1, → FX2, → FX3, that put it into that slot; the slot rows stay where they are, so you can load, play and compare without leaving. Esc leaves in one press. On a Twister: shift + tap any of a deck's SRC knobs to open (or leave) its Chain view; all 16 knobs play the four rows. Right-bottom turns Load on: knob 4 becomes the list cursor and knobs 1-3 load the highlighted effect into slots 1-3, glowing in their slot's colour, while knobs 5-16 keep playing the slots. The bank buttons step decks without leaving. Chain view has no send knobs.
  • Every FX slot can now have a Perform row of its own. A page can place deck.A.fx1, deck.A.fx2, deck.A.fx3 (likewise B, BG, PV, and master.fx1..fx3). Knob 1 is the slot's Metaknob (tap to bypass), knobs 2-4 are its parameters, and the row's title badge says FX1, FX2 or FX3. Beside the knobs: the effect's name (click to browse that slot), the chain's ⋮ menu, the slot's Dry/Wet and, for effects with more than three parameters, the page arrows. Drop an effect on the badge to load it into that slot. The deck's die and FX ON sit on the FX1 row only. On a Twister the three slot rows light in three slightly different shades of the FX colour. They make up Chain view, and you can also pick them for your own pages in Preferences > MIDI Controls > Perform Pages.
  • A slot row always shows its own slot, whatever the chain's FX row is doing (group or focus mode), so three slot rows show the whole chain at once. Its knobs are also MIDI/OSC targets that always mean the same parameter (/macro/deckA_fx_s2/knob/3 is slot 2's third parameter on its page), unlike the FX row's knobs, which change with focus.
  • Each slot remembers its own parameter page. Focusing a slot now opens on the page that slot was last on (it used to start on page 1), so the FX row in focus mode and the slot's own row always agree. The page goes back to 1 when the slot gets a new effect and moves with the effect when you swap slots.

docs.title: Web TV: The Desktop's Stock Looks (scripts/gen_stock_web_presets.py, web/presets/stock-*.lsd, web/playlists/default.lsdplay)
docs.text:
• The web TV now plays the desktop's built-in source looks. 32 new presets (stock-<source>) are generated from the same shipped defaults the desktop uses, so each source moves with the music the way it does in the app and starts from a fresh random roll inside its ranges every time it comes on air: two airings of the same source differ. They join the foreground playlist next to the hand-made web-* looks, which stay. Fluid Ink (its default carries no audio response) and Fractal Flame (not a web source) are left out. The 16 stock FX chains and 8 transitions on the web TV already carry the new responses and ranges.
  • Run scripts/gen_stock_web_presets.py after changing a stock source default, then the content and reactivity tests and render_check. Sources that run bright (Domain Warp Fluid, Hyper Slice, Hyperbolic Tiling, Mandelbox, Metaballs, Reaction Diffusion, plus the earlier full-frame ones) are tagged so the autopilot keeps feedback and bloom chains off them.

docs.title: Fractal Flame Picked From Browse Showed Nothing (rendering/FlameEngine.kt)
docs.text: • Fixed: picking Fractal Flame as a source (not a Garden preset) gave a black deck. With Smooth at 0, the starting flame's setting, the density buffer kept a mipmapped filter without a mip chain, which makes the texture sample as black. Garden presets all have Smooth above 0, so they looked fine. The filter now follows Smooth.

docs.title: Left/Right Balance: Polar Tunnel, Kaleidoscope, Feedback, Chladni Cymatics (default_filters/polar_tunnel.fs, kaleidoscope.fs, feedback.fs, sources/chladni_cymatics)
docs.text:
• Polar Tunnel no longer leaves the left side of the screen dark. The tunnel wraps the picture around its circle, and the picture's left and right edges (often the darkest part) met on the left. They now meet at the bottom, with the middle of the picture running along the top, so the tunnel is balanced left to right.
  • Kaleidoscope and Feedback's Kaleido with an odd number of segments (3, 5, 7…) are now mirrored left to right. Odd counts mirror across only one screen axis, and it used to be the horizontal one, so the pattern pointed sideways. It is now the vertical one. Even counts (including the default 6) look exactly as before.
  • Chladni Cymatics no longer has a seam on the left with a round plate. With Plate Shape toward Circular, a Frequency M between whole numbers (which the vibration makes almost always) left a hard line on the left of the plate. It now sits at the bottom, and the circular pattern mirrors left to right at every M.

docs.title: Sources Randomize Out of the Box (resources/stock_defaults/sources/, rendering/MorphState.kt, parameters/ModulatableParameter.kt, macro/MacroEngine.kt, ui/ParametersUndo.kt)
docs.text:
• The deck die (and the deck's Rand control) now does something on every stock source. Each of the 32 shader sources ships with a random range on the parameters that change its look: fractal and pattern types, colour modes and palettes, twists, folds, cell and wave sizes, glow, hue and saturation. A roll picks new values inside those ranges, and Rand fades between rolls as before. Brightness, Quality, Zoom (mostly), reseed triggers and other "is the picture still watchable" controls are left alone. Each range leaves room for the parameter's built-in audio response, so a roll never pins a response against its limit. Mandala and Fractal Flame keep the randomization they already had.
  • The four macro knobs take part. A roll on a parameter a knob drives now moves the knob to the new value, so the knob and the picture stay in step and the knob no longer snaps the value back on the next frame. The Initial Range slider and its dice are now available on knob-driven parameters too (still not on parameters an FX Metaknob drives).
  • Stepped parameters (types, modes, palettes, side counts) jump halfway through a Rand fade instead of flickering through every step in between, and each step is now equally likely (the first and last used to come up half as often).
  • Ctrl+Z after a die roll now puts the values back, along with the knob positions. It used to restore only the modulators, so a rolled look stayed. Fractal Flame decks keep the old behaviour (its values only make sense with the flame they came from).
  • Stock presets and presets you saved keep their own values and are not randomized; pick the source itself to get the ranges. A default you saved for a source replaces them (Remove Saved Default brings them back).
  • Second pass after a first look in the app: Cyclic CA no longer goes flat after a roll (a new threshold restarts the pattern from noise, a new state count keeps the spirals and changes their number of bands; Neighbourhood is no longer rolled, since von Neumann stays frozen noise for minutes). Gyroid flies slower and zoomed out, and also rolls Zoom and Wireframe. Mandala rolls its recipe (the 32-beat recipe drift now wanders around the rolled pick instead of pinning it at the end of the list), its lobe range stops at 8 so the slow lobe drift stays in range, and Hue Offset is no longer rolled (its LFO already sweeps the whole hue circle). Mandelbox and Mandelbulb start brighter with more glow. Reaction Diffusion's Kill Trim only rolls upward, away from the flooded solid-colour regime.

• The deck die and the deck's Rand control now roll the deck's effects as well as its source. 25 of the 27 stock effects ship random ranges on the inputs that change their look: angles, segment and arm counts, centres, palettes and modes, streak and facet sizes, colour casts. A roll on a deck with effects in its chain gives a new source look and a new effect look together; the whole-rig die and Rand All do the same for every deck and for the Master FX chain.
  • The effect's main knob (its Metaknob) is never rolled. It means "how much" (Bloom intensity, Feedback decay, Strobe rate) and stays yours; an effect turned down to zero stays off after a roll. Invert and Luma Key have nothing else worth rolling and ship no ranges. Brightness-style inputs, feedback gain and Strobe's Freeze Hold are left alone too, as are the drifts in Feedback and Fluid Smear beyond small amounts (they compound every frame).
  • The transition die now rolls only the transition's ranged inputs, inside their ranges, and moves the TRANS knobs that drive them. It used to set every input anywhere in its full range, which could push Luminous Flash's Spread or Film Burn's Burn Spread high enough to make the picture pop the moment a fade started. All eight stock transitions ship ranges (Linear Crossfade rolls its curve); those two stay at or below 0.42. Rand All rolls the transition too, as a jump rather than a fade (a transition only shows while it fades). Ctrl+Z undoes all of it.
  • The eight stock transition presets carry the same ranges, so AutoVJ, playlists and the web TV get them. Copies already in your library keep their old settings; delete them (or use Restore Factory Presets) to get the new ones.
  • The 16 stock FX chains carry the ranges too, so the starting chains roll out of the box (copies already in your library keep their old settings). A chain you saved yourself keeps what it stored, and a default you saved yourself for an effect or transition replaces the ranges, as it does the built-in responses.

docs.title: Reactivity Recipes: Transitions (resources/stock_defaults/transitions/, rendering/isf/ISFAutoBindEngine.kt, presets/TransitionOps.kt, ui/TransitionSave.kt, defaults/transitions/)
docs.text:
• Seven of the eight stock transitions now move with the music during a fade. Luminous Flash punches its midpoint flash on the kick, Film Burn flares its ember edge on the kick, Cyber Datamosh tears on the hats and shears its colours on the kick, Kinetic Zoom punches deeper on the kick and streaks harder when it's loud, Liquid Displacement melts further with the bass, Noise Dissolve fringes its edge on the kick, and Vortex Swirl surges with the bass. Each has bypassed alternates to switch on by clicking its AUD or LFO cell, as on sources and effects. Linear Crossfade has nothing to move. Nothing moves at rest: with the crossfader fully on A or B the visible deck is shown as is.
  • Spread (Luminous Flash) and Burn Spread (Film Burn) are left alone, and the Inferno Film Burn preset's Burn Spread went from 0.464 to 0.45: above about 0.45 the flash or the burn already shows at the very start of a fade, so the picture pops the moment a fade begins.
  • The eight stock transition presets carry the same responses, so AutoVJ, the Festival Elite playlist and the web TV show them. Copies already in your library keep their old settings; delete them (or use Restore Factory Presets) to get the new ones.
  • Save as Default for and Remove Saved Default are in the transition's ⋮ menu (Transitions row and Mixer TRANS tab): picking that transition from then on starts from your values and modulators. The Save button and the * beside the transition name no longer count the built-in responses as a change.
  • Cyber Datamosh's Blockiness is now 0 to 100 like every other slider (it was 8 to 64 blocks); the old range maps onto it, and the stock preset was converted. Transition presets you saved yourself with a Blockiness value need it re-set.
  • Fixed in passing: a default saved or removed for an effect or transition now applies to the next copy you pick straight away, not only after a restart (new copies used to take the starting values and Metaknob targets the app read at launch).

docs.title: Transitions Rest Exactly on A or B (rendering/Renderer.kt)
docs.text: • With the crossfader fully on A or B, the transition shader no longer runs. The visible deck is copied straight through, so the resting picture is exactly that deck whatever the transition or its settings do, and the GPU skips a full-screen pass (up to 48 texture reads per pixel for Kinetic Zoom). Fades look the same as before.

docs.title: Cyber Datamosh Resting on Deck B (default_transitions/cyber_datamosh.fs, web/shaders/transitions/cyber_datamosh.fs)
docs.text: • Fixed: Cyber Datamosh could garble deck B's colours with the crossfader fully on B. At the very end of the fade the glitch envelope dipped a hair below zero (the shader's value of pi rounds slightly high), and raising a negative number to a fractional power is undefined on the GPU, so the red and blue channels sampled from a bad position. The envelope is now clamped at zero. The web TV copy has the same fix.

docs.title: FX "Save as Default" Keeps Modulators (rendering/isf/ISFAutoBindEngine.kt, rendering/isf/ISFFilter.kt, ui/FXChainMacroStrip.kt)
docs.text: <ul> <li>Fixed: saving an effect as its default dropped its modulators. "Save as Default for " kept only the Metaknob targets, knob order and base values, so any LFO or audio modulator on the slot was lost on new copies. The default now stores full parameters, modulators included (MIDI mappings are left out, as for generator defaults, and each new copy gets its own modulator ids). Defaults saved before this keep loading as before.

docs.title: LFO Min/Max Moves Independently (parameters/CvModulator.kt, parameters/ModulatableParameter.kt, cv/Evaluators.kt, web/evaluator.js, resources/stock_defaults/sources/, defaults/presets/, web/presets/)
docs.text:
• Fixed: changing an LFO's Max also moved its Min. The Min/Max slider assumed every modulator swings evenly either side of its centre, but a beat LFO on a 0-to-1 parameter was secretly remapped to swing only upward from the centre, so the real minimum shifted whenever you moved Max. Every bipolar source (LFO, beat sine, beat phase, sample and hold) now swings evenly around its centre on any parameter, and the slider's Min and Max are exactly the lowest and highest the modulator reaches, relative to the base value. Audio, trigger and MIDI sources never go below zero, so their Min is the offset and Max is offset plus depth.
  • Behaviour change: an LFO with depth d on a 0-to-1 parameter used to sweep from the base up to base + d; it now sweeps base ± d, clamped at the parameter's limits. The stock presets (the web TV presets and FX chains, Mandala 7 and 10) and all reactivity recipes were rewritten to keep their original sweep. Recipe LFOs on 0-to-1 parameters got a matching offset, so their sweep is unchanged; the 3d mandala and 3d spiral 2 factory presets were converted the same way. Presets you saved yourself keep their numbers and will swing wider; lower their Depth, or raise Min, to taste.
  • The web evaluator and its golden vectors match.

docs.title: Harmonograph Removed From the Stock Set (rendering/VisualSourceRegistry.kt, presets/GeneratorDefaults.kt, web/)
docs.text: • Harmonograph is gone for now. It drew one thin curve of at most 128 segments, which read as a single piece of string rather than the dense rosette a harmonograph should make. It is out of the stock sources, the web TV (its shader and three presets, so the playlists no longer include them) and the tour scripts (which now use Quasicrystal). A copy already in your library stays and still loads. A rebuilt version that builds up many windings is planned for v1.1.

docs.title: Browse Badges Skip Empty Decks (ui/browser/LoadedMarks.kt)
docs.text: • Fixed a stray deck badge on Mandala. An empty deck quietly holds a Mandala placeholder, so Browse showed its letter (for example B) beside Mandala even though nothing was loaded there. Empty decks no longer get a badge; loading something puts it back, and ejecting removes it.

docs.title: Camera-Relative Lighting in Mandelbulb, Mandelbox and KIFS (library/sources/{mandelbulb,mandelbox,kifs})
docs.text: • The lit side of these fractals now always faces you. The light used to be fixed in the scene, so as the camera orbited (or you rotated) the view, the shaded side swung round and one side looked very dim. The light now turns with the camera, so the brightness stays steady all the way round. The KIFS fill light turns with it too. The web TV copies match.

docs.title: Knob Track and Master/Clock Colors (ui/MacroKnobWidget.kt, ui/PerformanceUiContext.kt)
docs.text:
• The unlit part of a knob's arc is easier to see. It was the deck color at 35% brightness, which nearly vanished into the dark knob face on Deck B (blue) and PV (plum). It is now brighter for every deck; the lit arc is unchanged.
  • Master and Clock now have real colors on screen: Master is red and Clock is yellow, replacing the greys. The Twister's LEDs can only show plain RGB, so greys came out wrong; the controller now simply uses the same colors as the screen (Clock used to be plum on the hardware, the same as PV).

docs.title: Black Is Transparent in Sources (rendering/Renderer.kt, library/sources/*)
docs.text:
• Generator sources now let the BG deck show through wherever they are black. Video Feedback and 29 other generators (everything except Chladni Cymatics, Dynamic Spiral, Icosa H3, Mandala and Fractal Flame, which keep their own alpha) write an alpha that follows their brightest channel, the way Fractal Flame does. Bright areas cover what is behind them and dark areas reveal it; the picture over a black BG is unchanged.
  • The renderer now stores source alpha as alpha instead of squaring it (colour x alpha, alpha kept as written), so sources with a partial alpha such as Chladni Cymatics blend a little more evenly.

docs.title: Reactivity Recipes: Sources (presets/StockDefaults.kt, presets/GeneratorDefaults.kt, resources/stock_defaults/sources/)
docs.text:
• Thirty-three sources now react to the music out of the box: Apollonian, Dynamic Spiral, Tunnel Scenes, Kali Set, Aurora Ribbons, Domain Warp Fluid, Voronoi Cells, Wave Ripples, Glitch Blocks, Metaballs, Halftone Matrix, Video Feedback, Mandelbulb, Mandelbox, KIFS, Pseudo-Kleinian, Hyperbolic Tiling, Icosa H3, Reaction Diffusion, Lenia, Cyclic CA, Nebula Volume, Celestial Engine, Chladni Cymatics, Escape Time, Girih Stars, Gyroid Hyperspace, Hyper Slice, Isometric Voxels, Quasicrystal, Thin Film, Mandala and Fractal Flame. Fractal Flame's recipe moves only the performance handles, camera push and tone (Breathe and Warp, a slow Spin sway, colour Drift, kick push on Magnify, kick flashes on Exposure), never the xform parameters the morph evolves. Mandala's four arm lengths each move differently (L1 jiggles with the amplitude, L2 is an 8-beat sine, L3 jumps to a new length every 16 beats, L4 rides a 6-beat ramp), the colours cycle once a beat, a new shape recipe arrives every 32 beats and a new lobe count every 256. On the simulations the always-on responses touch only the look and the speed; anything that could change what the pattern does (growth rules, thresholds) is gentle and bypassed, and Reaction Diffusion and Cyclic CA have a bypassed Reseed response that restarts the pattern on a hard kick (on by default in Lenia). Each has a hand-written set of audio and beat responses on its key parameters (for example the gasket breathing on the kick, aurora curtains rising with loudness, glitches landing on kick and hat hits). Where a parameter has more than one idea, the extra ones are wired but bypassed, so you only click an AUD or LFO cell to switch them on.
  • They are ordinary modulators: edit, bypass or delete them like any other. A default you saved yourself still wins over the shipped recipe. Recipes are part of each source's shipped default (see Stock Defaults Are Files below); a test checks every file against its shader's parameters.

docs.title: Reactivity Recipes: Effects (resources/stock_defaults/filters/, rendering/isf/ISFAutoBindEngine.kt)
docs.text:
• All 27 stock effects now come with audio responses. Each gets one running response and a few bypassed alternates, as the sources do: for example the bloom pumping on the bass, the RGB split snapping open on the kick, the feedback trails pushing outward on the kick, the gradient palette cycling when the music is loud, the radial blur bursting and the VHS tracking jumping on the kick. Invert, Luma Key and Video Strobe ship their responses bypassed only: a kick-driven invert, a moving key edge or a faster strobe is too much to switch on for you.
  • An effect's main knob still means "how much". When the response sits on the parameter the Metaknob drives, it multiplies (MUL) instead of adding, so it scales with the knob: an effect turned down to zero stays off, and turning it up makes the hits bigger too. Other responses sit on parameters that only show once the effect is on. Feedback and Fluid Smear, which build on their own past frames, get the gentlest responses. Pixelate is the one exception: its size starts at 1 (off), so a kick there makes 2-pixel blocks.
  • The 16 stock FX chains carry these responses (and the random ranges, see below), so the starting chains on every deck and on Master react to the music. Each chain keeps its own settings; inputs a chain does not store take the effect's default. Copies of the stock chains already in your library keep their old settings; delete them (or use Restore Factory Presets) to get the new ones. A default you saved yourself with Save as Default replaces the shipped response; Remove Saved Default brings it back. The Vortex Swirl transition shares an id with the Vortex Swirl effect but never picks up the effect's default.

docs.title: Stock Defaults Are Files (presets/StockDefaults.kt, presets/GeneratorDefaults.kt, rendering/isf/ISFAutoBindEngine.kt, resources/stock_defaults/)
docs.text:
• Each stock source and effect now ships one default file (stock_defaults/sources/<id>.json, stock_defaults/filters/<id>.json) in the same shape as the default you save yourself, listing only what differs from the shader: knob targets, Metaknob targets, and the built-in audio responses. It replaces the separate recipe files and the knob tables that lived in code. Nothing changes on screen; a default you save still replaces the stock one, and Reset/Remove Saved Default goes back to it.
  • Third-party shaders are unchanged: their knobs are worked out each time they load, and nothing is written until you choose Save as Default.

docs.title: Audio Response (audio/AudioEngine.kt, ui/AudioEnginePanel.kt, ui/AppPreferencesStore.kt)
docs.text:
• One Audio Response slider in Preferences > Audio Hardware (0% to 200%, default 100%, saved) sets how strongly everything that follows the music moves. It scales the Amp, Bass, Mid, High and Flux signals after auto gain, so every audio modulator follows it the same way, whether it came with a source or you added it. 0% means nothing follows the music; above 100% quiet passages move more and loud ones reach the top sooner. Beat detection, LFOs and the beat clock are not affected.
  • Use it instead of Input Gain to calm the picture down or wake it up: with Auto Gain on, the audio signals level themselves, so Input Gain mostly changes what beat detection hears. Input Gain now has a tooltip saying so.

docs.title: Audio Auto Gain (audio/AudioAgc.kt, audio/AudioEngine.kt, ui/AudioEnginePanel.kt, ui/AppPreferencesStore.kt)
docs.text:
• Audio-reactive parameters now respond the same at any input level. Amp, bass, mid and high (and their flux signals) used to be divided by a fixed scale, so a quiet feed barely moved anything and a hot one pinned everything at full. A new Auto Gain (AGC) option in Preferences > Audio Hardware, on by default, tracks each band's recent peak (instant attack, about 8 seconds to let go) and normalizes against it, so the peaks of the music reach full scale whatever the level. Silence and room noise are not boosted (at most about 12x). AGC Headroom sets how hot it runs, and a readout shows the boost per band. Switch AGC off to get the old fixed scale back.
  • Beat detection, downbeat detection and the silence gate still see the raw levels, so tempo tracking is unchanged. Settings are saved (audioAgcEnabled, audioAgcHeadroom). The web TV still uses the fixed scale.

docs.title: macOS Log Cleanup and Syphon (rendering/TextureStreamer.kt, rendering/Shader.kt, Main.kt)
docs.text:
• The Mac log is quiet again. A missing Syphon framework is now reported once instead of every two seconds, and the shader "no vertex array object bound" validation warning and the window-icon error no longer appear on macOS. None of these changed behaviour.
  • Syphon now ships with the Mac downloads. Both Mac zips include a universal (Apple Silicon and Intel) Syphon.framework, so Syphon video in and out can work there. It is built once by a manual CI workflow, not on every release.
  • Dynamic Spiral loses its dead Trail Decay knob. It did nothing (the shader no longer draws trails); trails belong to the Feedback effect. Presets that mentioned it were cleaned up, and the web TV copy matches.
  • Fewer false warnings: a Speed knob that feeds a phase (LSD_PHASES) no longer logs "Uniform not found" for every such source, and the Flame engine's startup line is no longer a warning.

docs.title: Downbeat Detection and Bar Length (audio/DownbeatDetector.kt, audio/AudioEngine.kt, cv/CVRegistry.kt, ui/TempoSyncPanel.kt, ui/PerformanceClockControls.kt, ui/ClockKnob.kt)
docs.text:
• The app can now find the first beat of the bar. Before, a "bar" was just every fourth beat counted from wherever the tracker started or you last tapped. Preferences > Tempo & Sync has a new Bar & Downbeat section: Downbeat: Auto (from the music) listens for where the kick and bass land hardest in the bar and moves the bar line there, so bar-length LFOs and sequences, the bar dots and the Twister clock knob's downbeat flash line up with the music. It needs the Audio Beat Tracker clock, a few bars of steady music, and works best on dance music with a clear kick; it is off by default (Manual). A confidence bar shows how sure it is, and the bar dots' tooltip repeats it. It only moves the bar line after a position clearly wins twice in a row, so a breakdown doesn't send it wandering.
  • Say where beat 1 is, and it stays said. SNAP (and RESYNC in Preferences) now makes the beat nearest to now beat 1 of the bar: it moves the beat count to the closest bar line, by at most half a bar, not just to the nearest whole beat. The first tap of a tap-tempo run does the same ("tap on the one"); the following taps only set the tempo and keep the bar line. Either one protects your answer from the detector for 16 bars, and afterwards the detector needs strong evidence to overrule it.
  • Beats per bar: a new setting (2 to 8, default 4) for waltzes and other metres. The bar dots, the clock knob flash and the detector follow it, and it sets the Ableton Link quantum too. With Link on, Link's quantum defines the bar and Auto downbeat pauses.
  • Beat counts are now kept so a bar starts on every multiple of the bar length; LFOs and sequencers set to a bar (or more) jump once when the bar line moves, and nothing else changes. Settings are saved (beatsPerBar, downbeatMode).
  • The web TV does not use this yet; it still counts bars from its own beat count.

docs.title: Web TV: Embed Mode for Spaz Radio (web/embed.js, web/embedmode.js, web/feedring.js, web/feed-worklet.js, web/dsp.js, web/ui.js, web/autopilot.js, web/renderer.js)
docs.text:
• The web TV can now run inside another app. index.html?embed shows only the picture: no TV body, controls, on-screen display, menu, ident or nameplate, no CRT warm-up, nothing that takes touches. It turns itself on, and it never plays the stream, uses the microphone, registers the service worker, polls the track name or follows a desktop live broadcast unless the host asks. This is what the Spaz Radio Android app will bundle in place of its oscilloscope.
  • The host feeds the audio. The host app plays the radio itself and pushes the decoded sound in with LSD.feed(pcm, sampleRate) (mono 16-bit or float samples, an ArrayBuffer, or base64). It goes through the same analysis as the radio did (bass, mid, high, flux, onset worklet, beat clock, energy sections), so the picture moves exactly as on spaz.org. When the host stops feeding, the picture just goes quiet (no "no signal" snow).
  • Host controls: LSD.setOption takes quality (auto / low / high), reactivity, reducedMotion, live and sync (milliseconds the picture is delayed to match the speaker); LSD.pause() / LSD.resume() stop and restart drawing and audio analysis when the picture is hidden. LSD.next(), prev() and hold() exist for later touch controls.
  • Smooth before sharp when embedded: the picture renders at a 720p-class budget and steps down faster (to a quarter of that) when frames run slow; heavy looks stay off unless the host asks for quality High, since the GPU test can't be trusted on phones. ?embed&debug adds an on-screen fps / resolution readout.
  • New headless check web/checks/embed_check.mjs and unit test web/tools/feedring.test.mjs.

docs.title: Web TV: At Home (web/ui.js, web/index.html, web/tv.css, web/autopilot.js)
docs.text:
• Click the TV to turn it on. The whole set is the power switch: any click on a TV that is off turns it on, and a click on the cabinet (not the picture or the other controls) turns it off.
  • Quieter by default: the TV no longer names every new look on screen; MENU › Announce looks turns that back on. Looks you pick with CH or FX are still named, and I shows the info any time.
  • Livelier by default: REACT starts at 200% (the range is now 25-400%), since most radio shows move the picture too little at 100%.
  • CH ▲ / ▼ work like a TV's channel buttons. ▲ goes to the next channel number and ▼ to the one before it, so ▼ then ▲ always brings you back where you were (a channel you've already seen keeps its FX chain). Before, ▼ went back to whatever look had been on before, and ▲ to a random one.
  • Fullscreen and microphone from the keyboard or MENU. S (or MENU › Fullscreen, or a double-click on the picture) toggles fullscreen. A (or MENU › Input) switches the picture from the radio to your microphone, so it follows the music in the room; the browser asks permission first, the mic is only analysed (never played back, so no feedback), and turning the TV off puts the radio back.
  • Clearer labels under the TV's buttons and knobs, and turning a knob no longer switches the TV off when you let go over it.
  • The TV says who made it. A Liquid LSD nameplate under the screen links to liquid-lsd.greenjon.com; the first power-on of a visit plays a short ident with the eye-and-drop logo; MENU › ABOUT describes the desktop app with a QR code to the site; pressing I (or clicking the picture) adds a Liquid LSD line; about every 30 minutes a one-line bumper invites viewers to make their own; the LIVE card says "from Liquid LSD". Shared links now show a preview picture and description.

• The screen stays on while the TV is on. Laptops and phones no longer dim and lock in the middle of a show (where the browser supports it).
  • Phone lock screen and media keys. The lock screen (and your keyboard's media keys) show the show playing on Spaz Radio and the look on air; play/pause turns the TV on and off, next and previous change the look.
  • Install it like an app. Your browser can install the web TV ("Install" / "Add to Home Screen"); it opens fullscreen with its own icon, and starts even without a network (showing no signal until the radio is reachable).
  • Kiosk mode for venue screens: add ?kiosk to the address and the TV body disappears, the picture fills the screen, it turns itself on, and the mouse pointer hides. Keyboard and swipe controls still work. If the browser won't start sound by itself, the screen says to click or press a key.
  • A TV service menu. The new MENU button (or M) opens a green on-screen menu like an old set's picture menu: SYNC, Announce looks, REACT, TIME, Reduced motion and Big GPU looks, plus Reset and About; the selected row explains itself. Arrow keys, clicks or the mouse wheel change the settings, and the TV remembers them.
  • SYNC for delayed speakers. With Bluetooth or other speakers that play late, the beat pulses used to land before the sound. MENU › SYNC delays the picture by up to 400 ms to match, and MENU › TAP SYNC works it out for you: tap Space (or the picture) on 8 beats you hear.
  • Reduced motion. If your system asks for less motion (or you turn it on in MENU), the TV calms down: the picture reacts at most 120% as strongly (the default is 200%), hard looks, flashing and glitch effects and flash transitions are left out, there is no cut on the drop, and crossfades take twice as long.
  • Looks that suit the tempo. Once the TV has the beat, slow music (under 95 BPM) brings up more calm, groove and mid-driven looks, and fast music (over 125) more hard, kick and hi-hat looks. It's a lean, not a rule: every look still comes up.
  • Effects answer the look instead of echoing it. A look that mostly follows the kick no longer gets an effect chain that only follows the kick too; it gets one that also moves with the mids or hats, so more of the music shows on screen. Looks made of fine dots or thin lines (spirals, harmonographs) no longer get pixelating, halftone, tunnel, displacement or motion-blur effects, which smeared them out to near black; Beat Spiral (the first look) is also much denser and brighter.
  • A LIVE title card with your name. When you go live, the web TV rolls in a red station ident, "LIVE" and your name, and keeps the name on its display. Set the name in Preferences › Web Broadcast › Broadcaster name (blank shows just LIVE). Older web pages simply ignore it. The LIVE badge on the TV now really switches, too.

docs.title: Snappier MIDI, and Esc Cancels the Unsaved-Deck Prompt (ui/UIManager.kt, Main.kt, ui/NavigationSurface.kt)
docs.text:
• Controller knobs and buttons now take effect in the same frame. Incoming MIDI used to be handled after the frame was drawn, so every turn reached the screen one frame late. It is now applied first. MIDI is also handled while the window is minimised, instead of piling up and replaying when you restore it.
  • Esc now cancels the "unsaved deck" prompt, as its Cancel button's tooltip always said. Before, Esc did nothing there.
  • Internal: the controller surfaces are built once instead of every frame, so the hardware knob layout is cached between frames.

docs.title: Old Feedback and 3D-View Settings Removed From Presets (models/PresetModels.kt, presets/PresetMigrator.kt, presets/PresetDependencyAnalyzer.kt)
docs.text:
• Presets no longer have a deck-level feedback section. Feedback has been an FX for a while; the leftover feedbackParameters field is gone from the preset format, along with its handling in the loader, the dependency check and the flame tools.
  • Your existing presets and sessions still load. The old section is simply skipped, and presets saved from now on don't contain it. Only zoom and Z-rotate are stored as the deck's framing.

docs.title: Stock FX Chain Fixes (defaults/fx_chains/*, web/tools/validate_content.mjs)
docs.text: • Six stock FX chains got back settings they had been silently losing. Renamed effect parameters had left them pointing at parameters their effects no longer have, so those settings were ignored: Pop-Art Comic Print's edge palette and overlay, Digital Bitcrush Mosaic's diamond pixels and split mode, Prismatic Crystal Kaleidoscope's spectral split, Grindhouse VHS Bootleg's phosphor mask and darker grade, Laser Concert Anamorphic's brighter grade, and Cosmic Black Hole Vortex's displacement (two values were out of range). Copies of these chains already in your library are not changed.

docs.title: Housekeeping: One Config Folder, Smaller Download (ui/shortcuts/ShortcutManager.kt, ui/FileSystemManager.kt, build.gradle.kts)
docs.text:
• Custom key bindings now live in ~/.liquid-lsd/keybindings.json, next to your source notes, instead of a second ~/.liquidlsd folder. Custom key bindings are reset once: the old file is not read. Copy ~/.liquidlsd/keybindings.json over if you want to keep them.
  • Removed the unused OpenAL audio library from the build, which makes the download smaller. Audio is unaffected.
  • Internal: the bundled transition presets are now seeded from default_transition_presets, so they no longer share a folder name with the stock .fs transitions. Existing installs are not affected; only fresh installs and "restore defaults" use it.

docs.title: Master Knobs Say LEVEL, Not ALPHA (macro/MacroEngine.kt, presets/SessionSerializer.kt)
docs.text:
• The Master bank's first three knobs are now labelled LEVEL A, LEVEL B and LEVEL BG (they were ALPHA A, ALPHA B, ALPHA BG), matching the Level faders everywhere else.
  • Saved sessions are relabelled when they load, but only knobs that still carry the old default label and still control the matching level. Knobs you renamed or rebound keep your label.

docs.title: Speeds Never Jump the Picture (rendering/isf/PhaseIntegrators.kt, rendering/isf/ISFParser.kt, rendering/isf/ISFVisualSource.kt, rendering/isf/ISFFilter.kt, cv/ClockAnchors.kt, cv/Evaluators.kt, every stock source and effect with a speed, web/isf.js, web/evaluator.js)
docs.text:
• Fixed pictures that jumped when a speed changed late in a set. The shaders multiplied each speed by the time since the app started, so the longer Liquid LSD ran, the further any change of speed threw the picture: an hour in, an LFO or the music on a speed made it jump every frame, and even turning a Speed knob, a macro or a preset morph scrubbed it. Liquid LSD now adds each speed up frame by frame, so changing it only changes how fast things move. This covers all 27 stock sources and the 5 effects with a speed or rate (Flight Speed, Morph Speed, Wave Speed, Hue Cycle Speed, Strobe Rate and the rest), on the desktop and the web TV. A freshly loaded source looks the same as before.
  • LFOs and step sequencers clocked in seconds or frames no longer jump when their period changes, whether from the knob, a controller, OSC, a macro or a preset morph. Beat-clocked ones were never affected and stay locked to the bar.
  • Shader authors: declare speeds as "LSD_PHASES": { "FlightPhase": ["FlightSpeed"] } in the ISF header and use FlightPhase instead of TIME * FlightSpeed (see the user guide, Visual Sources). The web TV's check that kept music off speed knobs now only applies to shaders that still multiply by time.

docs.title: Web TV: Viewer Controls (web/ui.js, web/index.html, web/tv.css, web/autopilot.js, web/renderer.js)
docs.text:
• Change channel. CH ▲ ▼ on the TV (or the arrow keys, or a swipe on the picture) skips to the next look or back to the previous one, with the FX chain it had.
  • FX swaps the FX chain on the look on air; HOLD keeps the look until you release it.
  • TIME sets how long each look holds (8, 16, 32 or 64 bars); REACT sets how strongly the picture reacts to the music (25-400%, 200% by default), for quiet or very loud streams. Both are remembered.
  • On-screen display: on every change the screen shows the channel, the look and its FX chain in phosphor green, plus the track playing on the radio. Click the picture or press I to see it again.
  • The heaviest looks only play on computers that can run them. At power-on the TV times one frame of its heaviest fractal (about a tenth of a second). Pseudo-Kleinian, Nebula, Apollonian, Hyper Slice, Mandelbulb, Icosa, Mandelbox, Lenia and Reaction-Diffusion only join the rotation if that frame is quick (discrete graphics, Apple Silicon, fast integrated chips); laptops with basic integrated graphics and phones keep the lighter looks. Measured on an Intel UHD (Tiger Lake GT1): 52 ms, so those stay off there.
  • Smoother on slower computers and phones. The web TV renders at a lower resolution when the graphics card can't keep up (and back up when it can), and never above 1080p internally, so 4K screens and laptops stay fluid. The next look's shaders load during the current one, so changes no longer stutter or show a look without its effects for a moment.
  • A beat light on the badge blinks on every beat: green when locked onto the music, amber when keeping time on its own.
  • While the desktop is broadcasting live the controls are locked and the screen says so. The badge now really switches to LIVE (it never did before).
  • Fullscreen keeps the on-screen display; on a phone the picture fills the width and the controls wrap.

docs.title: Web TV: On the Beat (web/beattrack.js, web/onset-worklet.js, web/dsp.js, web/autopilot.js, web/settings.json)
docs.text:
• The web TV finds the radio's beat and locks to it. Pulses, flashes and beat-synced LFOs now land on the kicks of whatever is playing, not just at roughly the right tempo. It locks within a few seconds, follows tempo changes, and keeps time through breaks. The timing allows for the browser's audio delay, so the picture matches what you hear.
  • Looks change on the bar. The autopilot counts its holds in bars (16 for the main looks, 32 for the background) and finishes each crossfade on a bar line, so the new look arrives with the music. The next look is loaded during the hold, so the change is never late.
  • No signal looks like no signal. If the radio stream drops or goes silent, the screen fades to analog snow with NO SIGNAL, and the TV reconnects to the stream on its own every 10 seconds.
  • The TV follows the song. When a track breaks down (the bass drops out) a calm or building look comes in on the next bar, and when the drop lands a hard look cuts in right on it, with a flash. All eight transitions are now in the rotation.
  • Very fast music (drum and bass) is followed at half time: every kick still lands on a beat or a half beat.

docs.title: Web TV: Every Source On Air, Nothing Deaf (web/presets/*, web/fxchains/*, web/playlists/*, web/tools/reactivity.test.mjs, web/checks/render_check.*, scripts/gen_web_presets.py)
docs.text:
• 48 new web presets give every web source a place in the rotation: Aurora Ribbons, Cyclic CA, Girih Stars, Glitch Blocks, Halftone Matrix, Harmonograph, Hyperbolic Tiling, Isometric Voxels, Kali Set, Metaballs, Quasicrystal, Thin Film, Tunnel Scenes, Video Feedback, Voronoi Cells and Wave Ripples each get a groove, a hard (or kick, hat or mid) and an ambient look. The ambient ones play on the background.
  • Ten more sources on the web TV: Apollonian, Escape Time (Julia sets), Fluid Ink, KIFS, Lenia, Mandelbox, Mandelbulb, Nebula, Pseudo-Kleinian and Reaction-Diffusion, with 27 new looks; every desktop generator except Fractal Flame now plays on the web. Flights lunge forward on the kicks.
  • 24 new FX chains on the web TV, all moving with the music: reactive versions of the desktop's stock chains (Cyberpunk, Bitcrush, FLIR, VHS, Hyperspace, Laser, Chrome, Mercury, Neon, Pop Art, Prism, Warmth, Drop Weapon, Wormhole, Black Hole, 3D Elevation) and new ones for effects the web TV never used (ink smear, ripple drop, CRT, thermal drop, mirror ball, halftone, motion blur, luma key). Every one of the 27 effects is now on air somewhere. None of them strobe: fast full-screen flashing is a photosensitivity risk on a public stream.
  • Fixed pictures that jittered after a few minutes on air. 23 presets modulated a speed (flight speed, flow speed, vibration speed...). The shaders multiply speed by the running time, so the longer the TV ran, the harder every wobble in the music jumped the picture. Those presets now move size, glow, colour and shape with the music instead.
  • Nothing deaf on the web TV. Seven presets that ignored the music are gone, the three trail chains now move with kicks, mids and hats, and a test keeps any preset or chain that doesn't react to audio or the beat out of the playlists.
  • Full-frame looks no longer wash out. Sources that fill the screen with colour (cellular automata, fractals, cells, ripples...) skip the trail and bloom chains, which piled up on them into one flat colour.
  • The drop strobe no longer flickers at random. It flashes the picture negative once per loud bass hit instead of running a strobe whose rate jumped with the bass.

docs.title: Sources: Clearer Badge, One Gain, Lighter Off-Air Decks (ui/PerformanceDeckControls.kt, ui/ParametersTabs.kt, ui/browser/*, ui/DeckSourcePicker.kt, rendering/Deck.kt, rendering/DeckRenderBudget.kt, rendering/Renderer.kt, rendering/VisualSourceRegistry.kt, presets/DeckOps.kt, parameters/ParameterResolver.kt, Main.kt)
docs.text:
• The badge says what a preset plays: curated-0001 · Fractal flame, the source dimmed after the preset name (dropped first when space is short; the tooltip always has it). In Browse a saved preset's info column starts with its source, and a preset whose source isn't installed shows ⚠ and says it won't load.
  • Gain is one deck parameter, Deck A/Gain (and so on), so a MIDI, OSC or macro mapping on it keeps working whatever the deck plays. Mappings saved to the old per-source address (Deck A/Mandala/Gain) still work. The duplicate Alpha rows under MST > LEVELS are gone; LEVELS is the level faders.
  • Deck Zoom and Deck Rotate are the deck's own framing rows on the SRC tab, so they no longer look like a second copy of a generator's Zoom. Picking a new source resets them; a preset keeps its own.
  • Clicking the stock source of the preset you're playing loads that source's defaults. Clicking the source a deck already plays bare still does nothing.
  • The A/B queue arrows say where they load: both rows' tooltips name the off-air deck the next item goes to.
  • Off-air decks cost less GPU. PV renders at half the output size unless it's streamed. With Off-air decks at half frame rate (Preferences > General, on by default), a deck the output can't show renders every other frame; its monitor runs at half rate and simulations on it run at half speed until it comes on air. Streamed decks always render in full.
  • Shaders no longer follow the mouse. iMouse / u_mouse read the centre of the frame, so moving the cursor around the UI doesn't steer the output.
  • A source that fails to compile is marked ⚠ in Browse, with the first compiler error on hover.
  • Bundled source fixes reach existing installs. On startup a bundled generator file you haven't edited is updated to the new version; an edited one is kept.
  • The empty-deck card has one Add Source button that opens Browse on the deck's sources and presets (the long flat preset menu is gone), in the theme's colours.
  • One name: sources are sources (a procedural one is a generator); "visual source", "Gen" and "Stock Generator" are gone.

• Tagged presets no longer show as unsaved the moment they load. Every garden, curated and imported flame (and any preset with tags or notes) showed * and a red Save right away, and loading something else over it asked about unsaved changes.
  • Changing sources no longer leaks GPU memory. Picking a generator or loading a preset left the previous one's buffers allocated (tens of MB per Fractal Flame load, plus simulation grids and feedback buffers), so a long queue of flames kept growing. An external-video stream you switch away from is disconnected too.
  • Save writes back where the preset came from. Saving a preset loaded from a subfolder (garden, imported-flames, your own folders) used to create a second copy at the top of presets/. Save As with a new name still saves to presets/. Auto Save follows the same rule.
  • A preset whose generator is missing won't load. It used to keep the previous generator, reset its parameters and show the preset's name on it. You now get a message naming the missing source, and the deck is left as it was. In a restored session such a deck comes back empty and is listed under missing items.
  • Presets of shaders added after startup now load. Sources picked up by Rescan Now could be picked, but their presets fell back to the previous generator.
  • Rescan Now and Add Folder no longer touch the GPU off the render thread, and rescanning no longer breaks effects and transitions already in use.
  • Deck Zoom and Rotate Z now work on Isometric Voxels and Wave Ripples. User shaders with inputs named RotateX / RotateY now count as 3D, like the bundled raymarchers.
  • Removed 16 deck parameters that did nothing (the old deck feedback and 3D-view controls). They no longer appear as MIDI/OSC/macro targets or get randomized, and new presets don't save them. Older presets still load.
  • Tooltips: Eject says it empties the deck and keeps its FX chain; the deck's die lists what it randomizes; Save is greyed out on an external-video deck, with the reason. A user shader's parameter no longer borrows the old Feedback description because of its name.
  • Docs: the Visual Sources page no longer promises live shader recompiling, and documents shader ids, is3D and the Eject behaviour.

docs.title: FX Polish (ui/FxChainHeader.kt, ui/FxSlotCell.kt, rendering/FxChain.kt, presets/FxShortlist.kt, presets/FxOps.kt, presets/SessionSerializer.kt, rendering/Renderer.kt, ui/FXChainMacroStrip.kt)
docs.text:
• BYPASS is now FX ON. The chain switch was lit while the chain was on, under a label that said the opposite. It now reads FX ON (lit = on), like each slot's power button, and whether it is on is saved with your session.
  • The unsaved • now means what it says. It lights up for any change the chain file stores: a slot, a parameter, a Dry/Wet, a link or a Metaknob target. Turning the Super Knob or a Metaknob is still performing, not editing, so it doesn't count. Revert to Saved now undoes parameter tweaks too.
  • One chain menu. The FX row's ⋮ and the chain's Edit tab show the same menu: Focus, Save As, Revert to Saved, Clear All Slots, Copy / Paste Chain. New Chain is gone: Clear All Slots empties the chain and starts a new Untitled one. Save As starts in the folder the chain came from.
  • Ctrl+Z undoes every FX change, wherever you make it: dragging slots to swap or copy, drops, Paste, Reset Parameters, Clear, Revert and Library loads. Stepping through the shortlist and FX queue steps are not undone step by step.
  • The shortlist arrows show where you are. The slot name's tooltip says which list ◀ ▶ walk and your place in it (★ 3/8, Blur 4/12). Stepping off either end of an effect's category now lands in your favorites.
  • The mouse wheel no longer swaps a live effect by accident. Hold Ctrl to step a slot with the wheel; a plain wheel scrolls as usual.
  • Middle-click: on the Super Knob it does nothing (centring it moved every linked slot), and on a focused parameter's knob it restores that parameter's default, like its ⟲ button.
  • A turned-down chain says so. When a chain's own Dry/Wet (set on its Edit tab) is below 100%, its name shows it (Wet 40%), and at 0% the name is dimmed.
  • A Metaknob with no targets says so: its knob reads NO TARGET instead of META, and the slot's tooltip explains.
  • Feedback and trail effects start clean when they come back. A slot that was bypassed, at 0% wet or in a switched-off chain no longer flashes the picture it held when it stopped.
  • One name per thing: the Edit block is SUPER KNOB & METAKNOBS, the link-all toggle is Link All (also on the Twister), slots are Slot 1-3, and the chain's level is Chain Dry/Wet. The duplicate Deck X/FXChain/DryWet parameter path is gone; MIDI / OSC mappings to it need relearning on Deck X/FX/DryWet.
  • Tooltips on the FX queue arrows say which deck the item goes to, and that Decks A and B share one A/B queue position.

• FX chains no longer all show as unsaved at launch. A chain restored from your session is compared with the file it came from, so the amber • and Save only light up when it really differs; the starting chains are clean too, and Revert to Saved works on them.
  • Saving over a chain file keeps its tags. Save used to write the file back with no tags. Save As also starts from the chain's tags, and the chain takes the name you saved it as.
  • A failed chain save tells you. A write error (disk full, no permission) now shows a message and the chain stays marked unsaved, instead of looking saved.
  • Eject and empty presets leave the FX chain alone. Ejecting a deck used to reset its FX chain's parameters, Super Knob and links and blank its name while keeping the effects, so a later Save wrote the reset values over the chain file. Clearing a deck's FX on purpose (Clear with FX) now also refreshes the FX row's knobs.
  • Resetting a focused parameter lands on its default. On rate/speed/decay-type parameters (the exponential focus knobs) the ⟲ button and the Twister tap used to leave the parameter at a different value; a parameter the Metaknob drives now resets by moving the Metaknob.
  • Ctrl+Z undoes FX changes made in Edit. Paste Chain, Clear Chain Slots, Paste Slot, Clear Slot and drops onto a chain or slot in the Edit bay can now be undone; before, Ctrl+Z skipped them.
  • The focus parameter page follows the effect. Replacing the focused effect with one that has fewer parameters (or hiding knobs) used to leave the row on a page that no longer exists, with knobs 2-4 blank.

docs.title: Linked FX Knobs Work, Relative Super Knob, Metaknob Fixes (macro/MacroEngine.kt, rendering/FxChain.kt, rendering/isf/ISFFilter.kt, ui/FXChainMacroStrip.kt, ui/FxLinkDefaults.kt, ui/LinkModeButton.kt, ui/FxSlotCell.kt)
docs.text:
• A linked slot's knob now moves its Metaknob. Before, turning knob 2-4 on a slot linked to the Super Knob did nothing and snapped back, and in Focus Mode a linked slot's knob 1 was dead. Turning it now moves just that Metaknob; the Super Knob carries on from there (Relative) or picks it up again when it reaches it (Pickup).
  • The Super Knob no longer yanks a Metaknob you set by hand. Moving a linked Metaknob any other way (its Edit row, MIDI, or editing a parameter it drives) is treated the same as turning its knob.
  • "Default FX chain linking" is now Linked or Unlinked, Linked by default. The Auto option (unlinked while a Twister is connected) is gone: a linked slot no longer costs you its knob. A saved Auto setting reads as Linked.
  • Fixed: a Metaknob with no targets came back as a Dry/Wet control after saving. An empty target list is now saved and restored as empty.
  • Fixed: a target naming a parameter the effect doesn't have drove Dry/Wet. It now drives nothing and shows (missing) in the target editors. A user shader that shares a stock effect's id no longer gets that effect's curated target.
  • A Metaknob aimed at Dry/Wet now owns it like any other target: the focus header's Wet slider moves the Metaknob instead of being overwritten every frame, and macro, MIDI and OSC writes to it are suspended.
  • Focus in Edit is the real focus. The CHAIN MACRO block's Focus used to be a separate, Edit-only state that never moved the knobs. Focusing there (row menu) now focuses the chain everywhere, and the block shows which parameters knobs 2-4 hold, with page arrows and Group Mode.
  • Removed Replace all links with... from the Metaknob row menu (it wiped every link at once); links are edited in the slot's Metaknob links block and on the Edit-row strip. Reset to Factory Default is now Remove Saved Default for , and both default items explain what they save and reset.
  • New: Super Knob response (Preferences), Relative by default. Every linked slot now moves as soon as you turn the Super Knob and keeps its own position: slots at 20% and 90% both rise, stay apart, both reach 100% at the top and 0% at the bottom, and come back when the Super Knob does. Pickup keeps the old behaviour (each slot waits until the Super Knob reaches it, then follows it exactly); a slot still waiting shows an amber link button with both values in its tooltip.
  • On the Twister, a slot waiting for Super Knob pickup blinks. In Pickup mode its LED strobes amber and dark (2 Hz) until the Super Knob reaches it, on the stock firmware and in native mode; on the stock firmware its ring is also dimmed. The ring keeps showing the Metaknob. Amber / dark rather than row colour / amber, because the FX rows' warm LED colours are too close to amber to read as a blink.
  • One word per thing. What a Metaknob drives are now its targets everywhere (Metaknob targets, Add Target, Remove Target), like macro knobs; Link only means a slot following the Super Knob; the knob-travel setting (full range, first half, ...) is the zone. A parameter's row menu in Edit has a single Metaknob Target check instead of a second copy of the zone list.
  • Swapping effects no longer moves their Super Knob link setting. Dragging an effect onto another slot (or reordering a chain) moves only the effects; each slot keeps its own link, as it already did for Ctrl+drop duplicate, paste and load.
  • A tap on the Super Knob's switch does nothing (it used to reset it to the centre, which moved every linked slot at once). Shift + tap is still Chain Link.
  • Rate, speed, frequency, decay and feedback parameters respond exponentially on the focus knobs 2-4 (also names built from those words, like fbDecay), so the slow end gets more of the knob. Turning focus on never changes the value.
  • A Metaknob with several targets starts where they all come closest to their defaults when a slot loads or resets, instead of matching only the first target and moving the others.

docs.title: Queue Header Declutter (ui/browser/QueueToolbar.kt)
docs.text:
• Export and Clear moved into a ⋮ menu at the right of each queue column's caption ("Export as playlist...", "Clear queue"), so the button row has room to breathe.
  • The A/B FX and BG FX queues no longer show a greyed play / pause button; they have no auto-advance, so the slot is gone.

docs.title: Pairs Follow the Twister Page (ui/PerfRows.kt, ui/ParametersState.kt, ui/PerformanceDeepEditBay.kt, ui/NavigationSurface.kt)
docs.text:
• A pair is now the two rows that share a half of a Twister page, in Browse and in Edit. On the MIXER page that makes Transitions + Master FX one pair and Master MST + Clock the other. Before, Browse paired Master MIX with Master FX and Transitions with Clock, so half of each pair had nothing to browse.
  • The Master pair is Transitions + Master FX, and both halves browse: the Master FX chain and the transition. It opens on the half you touched last (the Master FX chain at first). The Master badge and the main monitor open it, in place when the page shows those rows. The old Transitions + Clock pair is gone.
  • Master MST + Clock have nothing to browse, so they are not a pair view; they only pair in Edit (see below). On that Edit tab the Browse button is greyed with a tooltip saying so.
  • The Twister's pair walk is Deck A, B, BG, PV, Master; knob 13 (send and quick switch) is the Master pair.
  • The Master MIX row's pill is now MST, to match the Edit rail.

docs.title: Master Levels Editor and Clock Triggers (ui/ParametersTabs.kt, ui/PerformanceClockTriggers.kt, ui/PerformanceClockControls.kt, ui/ParametersState.kt)
docs.text:
• Edit's side rail is now MST OUT A B BG PV. MST has two sections, LEVELS and CTRL, and shows the Master MST row with the Clock row. OUT (the former MIX) has FX and TRANS and shows Transitions with Master FX.
  • LEVELS edits every deck's level and the master level in one grid (a deck's Gain is on its SRC tab). The master level moved here from TRANS, which now starts with Crossfade. Bindings, presets and macros are unchanged.
  • The Master MST row's gear opens MST > LEVELS, the Master FX gear opens OUT > FX and the Transitions gear OUT > TRANS. The gear stays lit on the row the editor is on.
  • The Clock row's tempo controls are a tidy 3 x 2 grid to leave room for the queue and randomize buttons at 1280 px: MAN AUDIO LINK over TAP SNAP [-|+], all the same size, with the BPM readout beside them and the four beat dots under it. /2 and x2 are gone (Preferences > Tempo & Sync still has them), RESYNC is now SNAP, and LINK is always in its cell (dim while Link is off).
  • The Clock row has queue and randomize buttons, with captions and button text in the same size and colour as the captions under the knobs. QUEUE (left): a caption line A/B | A/B FX | BG | BG FX | TRN over a line of ◀ ▶ pairs, with a play / pause button beside the caption on the A/B, BG and TRN queues (it toggles that queue's auto-advance, lit while running; the FX queues have no auto-advance). RAND (pushed to the right edge, with randomization on): A B ALL over BG PV (undo with Ctrl+Z). Every button is a Mixer parameter also listed on MST > CTRL, so right-click Learn MIDI / OSC works from either place. The A/B FX and BG FX queues gained those parameters (Mixer/fxQueuePrev, fxQueueNext, fxBgQueuePrev, fxBgQueueNext); only a MIDI CC (or a click) drives them, since the FX queues have no auto-advance. The buttons start right after the tempo controls (no room is kept for the Link button while Link is off), so a block is only left out on a window too narrow for it. Every other queue group, and the RAND block, has a faint tinted background, like the Library's queue columns, so it is clear which captions and buttons go together.

docs.title: Slots Bind the Library In Place (ui/ParametersState.kt, ui/LibraryPanel.kt, ui/BackNavigation.kt, ui/PairKnobTouch.kt)
docs.text:
• Clicking a source name, an FX chain name, an FX slot or the transition name now works right in the Perform view. Nothing moves: the Library below starts applying to that slot, and the slot's name and buttons (Save, Clear Slot) show on the Library's tab line with a ✕. The slot is outlined on its row and the list's border takes the row's colour. A click on a row applies it (Ctrl+Z undoes it); a double-click applies it and goes back to the plain Library. Esc, the ✕, or clicking the slot again stop without applying. Changing page stops too.
  • Deck monitors, the main output monitor and the Master M badge do the same for their default half: a deck's source, or the Master FX chain.
  • The pair view now only opens when the slot's rows are not on the current page, for example clicking the BG monitor from the A/B page, or sending to such a deck from the Twister.
  • Space, or maximizing the Library, pauses the binding; Esc or Space again brings it back.
  • The controller browses the list while a slot is bound, as in the pair view: knob 16 is the cursor (tap applies, Shift + tap queues), knobs 1-8 stay live on the page's first two rows, and touching one of them moves the binding to that row's slot. Shift + tap on a send knob moves the binding to that deck.

docs.title: One Header for Browse and Edit (ui/BayHeader.kt, ui/PerformanceDeepEditBay.kt, ui/PerformanceBrowseBay.kt, ui/NavigationSurface.kt)
docs.text:
• The pair view and Edit share one header line. Back, a Browse | Params switch, the target with its buttons, and what the queue plays next sit in the same place in both, so switching moves nothing. Edit now has a visible Back. On the Transitions pair, Params opens the transition editor.
  • The Master pair browses the Master FX chain when nothing has been touched yet, instead of showing an empty list.
  • Esc goes back to where you were after opening the Library from Edit or the pair view (Space, Ctrl+F, /, the menu or the controller), with the same slot bound.
  • Trying sources on a deck with unsaved changes asks once. Your Save or Discard answer is reused while that deck stays bound; Ctrl+Z still undoes each load.
  • Touching a controller knob no longer pulls the browser off the Queues or Macros tab, unless the touch moves the binding to another slot.
  • Controller in the pair view: right-middle steps the tab as in the Library, right-bottom steps the panes (Shift + right-bottom still clears the slot), and Shift + tap on knob 16 adds to the queue.
  • Saved presets, saved effects and saved transitions are highlighted as applied in a bound list, not just stock items.
