docs.title: Library List Polish (ui/browser/PresetListPanel.kt, ui/browser/LoadedMarks.kt, ui/browser/BrowseRecents.kt, ui/browser/BrowserPane.kt, ui/browser/QueueToolbar.kt)
docs.text:
• Library rows are easier to read. Stock items no longer show an empty box, long names are shortened with "..." (full name on hover), saved names like hyperspace_crash_zoom read "Hyperspace crash zoom" (the file name is unchanged), and the heavy-shader mark is a muted gauge with an explanation instead of a warning sign.
  • See at a glance which decks hold an item. Each deck that holds it gets one coloured chip (A, B, BG, PV, M), then colour bars when space runs out; a count appears only for many slots. Hover for the full list.
  • New Recent folder in Sources, FX and Transitions: the last 20 items you loaded or applied, newest first, kept across restarts (library/src_recent.json, fx_recent.json, transition_recent.json).
  • Same menus everywhere. FX and transition rows open their menu on right-click too, the words match across tabs (Rename..., Clone, Delete..., Add to '<playlist>'), every saved file and playlist has Reveal in File Manager, and a bound list's menu starts with Apply to . The tree's fold arrows, item counts and the header buttons (new playlist, new preset, save FX, save transition) have tooltips that say what they do.
  • Deleting a saved effect or transition also removes it from the queues and playlists, as deleting a preset already did.
  • Queues tab: an empty queue says how to fill it, all five columns have the same button strip (the FX queues' Auto button is greyed, since they have no timer), and the controller steps the columns left to right as drawn.
  • External video can be dragged onto a deck like a stock source.

docs.title: Library Keyboard and Dialogs (ui/browser/DockActions.kt, ui/ModalKeys.kt, ui/browser/BrowserPopupHandler.kt, ui/UIManager.kt)
docs.text:
• Enter runs the row's default action on every tab: in the Library what a double-click does, in a bound list apply. Before, only Transitions answered Enter.
  • Typing a letter while the list has the keyboard starts a search with it (keys bound to a shortcut, such as Q, keep their shortcut).
  • Delete follows Preferences > Shortcuts (Backspace works too) instead of being fixed.
  • Alt+click a Sources row to preview it on Deck PV.
  • Dialogs answer the keyboard. Rename, Delete, New Playlist and Export focus their text field, Enter confirms and Esc cancels without leaving the Library. The unsaved-deck prompt saves on Enter, and its buttons are the same width.
  • Esc that closes a menu or popup no longer also goes back a view.

docs.title: Edit View Polish (ui/ParamLabels.kt, ui/ParametersRenderer.kt, ui/ParametersTabs.kt, ui/PerformanceDeepEditBay.kt)
docs.text:
• Edit shows readable parameter names. Grid rows and Metaknob lists use the shader's own label, or split names like CellScale into "Cell scale". Presets, MIDI and OSC mappings are unchanged.
  • Properties is never empty in Edit. Opening a deck or Master, or switching tabs, selects the first knob-assigned parameter (or the first row).
  • Knob captions use the readable name too. Source and effect knobs that were labelled with a cut-off raw name ("TRACKINGJ") now carry the whole readable name ("TRACKING JITTER"), shortened with "..." only when the caption is too narrow; focus-mode effect knobs show "Tracking jitter". Looks and presets saved before keep the old stored caption until their knobs are rebuilt.
  • Fixed clipping: the side rail no longer cuts off "CTRL", the TRANS tab's transition selector fits its name, and the Min/Max fields in the macro and Metaknob binding editors no longer cut off "Max". CTRL and TRANS labels are in sentence case ("Queue prev", "Master level").

docs.title: KIFS Color Spread (library/sources/kifs/kifs.fs, rendering/SourceDocRegistry.kt)
docs.text: • New Color Spread knob (default 1, with Saturation and Brightness now also defaulting to 1). KIFS used to show about two colours, because the folds make every copy of a detail identical and the ramp only looked at the orbit trap. Color Spread shifts the hue by three things the folds do not erase: the fold level the orbit came closest at, the point's position in space, and the way the surface faces. Raise it for a wider spread of colours, 0 gives the old plain ramp, and the gold ramp ignores it. New KIFS decks start bright and fully spread; saved looks keep their own values.

docs.title: Reaction Diffusion Stays Out of the Black (library/sources/reaction_diffusion/reaction_diffusion.fs)
docs.text: • Reaction Diffusion no longer goes black when Regime, Feed Trim or Kill Trim are pushed. The chemistry dies out for good when the kill rate is too high for the feed rate, and the end of the Regime sweep sat in that dead zone. Kill is now kept inside the band where patterns exist (measured with a CPU port of the sim), which also stops the flat, flooded grid at the other edge; the Regime path was moved to stay inside it, and the trims are a little narrower. If the grid does go empty anyway (for example from a Diffusion change), it now reseeds itself.

docs.title: Lenia Recovers From Extinction (library/sources/lenia/lenia.fs)
docs.text: • Lenia no longer stays black after Growth Center is pushed too high. Above about 90 the growth peak sits above anything the field reaches, every cell decays to zero, and an empty grid can never grow again, so lowering Growth Center did nothing. The shader now checks a coarse lattice of cells each step and, when the whole grid is empty, reseeds it. Turning Growth Center back down brings the creatures back.

docs.title: KIFS Holds Still by Default (library/sources/kifs/kifs.fs, rendering/SourceDocRegistry.kt)
docs.text: • KIFS now starts static. Morph Speed and Flight Speed default to 0, so the object no longer reshapes or drifts until you raise them. Before, the defaults (0.2 and 0.15) kept it moving even with Rotate X/Y/Z at 0. Twist and Morph no longer turn the object. The per-level rotation now skips the outermost level, so the overall shape stays in place while the nested geometry inside twists, and an LFO on Twist reshapes the interior without spinning it. Rotate X/Y/Z is the only control that turns the whole object. The zero position now faces the shape. The camera looks straight at a face (a cube face for Menger and Mixed, a triangular face for Sierpinski and Octahedral) instead of down a corner. With Flight Speed raised, the dolly dives toward a corner of that face. Saved KIFS looks with non-zero Twist or Morph will look different, and every KIFS look is framed face-on now. Presets and decks that saved their own values are unchanged.

docs.title: Locked Values Are Linked to Their Knob Both Ways (macro/KnobDrive.kt, ui/ValueParamSection.kt, ui/CustomRangeSlider.kt, ui/ParametersRenderer.kt, rendering/isf/ISFFilter.kt)
docs.text:
• Editing the Value of a knob-driven parameter now moves the knob. Before, a parameter driven by a macro knob or an effect Metaknob had a read-only Value in Edit, and the knob moved the Value one way only. Now dragging, scrolling or typing in Initial Range runs the edit backwards through the link's curve and sets the knob, and the parameter follows in the same frame. A Metaknob that is itself on a macro knob passes the edit up to that macro knob. Other targets of the same knob move with it. Stepped and S-curve links land on the nearest position, and a typed value outside the link's range stops at the knob's end. The Max Points, Lobes, Recipe and Choice widgets are still locked, as is the Value cell in the parameter grid (click only).
  • Metaknob-driven parameters now look driven. They get the cyan accent bar, tint and label of a macro target, plus the [K1] badge when the Metaknob sits on a macro knob. Their tooltips name the Metaknob and its knob (Locked: Driven by its Metaknob [K1] link), and the Edit caption reads Linked to its Metaknob [K1]. Editing the value moves the knob. Randomize is off for a linked Value. (ModulatableParameter.metaDrivenBinding and metaDrivenKnob are refreshed by the filter each frame.)

docs.title: Browser Rows Show What Is Loaded Where (ui/browser/LoadedMarks.kt, ui/browser/PresetListPanel.kt, FXBrowserPanel.kt, TransitionBrowserPanel.kt)
docs.text:
• Every row in the Sources, FX and Transitions lists now carries colored badges in a fixed gutter to the left of the name, in the Library and in the Browse bay alike. Sources show the deck (A, B, BG, PV): a generator, saved preset or external stream loaded on two decks shows both, and a deck running a saved preset marks that preset's row only, not the generator underneath it. Stock effects show deck and slot (A2, BG3, M1 for Master FX), saved FX chains show the deck (B), and the current stock transition shows M. When the badges do not fit (an effect used in several slots, say) they collapse into one gray ×n chip; hover the gutter for the full list. Saved single effects (.lsdfx) and saved transitions (.lsdtrans) are not tracked per slot, so they carry no badge.
  • The old "●" prefix is gone: in the Browse bay the row applied to the bound deck, slot or transition is now tinted across the whole row.

docs.title: Monitor Drag Moves the FX Chain Too (presets/DeckOps.kt, ui/DeckControlPanel.kt)
docs.text: • Dragging one monitor onto another now carries the deck's FX chain along with the source, for Move, Copy and Swap. Before, only the source and its knobs travelled and each deck kept its own chain. Dropping a monitor on another opens one menu of nine choices, in groups of three: Move, Copy and Swap, each for Source, FX or Source + FX. (The old right-drag path never fired and the left-drag direct Move was dead code; both are gone.) A Source-only change leaves macro knob bindings aimed at the FX chain behind (the target deck's knobs lose them); an FX-only change leaves the knobs alone. Still not undoable. (DeckScope; DeckChange.CopyFrom/MoveFrom/SwapWith take a scope.)

docs.title: Edit Shows Two Rows (ui/PerfRows.kt, ui/ParametersState.kt, ui/rack/RackUnit.kt)
docs.text: • Edit now keeps the open unit's pair of rows on screen, as Browse does: a deck's SRC and FX rows, Master's Transitions and FX rows on the OUT side tab, and Master's MST and Clock rows on the MST side tab. Switching between SRC and FX (or FX and TRANS) no longer swaps the row, so nothing redraws. The lit gear marks the row the editor is on; clicking the other row's gear moves the editor to it, and clicking the lit one closes Edit. The editor bay is one row (74 px) shorter than before.

docs.title: Edit Side Rail: CTRL Is Its Own Tab (ui/ParametersTabs.kt, ui/ParametersState.kt)
docs.text: • The Edit side rail is now MST OUT A B BG PV. The queue, clock and morph triggers moved out of the output tab onto a new first MST tab (section CTRL, beside LEVELS). OUT holds FX and TRANS, and returns to whichever you last used. Master level moved to the top of MST > LEVELS, so TRANS starts with crossfade and fade speed. Every parameter is still modulatable; macro bindings follow their parameter to its new tab.

docs.title: Transitions Row Matches the FX Rows (ui/PerformanceTransitionsControls.kt, ui/PerformanceMatrixPanel.kt)
docs.text:
• The Transitions row is laid out like a deck FX row. Line 1 is the transition picker with the Edit gear at its end (the gear no longer sits under the XF badge). Line 2 is [⋮] [Save] [◀] [▶] [A] [B] [AUTO] [time] in equal cells. Save stores the current transition as a .lsdtrans preset and turns amber when it differs from its defaults; the ⋮ menu has Save As, Browse Transitions. The queue position (3/12) moved into the ◀ ▶ tooltips.
  • The MIXER page now runs Transitions, Master FX, Master MST, Clock. Transitions moves to the top row (Twister bank 3 knobs 1-4) since it is the row you perform with; Master MST drops to the third row (knobs 9-12). A saved copy of the MIXER page in library/perform_pages/ keeps its old order until you delete it.

docs.title: Edit FX Tab: Slots Are an Accordion (ui/ParametersTabs.kt, ui/ParametersState.kt)
docs.text: • Only one FX slot is expanded at a time in a chain's Edit FX tab, so a long effect no longer pushes the other slots off screen. Opening a slot collapses the others; collapsed slots show their Dry/Wet percentage on the header. The first filled slot is open by default. Chain Wet/Dry stays at the top, and the CHAIN MACRO section (Super Knob and Metaknob rows) has its own chevron to collapse it; Link all stays on its header. (ParametersState.fxExpandedSlot replaces fxSlotCollapsed; fxMacroCollapsed holds the macro section's state.)

docs.title: Step Sequencer: Glide Trace, Ghost Steps, Auto-Randomize, Snap, Keyboard, Undo Everywhere (ui/SeqSection.kt, ui/ModulatorUndo.kt, parameters/SeqPatterns.kt, rendering/MorphState.kt)
docs.text:
• The bars now draw the output line and a live dot. A white trace shows what the sequencer will really output: flat steps at 100% Step Hold, linear or S-curve slides below it, so Step Hold and Glide Curve are visible instead of guessed. A dot rides it at the current position.
  • Steps past the length show ghosted after the last playing step, so it is clear they are kept. Patterns shorter than 8 steps now keep 8-step-wide cells instead of stretching to fill the panel.
  • New Auto toggle (shown when randomization is enabled): preset and deck randomization also re-roll the pattern, and the deck's morph slides between patterns. Step Hold's randomize range now takes part in deck morphs too (it did nothing there before).
  • Snap menu (Off, 5%, 10%, 12.5%, 25%) for painting and nudging; keyboard editing (click a bar, then arrows, Delete, Enter while the pointer is over the bars); Euclid gets a Rotate slider and a hit preview; bars dim while the modulator is bypassed.
  • Ctrl+Z now covers the LFO, Audio and MIDI CC panels as well (one step per drag), not just the sequencer.
  • Internal: SeqPatterns.glide is the one glide formula for the evaluator and the editor trace (output unchanged; Evaluators.kt re-marked in sync_manifest.json, web vectors regenerated for the new randomizeSeqSteps field); CvModulator.randomizeSeqSteps; ModulatorSnapshot carries seqHold and seqSteps; ModulatorUndo replaces the sequencer-only undo wrapper.

docs.title: Toggle Buttons Share One Helper (ui/ButtonChrome.kt)
docs.text: • Selected toggle and pill buttons now use ButtonChrome.toggleButton: the Audio Continuous/Transient pair, the sequencer's Glide Curve, the beat-preset pills, and the Max Points and Lobes pills. A selected button now lightens on hover and darkens on press like other lit buttons (the old ones stayed flat), unselected ones use the theme's own button color instead of fixed greys, and the label ink is chosen to read on the fill instead of always black.

docs.title: Step Sequencer On by Default; Pattern Edits Undoable (ui/AppPreferences.kt, ui/AppPreferencesStore.kt, ui/SeqSection.kt)
docs.text:
• The step sequencer is now enabled by default, so its column and SEQ tab are there from the start. Turn it off in Preferences -> General if you don't want it. Settings saved before this change held the old default, so the first launch after updating turns it on once (sequencerDefaultedOn in the settings file); after that your choice sticks.
  • Ctrl+Z now undoes sequencer edits. A paint drag, a toolbar action (Randomize, Fill, Paste...) or a slider drag on the SEQ panel is one undo step.

docs.title: Wider Default Modulation Range (ui/ParametersRenderer.kt, ui/PropertiesPanel.kt)
docs.text:
• New LFO and Audio modulators now start at -100% to 100% (depth 1.0) instead of -50% to 50%. Existing modulators and presets are unchanged.
  • New modulators default to Clock Unit = Beat with an interval of 1 beat (was Time). This applies to the LFO and the Step Sequencer (CvModulator.genUnit). Saved presets keep their stored unit; the web evaluator test vectors were regenerated.
  • The LFO now has the same one-click Beat Presets row as the Step Sequencer (1/8 to 16 beats) above its Beat Div slider. The pill drawing is shared (ui/BeatPresetPills.kt).

docs.title: Tour Staleness Report (scripts/tour_staleness.py, scripts/render_tour.sh)
docs.text: • New scripts/tour_staleness.py lists which walkthrough videos need re-rendering, from git instead of a hand-kept list. Each render now stamps its commit in rendered_at.json; the script maps a tour's widget keys to source files and reports commits since then that touched them, the tour script or the renderer. Developer tooling only; see docs/developer/tour_renderer.md.

docs.title: Step Sequencer: Bar Editor, Pattern Tools, Phase and Offset (ui/SeqSection.kt, parameters/SeqPatterns.kt, cv/Evaluators.kt)
docs.text:
• The step grid of 32 text boxes is now a bar graph. Click and drag to paint a pattern (values snap to 5%, Shift for free), scroll over a bar to nudge it, double-click to type a value, right- or middle-click to reset. Rows hold up to 16 steps; the playing step is outlined.
  • New pattern toolbar: Randomize, Invert, Shift < / >, Copy / Paste (shared between sequencers, includes length), Fill... (Ramp Up/Down, Triangle, Alternate, Pulse, All On), Euclid... and Clear.
  • Length is a 1-32 slider instead of 8/16/32 buttons, so odd lengths work; steps past the end are kept. New Phase slider (with randomize) replaces the hidden value "Reset to Step 0" used to overwrite; the button is now "Sync to Step 1". New Offset slider beside Depth. Step Hold gets a randomize toggle and reads "100% (stepped)" / "0% (full glide)"; Glide Curve greys out when nothing glides.
  • Changing Clock Unit now converts the step duration instead of resetting it, and no longer leaves the old unit's randomize range behind.
  • Internal: playhead and evaluator share seqCyclePosition; pattern operations are pure functions in SeqPatterns (tests in SeqPatternsTest); CvModulator.randomizeSeqHold. The tour widget key seq_step_<i> is now seq_bars_<row>, and tours/modulation.json paints the pattern by dragging. The web evaluator is unchanged (the evaluator edit was a pure extraction; sync_manifest.json re-marked).

docs.title: Web Broadcast Hidden Behind Advanced; Relay Requires a Token (ui/PreferencesPanel.kt, server/server.js)
docs.text:
• The Web Broadcast preferences tab is now hidden by default. Turn on Show Advanced Preferences in General to show it; it also shows when a relay URL and token are already saved.
  • The relay server no longer has a default token. It exits at startup unless LSD_TOKEN (or lsd_relay_token in rc.conf) is set, since the old default was in the public repo. If you ever ran a relay without setting one, change its token.

docs.title: Tour Renderer: Live Pipeline Diagram (tour/PipelineDiagram.kt, tour/TourRunner.kt, rendering/FxSlotTaps.kt)
docs.text:
• The walkthrough now opens with a live schematic of the video pipeline before it shows any UI: decks, their FX chains, the transition, BG behind, master FX and the audience, with PV apart. Every box shows the real video at that point, each FX slot included, and the camera then zooms in on a generator, an effect and a transition to show their parameters (with live value bars) and the ways to control them. The diagram shrinks into a corner mini-map that comes back at the start of every chapter of every walkthrough video, lighting the part being discussed. Developer tooling only; nothing changes in the app.
  • Internal: new script actions pipe, pipe_add, pipe_focus, pipe_params, pipe_controls, pipe_tag, pipe_minimap, trans_param and deck_level; durationSec eases set_param, fx_param, trans_param, crossfade and meta_knob; move aims at pipe:<node>; a chapter's minimap lights nodes at its start; fx_param warns when the slot's Metaknob owns the parameter. The synthetic cursor is larger, and the renderer warns when a chapter's last caption is not up for at least 5 s before the chapter ends. FxSlotTaps copies each rendered FX slot into a 384x216 texture, only while the diagram is up. The intro is the first chapter of tours/overview.json; plan in .planning/pipeline-intro-plan.md.

docs.title: Transition Parameter Names (default_transitions/*.fs, ui/ParametersTabs.kt)
docs.text: • The eight stock transitions' parameters now have readable names in the Edit view's transition rows ("Burn Spread" instead of "burnSpread", "RGB Split" instead of "rgbSplit"), as effect parameters already did: the rows now show an ISF input's LABEL when it has one. Behaviour, parameter paths and existing mappings are unchanged.

docs.title: User Guide: Live Video Input and Three FX Slots (docs/user_guide/visual_sources.md, docs/user_guide/your_workspace.md)
docs.text: • New "Live Video Input" section on showing Spout, Syphon or PipeWire streams on a deck. The guide no longer describes four FX slots and a separate feedback loop: each deck has three slots, Feedback is an effect that can go in any of them, and the signal flow now includes Master FX and how BG shows through.

docs.title: Level Faders: Slider, Knob, MIDI and Modulation No Longer Fight (rendering/Mixer.kt, macro/MacroEngine.kt, parameters/SoftTakeover.kt, ui/DeckControlPanel.kt)
docs.text:
• The deck-tile level faders (A, B, BG, PV) now behave like the crossfader. Dragging a fader no longer snaps back when a Performance knob is bound to it: the knob follows the fader instead, and whichever moved last wins. A manual drag, wheel step or reset also mutes non-MIDI modulation on that fader and makes any MIDI/OSC mapping on it in Soft Takeover mode pick it up again instead of jumping.
  • The fader handle now marks the fader's own value (what a drag sets); the filled bar still shows the live level after modulation, so the two can differ while a modulator is active. The wheel steps from the fader's own value, not the modulated one.
  • Internal: Mixer.setLevelByUser; MacroEngine.mirrorLevelFader (linear, full-range bindings on Mixer/level*); the soft-takeover pickup rule is now one shared SoftTakeover.caught, used by MIDI, OSC and the FX Super Knob link. Tests in LevelFaderMirrorTest.

docs.title: Tour Renderer: FX, Transition, View and Overlay Actions (tour/, scripts/render_tour.sh)
docs.text:
• The deterministic --tour renderer can now script FX chains, Super Knob/Metaknob, transitions, the crossfader, Library/Preferences/theme changes and knob drags, draws a highlight ring on each target, can burn captions into the video, and writes chapter and caption JSON beside the video. scripts/render_tour.sh turns one script into the hero mp4/webm, poster, .vtt, chapter-tagged video and per-chapter silent loops. Developer tooling only; nothing changes in the app.
  • Internal: new widget keys across the deck rows, FX cells, browser tabs and list rows, deck preview faders, the FX chain BYPASS switch and Preferences (WidgetRegistry.note); script format in docs/developer/tour_renderer.md; checked bit-identical with scripts/tour_determinism_check.sh scripts/tour_phase3_test.json. Each walkthrough video is its own script under tours/ (render_tour.sh --all renders every one); the overview (about 5 minutes, six chapters) is tours/overview.json, and it loads sources by clicking them in the browser, raises BG with its preview fader and turns an FX chain on with its BYPASS switch, rather than doing these by script (new fx_chain_enable action for setup); the Modulation deep dive (tours/modulation.json) sets up an LFO, an audio modulator and a step pattern entirely through the Edit grid, using new type/key/scroll actions, ox/oy offsets for combo items and widget keys across the grid and modulator panels (every ButtonChrome.button is keyed by its label); first drafts of the other five deep dives are in tours/ too (fx_chains, mixing, library, hardware, output), driven by new rclick, fx_new and output_view actions, key with letters, Space, Backspace and Ctrl/Shift (app shortcuts such as Q fire), drag onto a target or point (drag-and-drop loads), and keys for the focus-mode Wet slider, page arrows and effect name, the chain Save and menu buttons, the Transitions row's A/B, AUTO, fade time, picker and die, plus btnid_<id> for every ButtonChrome.button with an id (stable when its text changes); tour renders no longer read or write the broadcast and OSC preferences (the relay URL and token stayed visible in the Web Broadcast panel) and skip the no-MIDI-device warning; a script with a soundtrack now shows the AUD column; captions sit in an opaque box beside the control being shown, steps can be timed relative to each other, captions can point to other chapters, and the renderer warns about captions too short to read and targets that are not on screen. A draft mode (--tour-draft, or render_tour.sh --draft: 30 fps, half size, NVENC) renders the whole tour in about 2 minutes instead of over 6, plus the hours a VP9 encode took; WebM is now opt-in (--webm) (soundtrack placeholder generated by scripts/make_tour_beat.sh); tour mode now discards dirty-deck prompts so scripted loads are never blocked.

docs.title: No-MIDI Warning Readable Again (ui/PopupManager.kt)
docs.text: • The "No MIDI Devices Connected" popup, shown when you right-click a knob to learn MIDI with no controller plugged in, was squeezed into a column one word wide. It now opens at a fixed readable width.

docs.title: Audio FFT Texture Now Live (audio/SpectrumAnalyzer.kt, audio/AudioEngine.kt)
docs.text:
• The audioFFT / iChannel0 spectrum row was always zero and now carries the live spectrum. Row 0 had been fed from the beat tracker's FFT, which the live audio path never ran, so every shader reading it saw silence (the waveform row 1 was unaffected). No bundled source uses the row, so it went unnoticed; third-party Shadertoy-style ISF that read it now react to audio.
  • Contract: 512 linear-frequency bins from 0 Hz to half the sample rate (bin spacing sampleRate/1024), Hann-windowed 1024-sample mono mix after input gain and channel routing. A full-scale sine reads 1.0; magnitude is mapped from -80 dB..0 dB onto 0..1. Attack is instant and release is a 0.08 s decay.
  • Cost: about 19 microseconds per 512-frame block on the dev machine (one 1024-point FFT plus 512 logs), no allocation. Beat detection is untouched: it never sees this FFT.
  • Internal: new SpectrumAnalyzer (double-buffered, written on the audio thread, read by AudioTexture); AudioEngine.copyAudioTextureData reads it and resetForOfflineFeed resets it, so tour renders stay bit-identical. The unused BeatTrackerEngine.copyMagSpectrum and its magSpectrum buffer were removed (beat results unchanged). Tests in SpectrumAnalyzerTest.

docs.title: Update Icon Instead of Popup (ui/MenuBar.kt, ui/UIManager.kt)
docs.text:
• A new version no longer opens a popup at startup. When the startup check finds one, a download icon appears in the menu bar; hover it for the current and latest version, click it for the same Download / Remind Later / Skip Version dialog as before. Skip Version hides the icon for that release.
  • Internal: UIManager no longer calls UpdatePromptModal.request; MenuBar reads UpdateChecker.lastResult.

docs.title: Output Monitor Choice (ui/OutputMonitors.kt, ui/MenuBar.kt, Main.kt)
docs.text:
• New Output → Output Monitor menu picks which screen the secondary output window fills. Automatic keeps the old behaviour (the first monitor that is not primary); naming a monitor fixes setups where that guess is wrong, notably Wayland, where the output could jump to the laptop screen instead of the projector. The choice is saved by monitor name and the output reopens at once if it is already running.
  • Internal: outputMonitorName in AppPreferences and AppPreferencesStore; OutputMonitors lists and resolves GLFW monitors.

docs.title: Eleven More Light Generators (library/sources/{cyclic_ca,metaballs,wave_ripples,harmonograph,aurora_ribbons,isometric_voxels,halftone_matrix,kali_set,girih_stars,glitch_blocks,voronoi_cells}/)
docs.text:
• Eleven more generators for integrated graphics, on desktop and web. Cyclic CA (self-organising spirals), Metaballs, Wave Ripples (interference of orbiting wave sources), Harmonograph (a glowing oscilloscope curve), Aurora Ribbons, Isometric Voxels (a Qbert-style cube field), Halftone Matrix (dots, LED pixels and CMYK screens), Kali Set (an inversion-fold fractal), Girih Stars (Islamic strapwork), Glitch Blocks and Voronoi Cells*. None carries the GPU-intensive triangle.
  • Costs on an Intel UHD at 1080p range from about 4 to 20 ms. Aurora Ribbons and Halftone Matrix are the heaviest; lower their Quality first. Harmonograph now draws a longer, spiralling trail of several windings with finer segments (Quality 48 to 128), so the figure reads as a rosette instead of a single swoosh. It evaluates its curve once into a small lookup strip and skips segments far from each pixel, and Metaballs has smooth glossy shading with a cheaper default Quality. Cyclic CA needs a few seconds to form its spirals, and Glitch Blocks reshuffles its sequence when you change Glitch Rate.
  • Four macro knobs each and a tooltip on every parameter.
  • Internal: stock ids in VisualSourceRegistry.DEFAULT_SOURCE_IDS, curated knobs and GeneratorDefaultsTest; Neighborhood, RatioPreset and Ribbons added to the BundledIsfRangesTest selector allowlist; web manifest entries and web/shaders/*.frag; user guide, rendering.md, licence and clean-room ledger rows. Only some per-source notes exist in .planning/light-sources-notes/.

docs.title: Five Light Generators for Integrated Graphics (library/sources/{quasicrystal,thin_film,tunnel_scenes,video_feedback,hyperbolic_tiling}/, rendering/VisualSourceRegistry.kt, rendering/SourceDocRegistry.kt, presets/GeneratorDefaults.kt)
docs.text:
• Five new generators that run comfortably on integrated graphics, on desktop and web. Quasicrystal (5 to 8 interfering gratings in four styles and four palettes), Thin Film (oil-slick iridescence), Tunnel Scenes (a synthwave grid, a Truchet tunnel or an N-sided wormhole, with no ray marching), Video Feedback (a classic feedback loop of zoom, rotation, drift and seed shapes) and Hyperbolic Tiling (a Poincare-disk {P,Q} tiling with edge glow). They carry no GPU-intensive triangle; the absence of the badge is the signal.
  • Measured about 2 to 6 ms per frame at 1080p on an Intel UHD (Tiger Lake GT1), one deck, at the defaults. Each has a Quality input for the rest. Video Feedback keeps a small persistent frame, so its cost is the same at any output size, and it is square, so a widescreen output shows about half of its height.
  • Four macro knobs each: Quasicrystal (Freq, Sharp, Spin, Drift), Thin Film (Flow, Scale, Film, Turb), Tunnel Scenes (Speed, Twist, Glow, Sway), Video Feedback (Zoom, Rot, Hue, Decay), Hyperbolic Tiling (Speed, Drift, Edge, Glow). Every parameter has a tooltip.
  • Internal: stock ids added to VisualSourceRegistry.DEFAULT_SOURCE_IDS; curated knobs in GeneratorDefaults.CURATED_KNOBS and GeneratorDefaultsTest; SeedShape, P, Q and Outside added to the BundledIsfRangesTest selector allowlist; web manifest entries and web/shaders/*.frag; user guide, rendering.md, licence and clean-room ledger rows.

docs.title: Nebula Volume and Three Simulation Generators Join the Stock Generators (rendering/VisualSourceRegistry.kt, rendering/SourceDocRegistry.kt, presets/GeneratorDefaults.kt, library/sources/{nebula_volume,reaction_diffusion,fluid_ink,lenia}/)
docs.text:
• Four new generators, desktop only. Nebula Volume (a ray-marched gas nebula with self-shadowing, a drifting inner light, a starfield and camera flight), Reaction Diffusion (Gray-Scott maze, worm, coral and spot patterns that grow and split), Fluid Ink (orbiting emitters stirring ink through an incompressible flow) and Lenia (a continuous cellular automaton of soft blobs, rings and stripes). They ship with the app, are restored if deleted, and are not part of the web player.
  • The three simulations run on fixed-size persistent grids (512, 384 and 256 square), so they cost the same at any output size and measured under 2 ms at 1080p on an RTX A2000 Laptop GPU. They re-seed themselves when the grid is empty, for example after a resize, and each has a Reseed latch (Reaction Diffusion, Lenia). They advance a fixed number of steps per frame, so they run faster at higher frame rates. They carry no warning triangle.
  • Nebula Volume carries the GPU-intensive triangle. The defaults take about 17 ms at 1080p on one deck; Quality, Lighting and Detail are the cost knobs, and the maximum of all three is very heavy (about 68 ms measured).
  • Lenia is a texture generator, not a creature simulator. It does not reliably produce the gliding creatures of the published Lenia; treat it as living bubbles, rings and stripes.
  • Four macro knobs each: Nebula Volume (Density, Cover, Turb, Speed), Reaction Diffusion (Regime, Diffuse, Speed, Relief), Fluid Ink (Force, Swirl, Turb, Fade), Lenia (Center, Width, Radius, Speed). Every parameter has a tooltip.
  • Internal: stock ids added to VisualSourceRegistry.DEFAULT_SOURCE_IDS; curated knobs in GeneratorDefaults.CURATED_KNOBS and GeneratorDefaultsTest; nebula_volume added to the StockGpuCostAuditTest heavy allowlist (LSD_COST 3) and to Source3DModeTest; the sims are LSD_COST 2. These are the first stock generators using PASSES (persistent FLOAT targets, one target per sub-step). No web/sync_manifest.json entry. Written from the published equations (rows in docs/developer/clean_room_provenance.md and docs/licenses/SHADERS_LICENSE.md); details in docs/developer/rendering.md; per-source notes in .planning/heavy-sources-notes/.

docs.title: Escape Time Generator (library/sources/escape_time/)
docs.text:
• New 2D generator, desktop only. Escape Time draws high-iteration Julia, Burning Ship Julia, relaxed Newton (three cubic roots) and Mandelbrot fractals with smooth colouring, orbit-trap glow, a fractional power and a Julia constant that orbits on its own (Morph Speed).
  • Detail scales the iteration cap and, above 0.75, turns on 2x2 antialiasing. It has its own Zoom (up to 3000x; fp32 goes blocky beyond that), Center X/Y and Rotation, and four colour modes. It carries the GPU-intensive triangle in the browser, though at the defaults it measured under 1.5 ms at 1080p on an RTX A2000 Laptop GPU.
  • Internal: stock id escape_time added to VisualSourceRegistry.DEFAULT_SOURCE_IDS, curated knobs, tooltips (SourceDocRegistry), FractalType added to the BundledIsfRangesTest selector allowlist, heavy-tag audit, user guide, rendering.md, licence and clean-room rows.

docs.title: Five Heavy Raymarched Fractals Join the Stock Generators (rendering/VisualSourceRegistry.kt, rendering/SourceDocRegistry.kt, presets/GeneratorDefaults.kt, library/sources/{mandelbox,kifs,mandelbulb,pseudo_kleinian,apollonian}/)
docs.text:
• Five new generators, desktop only. Mandelbox (box fold, sphere fold and a scale that can go negative, with a camera gliding in and out), KIFS (kaleidoscopic folds: Menger, Sierpinski, octahedral and mixed, with twist, morph and an endless self-similar zoom), Mandelbulb (animatable power, a Julia blend and a slow power swing), Pseudo Kleinian (a periodic mirror fold plus sphere inversion, flown through) and Apollonian (a sphere gasket, flown through). They ship with the app, are restored if deleted, and are not part of the web player.
  • Each has a Quality knob that scales ray-march steps, fold iterations and ambient-occlusion taps together, plus a Color Mode selector and a signed Flight Speed (negative reverses). The defaults are tuned for headroom: measured on an RTX A2000 Laptop GPU at 1080p, the defaults take roughly 5 to 11 ms per frame on one deck (Mandelbox 7.7, KIFS 4.8, Mandelbulb 5.2, Pseudo Kleinian about 11, Apollonian about 8.7). Raising Quality, or zooming in close, costs more. Two heavy decks plus a crossfade is the case to watch.
  • They carry the GPU-intensive warning triangle in the browser, like Icosa H3, Gyroid Hyperspace and Hyper-Slice. Expect them to run slowly on integrated graphics; lower Quality first.
  • Four macro knobs each, ready to play: Mandelbox (Scale, Fold, Radius, Speed), KIFS (Type, Scale, Twist, Morph), Mandelbulb (Power, Swing, Julia, Speed), Pseudo Kleinian (Slab, Invert, Core, Speed), Apollonian (Cell, Invert, Twist, Speed). Every parameter has a tooltip.
  • Internal: stock ids added to VisualSourceRegistry.DEFAULT_SOURCE_IDS; curated knobs in GeneratorDefaults.CURATED_KNOBS and GeneratorDefaultsTest; heavy allowlist in StockGpuCostAuditTest; Source3DModeTest expects them 3D. Each shader is LSD_COST 3, GLSL 3.30 only, with no web/sync_manifest.json entry (nothing in WebSyncTest or checkWebSync covers them). Written from the defining mathematics (rows in docs/developer/clean_room_provenance.md and docs/licenses/SHADERS_LICENSE.md); loop caps and timings in docs/developer/rendering.md; per-source notes in .planning/heavy-sources-notes/.

docs.title: Heavy Shaders Get a GPU-Cost Warning in the Browser (rendering/isf/ISFModels.kt, ui/browser/PresetListPanel.kt, ui/browser/FXBrowserPanel.kt)
docs.text:
• A warning triangle marks GPU-intensive stock shaders. Generators and effects whose author declared them heavy show a butter-coloured triangle at the right edge of their browser row, and the tooltip says "GPU-intensive: may run slowly on integrated graphics." Nothing is hidden or blocked; the badge only tells you what to expect. The raymarchers Icosa H3, Hyper Slice and Gyroid Hyperspace are tagged heavy.
  • New optional ISF header key LSD_COST (1 light, 2 medium, 3 heavy). Other ISF hosts ignore it, so shaders stay portable. Only 3 shows a badge; values outside 0-3 are clamped. Your own shaders in the stock folders can use it too.
  • Internal: ISFHeader.LSD_COST / gpuCost, AssetItem.gpuCost, PresetListPanel.drawCostBadge. Tagged in library/sources/ and its default_sources copy. Transition rows and saved presets do not badge yet. Test: StockGpuCostAuditTest.

docs.title: FX Metaknob Links and Focus Knobs Get a Real Editor (ui/FxMetaBindingEditor.kt, ui/FxMetaEdit.kt, ui/BindingEditorParts.kt, rendering/isf/FxMetaBinding.kt, rendering/isf/ISFFilter.kt)
docs.text:
• Edit what an effect's Metaknob drives, the same way you edit a source row's macro targets. In the Edit view, select a slot's Metaknob: the row strip shows one chip per linked parameter, Add Target (a menu of the parameters not linked yet, plus Dry/Wet) and the selected link's editor line: enable, link mode, response curve, step count, range bar, Min/Max and delete. The Edit bay shows the same editor for every link in a collapsible Metaknob links block under each slot header. Before, the only control was a right-click menu with link mode and invert.
  • All five response curves. Metaknob links now offer Linear, Exponential, Logarithmic, S-Curve and Step (with a step count), the same as macro targets, and use the same math. Existing links behave exactly as before.
  • Choose which parameters sit on the focus knobs. A collapsible Knobs block under each slot header lists the parameters in focus-mode knob order (knobs 2-4, three per page). Move them up or down, take them off the knobs, bring them back, or reset to the effect's own order. The order is saved with the slot and chain, and with Save as Default. A parameter the Metaknob drives shows a lock: its knob does nothing while the link is enabled. Without a custom order nothing changes (the effect's own order, minus what the Metaknob drives).
  • Fixed: focus knobs could go stale after changing a link. The Metaknob Link menu, the link buttons, Replace all links with... (formerly Retarget Metaknob) and Reset to Factory Default changed the links without updating knobs 2-4 or the page count, and their undo did not restore the links. They now update the knobs at once and Ctrl+Z puts the links (and the knob order) back. Dragging a range handle is one undo step.
  • Internal: FxMetaEdit is the single entry point for editing a slot's links and knob order (mutate, push a restore, re-sync FxMacroSync only when focusParameters changed). FxMetaBinding gained stepCount and delegates its transfer math to MacroCurve; FXSlotDto.knobLayout and FxDefaultDto.knobLayout are optional, so older presets load unchanged.

docs.title: Fractal Flame Generator With an Evolving Garden (experimental) (rendering/FlameSource.kt, FlameEngine.kt, FlameGenome.kt, FlameSampler.kt, presets/Garden.kt)
docs.text:
• New generator, Fractal Flame. Millions of points iterate through up to six transforms with 98 variations (the paper's 49, 46 more, hemisphere and plusrecip, from exp, log and the trigonometric and hyperbolic family to wedge, curve, bipolar and flux) and are drawn as feathered, glowing filaments. Everything is a parameter, so modulators, macros and MIDI/OSC learn work on every xform, affine and variation. The Edit row's SRC sub-tab has tabs for Look, Mods, each xform and the final xform; the default macro knobs are Zoom, Spin, Warp and Breathe, and Spin, Breathe, Warp and Drift move every xform at once. Math follows Draves & Reckase, "The Fractal Flame Algorithm" (clean-room, credited in the licenses page). Experimental: not in the stock generator set yet.
  • Evolving looks. The deck's die makes a brand-new random flame and frames the camera on it; blank, exploded, collapsed or fog-like candidates are rejected and re-rolled automatically. A new R / M / P / B button beside the die picks how the next morph target is chosen: Random, Mutate (default, strength = the Mutation parameter), Pool (a kept offspring) or Breed (a cross of two kept offspring, then mutated). It applies to the die and to the deck's Rand morph and is saved with the preset when not the default. Variation ids cross-fade during a morph instead of sweeping through every shape in between.
  • Keep, Skip and the Garden. The star at the end of the flame editor's tab strip keeps what is playing as an offspring preset in library/presets/garden/ (tagged garden, gen:N, parent:<name>, with a preview image shown in the browser tooltip). Skip discards the target the morph is heading to and picks another. Drifting flames now carry their own framing: Zoom and centre morph along with the genome, and the ZOOM knob drives a new Magnify multiplier instead. Keep saves the nearer morph end rather than a mid-morph blend, and Pool/Breed favour newer offspring and starred presets. The default macro knobs are now ZOOM, SPIN, WARP and EVOLVE (Mutation); Breathe moved off its knob. Breaking: every flame control is now stored and shown normalised (0-100, -100-100, angles -180-180; zoom-like controls have 50 = unchanged), so flame presets saved before this change, including Garden offspring and imported flames, load with different values and should be re-imported or re-made.
  • Holds its frame rate. A new preference, Flame GPU Budget (ms) (General, default 3 ms per flame deck, 0 = off), lowers the point count when a deck runs over budget and restores it when there is room, keeping brightness unchanged. Fewer points no longer dim the picture. Flame Quality (Low / Medium / High, General) replaces the per-flame Points, Passes and Kernel parameters: it is a per-machine setting, not stored in presets, and brightness is kept across tiers (saved values for the old parameters are ignored).
  • Flames are transparent where they are black. The tone-map pass now writes premultiplied alpha that follows the brightest channel, so the BG deck (and anything under a flame deck) shows through the dark areas instead of being covered by an opaque black frame.
  • The Garden starts stocked. About 150 curated Fractal Flame presets (with thumbnails) are installed into library/presets/garden/curated on first run, so Pool and Breed have material from the first launch. Restore Factory Presets re-adds any you delete; your own files are never overwritten.
  • Import .flame files. The Sources browser's ... menu has Import Flame...: pick a flame genome you own (a file with one or several flames) and each becomes a Fractal Flame preset in library/presets/imported-flames/. Xform weights, colours, affines (pre and post), final xform, up to four variations per xform (including pre_blur, which acts on the point before the others) with their parameters, and the camera (zoom, centre, rotation) carry over. What cannot is listed in the preset's notes and the log: variations the generator does not have (it now reads inversion as spherical and linear3D/spherical3D as their flat twins, with a note), extra variations or xforms beyond three and six, values outside the parameter ranges (clamped), the tone settings, 3D camera. The flame's 256-colour palette is kept and saved inside the preset (optional DeckPresetDto.palette), so presets stay portable and the Palette parameter shifts it. Flames from other programs have the image's y axis pointing down, so imports set the new FlipY camera parameter (also in the Look tab's camera section; it is the camera mirrored, not a mirrored genome). The reading of the affine coefficients and of the camera rotation was checked against reference renders of two flames. To make room for flames found in the wild, parameter ranges grew: translations to +-10, scales and shears to +-4, variation weights -4..4 (negative allowed), camera zoom 0.01-32, camera centre +-16, Julia-N/Julia-Scope power -20..20, and larger Blob waves, N-gon sides and Pie slices. A new Softness look parameter (point size, 1-10, default 3) smooths sparse flames, and imports set it from the original's smoothing filter. A new Smooth look parameter (0-1, default 0) is a density-estimation blur: sparse regions blur towards a coarser version of the image while dense ones stay sharp; imports start at 0.5. Imports start with Decay 0.85 and Toe 0 to fill in with far fewer points than the originals used. Mutate keeps its old jitter size and never shrinks an imported flame's larger scales.
  • Not yet: palette import, the web player version, a thumbnail grid in the browser.
  • Internal: see docs/developer/flame_source.md. New: FlameProbe/FlameQuality (quality gate on a hidden state texture), FlameSampler.mutate/random/breed (pure), FlameGovernor, SamplerStrategy on DeckMorphController with GenomeMorph.sampleMorphTarget(..., strategy, fresh) and vetoTarget(), DeckMorphSnapshot.origin (lineage), Garden/GardenThumbnails, FlameImporter (pure parser/mapper) and FlameImportOps, optional DeckPresetDto.samplerStrategy, AppPreferences.flameBudgetMs. Tests: FlameQualityTest, FlameSamplerTest, FlameGovernorTest, GardenTest, FlameProbeTest (GL, run under xvfb).

docs.title: Web TV Gets a web-* Preset Pack That Reacts to the Beat and the Bass (web/presets/, web/fxchains/, scripts/gen_web_presets.py)
docs.text:
• Ten new audio-reactive presets and five new FX chains for the web TV. Presets pulse on the beat or on multiples of it (every beat, every half beat, every 2, 4 or 16 beats), swell on kick drums, follow the mids and hats, and, in some, a feature appears only when the bass is loud (Mandala's fourth arm, a spiral's twist, an icosahedron's spikes). All eight web sources are used. The five new chains (web-kaleido, web-bloom, web-glitch, web-punch, web-drop-strobe) react too (bloom swells with bass, glitch on hats and bass hits, radial blur on kicks, strobe on bass drops).
  • Every preset runs through a rotating FX chain, so the same preset looks different from one visit to the next. The foreground playlist now lists 48 presets, the background playlist 9, and settings.json rotates 11 web-* chains. The seven older web presets were renamed with a web- prefix.
  • Batch 2 adds a second, deliberately different look for each source: a solid spiky crystal, a glassy prism, thick-walled gyroid caves, round-plate cymatics rings, a dense twelve-fold celestial flower, slow lava, a fine spiral galaxy, a sparse spark spiral, and two more mandalas. Two new FX chains, web-tunnel and web-vortex, join the rotation. web/checks/render_check.mjs now also fails near-black or washed-out presets and writes a contact sheet of every preset frame (needs ImageMagick).
  • Batch 3 sorts presets by energy: four ambient presets (slow cymatics, nebula, tides and crystal; only slow LFOs and loudness, so they sit in the background playlist), three groove presets (beat, mids and bass) and three hard presets (kicks, hats, two-beat jumps and bass-gated features). The reactivity test now fails an ambient preset that uses kick/hat flux or an LFO faster than 8 beats.
  • Batch 4 gives presets a single musical role: two driven only by hi-hats, three only by the mids, three that build up over an eight-bar phrase and land a bass-gated drop (with a matching web-build-drop FX chain), and two driven only by kick drums. The reactivity test checks the new build and hat tags.
  • Batch 5 completes the pack at 57 web-* presets (6 each of celestial, cymatics, fluid and gyroid, 7 icosa, 8 hyper-slice, 9 spiral, 9 mandala): four gyroid, three icosa and three hyper-slice presets, plus ten presets pinned to a signature FX chain (preset | chain in the playlist), such as the build-up presets with web-build-drop. The render check honours those pins, and its timeout was raised for the larger pack.
  • Presets are ordinary desktop .lsd files. Copy one to library/presets/ on the desktop and it plays there too (if it only uses sources the web has).
  • Internal: scripts/gen_web_presets.py writes the files from short definitions (beat LFO, kick/bass/mid/high followers and gates), and documents how modulators behave. web/tools/reactivity.test.mjs runs every preset and chain through the evaluator while sweeping a synthetic beat position and bass, kick, mid and hat levels, and fails if a preset's tags (beat, bar, bass, kick, mid, high, amp, bass-gated) are not backed by a parameter that moves, or if a bass gate would dip below its base at silence. render_check.mjs renders every preset through a different chain.

docs.title: Web Autopilot Runs Desktop-Format Presets, FX Chains and Transitions (web/preset.js, web/mandala.js, scripts/sync_web.py)
docs.text:
• A preset is now the same file on the desktop and the web. The web TV's autopilot loads real .lsd presets (with modulators, ranges and randomised bases), .lsdfxchain FX chains and .lsdtrans transitions. A preset written for one runs on the other, and modulated parameters (beat LFOs, audio, sequencers) behave the same. The desktop's 16 FX chains and 8 transition presets now ship with the web TV, and a playlist line can pin an FX chain to a preset (my-preset | my-chain); settings.json lists the transitions the autopilot rotates through.
  • Mandala presets work on the web. Lobes and Recipe Select pick from the same 296-recipe table as the desktop, so a Mandala preset looks the same in both places. Before, the web only understood raw arm and frequency numbers.
  • Internal: sync_web.py --apply copies defaults/fx_chains and defaults/transitions into web/content/, generates web/mandala_recipes.json from MandalaLibrary.kt, and lists everything in web/catalog.json (fxChains, transitionPresets; web-authored chains live in web/fxchains/, named web-*). Mandala.pickRecipe/hueSweepCycles are now plain functions shared with the render loop; WebMandalaVectorsTest writes web/tools/mandala_vectors.json and fails when it or the recipe table is stale (regenerate with UPDATE_WEB_VECTORS=1 ./gradlew test --tests '*WebMandalaVectorsTest*'). node --test web/tools/mandala.test.mjs web/tools/content.test.mjs replays the vectors and validates every web preset, FX chain and transition against the shader headers (web/tools/validate_content.mjs, also for preset authoring). The check found nine parameter names in the desktop's own shipped FX chains that their shaders no longer have (for example exposure on color_levels); both desktop and web ignore them.
  • Old web-only preset files were converted to the desktop format and their feedback moved into web-trails* FX chains.

docs.title: Web Beat Clock and Audio Signals Match the Desktop (web/beatclock.js, web/dsp.js, web/autopilot.js, web/renderer.js)
docs.text:
• During a live broadcast the web's beat phase now follows the desktop smoothly. The browser coasts on its own beat clock and blends in each clock message from the desktop instead of jumping to it, so network jitter no longer shows as stutter in beat-synced motion, and the phase never steps backward by a small amount (the same guard the desktop uses). A real jump (a tap-tempo correction, a seek) still snaps.
  • Standalone, tempo changes no longer jump the phase. The web's own tempo estimate is integrated into a running beat count; before, the beat position was bpm x time, so every tempo update rescaled the whole history.
  • Real per-band flux. audio_flux_amp/bass/mid/high are now computed like the desktop (half-wave rectified growth of each band's level, the amp flux a weighted sum of the bands) instead of all standing in for one bass-only trigger. audio_amp/bass/mid/high use the desktop's fixed scaling (level / 0.25) in place of the old peak-following normalisation, and the bands use the desktop's crossovers (bass up to 150 Hz, mid around 1 kHz, high from 5 kHz), so a preset's audio depths mean the same on both. The web's levels will look lower on quiet streams than before, as the desktop's do.
  • Internal: BeatFlywheel (web/beatclock.js) ports CVRegistry.getSynchronizedTotalBeats and adds anchor blending; dsp.js exports a pure bandSignals(); cvState.trigger_onset, beatPhase and beatSine are gone (beatSine is derived from the beat count in the renderer). Tests: node --test web/tools/*.test.mjs.

docs.title: Web Broadcast Carries FX Chains, Transitions and the Beat Clock (broadcast/WebPresetSerializer.kt, server/state.js, web/autopilot.js)
docs.text:
• A live broadcast now shows what the desktop shows on the web TV. The stream carries each deck's source parameters under their exact names, view zoom and roll, global alpha, the three FX slots (filter, wet amount, parameters) and chain wet, the master FX chain, the transition and its parameters, the A/B/BG levels, and Mandala's recipe. Before, the web saw only a few renamed source parameters and the crossfader.
  • The web follows the desktop's beat. Every message carries the beat count and tempo, so beat-synced modulation on the web is locked to the desktop instead of free-running.
  • Viewers who join mid-broadcast now get the current state, not the state at the last full snapshot. The relay keeps a merged copy and hands it to late joiners with the beat clock advanced.
  • Not compatible with old web clients. The wire format is now version 2; a browser still on the old page ignores the stream until it reloads, and the relay must be redeployed with the web client.
  • Internal: PROTOCOL_VERSION = 2 in WebPresetSerializer; FX slots are objects keyed "0".."2" so deltas can address a single parameter; an empty delta every second is a clock heartbeat. Mandala.uniformSnapshot() gives the shader-ready Mandala uniforms. Tests: WebPresetSerializerTest, and cd server && npm test for the relay state (state.js is split out of server.js so it needs no sockets). node web/checks/render_check.mjs replays wire messages through the real client handler.

docs.title: Web Client Repaired and Rebuilt on ISF (web/isf.js, web/graph.js, web/renderer.js, scripts/sync_web.py)
docs.text:
• The web TV works again and now renders what the desktop renders. It had been left behind by the move to ISF shaders and could not start. Every ISF source (including dynamic_spiral, icosa_h3, hyper_slice, gyroid_hyperspace, chladni_cymatics, celestial_engine, domain_warp_fluid), all 27 FX filters and all 8 transitions from the desktop library now compile and run in the browser, including multi-pass and persistent-buffer filters (bloom, fluid smear, feedback). Each deck has the desktop's three-slot FX chain with per-slot and chain dry/wet, the A/B crossfade uses the desktop transition shaders, and the master bus has its own FX chain. Mandala keeps its own renderer.
  • Built-in feedback is now the feedback FX filter, as on the desktop, so web presets carry feedback as an FX slot instead of a separate feedback block. The bundled web presets were converted and use the new parameter names and 0..1 ranges.
  • Internal: scripts/sync_web.py now also syncs default_filters and default_transitions into web/shaders/fx and web/shaders/transitions, drops uniform initialisers (illegal in GLSL ES 3.00), and generates web/catalog.json, which the client fetches to find sources, filters and transitions (assets compile on first use). web/isf.js ports the desktop ISF wrapper and multi-pass runner; web/graph.js is the deck/FX/transition/master pipeline. 3d_elevation.fs compared an int input to a float, which ES rejects; it now compares to 1.
  • Internal: node web/checks/shader_check.mjs compiles every catalog shader in headless Firefox, and node web/checks/render_check.mjs renders every source, filter, transition and bundled preset, failing on blank frames, console errors or GL errors (PNGs go to /tmp/lsd-render-check). Both need only firefox and node. Live-broadcast state from the desktop does not yet carry FX or transitions (next phase).

docs.title: Web Evaluator Matches the Desktop (web/evaluator.js, web/tools/evaluator.test.mjs, WebEvaluatorVectorsTest.kt)
docs.text:
• Modulated web parameters now come out the same as on the desktop. The web evaluator is a port of ModulatableParameter.evaluate() rather than its own approximation: ADD scales by the parameter's range, a bipolar source on a unipolar parameter is remapped to 0..1, depth and dcOffset apply per modulator, the result is clamped to the range and snapped to the steps of a stepped input, and MUL and SCALE behave as on the desktop. LFOs use the desktop shape (slope, morph, hold, the SQUARE duty), RANDOM waveforms draw the same values as the desktop for the same modulator, the step sequencer holds and glides identically, and audio sources honour the envelope follower (attack and decay). A parameter set to an explicit 0 stays 0.
  • What the web no longer accepts: the web-only operators (SUB, MIN, MAX, OVERRIDE), the SAW waveform and the amp/bass/onset aliases, none of which the desktop can load. A modulator the web cannot interpret is skipped instead of breaking the frame. midi_cc_* sources are skipped (no MIDI on the web), and audio_flux_* still follows the bass onset until the web gets per-band flux.
  • Internal: web/tools/evaluator_vectors.json holds golden results generated from the real desktop evaluator by WebEvaluatorVectorsTest, which fails when the file is stale (regenerate with UPDATE_WEB_VECTORS=1 ./gradlew test --tests '*WebEvaluatorVectorsTest*'). node --test web/tools/evaluator.test.mjs replays them against web/evaluator.js (no npm needed). evaluateParameter(param, ctx, spec) takes the per-frame context from makeEvalContext() and the clamp range and steps from paramSpec(isfInput); resolveBase resolves randomizeBase at load.

docs.title: Page Tabs Close Edit (ui/ParametersState.kt, ui/MenuBar.kt, ui/PerformSurface.kt)
docs.text:
• Clicking a Perform page tab now closes Edit and the Pair view, then shows that page. Before, the tab changed but the Edit bay stayed open over the rows you asked for. Clicking the tab of the page you are already on closes Edit too, so the whole tab is a big "back to the rows" target. A Twister bank change (or any controller command that selects a page) does the same. A module held open by an active Learn stays open.
  • Internal: ParametersState.leaveEditForPageChange() (collapse every rack module, then leavePair()); the tab click and PerformSurface.showPage call it before setting performancePageId.

docs.title: Twister Clock Knob: Beat Pulse, Tempo Ring, Push to Tap (ui/ClockKnob.kt, ui/PerformSurface.kt, control/KnobCommands.kt, control/KnobSurface.kt)
docs.text:
• The first knob of the Clock & Global row (MIXER page, knob 13) is now the clock knob. Its LED pulses in time with the beat: a dim plum at rest, a short flash of light plum on beats 2-4 and an orange flash on beat 1 of the bar, so you can find the bar line at a glance. Its ring shows the tempo across the beat tracker's BPM search range (Preferences > Tempo & Sync), so it moves when you tap or the tracker retunes. Pushing the knob taps tempo (on the press, not the release, so the tap lands when you push); turning it does nothing, since the BPM is deliberately not a knob. The pulse follows whichever clock is running (manual, audio or Ableton Link) and only shows while the MIXER page is up.
  • On the stock firmware, which has one hue per knob, the pulse is the ring brightness instead of a second colour. While the Twister is browsing the Library or a picker, the knob does its browse job instead.
  • Internal: ClockKnobFeed turns the beat phase, BPM and search range into a KnobLight; PerformPages.resolveInto returns the Clock knob's index (first knob of the global row). KnobSurface.pressDown(knob) lets a knob act on switch-down; KnobCommands then ignores that press's release. Colours are shared constants, so a frame allocates nothing, and ControllerFeedback sends only the few colour changes per beat.

docs.title: Twister XT Firmware: Native Mode with Ring Styles and RGB LEDs (control/NativeMode.kt, control/ControllerFeedback.kt, control/ControllerManager.kt, midi/MidiOutputPorts.kt, resources/controllers/midi-fighter-twister-xt.json)
docs.text:
• New optional profile, "Midi Fighter Twister (XT firmware, native mode)", for a Twister flashed with the custom XT firmware. The app switches the device into native mode while it runs: each ring follows its parameter (a bar, a bar with a centre detent for -100..100 parameters, a dot for endless and stepped ones, updating live as pages, effects and sources change) and the switch LEDs show the true row colour instead of the nearest of 126 hues. There are no hardware banks: the bank-step button (right-top, Shift + right-top for back) walks the Perform pages, and the other side buttons keep their stock jobs.
  • Opt-in, and the stock profile is unchanged. Both profiles fit the same device name, so in Preferences → MIDI Controls → Controller Profiles a Use profile selector appears for a device that more than one profile fits; the choice is remembered per device and applies immediately. Automatic matching still picks the stock profile.
  • The device is released when the app lets go of it: on quit, unplug and profile change the app turns every switch LED black and returns the Twister to normal. After a crash the Twister stays in native mode until it is replugged. Native mode has no ring brightness, so the live send knobs in the Library and Pair view leave the ring off and the switch LED shows the target colour.
  • Internal: NativeSysex builds the SysEx messages (one setting per message; the firmware misreads several in one); MidiSink.sendSysex and an ordered, never-coalesced SysEx FIFO in CcQueue are drained before control changes, and DeviceSink.close flushes them. Profiles gain output.native (SysEx header and a ring style per MeterType, editable in the JSON) and banks.virtual (the app's pages stand in for hardware banks); both are validated. ControllerFeedback sends the ring style and RGB colour only when they change, before the ring position. KnobSurface.currentPageId lets a virtual-bank profile step pages from the page on screen. The profile choice is controllerProfileChoices (device name without its [hw:...] suffix to profile id); ControllerProfileStore.matchFor honours it and candidatesFor lists the options.

docs.title: Source Knobs Control the Video After a Source Switch (presets/GeneratorDefaults.kt, rendering/DynamicVisualSource.kt, rendering/VisualSourceRegistry.kt)
docs.text:
• The four default knobs of a generator now drive it. The default bindings pointed at a parameter path no parameter had (Deck A/Speed instead of Deck A/<source name>/Speed), so after loading or switching a source the knobs and rings moved but the picture did not, and bipolar parameters showed as unipolar on the knob. Both are fixed for newly loaded sources. A preset or session saved with the old binding paths keeps the dead knobs until you re-save the generator default or rebind the knob.
  • Custom (meta.json) source parameters with a negative minimum are now bipolar unless the file says otherwise; before, a missing type meant unipolar.
  • Internal: GeneratorDefaults.deckParamId builds Deck/<displayName>/<param>; ParamMeta.type is nullable and ParamMeta.meterType() falls back to ModulatableParameter.defaultMeter.

docs.title: Angles Read as Degrees Everywhere (ui/ValueFormat.kt, parameters/ModulatableParameter.kt, ui/FxParamCell.kt)
docs.text:
• A -3.142..3.142 range now reads as -180..180 on knob faces, macro binding readouts and range fields, the Min and Max fields of the binding editor, and the effect parameter cell (for example RGB Split's Angle). Typing a value uses degrees too. The ranges the app treats as an angle now cover any author's rounding of pi from 3.1 to 3.2 (3.14, 3.141, 3.142 and so on); the shader still receives radians.
  • Internal: ValueFormat.scaleFor(min, max) returns ValueFormat.DEGREES for ModulatableParameter.isPiRange; code that converts angles itself still uses the three-argument form.

docs.title: Stepped Parameters Snap to Their Choices (parameters/ModulatableParameter.kt, rendering/isf/*, ui/DiscreteTicks.kt, ui/ParametersRenderer.kt, ui/MacroKnobWidget.kt, library/sources/*, default_filters/*)
docs.text:
• Mode, palette and count parameters now snap to real choices. A knob, LFO, audio source, macro, MIDI or OSC move used to sweep these continuously while the shader saw the value rounded down (so 0.99 read as 0). They now land exactly on a choice, and rounding is to the nearest one. This covers the 3D mode and blend mode, the transition curve and tint modes, and about 25 mode, palette and count inputs across the stock effects and sources (Kaleidoscope segments, Polar Tunnel symmetry, Retro CRT scanlines, Dynamic Spiral max points, and so on). Saved values load unchanged and snap when used.
  • Stepped knobs show their choices: one tick per choice around the ring (none above 16), and the focus-mode value shows the choice's name where it has one. Hovering the value says how many choices there are. The Max Points tooltip no longer claims it cannot be modulated; it can, and it snaps.
  • The VAL panel gives every stepped parameter a choice list (for example the 3D mode, a palette or a blend mode), showing the choice names where the effect defines them, instead of a plain slider. The live value and the starting value read as the choice name or number too. Parameters with more than 16 choices (scanline count, Max Points) keep their slider.
  • Internal: ModulatableParameter gains steps/labels and snaps in evaluate() (baseValue stays continuous). ISF long/int/bool inputs fill them from VALUES/LABELS; a new optional "STEP" header key marks a float input as discrete (see docs/developer/rendering.md). ISFVisualSource.createParameters now honours VALUES, MIN/MAX and an integer default for long inputs, and integer uniforms are rounded, not truncated. MeterType.DISCRETE is split from ENDLESS (bounded sweep plus ticks). The dead Background/Style branch in ValueParamSection is removed, and the hard-coded mode3D combo (MODE_3D_LABELS) is replaced by a generic chooser built from DiscreteTicks.choices. web/shaders re-synced for the annotated sources. StockDiscreteInputsAuditTest checks every stepped stock input.

docs.title: Twister: One Profile, Ready-Made Utility Settings (resources/controllers/midi-fighter-twister.json, midi-fighter-twister.mfs, control/ControllerProfileStore.kt)
docs.text:
• The Twister now has a single built-in profile, the former six-button one: the app steps the banks (right-top, Shift + right-top for back), right-middle opens the Library (Shift + right-middle: on the FX tab), left-middle toggles Chain Link (Shift + left-middle taps tempo), left-top goes back (Shift + left-top toggles Edit mode), and right-bottom opens the row picker (Shift + right-bottom toggles Pair view). All six side buttons are CC Hold. The firmware-bank "standard" profile and the separate midi-fighter-twister-6btn id are gone; a user profile copied from -6btn keeps working under its own name.
  • Knob 16's ring tracks the browse cursor: in the Pair view and the Library it shows the cursor's position in its list instead of sitting at 50% (full when there is no cursor yet). Internal: NavSurface.browsePosition, LibraryNavigation.cursorPosition, BrowserPane.treeIndex.
  • Live send knobs light their whole ring at half brightness: while the Library or Pair view can send the highlighted item, knobs 9-13 show a full ring in the target's colour at 50% brightness (ring brightness is sent on channel 6, 65-95, so any ring style shows it as a full ring only if the Utility makes it a bar). Internal: KnobFeedbackDef.indicatorChannel / indicatorBrightnessMin/Max, KnobLight.ringBrightness; the Twister profile sets indicatorChannel 5 (0-based) and every ring now gets one extra brightness message.
  • New midi-fighter-twister.mfs, saved from Preferences → MIDI Controls → Controller Profiles → Save Utility Settings... (the folder is remembered; Open Folder shows it): load it in the Midi Fighter Utility to set every encoder to relative, every button to CC Hold and every LED to black in both states. This also fixes unused knobs glowing the factory blue while browsing or editing.
  • Internal: profiles gain an optional utilityFile, read by ControllerProfileStore.utilityFileBytes; the folder is the utilitySettingsDirectory preference. ControllerProfileStore.BUILT_IN_NAMES has one entry; the runtime and profile tests use it for the side-button layout (six CCs per bank).

docs.title: Browser Lists Glide to the Selection (ui/SmoothScroll.kt, ui/browser/*)
docs.text:
• Stepping through a browser list (knob 16, arrow keys) now eases the list toward the selected row instead of snapping, which is easier on the eyes. A selection far outside the view (a list that has just opened) still jumps straight there.
  • Internal: the setScrollHereY calls in the browser panels are replaced by SmoothScroll.follow, called every frame for the selected row.

docs.title: Focus Knobs Skip the Parameter the Metaknob Already Moves (rendering/isf/ISFFilter.kt, macro/FxMacroSync.kt, rendering/FxChain.kt, ui/PerfKnobSpec.kt, ui/FXChainMacroStrip.kt)
docs.text:
• In FX focus mode, knobs 2-4 no longer offer a parameter that knob 1 (the Metaknob) is already driving. Previously the first parameter appeared twice, and its second knob did nothing. The parameter list and page count now leave out Metaknob-owned parameters, so every knob does something. Changing a parameter's Metaknob link updates the knobs straight away.
  • Internal: ISFFilter.focusParameters feeds FxMacroSync.syncFocusMode, FxChain.totalParamPages and FxRowState.of. Test fixtures that need all parameters pin the Metaknob to dry/wet.

docs.title: Metaknob-Owned Values Show a Lock; FX Browser Menu Loads Are Undoable (ui/ParametersRenderer.kt, ui/ValueParamSection.kt, ui/browser/FXBrowserPanel.kt)
docs.text:
• An effect parameter driven by its Metaknob link now shows it is locked: the VAL cell gets the same highlight as a macro-bound value, its tooltip names the link, middle-click reset is ignored, and the VAL panel greys out its controls with a "Driven by its Metaknob link" note. Disable the link to edit by hand.
  • "Load to / Slot n" in the FX browser's right-click menu can be undone with Ctrl+Z, like every other way of loading an effect.
  • Internal: ModulatableParameter.metaDrivenBy is read by the value cell and VAL section; the menu paths pass undoable = true to FxOps.

docs.title: Light Theme: First Contrast Pass (ui/TangoPalette.kt, ui/CvTheme.kt, and the panels that used white-alpha or pastel literals)
docs.text:
• Hover and press washes, grid cell stripes, header tints and locked-control captions that were white-on-dark now have light-theme versions (icon buttons, link-mode chips, the parameter grid and its headers, slider captions), so they no longer vanish on a light panel.
  • Status text (OK / warning / error) and the queue column headers use darker Tango shades on the light theme (Broadcast, MIDI and Shortcuts preferences, save and popup warnings, rack titles, preset-list errors).
  • Modulation signal colours (value, MIDI, LFO, sequencer, audio) are darkened on the light theme for contrast. The dark theme is unchanged.
  • Internal: new TangoPalette Roles (HOVER_OVERLAY, PRESS_OVERLAY, HEADER_TINT, CELL_WASH, HOVER_BORDER, TEXT_FAINT, TEXT_DIM, TEXT_OK, TEXT_WARN, TEXT_ERROR, QUEUE_AB_TEXT, QUEUE_BG_TEXT); CvTheme.LIGHT_THEME_SCALE. Remaining literals are listed in .planning/theme-color-audit.md.

docs.title: Controller FX Tap Applies; Browser Scope Is Remembered per Kind; Tooltips Mention the Pair View (ui/browser/DockActions.kt, ui/browser/FXBrowserPanel.kt, ui/browser/ApplyTarget.kt, ui/browser/BrowserPane.kt)
docs.text:
• Tapping an FX in the Library from a controller applies it to the live deck like a double-click: a single effect goes into the first empty slot (the last slot when all are full, since a controller has no popup), a chain replaces the deck's chain. Ctrl+Z undoes it and a toast says where it landed. Shift + tap still adds it to the FX queue.
  • The browser remembers your place per kind: the folder, search and cursor you left in Sources, FX or Transitions now carry over between the Library and every deck, slot and transition (moving between pairs no longer resets them). Choosing a whole FX chain still starts in saved chains and gets its own memory, because it can only list chains.
  • Tooltips on the source badge, chain name, FX slot names, transition picker and the deck/Master monitors now say they open the pair view.

docs.title: Shift + Tap on a Send Knob Switches Pairs (control/KnobCommands.kt, control/NavSurface.kt, ui/NavigationSurface.kt)
docs.text: • In the pair view, Shift + tap on knob 9-12 (or 13 for Master) jumps to that deck's pair without sending anything, and it works with nothing highlighted. A plain tap still sends the highlighted item.

docs.title: Twister Bank Buttons Walk the Pairs in the Pair View (control/ControllerRuntime.kt, control/KnobSurface.kt, ui/PerformSurface.kt, ui/UIManager.kt)
docs.text:
• In the pair view a bank change moves to the next pair (Deck A > B > BG > PV > Master > Transitions/Clock, wrapping) instead of changing the Perform page: a higher bank button is the next pair, a lower one the previous, and a bank-step button steps by one. You can reach every destination without the mouse or a send.
  • The device keeps the bank you pressed while a pair is focused (it is no longer pulled back to the page's bank); outside the pair view banks still pick the Perform page.
  • Internal: KnobSurface.stepPair / pairFocused.

docs.title: Pair Focus View: Browse a Deck's Source and FX Together (ui/ParametersState.kt, ui/PerfRows.kt, ui/PerformanceDeepEditBay.kt, ui/PerformanceBrowseBay.kt, ui/PairKnobTouch.kt, ui/NavigationSurface.kt, ui/BackNavigation.kt, ui/ViewState.kt, control/NavSurface.kt)
docs.text:
• Clicking a badge now focuses a pair of rows: a deck's SRC badge, FX chain name or slot, the Master FX chain or slot, the transition name, a preview monitor, or the controller's picker button shows that pair's two rows (deck SRC + FX, Transitions + Master FX) with the Browse list below. Every other row hides (the deck monitors stay visible).
  • The Browse list follows the half you touched: click a row's slot, or turn a knob on it, and the list switches to that half (SRC to sources, an FX slot or chain to effects, the transition to transitions). Master MST and Clock have nothing to browse.
  • Back, Parameters, Esc: a Back button and one Esc (or the controller's back button) return to Perform. Parameters opens the full parameter editor on the half you touched. The editor no longer has a Browse tab; the row's EDIT gear still opens it directly.
  • Twister: knobs 1-8 are the pair's two rows (live while you browse), 9-12 send the highlighted item to A/B/BG/PV and 13 to Master FX, knob 16 is the cursor. A send moves the focus to the destination deck's pair.
  • No more bound Perform dock: the Library dock in Perform is always the plain Library; binding happens in the pair view. Entering the full Library leaves the pair view.
  • Internal: ParametersState.focusedPair, PerfRows.PAIRS, NavSurface.browseLiveKnobs (replaces browseRowLive); SectionMode, rackSectionMode, openBrowseTab, dropStaleDockSelection and ViewState.dockBound removed.

docs.title: Library / Browser / Edit Lifecycle: Consistent Exits, Edit-Bay Unbind, Send Knobs Stay in the Library (ui/ParametersState.kt, ui/BackNavigation.kt, ui/PerformanceBrowseBay.kt, ui/browser/BrowserDock.kt, ui/LibraryNavigation.kt, ui/browser/FXBrowserPanel.kt)
docs.text:
• Every way out of Edit ends the browse binding: Esc, the EDIT gear, Space, Ctrl+F, Menu > Library, Close Edit and the controller's Library button used to leave the Perform dock bound and the bay on Browse. Now closing the last open bay always returns to an unbound Library and Params.
  • The pair view's chip has the unbind button: the X (and a double-click on a list row) leaves the pair view. Esc and the controller back button do the same in one press.
  • Clicking the slot you already have bound re-selects its tab after you wandered to another Library tab (the chip showed "paused" and nothing happened).
  • Twister send knobs from Library FULL only load: the view, scope and cursor stay put, so you can send several items in a row; FX sends toast where they landed. From the pair view a send moves the focus to the target's pair. FX chain and slot sends are now undoable (Ctrl+Z).
  • Internal: bindingFor(..., onEnd) replaces ownsSelection; ParametersState.dockSelectionEpoch; collapseAllRackModules owns the end-of-Edit reset.

docs.title: Bundled ISF Inputs Are Normalized to 0..1 / -1..1 (default_sources/*, default_filters/*, default_transitions/*, ui/ValueFormat.kt, rendering/isf/ISFAutoBindEngine.kt, defaults/*)
docs.text:
• 109 generator, FX and transition inputs that used raw ranges now span 0..1 or -1..1 (Domain Warp Fluid: Warp 0-4, Swirl -3..3, Speed -2..2, Viscosity, Gloss, Hue Cycle Speed; the FX amounts, intensities, decays, speeds, twists and radii; the transition amounts). They read as 0 to 100 in the UI. The shaders remap to their original working units, so the visuals at equivalent settings are unchanged.
  • Zoom (and the Celestial Engine / Chladni Scale) is centered: 50 is 1x, with an exponential feel either side.
  • Kept as-is: enums and counts (palettes, modes, segments, symmetries, Max Points, pixel size, strobe Hz, frequency integers) and angles in +-180 degrees.
  • More angles show in degrees: the 0..2PI inputs (Hyper Slice 4D rotations, Spike Phase, wave phase) now span +-PI, and Halftone Screen Angle is +-180 degrees instead of 0..90.
  • Breaking, deliberately: saved presets and sessions that stored old-unit values for these inputs will clamp or look different. The shipped FX chains and transitions were converted; web broadcast shaders were re-synced.
  • Internal: ISFAutoBindEngine.CURATED Metaknob ranges converted to the new units.

• Anything that spans 0 to 1 or -1 to 1 now reads as 0 to 100 or -100 to 100: parameter and LFO/Seq/MIDI value boxes, sequencer steps, macro knob faces and readouts, FX parameter cells and their tooltips, and the macro binding Min/Max fields. A decimal shows only when needed (37, 37.4); typing 37.4 stores 0.374.
  • Stored values are unchanged: presets, MIDI, OSC and shader uniforms still use 0 to 1. Angles stay in degrees and parameters with their own units keep them. The OSC preferences panel stays raw on purpose.
