The loop's bad-value test is abs(x) < 1e4 (the spec's 1e10 would let huge points through to be drawn off-screen), NaN included. r2 carries a +1e-9 guard, so variations that scale the point by 1/r (flower, conic, scry) return (0,0) at the exact origin rather than NaN, a deviation the spec allows; those that do not multiply by the point (log, polar2, escher, cpow) use the exact r² and give NaN there. A variation with a "non-standard weight" (loonie, scry, whorl, flux) returns its finished output from its case instead of being multiplied by the weight again. edisc clamps X >= 1 and |x/X| <= 1 because single-precision rounding hits those bad values far more often than double. Parameter ranges are the spec's generator ranges, mirrored around the default when the default sits on an edge (so min < default < max always holds), and disc2's twist spans +-2 pi because the spec defines it beyond +-2 pi. The importer reads a parameter from <name>_<label lower-cased> and also under any alias prefix (oscilloscope_* for oscope).

docs.title: Genome as parameters (FlameGenome)
docs.text: Parameters are built in Kotlin (not meta.json): 19 globals, six xforms and a final xform (weight, colour, speed, pre/post affine, four variation slots of id, weight and four normalised parameters A..D). Names are the preset keys (X2 PreRot, X2 V1 Id). pack() writes the uXf uniform array: weight-0 xforms are compacted, Spin/Breathe/Warp/Drift are applied, and each slot is [idA, wA, idB, wB] plus A's and B's parameters so a morph cross-weights two variation ids instead of sweeping through the ids in between. FlameVariations.real/normalised map the stored 0..1 values onto each variation's own range with 0.5 as the default.

docs.title: Morph and sampling
docs.text:
DeckMorphController owns A and B. A source that implements GenomeMorph picks its own targets (sampleMorphTarget(from, target, random, strategy, fresh)), keeps discrete parameters out of the lerp (isDiscreteMorph) and receives the live A/B/t (onMorphUpdate). SamplerStrategy { RANDOM, MUTATE, POOL, BREED } is DeckMorphController.strategy (default MUTATE, persisted as optional DeckPresetDto.samplerStrategy, written only when not MUTATE; null on load leaves the deck's setting alone). forceRandomize makes A a fresh genome (Random, or the Garden strategy) and B follows the strategy; vetoTarget() resamples the end the morph is heading to. Zoom, CenterX and CenterY are morph parameters: every target carries its framing (the gate verdict's for Random/Mutate/Breed, the offspring's own for Pool; FlameSampler.mutate skips them), so the camera drifts with the genome. The ZOOM macro knob drives the pinned Magnify multiplier (engine zoom = Zoom x Magnify) because macros write base values that the morph would overwrite. Each DeckMorphSnapshot.origin carries the genome's FlameLineage (parent names and tags) through promotions.

FlameSampler is pure: mutate (gaussian jitter on xform parameters, id swaps, xform birth/death), random (2-5 xforms, contractive pre-affines, 1-3 distinct variations from a weighted pool) and breed (whole-xform crossover, at least two active, then mutate). Final xform, camera, tone and modifier parameters are never part of a proposal. Only xform parameters are morph-enabled (randomizeBase); changing a parameter's default morph flag does not affect old saves, because applyDto restores the saved flag.

docs.title: Quality gate (FlameProbe, FlameQuality)
docs.text: Every Random, Mutate and Breed candidate is run through the engine's own iterate shader on a hidden 128x128 state texture (40 passes, one 256 KB readback; GL state is saved and restored) and judged by FlameQuality.analyse: diverged (points reseeded), collapsed, line (covariance), exploded (too big to frame) or fog (every grid cell hit with near-uniform counts). FlameSource.sampleMorphTarget retries up to 8 times, then falls back (starter for a fresh request, no change for a drift). The same analysis frames the camera for a fresh genome, since Zoom/CenterX/CenterY are not part of the morph. Thresholds are constants in FlameQuality; FlameProbeTest prints the rejection rates, and FLAME_SHEET=/tmp/sheet.png xvfb-run ./gradlew test --tests '*FlameProbeTest.contactSheet' writes a contact sheet of random genomes (red border = rejected). Kept Pool picks skip the gate.

docs.title: Garden (presets/Garden.kt, GardenThumbnails.kt)
docs.text: Garden.keep(deck, ...) saves the live deck (mid-morph: the nearer end, FlameSource.nearerEndValues(), swapped into the parameters just for the synchronous DTO build and restored after) through PresetRepository.saveDeckPresetAsync to library/presets/garden/<slug>-NNNN.lsd with tags garden, gen:N (youngest parent + 1) and parent:<name>, and writes <name>.png (256x144, blitted from the deck's output texture). Garden.pool(sourceId) reads the folder back (cached by modification time) for the Pool and Breed strategies; GenomePool.pick draws with weights: age rank 1..2 (newest 2x) times 3 for presets starred in the Sources browser (BrowseFavorites SRC keys, matched by absolute path via Garden.favoritePaths()). The browser lists the folder as a subfolder of Saved presets; no new browse root exists. PresetListPanel shows a preset's sibling png in its hover tooltip.

docs.title: Importer (FlameImporter, presets/FlameImportOps.kt)
docs.text: FlameImporter.parse(xml) reads a <flame> or <flames> file (DOCTYPE refused, BOM stripped) into Imported(values, palette, notes): xform weight/colour/symmetry (colour speed = (1 - symmetry) / 2), coefs and post affines decomposed into rotation, scales, shear and translation with the QR split that FlameGenome.pack inverts, up to three variations per xform by strongest weight (names and <variation>_<param> attributes follow the paper; julian, juliascope, radial_blur, gaussian_blur are aliases, and so are inversion -> spherical (observed to be identical) and linear3d/spherical3d -> their 2D twins, the last two with an import note because z is not modelled), the camera (Zoom = 2 * scale / height, centre, rotation), and the palette as 768 bytes (embedded in the preset: FlameImporter.toPresetDto writes it as base64 into the optional DeckPresetDto.palette; Deck.toDto/applyDto carry it through FlameSource.customPalette, which FlameEngine.setPalette uploads into the 256x1 palette texture; null = the procedural cosine palette, and a preset without a palette clears the deck's). The Palette parameter still shifts it cyclically. Weights above 2 are scaled together; out-of-range values are clamped and noted. Unknown variation attributes are detected heuristically for the notes only. The image's y axis is taken to point down: the importer sets the camera parameter FlipY (engine: p.y *= uFlipY after the camera rotation in the splat vertex shader), it does not conjugate the genome, which would change flames whose variations are not reflection-symmetric. Options.transposed (off) reads coefs the other way and Options.flipRotation (off) turns rotate the other way; both defaults and FlipY were checked against reference renders of rings2-1.flame (ring centre) and blob-2.flame (rotated, off-centre, asymmetric: only the unflipped rotation puts the burst in the right place and the transposed reading gives straighter rays than the reference). FlameProbeTest.importerConventionSheet (env FLAME_IMPORT_SHEET, FLAME_IMPORT_FILE) draws a file under the four option combinations for comparison with a reference render. Parameter ranges are deliberately wide so wild flames import unclamped (translations +-10, scales/shears +-4, slot weights -4..4, Zoom 0.01-32, centre +-16, Julia power -20..20); FlameSampler.mutate caps the range used for its jitter at 4 and lets an existing larger pre-scale stand, so drift behaves as before. All continuous parameters are stored normalised (0..1 or -1..1, angles in radians) so the UI shows 0..100 / -100..100 / -180..180; FlameUnits.of(name) holds the per-parameter map (linear, Exponential with 0.5 = neutral for zoom-like values, Neutral piecewise for Breathe/Warp) and every consumer (engine v(), FlameGenome.pack, FlameSource.setupUniforms, importer put, sampler) converts to real units at the boundary; FlameSampler.mutate/random/breed take and return stored values but work in real units inside. FlameUnitsTest.everyContinuousParameterIsNormalised fails for any new parameter that is not 0..1, -1..1, an angle or discrete. Softness (the uSize of the splat point sprite, 1-10, default 3) is a per-flame look parameter; the engine multiplies exposure by (3 / Softness)^2 so the mean density stays put. The quality tier no longer has a kernel. The importer sets Softness to twice the file's filter radius scaled to a 1080 px deck (IMPORT_DECK_HEIGHT, clamped 3-10) Toe to 0 (the toe is an absolute threshold on decay-normalised density, so on sparse imports it removes nearly everything; Sharpness above about 3 shrinks soft sprites to a core, which defeats Softness) and Decay to IMPORT_DECAY (0.85): the originals assume millions of samples per image, and the in-view hit count is the limit (rings2-1: about 3% of points land in view at the file's camera, so an HD deck gets ~0.1 effective samples per pixel against the original's ~10; decay cannot close that gap, hence the Smooth blur below). Smooth (0-1, 0 = off, imports set IMPORT_SMOOTH 0.5) is a density-estimation blur in the tone-map shader (estimate()): while Smooth > 0 the engine calls glGenerateMipmap on the density texture (min filter LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR, set when the FBO is created; the shader reads level 0 explicitly with textureLod otherwise), and the shader walks mip levels 5 down to 0, mixing each finer level in with smoothstep(0, 3*Smooth, a*(1-Decay)*uNorm) of its own density. Dense pixels end up at level 0 (sharp), sparse ones at the finest level that is dense enough. Mips preserve the mean, so total light is kept; the blur runs on the raw density before Toe and the log. uNorm is the same factor the engine folds into uExposure (n/rows, passExposure, (3/Softness)^2), so the threshold does not move with the quality tier, the governor or Softness. Cost: mip generation plus up to 6 fetches per pixel, only while Smooth > 0; the threshold constant 3 is tuned by eye. FlameImportOps.importFile writes one preset per flame into library/presets/imported-flames/ (never overwriting). Entry point: Sources browser ... menu, Import Flame....

docs.title: Offline curator (tools/FlameCurator.kt, FlameViability, FlameAesthetics)
docs.text: Builds the shipped flame library (no third-party genomes: the importer's input is user-supplied only). ./gradlew curateFlames -Pargs="--candidates 20000 --minutes 45 --out build/curated-flames" needs a GL 3.3 context and runs a quality-diversity (MAP-Elites) search: proposals are fresh FlameSampler.random or mutate/breed of archive elites, and each passes a funnel of filters: FlameViability (numbers only: three or more active xforms, no xform over 97% of the weight, not all pre-affines singular, not all linear-only and expanding; expanding affines alone are fine because variations fold space), the FlameProbe gate, a real 512x288 render (14 frames, Decay 0.85, Smooth 0.3, governor off, Medium tier) scored by FlameAesthetics.score, and four re-renders with the handles pushed (Spin +-0.8, Warp 0.3, Breathe 0.85) whose worst score blends into the final one. FlameAesthetics is pure maths on an RGBA readback: coverage, luma entropy, Sobel edge density at two scales, hue spread and dominance, plateau share, clipping, symmetry; the score is a geometric mean of trapezoid bands, so one bad axis sinks it (all ranges are guesses tuned on contact sheets). The archive cell is fill x structure x hue x symmetry (525 cells, --per-cell elites each). Output: curated-NNNN.lsd + thumbnail, metrics.csv and sheet.html: click a flame to cycle keeper, seed (breeding stock), reject, then Download decisions.txt and run --apply <dir> decisions.txt (deletes rejects, adds the seed tag to seeds; --sheet <dir> rebuilds an older sheet). Seeds are skipped by the Pool strategy (Garden.SEED_TAG, filtered in FlameSource.sampleMorphTarget) but Breed draws them, since breeding copies whole xforms and not palette, tone or camera. --seed-dir <dir> --out <other> starts a new search from the picks: most parents are the seeds and only 8% of proposals are fresh random, so the search follows the user's taste. Render resolution matters: the Smooth blur works in absolute mip levels, so a small render shows blocky plates that the app does not.

docs.title: Auto-governor (FlameGovernor)
docs.text: Fed the engine's GPU timestamp samples, it scales the iterated and drawn rows (the quality tier's point count stays the ceiling) to hold the flameBudgetMs preference (default 3 ms, 0 = off): smoothed time, proportional steps, shed fast and recover slowly.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: FlameGenomeTest, FlameVariationsTest (Kotlin mirror of the deterministic formulas against hand-derived pairs and every deterministic pair of the spec), FlameShaderValuesTest (GL: the real vari() on spec pairs), FlameSamplerTest, FlameQualityTest, FlameGovernorTest, FlameEditorLayoutTest, GardenTest, and the GL tests FlameShaderCompileTest and FlameProbeTest (skipped without a GL context; run them under xvfb-run). GL tests that draw must share one context per JVM: Geometry caches its fullscreen-quad VAO.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Files in library/sources/<id>/ are extracted once and never overwritten: delete the folder after changing a bundled source's resources.
  • A saved session or preset keeps each parameter's saved randomizeBase flag, so old saves do not pick up a changed morph default; re-add the source.
  • gradlew run does not forward -D flags; the engine's measuring switches are env vars (FLAME_N, FLAME_DENSITY, FLAME_SKIP).

Shipping the curated set. The flames you keep after --apply are copied into defaults/presets/garden/curated/ (.lsd plus thumbnail); PrepareDefaultAssetsTask adds everything under defaults/presets/garden/ to the bundled presets manifest as garden/curated/<name>; FileSystemManager.ensureDefaultLibrary extracts them into library/presets/garden/curated/ on first run without overwriting anything. Garden.pool walks its folder recursively, so Pool and Breed use them immediately. The set (158 flames from the second review round, 2026-10-12) is about 16 MB of resources.

docs.title: ImGui Upgrade & Modernization Guide
docs.text: This document details the multi-architecture ARM64 investigation for imgui-java (io.github.spair), the rationale for our two-phase upgrade strategy, and a comprehensive migration guide for future upgrades to Dear ImGui 1.92.x.

docs.title: Architecture Support Matrix & Findings
docs.text: During our investigation of all published io.github.spair:imgui-java artifacts on Maven Central from 1.86.11 through 1.92.7.1, we identified the exact state of ARM64 support across target platforms:

docs.title: 1. Apple Silicon (macOS ARM64 / aarch64)
docs.text:
• Version 1.86.11: imgui-java-natives-macos-1.86.11.jar packaged libimgui-java64.dylib compiled exclusively for x86_64. On Apple Silicon JVMs, running the application crashed on startup with: text java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: ... libimgui-java64.dylib: mach-o file, but is an incompatible architecture (have 'x86_64', need 'arm64')
  • Version 1.86.12 (First ARM64 Release): Starting with release 1.86.12, the upstream maintainer repackaged the macOS dylib as a Mach-O Universal Binary containing both x86_64 and arm64 architectures merged via lipo.
  • Subsequent Releases (1.87.0 through 1.92.7.1): All later versions retain universal binary packaging for macOS.

docs.title: 2. Linux ARM64 (linux-arm64 / aarch64)
docs.text:
• Upstream Status across ALL Releases: In every release of io.github.spair:imgui-java-natives-linux up to and including the latest 1.92.7.1, the bundled libimgui-java64.so is strictly an ELF 64-bit x86-64 shared object.
  • Upstream issue #105 ("Make it work in arm64 linux") remains open. Upstream does not publish an official imgui-java-natives-linux-arm64 artifact.
  • Impact: Upgrading imgui-java resolves macOS ARM64 out-of-the-box, but does not natively resolve Linux ARM64 without custom native build steps or an architecture-aware dynamic loader.

docs.title: Two-Phase Upgrade Strategy
docs.text: Metric Phase 1: Target 1.86.12 Phase 2: Target 1.92.7.1 (Current) macOS ARM64 Support Full (Universal x86_64 + arm64) Full (Universal x86_64 + arm64) Linux ARM64 Support No (Upstream limitation) No (Upstream limitation) Breaking API Changes 0 (Drop-in compatible) Implemented across UI codebase Regression Risk Zero Verified via test suite & styling fixes Status Completed Completed & Active

docs.title: Phase 1: Stable Adoption (1.86.12)
docs.text: We adopted 1.86.12 to immediately provide native Apple Silicon execution and unblock macOS ARM64 binary smoke testing without introducing source code churn, behavioural drift, or UI regression.

docs.title: Phase 2: Modernization (1.92.7.1)
docs.text: Adopted 1.92.7.1 to modernize Dear ImGui, upgrading the keyboard input system to the New Key API, switching to 64-bit texture handles, modernizing backend lifecycle methods, supporting dynamic font scaling, and enabling native multi-selection primitives.

docs.title: Phase 2 Migration Guide: Breaking Changes & Fixes
docs.text: Upgrading from 1.86.x to 1.92.x introduces breaking changes across GLFW/GL3 backends, font management, keyboard input handling, 64-bit texture handles, and draw list APIs.

docs.title: 1. 64-bit Texture Handles (ImTextureID changed from Int to Long)
docs.text:
• Symptom: text DeckControlPanel.kt:82:21 Argument type mismatch: actual type is 'Int', but 'Long' was expected. MixerMonitorPanel.kt:45:21 Argument type mismatch: actual type is 'Int', but 'Long' was expected. VideoExportModal.kt:124:19 None of the following candidates is applicable: static fun image(p0: Long, ...): actual type is 'Int', but 'Long' was expected.
  • Cause: Upstream Dear ImGui switched ImTextureID from a 32-bit integer to a 64-bit pointer/scalar (Long in Java bindings) to support 64-bit handles and modern graphics APIs.
  • Fix: Convert OpenGL texture handle ints with .toLong(): ```kotlin // DeckControlPanel.kt:82 ImGui.image(deck.getOutputTexture().toLong(), imgAvailW, imgAvailH, 0f, 1f, 1f, 0f)

// MixerMonitorPanel.kt:45 ImGui.image(mixer.getOutputTexture().toLong(), imgAvailW, imgAvailH, 0f, 1f, 1f, 0f)

// VideoExportModal.kt:124 ImGui.image(previewTexId.toLong(), previewW, previewH, 0f, 1f, 1f, 0f) ```

docs.title: 2. Backend Lifecycle Methods (dispose() $\to$ shutdown())
docs.text:
• Symptom: text UIManager.kt:614:18 Unresolved reference 'dispose'. UIManager.kt:615:19 Unresolved reference 'dispose'.
  • Cause: imgui-java-lwjgl3 backend classes (ImGuiImplGlfw and ImGuiImplGl3) replaced the custom .dispose() method with standard Dear ImGui .shutdown().
  • Fix: kotlin // UIManager.kt:614-615 imGuiGlfw.shutdown() imGuiGl3.shutdown()

docs.title: 3. Font Atlas Dynamic Rebuild (updateFontsTexture())
docs.text:
• Symptom: text UIManager.kt:329:22 Unresolved reference 'updateFontsTexture'.
  • Cause: ImGuiImplGl3.updateFontsTexture() was removed. The backend now exposes discrete destroyFontsTexture() and createFontsTexture() operations.
  • Fix: Replace updateFontsTexture() with destroy and recreate calls: kotlin // UIManager.kt:329 imguiGl3.destroyFontsTexture() imguiGl3.createFontsTexture()

docs.title: 4. Input System Overhaul (getKeyIndex() Removed)
docs.text:
• Symptom: text Unresolved reference 'getKeyIndex'.
  • Cause: Dear ImGui overhauled its keyboard input pipeline (the "New Key API"). ImGuiKey constants are now direct key identifiers rather than indices into the legacy io.KeysDown array. ImGui.getKeyIndex(...) was removed.
  • Impacted Files:
  • src/main/kotlin/llm/slop/liquidlsd/ui/ParametersKeyboard.kt
  • src/main/kotlin/llm/slop/liquidlsd/ui/UIManager.kt
  • src/main/kotlin/llm/slop/liquidlsd/ui/browser/BgQueueActionsPanel.kt
  • src/main/kotlin/llm/slop/liquidlsd/ui/browser/PlaylistEditorPanel.kt
  • src/main/kotlin/llm/slop/liquidlsd/ui/browser/PresetListPanel.kt
  • src/main/kotlin/llm/slop/liquidlsd/ui/browser/QueueActionsPanel.kt
  • Fix: Pass the ImGuiKey enum constants directly to ImGui.isKeyPressed and ImGui.isKeyDown: ```kotlin // Legacy (1.86.x): ImGui.isKeyPressed(ImGui.getKeyIndex(ImGuiKey.UpArrow)) ImGui.isKeyPressed(ImGui.getKeyIndex(ImGuiKey.Enter))

// Modern (1.92.x): ImGui.isKeyPressed(ImGuiKey.UpArrow) ImGui.isKeyPressed(ImGuiKey.Enter) ```

docs.title: 5. Multi-Color DrawList Colors (Long $\to$ Int)
docs.text:
• Symptom: text UIThemeStyler.kt:235:78 Argument type mismatch: actual type is 'Long', but 'Int' was expected.
  • Cause: In 1.86.x, ImDrawList.addRectFilledMultiColor expected Long values for packed 32-bit colors. In 1.89+, parameter types were standardized back to standard 32-bit integer color values (Int).
  • Fix: Remove .toLong() conversions: ```kotlin // UIThemeStyler.kt:232-235 val leftCol = getNeonBgColor((posX / displayWidth).coerceIn(0f, 1f)) val rightCol = getNeonBgColor(((posX + panelW) / displayWidth).coerceIn(0f, 1f))

dl.addRectFilledMultiColor(posX, posY, posX + panelW, posY + panelH, leftCol, rightCol, rightCol, leftCol) ```

docs.title: 6. Dynamic Font Scaling Parameter in pushFont
docs.text:
• Symptom: text UITheme.kt:685:36 No value passed for parameter 'p1'.
  • Cause: Dear ImGui 1.92 added dynamic runtime font scaling support directly to pushFont. In the Java bindings, the signature is ImGui.pushFont(ImFont font, float fontSize).
  • Fix: Pass 0f (which instructs ImGui to use the font's native baked size) or font.fontSize: kotlin // UITheme.kt:685 if (pushed) ImGui.pushFont(font, 0f)

docs.title: 7. Deprecated Style Attribute Removal (TabMinWidthForCloseButton)
docs.text:
• Symptom: text UIThemeStyler.kt:267:12 Unresolved reference 'setTabMinWidthForCloseButton'. UIThemeStyler.kt:267:46 Unresolved reference 'getTabMinWidthForCloseButton'.
  • Cause: tabMinWidthForCloseButton was deprecated and removed from ImGuiStyle in Dear ImGui upstream.
  • Fix: Remove line 267 from UIThemeStyler.copyStyleSizes: kotlin // Remove: // to.setTabMinWidthForCloseButton(from.getTabMinWidthForCloseButton())

docs.title: RFC: Relative Knob Dragging & Cursor Locking / Restoration
docs.text:
• Status: Implemented
  • Author: Antigravity Pair Programming
  • Target Subsystem: ui/MacroKnobWidget.kt, ui/UIManager.kt, Main.kt, ui/PreferencesPanel.kt
  • Related Docs: UI Architecture, ARCHITECTURE.md, DECISIONS.md

docs.title: 1. Problem Statement & Motivation
docs.text: In Liquid LSD, real-time performance often involves serial adjustments across banks of rotary controls—such as tweaking an FX Chain's Super Knob, adjusting individual slot Dry/Wet and parameters in Focus Mode, or sweeping Macro Bank controls.

docs.title: Current Behavior
docs.text: Currently, MacroKnobWidget uses standard Dear ImGui coordinate tracking (io.mousePos.x - dragStartX, io.mousePos.y - dragStartY). As the performer drags: 1. The mouse cursor visually traverses across the screen (often 100–200 pixels vertically or diagonally). 2. When the performer releases the mouse button, the cursor remains at the displaced screen position—often inches away from the knob that was just manipulated. 3. To adjust the next knob in the row or rack, the performer must physically locate and reposition the cursor back across the screen.

docs.title: Proposed Improvement
docs.text:
When click-dragging a knob: 1. Hide the cursor on drag initiation. 2. Keep the cursor confined or anchored at its initial press position while accumulating relative motion deltas. 3. On mouse release, show the cursor at the exact coordinates where the click originated.

This behavior mimics industry-standard DAW and pro-audio tools (Ableton Live, Bitwig Studio, Native Instruments, Serum, FabFilter, Blender) and drastically streamlines live manipulation by preserving hand-eye alignment and spatial muscle memory.

docs.title: 2. Architectural Approaches
docs.text:
Three technical patterns exist for implementing this behavior in a GLFW + Dear ImGui application:

Approach Description Advantages Drawbacks & Platform Risks 1. Naive Hide + Warp on Release Hide cursor via ImGui.setMouseCursor(None) or glfwSetInputMode(GLFW_CURSOR_HIDDEN). Let the OS cursor wander invisibly. On mouse up, call glfwSetCursorPos(window, startX, startY). Minimal code changes; retains existing absolute io.mousePos math. Fails completely on Linux Wayland; cursor freezes at screen edges; can wander onto other monitors. 2. Pointer Lock / Relative Mode (GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED) On drag start, switch GLFW window cursor mode to GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED. The OS locks the cursor, hides it, and emits raw relative motion deltas. On mouse release, revert to GLFW_CURSOR_NORMAL. Fully supported on Wayland via zwp_pointer_constraints_v1; infinite sweep (never hits monitor edge); standard across games and 3D tools. Requires reading raw deltas (io.mouseDelta or GLFW cursor callback) rather than absolute positions; requires decoupling ImGui cursor state during grab. 3. Continuous Per-Frame Warping Hide cursor and warp pointer back to (startX, startY) every frame during drag, accumulating frame-by-frame deltas. Infinite sweep on X11 and Windows. Fails on Wayland; causes mouse acceleration jitter and high event overhead on macOS.

docs.title: A. Linux Wayland Security Restrictions (GLFW_PLATFORM_WAYLAND)
docs.text:
• The Constraint: Liquid LSD runs natively on Linux under Wayland (see Wayland guards in Main.kt and WindowFrameController.kt). Under the Wayland security model, compositors strictly prohibit client applications from warping the global pointer in normal mode. Calling glfwSetCursorPos() in GLFW_CURSOR_NORMAL or GLFW_CURSOR_HIDDEN generates GLFW_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE or is silently dropped.
  • Impact: If Approach 1 or 3 is used on Wayland, the cursor will disappear during drag, but upon mouse release it will fail to jump back, reappearing inches away or on another display.
  • Resolution: Wayland compositors (GNOME Mutter, KDE KWin, Sway, Hyprland) only support pointer confinement/locking via the zwp_pointer_constraints_v1 and wp_relative_pointer_manager_v1 protocols. GLFW binds these protocols strictly through GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED. Therefore, relative mode (Approach 2) is the only robust cross-platform path that functions correctly on Wayland.

docs.title: B. The Screen Edge Deadzone (Monitor Boundary Clipping)
docs.text:
• The Constraint: If the cursor is merely hidden but allowed to travel across the desktop (Approach 1):
  • Upper racks, FX rows, and menu-adjacent knobs are positioned near the top of the window.
  • Dragging upward to increase a knob value causes the invisible OS pointer to hit the top of the physical monitor (Y = 0) after 20–40 pixels.
  • Once the OS cursor hits the display edge, the operating system stops generating delta events.
  • Failure mode: The performer continues moving their physical mouse, but the knob freezes partway through its sweep.
  • Multi-Monitor Bleed: An unconfined invisible cursor can travel onto an external display (e.g. Liquid LSD's secondary projection window secondaryWindow) or click into an OS dock or taskbar.

docs.title: C. Click vs. Drag Disambiguation (Micro-Movement Jitter)
docs.text:
• The Constraint: MacroKnobWidget multiplexes multiple mouse interactions:
  • Left Click: Select knob / inspect bindings (onSelect()).
  • Right Click: Toggle MIDI / modulation learn (onToggleLearn()).
  • Middle Click: Reset knob to default value (0.5).
  • Scroll Wheel: Fine increment adjustment.
  • Edge Case: Physical human fingers rarely execute a pure 0-pixel click. On mouse-down, 1–2 pixels of micro-motion almost always register. If the cursor is hidden immediately on isActivated, an ordinary click to select or inspect will cause the cursor to vanish for 40–80 ms and reappear—producing an annoying visual blink.
  • Resolution: Implement a drag deadzone (e.g. 3–4 pixels of Euclidean travel, matching ImGui.isMouseDragging(0, 3.0f)). The cursor remains visible as an arrow during mouse-down, and only switches to hidden/relative mode once intentional drag displacement is established.

docs.title: D. ImGui Event Pipeline & 1-Frame Teleport / Hover Bleed
docs.text:
• The Constraint: Dear ImGui processes window and cursor inputs during glfwPollEvents() at the start of each frame.
  • Hover Bleed: If the cursor travels invisibly across the UI, any UI elements underneath its path must not trigger hover styling, cursor changes, or tooltips. (ImGui's active widget system suppresses most click routing, but complex custom hitboxes or child windows may still test mouse coordinates).
  • Release Timing: When the cursor is restored to origin on mouse release, the position change is applied to GLFW. ImGui updates io.mousePos on the subsequent event poll. Any logic must ensure the mouse release is registered at the origin or after the position has stabilized, preventing a 1-frame "teleport" artifact where an unrelated widget briefly evaluates hover.

docs.title: E. Absolute Pointing Hardware (Touchscreens, Stylus / Digitizers)
docs.text:
• The Constraint: Liquid LSD supports touch hardware (see TouchConsoleController.kt). Performance rigs frequently use Microsoft Surface devices, touch monitors, or Wacom pens.
  • Failure Mode: Absolute digitizers enforce hardware-level coordinates on every touch contact. Attempting to lock or warp cursor coordinates on a touchscreen causes severe stuttering, driver fighting, or wild coordinate jumps.
  • Resolution: Relative cursor locking must be bypassable when touch events are detected, and must have a clear preference toggle in user settings.

docs.title: F. Window Focus Loss & Emergency Recovery Invariants
docs.text:
• The Constraint: If the performer is dragging a knob and:
  • An OS notification steals focus,
  • The user presses Alt+Tab or the Super key,
  • A modal prompt opens (e.g. unsaved preset dialog),
  • The application is minimized or secondary window interacts...
  • Critical Safety Invariant: The application must never leave the user with a trapped or invisible cursor on their desktop.
  • In Main.kt (glfwSetWindowFocusCallback), if the window loses focus while a knob drag is active, GLFW_CURSOR_NORMAL and ImGuiMouseCursor.Arrow must be forcefully restored immediately.
  • MacroKnobWidget must cleanly abort any relative drag state if !io.mouseDown[0] or if focus is lost.
  • Widget-side state is global, not per-instance: MacroKnobWidget is a singleton object, and its drag-tracking fields (activeKnobId, dragStartX, dragStartY, dragStartValue) are module-level, not per-widget. This is safe today because only one knob can be dragged at a time, but it means the focus-loss recovery hook must explicitly reset activeKnobId = null (and the lock-related fields added below) in addition to restoring GLFW cursor mode — resetting only the OS cursor state and leaving a stale activeKnobId behind would let the next frame's isActive && activeKnobId == id check misfire.

docs.title: G. High-DPI and Content Scaling
docs.text:
• The Constraint: GLFW cursor coordinates (glfwGetCursorPos, glfwSetCursorPos) operate in virtual screen coordinates (window points), whereas framebuffer dimensions and physical display pixels may be scaled (e.g. 2x on macOS Retina, 1.25x/1.5x on Wayland fractional scaling).
  • Any stored coordinates must strictly remain in window points matching ImGui.getIO().mousePos.

docs.title: 4. User Preference & Ergonomics
docs.text:
• Visual Feedback: When the cursor is hidden, the knob must clearly convey that it is being manipulated. MacroKnobWidget already rotates the indicator needle and illuminates an active border ring (Electric Cyan / accent tint).
  • Configurable Setting: In PreferencesPanel (under Category.GENERAL): [x] Lock cursor to knob while dragging (default: true) This provides an immediate escape hatch for users with touch devices, specialized trackballs, or personal preferences for standard cursor movement.

docs.title: 5. Recommended Implementation Plan
docs.text:
This plan follows the codebase's existing patterns rather than introducing new ones: preferences persist through UITheme.settings + AppPreferencesStore, and actual GLFW calls are issued only from the code that already owns the window handle (UIManager/Main.kt), not from the stateless MacroKnobWidget object.

  1. Preference Configuration (follows the existing autoVjDirtyBehavior/theme precedent, not a new config class):
  2. Add lockCursorOnKnobDrag: Boolean = true as a field on the UITheme.settings data class (UITheme.kt), with a var get/set wrapper on UITheme that goes through settings.copy(...), mirroring UITheme.autoVjDirtyBehavior (UITheme.kt:134-136).
  3. Load/save it as a Properties entry in AppPreferencesStore.kt, mirroring the existing autoVjDirtyBehavior/theme read (AppPreferencesStore.kt:215-235) and write (AppPreferencesStore.kt:333) blocks.

  4. Add a checkbox in PreferencesPanel.kt's drawGeneralPreferences (PreferencesPanel.kt:194).

  5. Lock-request state in MacroKnobWidget (widget signals intent; it does not touch GLFW itself):

  6. Add module-level fields alongside the existing dragStartX/dragStartY/dragStartValue (MacroKnobWidget.kt:76-78): isDragLocked: Boolean, lockOriginX: Float, lockOriginY: Float.
  7. On isActivated (mouse press): record dragStartX/dragStartY/dragStartValue as today (MacroKnobWidget.kt:131-135); do not engage the lock yet.
  8. Each frame while isActive: compute Euclidean travel from (dragStartX, dragStartY). Once it exceeds a ~3px deadzone (matching ImGui.isMouseDragging(0, 3.0f)) and UITheme.lockCursorOnKnobDrag is enabled, set isDragLocked = true and latch lockOriginX/Y to the current io.mousePos. This satisfies the click-vs-drag disambiguation in Section 3.C without any GLFW call happening inside the widget.

  9. Expose the request as a tiny public surface MacroKnobWidget already needs: e.g. val wantsCursorLock: Boolean (true only on the frame lock should engage) and val wantsCursorRelease: Boolean (true on the frame the drag ends while isDragLocked), plus lockOriginX/lockOriginY getters. Continue driving applyDragDelta off io.mousePos - dragStartX/Y exactly as today — under GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED these deltas keep accumulating correctly since GLFW/ImGui still updates a virtual mousePos.

  10. Pointer grab execution in UIManager (this is the piece the original plan omitted — only UIManager/Main.kt hold windowHandle):

  11. After the frame's widget drawing (where UIManager.render already calls into PerformanceMatrixPanel → MacroKnobWidget.draw), check MacroKnobWidget.wantsCursorLock / wantsCursorRelease and act on windowHandle (UIManager.kt:32):
    • On wantsCursorLock: glfwSetInputMode(windowHandle, GLFW_CURSOR, GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED).
    • On wantsCursorRelease, in this exact order (see Section 3.A — reversing this order breaks the Wayland restore):
    • While still GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED, call glfwSetCursorPos(windowHandle, lockOriginX, lockOriginY). This sets GLFW's virtual position / the Wayland pointer-constraint position hint while the constraint is still active.
    • Only then call glfwSetInputMode(windowHandle, GLFW_CURSOR, GLFW_CURSOR_NORMAL) to release the lock. Calling glfwSetCursorPos after switching to GLFW_CURSOR_NORMAL is silently dropped on Wayland (Section 3.A) and must not be relied on.

  12. Bypass the whole lock path when a touch/stylus contact is active (Section 3.E) — gate on the same touch-detection signal TouchConsoleController uses, if applicable to the pointer driving this drag.

  13. Global Focus & Interruption Safety:

  14. Hook into the existing glfwSetWindowFocusCallback in Main.kt (Main.kt:308) to force GLFW_CURSOR_NORMAL immediately if focus leaves the application while locked, and additionally call a new MacroKnobWidget.abortDrag() to clear activeKnobId/isDragLocked (see Section 3.F note above) — resetting cursor mode alone is not sufficient.

  15. Docs:

  16. Per this project's release convention, land docs/developer/ui.md, docs/release_notes.md/RELEASE_NOTES.md, and the relevant PreferencesPanel tooltip alongside the code change, plus a DECISIONS.md entry — not deferred to a follow-up.

docs.title: Mandala Visual Source - Future Feature Roadmap & UX Notes
docs.text: This document captures design ideas and proposed features for future iterations (v2+) of the Mandala visual source selector and recipe management system in Liquid LSD Desktop.

docs.title: 1. Visual Recipe Vault / Gallery Popover (Idea #2)
docs.text:
• Concept: A visual modal window or popover grid displaying pre-rendered thumbnail snapshots or live GPU micro-previews of all ~300 built-in recipes.
  • Filtering: Category tabs across the top (All, 3 Lobes, 4 Lobes, 5 Lobes, 6 Lobes, 8+ Lobes).
  • Interaction: Clicking any thumbnail instantly updates Lobes.baseValue and Recipe Select.baseValue to match the target recipe.
  • Challenge / Note: Each recipe's appearance depends on current arm parameters (L1, L2, L3, L4) and rotation/color settings. Micro-previews will need default reference parameters for snapshot rendering.

docs.title: 2. Geometric Tagging & Humanized Naming (Idea #3)
docs.text:
• Concept: Assign human-readable names and geometric style tags/badges to the ~300 recipes instead of displaying raw math vectors like [26, 23, 14, 14].
  • Taxonomy / Tags:
  • Starburst, Floral / Petal, Lattice / Mesh, Harmonic Ring, Crystalline, Spike Ring.
  • UI Presentation:
  • Recipe display: #7: Floral Weave (4 Lobes · [26, 23, 14, 14]).
  • Enables tag filtering in the visual browser or preset search.

docs.title: 3. Dual Indexing Modes: Local vs. Global Recipe Index (Idea #4)
docs.text:
• Concept: Re-evaluate parameter mapping between local lobe-relative indexing vs. global recipe indexing.
  • Local Indexing (Current):
  • Recipe Select (0.0..1.0) maps relative to the array of recipes for the currently active lobe count.
  • Pro: Modulating Lobes with an LFO keeps the recipe relative position steady within each lobe count group.
  • Global Indexing:
  • A separate or toggled parameter (Global Recipe ID from 0..300) that sweeps sequentially through all recipes across all lobe counts.
  • Pro: Sweeping an LFO across the global index moves continuously through all 300 recipes in the library.

docs.title: 4. Favorites & Performance Quick-Slots (Idea #5)
docs.text:
• Concept: Performers often rely on 10–20 go-to Mandala recipes during live VJ sets.
  • Quick-Slots:
  • Add "Star" / Favorite bookmarking to save recipes into quick-recall slots (e.g. [ Fav 1 ] [ Fav 2 ] [ Fav 3 ] [ Fav 4 ]).
  • Render quick-recall buttons on the Deck / Parameters UI for zero-latency switching during live performances.

Created on 2026-07-20 to track future UI/UX enhancements for Mandala Visual Generator.

docs.title: Modulation System
docs.text: Every visual parameter in Liquid LSD is a ModulatableParameter. Each parameter holds a base value and a list of CvModulator instances. Once per frame evaluate() computes the final driven value by combining those modulators. This document explains the full pipeline.

docs.title: ModulatableParameter
docs.text:
File: parameters/ModulatableParameter.kt

baseValue ──┐
            ├──► evaluate() ──► value  (clamped to [minClamp, maxClamp])
modulators ─┘                     │
                                  └──► history (CvHistoryBuffer, 200 samples)

Key properties:

Property Purpose baseValue Starting value before any modulation baseMin / baseMax Randomization range for baseValue at preset-load time randomizeBase If true, baseValue is re-rolled at preset-load from [baseMin, baseMax] minClamp / maxClamp Hard output clamp; also determines polarity (see below) meterType MONOPOLAR (default), BIPOLAR (minClamp < 0), ENDLESS, DISCRETE modulators CopyOnWriteArrayList<CvModulator> — safe for read-heavy concurrent access modulatorFilter Optional @Volatile predicate; when set only matching modulators are evaluated (used by deck-preview mode) value Last evaluated output (internal set; updated every evaluate() call) history CvHistoryBuffer ring buffer — read by the oscilloscope in PropertiesPanel scopeTimebase ScopeTimebase (AUTO, 1s, 10s, 100s, 15m, 2.5h, 24h) — transient per-parameter oscilloscope zoom

MIDI mapping fields (mappedMidiId, midiMapMin, midiMapMax) are deprecated. Use MidiMappingManager profiles instead.

docs.title: evaluate() — per-frame pipeline
docs.text:
// Simplified from ModulatableParameter.evaluate()

result = baseValue

for (mod in modulators) {
    if (bypassed || not registered || filtered) continue

    rawCV = evaluateModulator(mod)          // Evaluators.kt — see below

    // Same shape for every source and target.
    rawModAmount = rawCV * depth + dcOffset   // CvModulator.lfoShape

    // Scale to parameter range
    scalar = if (ADD) then (range / 2) for bipolar, else range for monopolar; else 1.0
    modAmount = rawModAmount * scalar

    result = when (operator) {
        ADD   -> result + modAmount
        MUL   -> result * (1 + modAmount)
        SCALE -> result * (1 - depth + modAmount)
    }
}

value = result.coerceIn(minClamp, maxClamp)

Polarity: if minClamp < 0, the parameter is bipolar; only the ADD scalar differs (range / 2 for bipolar, range otherwise). A bipolar source (LFO, sample-and-hold) swings dcOffset ± depth on every parameter, so on a 0..1 parameter it goes below the base value unless dcOffset lifts it; unipolar sources (audio, trigger, MIDI CC) span dcOffset .. dcOffset + depth. (Before 2026-10-27 a bipolar source on a monopolar parameter was remapped to [0, 1] first; stock presets and recipes were rewritten to keep their sweep.)

docs.title: CvModulator — Full Field Reference
docs.text: File: parameters/CvModulator.kt Serializable — all fields are stored in .lsd preset files.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text: Field Type Purpose sourceId String Which CV signal drives this modulator. Registered IDs: lfo, beatPhase, sampleAndHold, audio_amp, audio_bass, audio_mid, audio_high, audio_flux_amp, audio_flux_bass, audio_flux_mid, audio_flux_high, bpm, midi_cc_<ch>_<cc> (trigger_onset/trigger_accent exist only in the WebGL2 web client's dsp.js/evaluator.js — see docs/developer/web_subsystem.md — not as a desktop CvModulator source) operator ModulationOperator How this modulator combines with the accumulated result bypassed Boolean If true, skipped entirely in evaluate() id String (UUID) Unique identity for undo/copy-paste tracking

docs.title: LFO 1 (Carrier) — applies to all sourceIds that use waveform evaluation
docs.text: Field Type Range Purpose depth Float [0, 1] Peak modulation depth dcOffset Float [-1, 1] Constant offset added after depth scaling waveform Waveform — Shape: SINE, TRIANGLE, SQUARE, RANDOM subdivision Float Seconds (TIME), beats (BEAT), or frames (FRAME) One cycle duration phaseOffset Float [0, 1] Phase shift within the cycle slope Float [0, 1] Asymmetry: 0 = sharp fall/slow rise, 0.5 = symmetric, 1 = slow rise/sharp fall morph Float [0, 1] Waveshaping softness (0 = linear triangle, 1 = near-sine via cosh approximation) hold Float [0, 0.99] Plateau width at peak (compresses the transition region) genUnit GenUnit TIME, BEAT, or FRAME Whether subdivision is measured in seconds, musical beats, or render frames (1-10000). Only meaningful for lfo. lfoSpeedMode LfoSpeedMode SLOW/MEDIUM/FAST UI-only speed range hint for the slider

docs.title: Randomization Ranges
docs.text:
Every continuously-valued field has a Min/Max pair and a randomize* flag:

depthMin / depthMax / randomizeDepth
subdivisionMin / subdivisionMax / randomizeSubdivision
phaseOffsetMin / phaseOffsetMax / randomizePhaseOffset
slopeMin / slopeMax / randomizeSlope
morphMin / morphMax / randomizeMorph
holdMin / holdMax / randomizeHold
dcOffsetMin / dcOffsetMax / randomizeDcOffset

When the preset randomize action fires, randomizeActiveValues() samples uniformly within each [min, max] range. For beat-based subdivision the sample is drawn from a discrete set of musical values {1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1, 2, 4, 8 … 256}. For frame-based subdivision, it samples discrete integers in [min, max].

docs.title: Modulation Range Bounds (Min/Max Mode)
docs.text:
For LFO 1 and Audio followers, the UI presents human-readable Min Value and Max Value modulation bounds rather than abstract depth (amplitude) and dcOffset (center).

  • Mapping:
  • $\text{Min} = \text{dcOffset} - \text{depth}$
  • $\text{Max} = \text{dcOffset} + \text{depth}$
  • $\text{depth} = (\text{Max} - \text{Min}) / 2$
  • $\text{dcOffset} = (\text{Max} + \text{Min}) / 2$
  • Methods: CvModulator.getLfoMin(), CvModulator.getLfoMax(), CvModulator.withLfoRange(min, max).
  • Randomization Range Storage: When lfoMinMaxMode is true, the two-tier randomization sliders store the bounds for the Minimum limit in dcOffsetMin / dcOffsetMax (with flag randomizeDcOffset) and the bounds for the Maximum limit in depthMin / depthMax (with flag randomizeDepth). This ensures complete preset serialization compatibility without altering the underlying DTO schema.

docs.title: Audio Envelope Followers — applies when isAudioSource(sourceId)
docs.text:
When a modulator uses an audio band source (audio_amp, audio_bass, audio_mid, audio_high), it can apply an independent asymmetric one-pole IIR envelope follower:

Field Type Range Purpose followerMode AudioFollowerMode RAW, PUNCHY, SMOOTH, SLOW, AMBIENT, CUSTOM Envelope dynamics preset mode attackMs Float [0, 500] ms Rise time constant ($\tau_{\text{att}}$) decayMs Float [10, 3000] ms Fall time constant ($\tau_{\text{dec}}$) attackMsMin / attackMsMax Float [0, 500] ms Randomization bounds for attack time decayMsMin / decayMsMax Float [10, 3000] ms Randomization bounds for decay time randomizeAttackMs / randomizeDecayMs Boolean true/false Enables randomization for attack/decay
  • Evaluation Pipeline: Implemented in AudioFollowerTracker inside Evaluators.kt. Uses framerate-independent exponential one-pole smoothing: $$\alpha = 1 - e^{-\Delta t / \tau}$$ $$\text{If } x > y_{\text{prev}}: \quad y = y_{\text{prev}} + \alpha_{\text{att}} \cdot (x - y_{\text{prev}})$$ $$\text{If } x \le y_{\text{prev}}: \quad y = y_{\text{prev}} + \alpha_{\text{dec}} \cdot (x - y_{\text{prev}})$$
  • Dual-Trace Scope: In OscilloscopeDrawer.drawOscilloscope, ghostHistory receives the un-followed raw band energy ($35\%$ alpha) while the main line plots the filtered follower output.

docs.title: LFO 2 (Modulator) — only evaluated when sourceId == "lfo"
docs.text:
LFO 2 is a second oscillator that modulates properties of LFO 1. It has its own waveform, speed, phase, slope, morph, and hold:

Field Purpose modWaveform LFO 2 shape modSubdivision LFO 2 cycle duration modPhaseOffset LFO 2 phase shift modSlope LFO 2 asymmetry modMorph LFO 2 waveshaping modHold LFO 2 plateau modGenUnit TIME, BEAT, or FRAME for LFO 2's clock generatorModMode How LFO 2 acts on LFO 1: NONE, AM, PM, or ADD generatorModDepth How much LFO 2 influences LFO 1

Randomization ranges also exist for all mod-fields (modSubdivisionMin/Max, etc.).

docs.title: Enums
docs.text: File: parameters/Enums.kt

docs.title: ModulationOperator
docs.text: Value Formula ADD result + modAmount — adds CV signal scaled to parameter range MUL result * (1 + modAmount) — multiplicative ring-mod style SCALE result * (1 - depth + modAmount) — attenuates the base value

docs.title: Waveform
docs.text: Value Shape SINE Standard sinusoid TRIANGLE Linear ramp with slope-controlled asymmetry SQUARE Duty-cycle set by slope RANDOM Per-cycle sample-and-glide (deterministic from subdivision + phaseOffset hash)

docs.title: GenUnit
docs.text:
Value Meaning TIME subdivision is a period in seconds BEAT subdivision is a number of beats (synced to CVRegistry.getSynchronizedTotalBeats()) FRAME subdivision is a number of render frames (1 to 10,000 frames, synced to CVRegistry.getRenderFrameCount())

When genUnit == BEAT the subdivision randomizer draws from the discrete musical grid rather than a continuous uniform. When genUnit == FRAME, the randomizer and UI lock strictly to integer frame counts. Beat mode uses getSynchronizedTotalBeats() which is an interpolated estimate updated from the JACK audio thread via @Volatile fields in CVRegistry. Frame mode uses monotonic render frame ticks updated on each frame.

Period changes stay continuous (ClockAnchors). A TIME or FRAME generator's position is clock / period, and the clock is the seconds (or frames) since start, so changing the period moved the position by clock times the change in 1 / period: an hour in, turning an LFO's rate, a macro or OSC on its subdivision, or a preset morph lerping it jumped the LFO, every frame while it moved. ClockAnchors (one per ModulatableParameter, keyed by modulator id, separate tables for LFO 1 / sequencer and LFO 2) keeps a shift that absorbs clock / old - clock / new when the period changes, so only the rate changes. It is per parameter because the same preset on two decks shares modulator ids. evaluateModulator, evaluateModulatorAtOffset and seqCyclePosition take it as an optional argument (ModulatableParameter.evaluate and the sequencer playhead pass clockAnchors); look-ahead offsets never move it, and a clock-unit change resets it. BEAT generators are not anchored: they stay locked to the bar. RANDOM waveforms still reseed when the period changes (the seed hashes it). The web evaluator mirrors it in anchoredCycles, keyed by modulator id in ctx.anchors, since broadcast messages replace the modulator objects.

docs.title: GeneratorModMode (LFO 2 interaction)
docs.text: Value Effect on LFO 1 NONE LFO 2 disabled; LFO 1 runs independently AM Amplitude Modulation — carrierVal * (1 + lfo2Val * depth) PM Phase Modulation — shifts LFO 1's phaseOffset by lfo2Val * depth before evaluation ADD Additive — carrierVal + lfo2Val * depth

docs.title: LfoSpeedMode
docs.text: UI hint only (SLOW, MEDIUM, FAST). Controls the slider range shown in PropertiesPanel when the user adjusts subdivision in time mode. Does not affect evaluation.

docs.title: Waveform Math
docs.text: File: parameters/WaveformMath.kt

docs.title: calculateAdvancedLFO(phase, morph, hold, slope, waveform) — used by lfo, beatPhase, sampleAndHold
docs.text:
1. If waveform == SQUARE:
   - slope functions as Duty Cycle D in [0.001, 0.999] (PWM)
   - Threshold voltage: V_th = 1.0 - 2.0 * D
   - Slices symmetric triangle through threshold V_th with rising edge aligned to phase 0.0
   - Scales by 1.0 / (1.0 - safeHold) and clamps to [-1, 1]
   - Applies morph log-cosh waveshaping
2. If non-square (SINE, TRIANGLE):
   - Extreme slope boundary:
     - `slope >= 0.999f`: evaluated as a pure unidirectional rising sawtooth ramp (`phase.toFloat()`, 0 to 1) with instantaneous wrap to 0 at the period boundary (no reverse fall slope).
     - `slope <= 0.001f`: evaluated as a pure unidirectional falling sawtooth ramp (`(1.0 - phase).toFloat()`, 1 to 0) with instantaneous wrap to 1 at the period boundary.
     - `0.001f < slope < 0.999f`: computes raw asymmetric triangle (ramp up to 1 from [0, slope), ramp down to 0 from [slope, 1)).
   - Stretch by hold: plateau the peak by compressing transition into (1 - safeHold) of the cycle
   - safeHold is clamped to [0.0, 0.999] to prevent division by zero while enabling steep vertical edges
   - If `morph >= 0.999f`: bypasses waveshaper entirely and returns `shaped` directly (zero rounding, zero peak deceleration, exact linear segments).
   - Otherwise, apply morph via log-cosh waveshaper:
       k = lerp(1.5, 15.0, morph)         (higher k = sharper, more triangle/square-like; lower k = rounded sine)
       shaped = log(cosh(k * tri)) / (k * maxVal)
3. Output in [-1, 1]

morph = 0 → rounded sine-like corners. morph = 1 → pure linear sharp transitions with zero apex rounding. Hold defaults to 0.999 for square waves.

docs.title: RANDOM waveform
docs.text: Uses a deterministic per-cycle hash seeded from (subdivision, phaseOffset, modulator.id). Each cycle independently samples previousValue and currentValue from the hash, then interpolates between them using the hold/morph shaping above (calculateRandomWaveform in Evaluators.kt).

docs.title: Evaluators — evaluateModulator() Dispatch
docs.text:
File: cv/Evaluators.kt

evaluateModulator(mod) → Float   (range [-1, 1])

  "beatPhase"     → phase-locked to beat; RANDOM uses per-cycle hash
  "sampleAndHold" → always beat-clocked; RANDOM waveform only
  "lfo"           → full generator:
                    1. evaluate LFO 2 (mod* fields) if generatorModMode != NONE
                    2. apply PM shift to LFO 1 phase if mode == PM
                    3. evaluate LFO 1 (carrier) in TIME or BEAT clock
                    4. combine: AM → carrier*(1+lfo2*depth)
                                ADD → carrier + lfo2*depth
                                PM/NONE → carrier
  "audio_*"       → CVRegistry.get(id) — pushed from AudioEngine each frame (includes audio_flux_* onset/transient signals)
  "bpm"           → CVRegistry.get("bpm")
  "midi_cc_*"     → MidiEngine.getCcValue(channel, cc)
  else            → CVRegistry.get(id) — any registered custom source

docs.title: Reactivity Recipes
docs.text:
Shaders ship hand-written audio and beat responses ("recipes"). Once applied they are ordinary modulators; how strongly audio modulators respond is set by Audio Response, on the signals (see audio_dsp.md), not per modulator.

  • Files: a recipe is the modulators of a parameter in the shader's shipped default, src/main/resources/stock_defaults/sources/<id>.json (effects: stock_defaults/filters/<id>.json, params instead of parameters), read by StockDefaults. The file has the shape of a saved default but is sparse: parameters.<name> may set baseValue (or any other ParameterDto field) and modulators; macroBank.knobs holds the 4 knobs (label, bindings[0].parameterId = bare parameter name, optional curve). Each modulator is a ModulatorDto and must give sourceId, operator and a non-zero depth; alternates carry "bypassed": true. name (per modulator) and note (per parameter) are ignored notes. The RANDOM waveform is the sample-and-hold.
  • Applying: GeneratorDefaults.resolve (user file, then shipped file, then heuristic) lays the file over the shader's own parameters with StockDefaults.overlayParameters: named fields replace the shader's, and modulators replace the parameter's modulators with fresh copies (no ids, so envelope followers are never shared between decks; laying it over twice does not stack it). Knob start positions come from the merged base values. A saved user default replaces the shipped one wholesale. Loading a preset that stores its own parameters replaces it too.
  • Authoring rule: an LFO on a 0..1 parameter that sits at (or near) its minimum swings both ways around the set value. To sweep upward use depth = dcOffset = d/2 (range base .. base + d). StockDefaultsTest.lfoSwingsFitTheirParameters fails when any LFO swing leaves its parameter's range (the clamp would flatten part of every cycle); A MUL LFO must keep its factor 1 + dcOffset ± depth non-negative. everyShippedSourceDefaultIsValid checks parameter and knob names against the shader, one active modulator per parameter, and |depth| <= 1; everyShippedFilterDefaultTargetsRealInputs and everyShippedFilterResponseIsValid do the same for effects (swings included), everyShippedTransitionDefaultIsValid for transitions, and ISFAutoBindEngineTest checks that a stock filter gets its shipped modulators and that a saved default replaces them.
  • Random ranges (sources): the same file turns randomization on per parameter with "randomizeBase": true, "baseMin": lo, "baseMax": hi (shader units). Every stock shader source but Mandala (meta.json defaultMin/defaultMax) and Fractal Flame (genome) has them on its look parameters; Brightness, Quality, Detail-style cost controls, Reseed and most Zoom/Center inputs stay off, as do Escape Time Power and Core Size (their motion looks like an error). StockDefaultsTest.shippedRandomRangesFitTheirParameters fails when a range leaves the parameter or when a running ADD response (an LFO's dcOffset ± depth, a follower's depth) would push either end of it past the limit, so hue ranges with the stock drift stop at about 0.65. Draws go through ModulatableParameter.sampleBase (a stepped parameter draws a whole step uniformly), and DeckMorphController.update holds a stepped parameter at the nearer end (isStepped, like GenomeMorph.isDiscreteMorph). Every randomize writes through ModulatableParameter.writeBase: when a macro knob drives the base (baseDriver, set by MacroEngine.rebuildResolvedBindings from the first enabled base binding, KnobDrive.driver), the knob moves to the inverse-mapped position, otherwise the knob's tick would overwrite the roll next frame. The dice call ParametersUndo.pushRandomizeUndo, which also restores every base value and canonical knob position (a GenomeMorph source's parameters excepted).
  • Random ranges (effects and transitions): same keys in stock_defaults/filters|transitions/<id>.json, applied by FxDefaultDto.applyParametersTo (applyDto). Who rolls them: Deck.getAllRandomizableParameters includes FxChain.slotRandomizableParameters() (each enabled slot's Dry/Wet and inputs), so the deck die / deck Rand roll the deck's effects; Mixer.getAllMixerRandomizableParameters uses the same call for the Master chain. Mixer.randomizeTransition (ISFFilter.randomizeTransitionInputs: every input but progress, through randomizeBaseValue, so only randomizeBase inputs move, and writeBase moves the TRANS knob that drives them) backs the transition die and the end of Mixer.randomizeAll; transitions sit in no DeckMorphController, so Rand All jumps them rather than morphing. No range sits on an input a shipped Metaknob binding targets (StockDefaultsTest.noRandomRangeOnAMetaknobTarget): ISFFilter.applyMetaKnobBinding rewrites that base every frame, and the Metaknob means the amount, which stays the performer's. shippedFilterRandomRangesFitTheirParameters applies the source check to effects (every effect but Invert and Luma Key must have a range), everyShippedTransitionDefaultIsValid to transitions (each must have one), and transitionResponsesStayInsideTheAtRestLimits measures reach from baseMax when an input is ranged. Menu (long) inputs take ranges like stepped floats (3D Elevation mode, Film Burn tint, Linear Crossfade curve). The stock transition presets carry the ranges (shippedTransitionPresetsCarryTheShippedResponse), and so do the stock FX chains. Engine tests: FxDiceTest.
  • Effects: ISFAutoBindEngine.shippedDefault lays params over the filter and FxDefaultDto.applyParametersTo puts them on the slot, in ISFFilter init (user override by content hash, then shipped file, then heuristic). The Metaknob writes its target's base every frame, and modulators ride on top. A response on the Metaknob's own input therefore uses MUL, so a knob at zero stays off and the hits scale with the knob; ADD responses go on inputs that only show once the main amount is up (angle, fringe, flow speed). Feedback-style filters (Feedback, Fluid Smear) integrate per frame, so their depths are small. A shipped filter file is ignored when any input it names (Metaknob target or params key) is missing from the shader (a user shader that shares a stock id). Loading an FX chain applies the chain's stored slot parameters (FxChain.applyFxSlot), which replace the shipped response; inputs the chain does not store keep the filter's resolved default. The 16 stock chains in defaults/fx_chains/ (and their identical web/content/fxchains/ copies) were rebuilt so every stored input carries its effect's shipped modulators and random range, keeping the chain's own base values; StockDefaultsTest.shippedFxChainsCarryTheShippedDefaults fails on drift, a differing web copy, or an LFO swing that leaves its parameter at the chain's base.
  • Transitions: stock_defaults/transitions/<id>.json, same shape as an effect's file, usually without metaBindings (the TRANS bank's K2-K4 follow the first three float inputs, TransitionMacroSync, so the heuristic Metaknob is kept). ISFFilter.isTransition (set by ISFTransitionRegistry) picks the folder, so effect and transition ids may collide (vortex_swirl is both). Transitions carry a contentHash too, so Save as Default / Remove Saved Default (TransitionSave.drawDefaultMenuItems) use the same override store as effects. Responses only play during a fade: at progress 0 or 1 Renderer.renderMixer copies the visible deck through. Never modulate progress. An input that leaks at the ends makes the picture pop as a fade leaves rest, so StockDefaultsTest.transitionResponsesStayInsideTheAtRestLimits caps the highest value any modulator (bypassed included) can push luminous_flash.spread and film_burn.burnSpread to (0.45), in shipped defaults and in the stock presets. The presets in defaults/transitions/ (and their web/content/transitions/ copies) store full parameters, so they carry the shipped modulators themselves; shippedTransitionPresetsCarryTheShippedResponse fails when they drift. TransitionOps.isModified compares against the resolved default, so the shipped response does not mark a stock transition modified.
  • Registries hand out ISFFilter.newInstance(), which resolves the default afresh, so a default saved or removed in this session applies to the next copy; clone() (copying an instance's own values) is no longer how a stock filter or transition is created.
  • Audio levels: recipes are tuned against the AGC (audio/AudioAgc.kt), which normalises each band against its own recent peak. The web TV still uses the fixed 0.25 scale, so recipes will read quieter there until the AGC is ported.
  • Not covered yet: the stock FX chain files (they still store slots without modulators; to be regenerated from the shipped responses once those are approved). Every one of the 27 effects has a response; Invert, Luma Key and Video Strobe only bypassed ones. Pixelate's identity is size 1, not 0, so its MUL kick makes 2-pixel blocks at the off position. Fractal Flame's recipe only touches Breathe, Warp, Spin, Drift, Magnify, Exposure, Brightness, Decay, Vibrancy and Mutation, never the morph-driven xform parameters. Fluid Ink has none, and Harmonograph left the stock set.

docs.title: Serialization
docs.text:
CvModulator is @Serializable (kotlinx-serialization). The DTO conversion lives in models/PresetModels.kt:

  • ModulatorDto.toDomain() — load path; includes a one-line migration: "gen1" / "gen2" → "lfo" to silently upgrade patches saved before the rename.
  • CvModulator.toDto() — save path; field names are stable (some use @SerialName aliases, e.g. weight for depth).

Do not rename CvModulator fields without adding a corresponding @SerialName or migration in toDomain().

docs.title: ParameterResolver
docs.text:
File: parameters/ParameterResolver.kt

getAllParameterPaths(mixer) returns every (path, ModulatableParameter) pair in the mixer, using the standard hierarchical path format (e.g. "Deck A/Mandala/Lobes", "Deck A/View/Zoom", "Deck A/FB/Decay"). Used for undo snapshots and MIDI learn target resolution.

All dynamic visual sources (Mandala, plus pure-ISF sources like dynamic_spiral and icosa_h3 loaded via ISFVisualSource) inherit from DynamicVisualSource, exposing their parameter map generically as "Deck <X>/<DisplayName>/<Param>" plus "Deck <X>/<DisplayName>/Gain". (The standalone DynamicSpiral.kt and Icosahedron.kt Kotlin classes referenced by older docs were retired when those generators were migrated to pure ISF v2.0 shader files — see DECISIONS.md.)

The overall parameter categories cover: - Deck Visual Source: mapped dynamically from source.parameters (e.g. Lobes, Recipe Select, L1–L4, Thickness, Hue Offset, Hue Sweep, Depth, etc.) + Gain - Deck View: 3DMode, Zoom, RotateX, RotateY, RotateZ, Persp, DepthDim, Separation, BlendMode - Deck Feedback: Decay, Gain, Zoom, Rotate, HueShift, Blur, Chroma, Mode, Kaleido - Mixer: crossfade, xfadeSpeed, levelA, levelB, levelBG, levelPV, masterLevel, queuePrev, queueNext, bgQueuePrev, bgQueueNext, randDeckA, randDeckB, randDeckBG, randDeckPV, randAll

docs.title: Crossfade Manual Takeover & Auto-Centering
docs.text:
Files: rendering/Mixer.kt, ui/MixerPanel.kt, ui/ParametersRenderer.kt, ui/PropertiesPanel.kt, midi/MidiMappingManager.kt

The master crossfader (Mixer/crossfade) implements a performance takeover workflow: 1. Manual Takeover (Mixer.onCrossfadeManualTakeover()): Triggered when the user interacts with the crossfader slider via mouse or incoming hardware MIDI CC. - Disarms Auto-VJ (PlayQueueManager.isAutoVJEnabled = false). - Halts any active automated fade (Mixer.isAutoFading = false). - Mutes all non-MIDI modulators on the crossfader (mod.bypassed = true), ensuring immediate 1:1 manual authority. 2. Auto-Centering on Unmute (Mixer.onCrossfadeCvUnmuted()): Triggered when any CV modulator on Mixer/crossfade is unmuted or assigned. Snaps baseValue to 0.0f to ensure modulation oscillates symmetrically between decks. - Resets crossfade.baseValue = 0.0f (and baseMin/baseMax if non-randomized). - Guarantees immediate full-range, unbiased $[-1.0, +1.0]$ oscillation without waveform clipping against previous manual hold positions. Modulator dcOffset provides optional deck bias.

docs.title: Continuous Constrained Random Morphing
docs.text:
Files: rendering/MorphState.kt, rendering/Deck.kt, rendering/Mixer.kt

The randomization parameters (Mixer/randDeckA, randDeckB, randDeckBG, randDeckPV, randAll) operate as continuous morphing controllers: * Two-State Snapshot Model: Each DeckMorphController maintains two state snapshots (state0 and state1) storing base values and all active modulator parameters. * In-Place Zero-Allocation Lerping: Per-frame interpolation mutates runtime fields directly on CvModulator and ModulatableParameter without creating garbage collection pressure on the render thread. * Boundary Hysteresis: Re-rolls opposite state targets at the $0.01$ and $0.99$ normalized thresholds via a flip-flop state machine (READY_FOR_ONE / READY_FOR_ZERO). * Shortest-Path Angle/Hue Wrapping: Uses modular circular arithmetic on angle and hue parameters to prevent unwanted unwinding spins.

docs.title: Operations & Performance Tuning
docs.text: This guide covers JVM Garbage Collector tuning, real-time audio configuration across operating systems, CLI diagnostics, and troubleshooting procedures for Liquid LSD.

docs.title: Low-Latency JVM Tuning (ZGC)
docs.text:
To maintain 60+ FPS visual rendering and sub-millisecond audio analysis without frame stuttering or audio dropouts (xruns), Liquid LSD should be launched with the Z Garbage Collector (ZGC):

# Linux / Windows:
java -XX:+UseZGC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=2 --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED -jar build/libs/liquid-lsd-desktop-1.0-SNAPSHOT-all.jar

# macOS (requires -XstartOnFirstThread):
java -XstartOnFirstThread -XX:+UseZGC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=2 --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED -jar build/libs/liquid-lsd-desktop-1.0-SNAPSHOT-all.jar

docs.title: Key Flags Explained
docs.text:
• -XX:+UseZGC: Enables the Z Garbage Collector, designed for concurrent execution with pause times typically below $1\text{ ms}$.
  • -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=2: Advises the JVM GC scheduler to keep pause times under 2 milliseconds, well within 60 FPS frame boundaries ($16.6\text{ ms}$).
  • -XstartOnFirstThread (macOS only): Forces the JVM to spawn the application on the initial OS process thread (Thread 0), which is mandatory for Cocoa event polling and GLFW initialization.
  • --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED: Authorizes LWJGL/Unsafe native method access without JVM restricted method warnings on JDK 21+.

docs.title: Linux (x86_64 & ARM64)
docs.text:
• Audio Engines: Supports native PipeWire-JACK and JACK2 servers via JackClient.kt, or Java Sound system capture (JavaSoundClient.kt).
  • Real-Time Permissions: Configure /etc/security/limits.d/audio.conf to grant real-time priority: text @audio - rtprio 95 @audio - memlock unlimited

docs.title: macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon)
docs.text:
• Audio Engine: Runs out-of-the-box using JavaSoundClient.kt capturing from standard input devices (microphone, line-in, or virtual audio cables like BlackHole/Loopback). Also supports optional JACK2 for macOS.
  • Apple Silicon Native: Always run native ARM64 JVM builds (zulu17-ca-jdk17.x or bundled Adoptium ARM64) to prevent Rosetta 2 translation overhead.
  • Main Thread Event Loop: GLFW and Cocoa windowing require -XstartOnFirstThread. Launching via the provided run-mac-arm.command or run-mac-intel.command script sets this automatically and detects the bundled JRE in jre/macos-<arch>/Contents/Home/bin/java.

docs.title: Windows (x64)
docs.text:
• Audio Engine: Runs out-of-the-box via JavaSoundClient.kt system audio capture. Supports optional JACK2 for Windows with ASIO drivers.
  • GPU Performance: Ensure java.exe is assigned to "High Performance GPU" in Windows Graphics Settings.

docs.title: Audio Connectivity Diagnostics (Linux CLI)
docs.text: When diagnosing input port connections under PipeWire/JACK on Linux:

docs.title: jack_lsp
docs.text:
Lists active JACK ports and connections:

jack_lsp
jack_lsp -c    # Display active link routing

docs.title: jack_connect
docs.text:
Manually routes audio from system capture to Liquid LSD:

jack_connect system:capture_1 lsd:input_1
jack_connect system:capture_2 lsd:input_2

docs.title: pw-link (PipeWire Native)
docs.text:
pw-link -l                          # List active PipeWire links
pw-link system:capture_1 lsd:input_1 # Establish link

docs.title: 1. Startup Graphics Crash (LWJGL / OpenGL)
docs.text:
• Symptoms: Immediate crash with hs_err_pid.log.
  • Causes:
  • System GPU does not support OpenGL 3.3+.
  • GLFW/OpenGL calls executed off Thread 0.
  • Resolution:
  • Update graphics card drivers.
  • Launch with standard sandbox rules and inspect stdout for GLDebug driver error logs.

docs.title: 2. Audio Dropouts (xruns)
docs.text:
• Symptoms: Audio stuttering or console logs displaying xrun.
  • Resolution:
  • Increase JACK buffer size (from 128 to 256 or 512 frames).
  • Verify ZGC is active (-XX:+UseZGC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=2).

docs.title: 3. MIDI Controller Input Not Detected
docs.text:
• Symptoms: Moving knobs does not register in MIDI Learn mode.
  • Resolution:
  • Confirm device USB connection using lsusb (Linux) or Device Manager (Windows).
  • Verify another DAW application does not have exclusive lock access to the MIDI device.
  • Review startup console logs for MidiEngine device initialization messages.

docs.title: Preset, Queue & Notes Management Architecture
docs.text: This section documents preset serialization DTOs, async I/O worker pools, NotesManager synchronization, AutoVJ play queue orchestration, and playlist parsing in Liquid LSD.

docs.title: 1. PresetManager (PresetManager.kt)
docs.text: PresetManager.kt manages asynchronous preset saving, loading, and session persistence.

docs.title: Asynchronous I/O Executor
docs.text:
To prevent file system I/O from blocking OpenGL rendering on Thread 0, JSON serialization and file operations run on a dedicated single-threaded daemon executor:

private val presetIoExecutor: ExecutorService = Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor { runnable ->
    Thread(runnable, "PresetManager-IO").apply { isDaemon = true }
}

docs.title: Auto-Healing Preset Loader (sanitizePresetDto)
docs.text: To eliminate schema drift and prevent dirty-flag trip bugs when shaders or feedback parameters evolve: - When DeckOps.request reads a preset file on presetIoExecutor, PresetMigrator.sanitizePresetDto(dto) verifies the incoming parameter map against the target visual source's meta.json and canonical feedback parameter specifications. - Fills Missing Parameters: Injects default ParameterDto instances for any newly introduced visual source or feedback parameters (fbKaleido, Stellation, Support H, etc.). - Prunes Obsolete Keys: Strips unknown or deprecated legacy fields (e.g. sourceSelect, globalScale). - Background Auto-Save: If schema changes are detected, DeckOps immediately and quietly rewrites the updated .lsd file to disk on presetIoExecutor without blocking the main rendering thread.

docs.title: Thread-Safe Deferred Queue (DeckOps.drainOnGlThread) & Canonical Baseline Caching
docs.text: Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) generated on the background executor are offered to DeckOps' single queue. - Every frame, Thread 0 invokes DeckOps.drainOnGlThread(mixer). - It polls the queue, resets baseline parameters and applies incoming DTO parameter values to Deck instances safely on Thread 0. - Captures a canonical snapshot of the initialized deck (deck.toDto(...)) into cachedDtoA/cachedDtoB/cachedDtoBG/cachedDtoPV, ensuring that newly loaded presets start with a clean dirty flag (isDeckDirty == false). - Triggers NotesManager.syncFromDto(deckLabel, dto) to load patch and parameter notes into memory.

docs.title: Active Preset Timestamp Tracking
docs.text:
PresetManager tracks file modification timestamps for active deck presets:

var activePresetMtimeA: Long? = null
var activePresetMtimeB: Long? = null
var activePresetMtimeBG: Long? = null
var activePresetMtimePV: Long? = null
  • Populated from File.lastModified() prior to spawning background load tasks.
  • Updated upon completing successful saveDeckPresetAsync operations.
  • Consumed by DeckControlPanel to draw hover tooltips (Last saved: yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm v<version>).

docs.title: Clean First-Run & Session Lifecycle (startEmpty, loadSession)
docs.text:
• Initial App Launch: Newly instantiated decks default to isEmpty = true. When launching without a pre-existing last_session.json (or when StartupBehavior.EMPTY is active), PresetManager.startEmpty(mixer) is invoked.
  • Empty Deck State: Resets parameters across all available visual sources and 2D/3D view pipelines, clears FBO framebuffers, and leaves all deck monitors as blank black screens with the Parameters Launchpad activated ("Add Source" / "Load Preset").

docs.title: External Video Streams Excluded from Presets (ExternalVideoSource)
docs.text:
• No Preset Persistence: Decks whose active visual source is an ExternalVideoSource (Spout2 on Windows, Syphon on macOS, PipeWire on Linux) cannot be saved as .lsd presets.
  • Rationale: External video streams possess 0 procedural generator shader parameters, are ephemeral runtime inter-process handles, and can become dead "ghost" presets if saved. Direct live selection from the "External video" folder of the SRC browser guarantees stream presence and connects immediately.
  • UI & Controller Guards: The Save icon buttons in DeckControlPanel and PerformanceBrowseBay (Gen Browse) are visibly disabled (ImGui.beginDisabled) with an explanatory hover tooltip (External video streams (<source name>) cannot be saved as presets., powered by allowWhenDisabled in TooltipHelper.kt). Keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+S/Cmd+S), DeckPresetController.handleSaveDeck, DeckPresetController.saveDeckPreset, and PresetRepository.saveDeckPresetAsync early-return immediately without action.
  • Dirty Checking: PresetManager.isDeckDirty unconditionally returns false for ExternalVideoSource, avoiding spurious unsaved changes prompts when switching sources or ejecting decks.

docs.title: 2. Notes System Manager (NotesManager.kt)
docs.text:
NotesManager.kt manages memory buffers and persistence for the 3-tier Note System:

  • Global Source Notes: Stored in ~/.liquid-lsd/source-notes.json. Loaded eagerly at app startup via NotesManager.loadSourceNotes(). Saved synchronously whenever edited.
  • Deck DTO Synchronization:
  • syncFromDto(deckLabel, dto): Extracts dto.presetNotes and dto.paramNotes into deck memory maps on preset load.
  • syncToDto(deckLabel, dto): Embeds current in-memory preset and parameter notes into DeckPresetDto prior to serialization.

docs.title: DTO Schema Notes Fields (PresetModels.kt)
docs.text:
DeckPresetDto includes:

val presetNotes: String = "",
val paramNotes: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()

docs.title: 3. PlayQueueManager (PlayQueueManager.kt)
docs.text: PlayQueueManager.kt controls the volatile RAM play queue and AutoVJ set transitions.

docs.title: AutoVJ Crossfading Pipeline
docs.text: When triggerNext() is called: 1. Identifies the inactive/standby deck from mixer.crossfade.value. 2. Checks if the standby deck has a manually staged override (stagedDeckA or stagedDeckB). - If staged, Auto-VJ starts the crossfader transition (mixer.isAutoFading = true) directly to the staged preset without pulling from the queue or advancing activeIndex. - If not staged, polls the next preset file path from the queue, loads it in background via DeckOps.request(slot, DeckChange.Preset(file), LoadOrigin.QUEUE), advances activeIndex, and starts the crossfader transition.

docs.title: Manual Deck Loading & Line-Jumping Behaviors
docs.text:
• Auto-VJ OFF: Manually loading presets to any deck keeps the queue contents and activeIndex completely untouched.
  • Auto-VJ ON (Active Deck): Loading a preset into the live deck plays immediately; Auto-VJ remains ON and transitions to the standby deck on the next trigger.
  • Auto-VJ ON (Standby Deck / "Jump the Line"): Loading a preset into the inactive deck flags it as staged. The next Auto-VJ trigger crossfades to that staged visual without overwriting it, preserving the next queue track for the subsequent cycle.
  • Deck PV (Preview): Manual loading on Deck PV is independent and never affects Auto-VJ or deck staging.
  • Auto-VJ Mid-Session Arming: Turning Auto-VJ ON while presets are playing manually arms the system for the next advance trigger without causing immediate jump cuts.

docs.title: Deck Changes: DeckOps (presets/DeckOps.kt)
docs.text: Every change to what a deck holds goes through DeckOps.request(slot, change, origin); see the DeckOps entry in DECISIONS.md for the rationale. DeckChange is Source, Preset, Eject, CopyFrom, MoveFrom or SwapWith (each takes a DeckScope: SOURCE, FX or BOTH, default BOTH; the deck FX chain is not in DeckPresetDto, so it travels as an FXChainDto snapshot); LoadOrigin is MANUAL or QUEUE. - Request time (calling thread): drop a no-op Source change, run the dirty guard, then either queue the change or read the preset on presetIoExecutor and queue the result. - Dirty guard: a clean deck proceeds. MANUAL uses UITheme.manualLoadDirtyBehavior (PROMPT calls DeckOps.prompt, wired to PopupManager.requestDeckConfirm; DISCARD; AUTO_SAVE). QUEUE uses UITheme.autoVjDirtyBehavior (SKIP drops the load, AUTO_SAVE, AUTO_DISCARD). - Ordering: each accepted request is stamped with a per-slot sequence number (after the dirty prompt, before the async preset read). The drain skips an op older than the last one applied to that slot and reports it to onResult(false), so a slow preset read never overwrites a newer generator pick. - Drain (DeckOps.drainOnGlThread, once per frame in Main): for each queued change, push undo (MANUAL Source/Preset only, via DeckOps.undoSink), apply it, install the macro bank, update PresetManager bookkeeping, toast if bound knobs were replaced, then call DeckOps.postApply (the UI clears the selection and shows the SRC sub-tab after a source change).
