Once per drain: MidiMappingManager.invalidateBindings, ParameterResolver.clearCache, BroadcastEngine.notifyStateChanged. - Dirty check: DeckOps.isDirty (PresetManager.isDeckDirty delegates) compares deck.toDto with the cached DTO, plus the macro bank's labels and bindings with the signature PresetManager.setActive captured. - All UI and queue call sites go through DeckOps.request; the old PresetRepository.loadDeckPresetAsync shim and the queue managers' own handleDirtyDeck are gone. request returns false when the change was dropped (no-op, prompt cancelled, or QUEUE SKIP); queue managers then leave their position unchanged. DeckOps.wouldSkipQueueLoad lets BG skip before its dip-to-black. Callers that must act once the deck holds the change pass onResult to request: it fires once, true after the drain applied it, false if dropped, prompt-cancelled, unreadable or failed (VideoExportModal starts its export from it).

docs.title: 4. Background Queue Manager (BgQueueManager.kt)
docs.text: BgQueueManager.kt controls the background video / generator deck (Deck BG) playlist and single-deck dip-to-black transitions.

docs.title: Dip-to-Black & Modulation Pipeline
docs.text:
• Transition States: IDLE -> FADING_OUT -> FADING_IN -> IDLE.
  • Modulation & MIDI Triggers: Symmetrically modulated by Mixer/bgQueuePrev and Mixer/bgQueueNext, along with dedicated MIDI CC bindings (Global/bgQueuePrev, Global/bgQueueNext).
  • Dirty Deck Guard: Observes UITheme.autoVjDirtyBehavior (SKIP, AUTO_SAVE, AUTO_DISCARD) when transitioning or advancing on Deck BG; loads go through DeckOps with LoadOrigin.QUEUE.
  • Double-Click Playback: Double-clicking any track in BG Queue triggers immediate playback with dip-to-black (playIndex(index, mixer, withDipToBlack = true)), while double-clicking in the A/B Queue triggers standby deck load and auto-fade crossfading.

docs.title: 5. Transition Queue Manager (TransitionQueueManager.kt)
docs.text: TransitionQueueManager.kt manages the volatile Transition Queue engine (Phase 2).

docs.title: Unified Queue Item Resolution
docs.text: The transition queue supports two types of transition items seamlessly: 1. Transition Presets (.lsdtrans): Customized transition presets containing shader ID, customized parameter values (wipe angle, smoothness, glitch rate), and dry/wet settings. 2. Stock Shaders (.fs files or shader IDs): Raw transition filters loaded with standard parameter defaults.

docs.title: Auto-Advance Crossfade Hook Timing
docs.text: Auto-advance triggers inside PlayQueueManager.triggerNext(), triggerPrevious(), and playIndex() immediately before crossfading begins (mixer.targetCrossfade = ...), ensuring the new transition is loaded into mixer.transitionFilter prior to the crossfader moving.

docs.title: 6. PlaylistManager & PlaylistParser
docs.text:
• PlaylistManager.kt: Handles CRUD operations on setlists (.lsdplay files), supports reordering presets, and provides removePresetFromAllPlaylists(presetAbsPath) to clean up deleted preset file references across all playlist files on disk.
  • PlaylistParser.kt: Parses text and DTO playlist formats, using primary resolution in library/presets/ (and fallback to legacy presets/patches/) with auto-extension matching (.lsd, .json, .patch).
  • PlayQueueManager.kt / BgQueueManager.kt: Provides removeFileFromQueue(file) to remove all references to a deleted file from both queues and shift active index/shuffle state.

docs.title: 7. Factory Presets & Playlists Bundling (defaults/, First-Run Seeding)
docs.text: To ensure users never start with a blank screen on clean git clones or new releases while protecting user customizations:

docs.title: Version-Controlled Defaults (defaults/)
docs.text:
• Curated presets and playlists are kept under version control in defaults/presets/ and defaults/playlists/.
  • Syncing from Library: Developers can run ./gradlew syncDefaultsFromLibrary to copy curated .lsd presets from library/presets/ and .lsdplay setlists from library/playlists/ into defaults/.
  • Automated Packaging (prepareDefaultAssets): During build, Gradle automatically generates manifest.txt indices and packages the contents of defaults/ into the classpath (/default_presets/ and /default_playlists/).

docs.title: Safe First-Run Seeding (FileSystemManager.ensureDefaultLibrary)
docs.text:
• On first launch, FileSystemManager.ensureDefaultLibrary() checks for the presence of library/.defaults_installed.
  • If uninitialized, it extracts all bundled presets into library/presets/ and bundled playlists into library/playlists/ (skipping any existing files to protect user data), then records library/.defaults_installed.
  • Deletion Safety: If a user intentionally deletes a factory preset or playlist, the existence of library/.defaults_installed ensures it will not be resurrected on subsequent application launches.
  • First-Run Visual Autoload: When starting without a pre-existing last_session.json (and without --empty), PresetManager.loadSession automatically loads the first available starter preset (preferring 3d mandala) onto Deck A so the user is immediately greeted with live graphics.

docs.title: Factory Restore Action (FileSystemManager.restoreFactoryPresets)
docs.text:
• Users can trigger File > Restore Factory Presets... (or via the empty preset browser button) at any time.
  • Calls ensureDefaultLibrary(forceRestore = true) which re-extracts any missing factory presets and playlists without touching or overwriting custom presets.

docs.title: 8. Canonical Per-Deck Macro Banks (MacroEngine, MacroBankSerializer, SessionSerializer)
docs.text: The 19" Modular Video Rack chassis UI (rack/, rack/ui/ — faceplates, rear patch-cable view, per-unit dynamic macro banks) documented in earlier revisions of this file has been removed entirely and replaced by Performance Mode (PerformanceMatrixPanel.kt, a 4×4 knob matrix toggled with F4; see docs/user_guide/macros_and_rack.md). Historical rack design notes are kept for reference in docs/archive/modular_video_rack_proposal.md, marked retired/superseded.

docs.title: 12 Always-Resident Canonical Banks
docs.text: MacroEngine registers 12 canonical, always-resident banks by id (MacroEngine.CANONICAL_BANK_IDS): DECK_A, DECK_B, DECK_BG, DECK_PV, DECK_A_FX, DECK_B_FX, DECK_BG_FX, DECK_PV_FX, TRANS, MASTER, and MASTER_FX. MacroEngine.canonicalIdForDeckLabel(deckLabel) maps a deck label ("Deck A", "Deck B", "Deck BG", "Deck PV", "Master") to its generator bank id, falling through to TRANS for anything else, while targetBankIdFor() maps per-deck insert FX banks. Both the Performance Matrix's tabs and the Edit-row macro strip (PerformanceMacroStrip) read and write these same underlying banks — the matrix is a live control view onto them (dragging a knob live-updates MacroControl.value; editing bindings happens in the Edit-row strip and the Properties editor).

docs.title: SessionSerializer Is the Sole Bank Registrar
docs.text: SessionSerializer.kt is the only site that calls MacroEngine.registerBank(): both loadSession() (restoring session.deckMacroBanks[canonicalId] per canonical id) and startEmpty() register all 12 canonical banks on startup. There is no per-unit/dynamic bank registration anymore.

docs.title: Per-Deck Persistence (MacroBankSerializer, PresetRepository)
docs.text: Each deck's own canonical bank snapshot travels with its preset file, not just the session: - Save: PresetRepository.saveDeckPresetAsync() resolves the deck's canonical bank via MacroEngine.canonicalIdForDeckLabel(deckLabel) + MacroEngine.getBank(canonicalBankId), deep-copies it immutably with MacroBankSerializer.snapshotForPreset(), and bundles it into DeckPresetDto.macroBank. - Load: MacroBankSerializer.install(deckBank, targetBank) performs a full swap, not a merge — loading a preset is meant to load exactly the knob layout it was saved with. A null/empty deckBank (older presets, or an empty deck slot) clears the target bank to blank rather than leaving stale bindings behind. - Session-level: SessionSerializer separately bundles all 12 canonical banks into SessionStateDto.deckMacroBanks so the full macro state round-trips even without touching individual preset files.

docs.title: 9. FX Presets, Playlists & Live Queues
docs.text: The [ FX ] Library view mode (see docs/developer/ui.md §8 and docs/user_guide/presets_and_library.md) is backed by its own preset/queue manager family, parallel to but independent from the .lsd preset managers documented above.

docs.title: One Mutation Path: FxOps.kt
docs.text:
FxOps.kt is the single entry point for changing what's loaded in any FxChain (the four decks' fxChain and Mixer.masterFxChain): loadChain, applyChain, clearChain, setSlotFilter, loadSlot, applySlot, clearSlot, and applyItem (the deterministic playlist/queue path: a .lsdfxchain replaces the chain, a .lsdfx becomes slot 1 of an otherwise empty chain). It is used by the Perform rows, Edit, the FX browser and toolbar, FX playlists, and both live FX queues.

Every op is queued and applied in FxOps.drainOnGlThread(mixer), called once per frame from the render loop right after DeckOps.drainOnGlThread. That matters because async file loads complete on PresetManager.presetIoExecutor: replacing a slot disposes the old ISFFilter (deleting its GL framebuffers), which must happen on the GL thread, and swapping FxChain.slots mid-frame would race the renderer. After each op, FxMacroSync.syncFor() refreshes that chain's FX row knobs. Never mutate FxChain.slots directly from a CompletableFuture callback.

docs.title: FX Chains Are Session State, Not Preset State
docs.text: Deck presets (.lsd, DeckPresetDto) carry no FX. Every chain is persisted in the session instead: MixerDto.masterFxChain, deckAFxChain, deckBFxChain, deckBGFxChain, deckPVFxChain. On a fresh session, Mixer.loadDefaultFxChains() seeds all five from bundled .lsdfxchain files.

docs.title: FXQueueManager.kt / FXBgQueueManager.kt
docs.text: Mirror PlayQueueManager.kt / BgQueueManager.kt but operate on FX assets instead of visual presets: - Volatile RAM queue: CopyOnWriteArrayList<File> of .lsdfx / .lsdfxchain / .lsdfxplay entries, with isRepeatEnabled, isShuffleEnabled, activeIndex, and playbackHistory for shuffle back-stepping (initializeShuffle(), playedIndices). - FXQueueManager applies deterministically to the crossfader-active deck (A or B); FXBgQueueManager drives Deck BG independently, same as the non-FX background queue. - UI: FXQueueActionsPanel.kt (A/B FX Queue) and FXBgQueueActionsPanel.kt (BG FX Queue), two of the five columns of the Library's Queues tab (ui/browser/QueuesPane.kt). - Export Queue to Playlist: Both managers support instantly exporting the current live queue to a new .lsdfxplay playlist file (BrowserPopupHandler.kt "Export Live FX Queue (A/B) as Playlist" / "Export Background FX Queue as Playlist" popups).

docs.title: FX Playlists (.lsdfxplay)
docs.text: FXPresetModels.kt defines FXPlaylistDto, an ordered list of FX asset paths persisted by PresetRepository and FileSystemManager under library/fx_playlists/. A playlist is an entry in the FX tab's folder tree (BrowserPane): selecting it lists its rows, which support drag-and-drop insertion, reordering, double-click application and context-menu actions; the list edits are ui/browser/PlaylistEdit.kt (PlaylistItems), shared with transition playlists. The old column editors (PlaylistEditorPanel, FXPlaylistEditorPanel) are gone.

docs.title: FXBrowserPanel.kt
docs.text: Unifies the formerly separate FXPresetListPanel (single .lsdfx presets) and FXChainListPanel (.lsdfxchain chains) into the Library's FX tab with ISF stock filters, saved singles, and saved chains, tier badges, and an All / Stock / Singles / Chains filter menu. Stock (built-in ISF) filters and presets load into any deck's or Master's 3-slot FX chain via FxOps; saved presets and chains can additionally be added to FX playlists and live FX queues. "Load to" submenus for stock/single items let you target any of the 3 slots, while chains load directly. (The .lsdfxbank format was removed along with FxBank: Master FX is a plain FxChain now.)

docs.title: FX Metaknob / Super Knob Persistence
docs.text: FXSlotDto (in PresetModels.kt) carries metaKnob: ParameterDto?, metaBinding: FxMetaBindingDto? (legacy singular), metaBindings: List<FxMetaBindingDto>? (each with target, range, curve, stepCount, linkMode, invert, enabled) and knobLayout: List<String>? (focus-knob parameter order; null = authored order; names the shader lacks are dropped on load). FxDefaultDto (Save as Default, library/isf_overrides/<hash>.json) carries the same metaBindings and knobLayout (see rendering/isf/FxMetaBinding.kt); FXChainDto carries superKnob: ParameterDto? and slotSuperKnobLink: List<Boolean>?. Both are baked at save time — a saved slot/chain preset always restores the exact Metaknob binding/position it had when saved, even if ISFAutoBindEngine's resolution for that shader (curated table, or a since-changed user override under library/isf_overrides/) has since changed. There is no live re-resolution path from a saved preset; re-save (or an explicit future "re-resolve" UI action) is required to pick up a changed binding.

docs.title: FX Chain Dirty Tracking Criteria
docs.text: FxChain.isDirty() / computeIsDirty() tracks unsaved structural edits to an FX chain without falsely triggering during live performance knob sweeps. - Criteria: An FX chain is marked dirty (• indicator on the chain name button and Alert-colored Save button) only if: 1. An effect is added, removed, or replaced in any slot (filter ID mismatch against the loaded baseline). 2. The ordering of effects across slots is altered (e.g. slots swapped or moved). - Performance Parameter Immunity: Continuous movements of the Superknob, linked slot Metaknobs, Dry/Wet blends, and individual effect parameters do not mark an FX chain as dirty.

docs.title: OpenGL Rendering Pipeline & Visual Sources
docs.text: This document details the OpenGL graphics rendering pipeline, Framebuffer Object (FBO) ping-pong architecture, shader management, SourceDocRegistry, and visual source math in Liquid LSD.

docs.title: Per-Deck FX Chain & ISF Transition Pipeline
docs.text:
Following the 100% ISF Pipeline Migration (see ARCHITECTURE.md §3), each Deck's render path is a single generator pass into cleanFBO followed by a chain of 3 modular ISF FX slots. There is no separate hardcoded 3D-projection pass and no Deck-level ping-pong feedback loop — both are now ordinary ISF filters a performer loads into any FX slot (default_filters/3d_elevation.fs, default_filters/feedback.fs). The legacy tri_planar.*/tetra_kaleido.* shaders and the old Deck.fbGain/fbDecay/etc.-driven feedback.frag ping-pong stage were retired from the render path in Phase 6 and their files have since been deleted from src/main/resources/shaders/. The matching deck-level fb* and 3D-view parameters (view3DMode, viewRotateX/Y, viewPersp, ...) are gone from Deck too: old presets may still carry them under feedbackParameters / viewParameters; DeckPresetDto no longer has a feedbackParameters field, so that key is dropped on load (unknown keys are ignored), and the dead viewParameters keys are never read or written. Only viewZoom and viewRotateZ remain.

Source instances. VisualSourceRegistry holds the master of each source (it owns the shader). A deck holds one clone, made fresh from the registry on every pick or preset load (VisualSourceRegistry.find); setting Deck.source disposes the clone it replaces. A clone's dispose() only frees its own buffers (feedback FBOs, ISF pass targets, the flame engine, an external-video receiver), and all of them are re-created on the next render, so undo can put a disposed clone back.

[VisualSource (Mandala / DynamicVisualSource / ISFVisualSource / ExternalVideoSource)]
                 │
                 ▼
     [Renderer.render()] — 2D View Pass: uZoom / uRotateZ applied directly in vertex space
     (skipped for native-3D sources — Renderer.renderDeck() forces zoom=1.0/rotateZ=0.0
     when deck.source.is3D, since those sources handle their own camera transform)
                 │
                 ▼
            [deck.cleanFBO]  (Composited clean source frame)
                 │
                 ▼
     [FX Slot 1] (deck.fxSlots[0] — any ISF filter: Kaleidoscope, Radial Blur,
                  RGB Split, Polar Tunnel, Color Levels, Gradient Map, Bloom, Glitch, Mirror, Feedback, etc.)
                 │
                 ▼
     [FX Slot 2] (deck.fxSlots[1])
                 │
                 ▼
     [FX Slot 3] (deck.fxSlots[2])
                 │
                 ▼
     [Mixer.kt Transition Stage] — Renderer.renderMixer()
     [mixer.transitionFilter (ISF)] -> [mixer.blendFBO] -> [mixer.frag composite over Deck BG]
                 │
                 ▼
            [mixer.masterFBO] ──► Screen

docs.title: Execution Steps
docs.text:
1. Source Render & View Stage (Renderer.render() / Renderer.renderDeck()):
  2. 2D Sources (!source.is3D): The active 2D source renders directly into cleanFBO via blit.vert (or the source's own multi-pass topology), passing uZoom (deck.viewZoom), uRotateZ (deck.viewRotateZ), and uAspectRatio directly into the vertex shader.
  3. Native 3D Sources (source.is3D == true): e.g. icosa_h3, hyper_mesh. These handle their own rotation (Rotate X/Y/Z) and camera zoom internally and render straight into cleanFBO; renderDeck() forces the Deck's viewZoom/viewRotateZ to identity (1.0/0.0) for these sources rather than routing through a separate projection FBO.
  4. External Video Ingest Sources (ExternalVideoSource): Ingest live video streams from external applications via Spout2 (Windows), Syphon (macOS), or PipeWire 0.3 (Linux) (PipeWireReceiverImpl in TextureReceiver.kt and fetchPipeWireStreams() in ExternalVideoDiscovery.kt). Renderer.renderExternalVideoSource() blits the active incoming texture (currentTextureId) via view2DShader straight into cleanFBO, applying the same uZoom/uRotateZ/uAspectRatio uniforms as 2D sources.
  5. Persistent-history generators: sources with hasFeedback == true (e.g. trail-based generators like Dynamic Spiral) maintain their own fb1/fb2 ping-pong pair directly on the DynamicVisualSource instance (not on Deck), lazily (re)allocated by Renderer.render() to match cleanFBO's dimensions.
  6. FX Slot Chain (Serial Processing Stage): Renderer.renderDeck() loops over deck.fxSlots (FxChain.SLOT_COUNT = 3). For each enabled slot with dryWet > 0.0, it renders the running texture (starting from cleanFBO.texture) through that slot's ISFFilter into the chain's per-slot buffer, then blends dry (previous stage's output) against wet (this stage's output) via glBlendColor(..., 1.0 - dryWet) when dryWet < 1.0. The final enabled slot's texture becomes the deck's effective output (Deck.getOutputTexture()); if no slots are enabled, cleanFBO passes through unchanged.
  7. Mixer Transition & Compositing (Renderer.renderMixer()): Deck A and Deck B's effective output textures feed the active ISF transition filter (mixer.transitionFilter — Renderer.kt caches a linear_crossfade instance so an unassigned transition never allocates/disposes filters mid-frame) into mixer.blendFBO, then a composite pass blends that over Deck BG with channel levels, bloom, and master alpha into mixer.masterFBO. With the crossfader fully on one side (progress exactly 0 or 1, Renderer.restingTexture) the transition pass is skipped and that deck's texture is copied into blendFBO instead, so the resting picture is exact and costs one copy. Transition parameters and their modulators keep updating, so a fade starts from their current values.

docs.title: Dynamic Render Resolution & Viewport Scaling
docs.text:
Liquid LSD supports arbitrary user-defined render resolutions and aspect ratios (e.g. 1080p, 720p, 540p, 4K, 4:3 UXGA 1600x1200, 1:1 Square 800x800, or Custom) configured via UITheme:

  • Dynamic Pipeline Resizing: Mixer.resize(width, height) and Deck.resize(width, height) reallocate cleanFBO and masterFBO on the main OpenGL thread without interrupting playback or dropping preset states; each DynamicVisualSource's own persistent-history fb1/fb2 pair (see above) is disposed and lazily recreated on next render rather than eagerly resized.
  • Shader Aspect Awareness: Generative fragment shaders evaluate float aspect = uResolution.x / uResolution.y; from targetFBO dimensions, rendering undistorted geometry across any aspect ratio.
  • Display Scaling with ViewportHelper: ViewportHelper.kt computes letterbox, pillarbox, and fill coordinates for secondary monitor outputs and background video blits:
  • FIT: Preserves exact content aspect ratio with letterboxing or pillarboxing.
  • FILL: Centers and crops edges to completely fill the target screen.
  • STRETCH: Stretches content to fill the target viewport.
  • Aspect-Adaptive UI Previews: MixerLayoutCalculator dynamically adjusts Deck A, Deck B, Deck PV, and Master preview monitor heights to match the active render aspect ratio.

docs.title: FBO-Count & GPU-Memory Telemetry
docs.text:
FBO.kt's companion object tracks every live FBO instance app-wide in a ConcurrentHashMap<framebufferId, estimatedByteSize>, populated on construction and cleared on dispose(). Byte size is format-aware (GL_RGBA8 = 4 bytes/px, GL_RGBA16F = 8, GL_RGBA32F = 16). This is exposed as PerformanceStats.fboCount / PerformanceStats.fboMemoryMB and rendered in the menu bar telemetry HUD as FBO: N (XMB) (MenuBar.kt), covering all live FBOs in the core render pipeline (cleanFBO, masterFBO, etc.) app-wide. This instrumentation was added deliberately before any pooled FBO allocator, so a real GPU-memory bottleneck would show up in this readout first rather than being addressed speculatively.

The 19" Modular Video Rack chassis UI (rack/, rack/ui/), including its RackMicroMonitor confidence-preview downscaling and RackPipeline ping-pong stage buffers, was removed when the workspace was replaced by the Perform view (PerformanceMatrixPanel.kt); see docs/archive/modular_video_rack_proposal.md for retired design history.

docs.title: Source Documentation Registry (SourceDocRegistry.kt)
docs.text:
SourceDocRegistry.kt is an immutable singleton repository storing documentation for visual sources and parameters:

  • Source Descriptions: sourceDescriptions: Map<String, String> keyed by sourceId. Covers the currently-bundled built-in engines (mandala, dynamic_spiral, icosa_h3) plus stale dead-code entries (colors, gyroid, chladni, attractor_feedback, hyper_mesh, hyper_slice) left over from the legacy-source removal (see below) that no VisualSourceRegistry entry resolves to anymore — harmless (map lookups simply never hit them) but worth pruning next time this file is touched.
  • Parameter Descriptions: paramDescriptions: Map<String, String> keyed by "<sourceId>/<paramName>", "feedback/<paramName>", or "mixer/<paramName>".
  • UI Lookup API: Surfaced by ParametersRenderer and DeckControlPanel to draw rich tooltips.

docs.title: Pluggable Dynamic Visual Sources (VisualSourceRegistry.kt)
docs.text:
Beyond hardcoded generators, the engine loads dynamic shaders from library/sources/:

  • VisualSourceRegistry: Scans subfolders on startup, parses meta.json, compiles shader.frag against standard vertex shaders (blit.vert), and builds DynamicVisualSource templates.
  • Shader Ownership: The master template in VisualSourceRegistry owns the OpenGL shader program (ownsShader = true). Deck clones share shader program handles safely (ownsShader = false) to eliminate duplicate compilation overhead.
  • Polymorphic Draw Topology: Visual source rendering in Renderer.render() is fully polymorphic with zero source-type checks (is Mandala, is HyperMesh). Each visual generator overrides DynamicVisualSource.drawTopology():
  • Default: Renders a fullscreen quad via Geometry.drawFullscreenQuad().
  • Mandala: Binds ribbon VAO and draws triangle strips via glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP, 0, (POINTS + 1) * 2).
  • HyperMesh: Binds 4D polychoron strut and node VAOs and renders indexed triangles via glDrawElements(GL_TRIANGLES, ...).
  • Error Fallbacks: If custom GLSL fails compilation, a fallback checkerboard shader is bound so the application avoids crashing.

docs.title: $H_3$ Coxeter Icosahedral Raymarcher (icosa_h3)
docs.text:
The icosa_h3 visual source is a single ISF shader (icosa_h3.fs) that combines what were previously three separate visual sources (icosa_dodeca, icosahedron, icosa-v3) into one $H_3$ Coxeter Reflection Group Iterated Function System (IFS) raymarcher. It evaluates two independent stellation families sharing the same folded-chamber substrate and crossfades between them with the Spike Mode parameter, so the whole design space of the three predecessors is reachable from one shader:

  • Smooth duality-morph family (from icosa_dodeca): a continuous 4-phase Icosahedron ↔ Dodecahedron ↔ Great Stellated Dodecahedron ↔ Great Icosahedron cycle, with truncation/cantellation duals.
  • Spike + blocker stellation CSG (from icosa-v3): an independently-phased pole sweep that extrudes pyramid spikes and blunts their tips with a chopping plane.
  • The brute-force 60-plane orbit approach of the original icosahedron source (which required Icosahedron.kt to generate the plane orbit on the CPU every frame) was dropped in favor of the GPU-only domain-folding technique below — it only ever covered the icosahedron's own stellations, not the icosahedron/dodecahedron duality, and its CPU dependency doesn't fit the ISF model.

docs.title: 1. Fundamental Mirror Planes
docs.text: The $H_3$ Coxeter group (icosahedral symmetry $I_h$, order 120) is defined by three normalized mirror planes with dihedral angles $(\pi/5, \pi/3, \pi/2)$: $$n_0 = (1, 0, 0)$$ $$n_1 = \left(-\frac{\phi}{2}, -\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2\phi}\right)$$ $$n_2 = (0, 1, 0)$$ where $\phi = \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2} \approx 1.61803398875$.

docs.title: 2. Chamber Vertices & Slerp Generator $v(t)$
docs.text:
The corners of the fundamental spherical triangle represent the primary symmetry axes: - 3-Fold Axis $C_3$ (Icosahedron face normal / Dodecahedron vertex): $C_3 = \text{normalize}(n_1 \times n_2) = \left(\frac{\phi - 1}{\sqrt{3}}, 0, \frac{\phi}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$ - 5-Fold Axis $C_5$ (Dodecahedron face normal / Icosahedron vertex): $C_5 = \text{normalize}(n_0 \times n_1) = \left(0, \frac{1}{\sqrt{\phi + 2}}, \frac{\phi}{\sqrt{\phi + 2}}\right)$ - 2-Fold Axis $C_2$ (Edge midpoint): $C_2 = (0, 0, 1)$

The generator vector $v(t)$ continuously slerps between $C_3$ and $C_5$: $$v(t) = \frac{\sin((1-t)\Omega)}{\sin\Omega} C_3 + \frac{\sin(t\Omega)}{\sin\Omega} C_5,\quad \Omega = \arccos(C_3 \cdot C_5) \approx 0.652358\text{ rad}$$

docs.title: 3. Kaleidoscopic Symmetry Folding
docs.text:
Any raymarching sample point $p \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is folded iteratively into the fundamental chamber:

vec3 foldH3(vec3 p) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i) {
        p -= 2.0 * min(0.0, dot(p, n0)) * n0;
        p -= 2.0 * min(0.0, dot(p, n1)) * n1;
        p -= 2.0 * min(0.0, dot(p, n2)) * n2;
    }
    return p;
}

docs.title: 4. Signed Distance Field & Continuous Stellation Plane Tilting
docs.text:
In folded chamber space ($p' = \text{foldH3}(p)$), the generator vector $v(t)$ defines the face normal. Its adjacent reflection normal vector $v_{\text{adj}}(t)$ (derived from $C_3$ reflected across $n_0$ and $C_5$ reflected across $n_2$) defines the sloping stellation facet: $$C_3^{\text{adj}} = (-C_3.x, 0, C_3.z),\quad C_5^{\text{adj}} = (0, -C_5.y, C_5.z)$$ $$v_{\text{adj}}(t) = \text{slerp}(C_3^{\text{adj}}, C_5^{\text{adj}}, t)$$

The continuous stellation plane vector $v_{\text{morph}}$ tilts continuously between the flat face $v(t)$ at $s=0$ and the Kepler-Poinsot star facets $v_{\text{adj}}(t)$ at $s=1$: $$v_{\text{morph}} = \text{normalize}(\text{mix}(v(t), v_{\text{adj}}(t), s))$$ $$SDF(p) = p' \cdot v_{\text{morph}} - h$$

  • Convex Core ($s=0$): Evaluates flat Platonic/Archimedean faces.
  • Kepler-Poinsot Stellations ($s=1$): Tilts face planes into intersecting star pyramids with exact sharp apexes at $r = h / (v \cdot v_{\text{adj}})$.
  • Smooth Emergence ($0 < s < 1$): Spikes grow out of the face centers with continuous facet tilting.

docs.title: 5. Independent Spike + Blocker Stellation CSG
docs.text: A second stellation family shares the same foldH3 substrate but is driven independently of Morph: Spike Phase sweeps a pole corePole around the $C_3$–$C_5$ arc (via a general slerpArc(p0, p1, t) valid for $t$ outside $[0,1]$, unlike the fixed-angle $v(t)$ generator above), which is then reflected across $n_0$ and $n_2$ to obtain two adjacent spike poles. Spike Sharpness tilts each spike pole from its flat core position toward the reflected (fully extruded) position, and the two resulting half-spaces are intersected (max) to form the spike shape. A third blockerPole — the same arc sampled one phase-step ahead — chops the spike tips off, with Blocker Size controlling how much survives: $$SDF_{\text{spike}}(p) = \max\big(\max(d_{\text{spike1}}, d_{\text{spike2}}),\ d_{\text{blocker}}\big)$$ This is the same domain-folded CSG technique as the old icosa-v3 source (evaluating only a handful of dot products instead of brute-forcing 60 planes), now running as one branch of mapSDF alongside the duality-morph family above.

docs.title: 6. Family Crossfade & Facet-Aware Coloring
docs.text: Spike Mode linearly crossfades the two families' SDF values, edge-seam distances, and a per-family "which half-space is dominant" index (mix(dSmooth, dSpikeFinal, mode), etc.), producing a continuous blend between the smooth duality morph and the spiky CSG rather than a hard switch between two shaders. The dominant-half-space index feeds a dedicated Color Mode = 0 ("Facet Family") coloring path that assigns each active facet family its own stable hue, on top of the inherited Chamber Sectors / Depth Gradient / Normal Spectrum modes and a new animated Fresnel-driven Iridescent mode.

docs.title: 7. Multi-Layer Crystal Raymarching
docs.text:
• Under-Relaxation: Ray steps use a conservative $0.5\times$ scaling factor on miss (t += dist * 0.5), tuned to stay stable on the acute needle ridges the spike family can produce.
  • Front-to-Back Transparency: Steps through transparent outer faces (Opacity 0.6–0.8) to accumulate color and reveal inner self-intersecting facets without depth sorting.

docs.title: Heavy Fractal Raymarchers (mandelbox, kifs, mandelbulb, pseudo_kleinian, apollonian)
docs.text:
Five stock ISF generators (library/sources/<id>/<id>.fs, identical copy in src/main/resources/default_sources/) share one structure with icosa_h3 and gyroid_hyperspace: a distance-estimated raymarch, LSD_COST 3, is3D with their own Zoom/RotateX/Y/Z, orbit-trap palettes selected by ColorMode, a tetrahedral-difference normal, a small AO tap set and a signed FlightSpeed. There is no include mechanism, so each file inlines its helpers. They target an NVIDIA RTX A2000 as the floor and are desktop only: GLSL 3.30 core, no web/sync_manifest.json entry. Per-source derivations and known issues are in .planning/heavy-sources-notes/<id>.md.

Every one exposes a normalised Quality input that remaps to live loop counts under constant caps (for (i = 0; i < MAX; i++) { if (i >= n) break; }), so Quality trades fidelity for speed during a set.

Source Algorithm Constant caps Default Quality: steps / iterations / AO taps mandelbox Box fold + sphere fold + scale, running-derivative DE (z <- s * sphereFold(boxFold(z)) + c, DE = norm(z) / dr) march 128, fold 12, AO 4 0.5: 88 / 9 / 2 (range 48-128 / 6-12 / 0-4) kifs Fold into a fundamental domain, scale about the IFS fixed vertex, per-iteration rotation, base-shape SDF / s^n; four constructions via SurfaceType march 112, fold 12, AO 4 0.5: 80 / 9 / 2 (range 48-112 / 5-12 / 0-4) mandelbulb Triplex power map z^n + c in spherical coordinates, DE 0.5 log(r) r / dr; analytic bounding sphere skips misses march 80, iter 10, AO 4 0.5: 64 / 8 / 3 (range 48-80 / 6-10 / 2-4) pseudo_kleinian Periodic triangle-wave slab fold, sphere inversion scale capped at kmax, offset, DE (norm(p) - core) / dr march 120, iter 12, AO 4 0.33: 72 / 8 / 2 (range 48-120 / 6-12 / 1-4) apollonian Cell wrap, optional y twist, capped sphere inversion, same DE form march 120, iter 12, AO 4 0.08: 54 / 6 / 1 (range 48-120 / 6-12 / 1-4)

escape_time (2D, below) is a sixth heavy generator in the same registry but is not a raymarcher.

Worst case per pixel is steps x iterations estimator passes (for example 88 x 9 = 792 for the Mandelbox default, 1536 at Quality 1); rays that miss or hit early cost far less. No shader uses textures, float buffers or extra passes.

Measured cost (RTX A2000 Laptop GPU via PRIME offload, GL_RENDERER confirmed, 1920x1080, hidden GL 3.3 context, offscreen RGBA8, glFinish-timed average of several frames; indicative only, GPU clocks not locked, single deck, no compositing):

Source Default Quality 1 Quality 0 Notes mandelbox 7.7 ms 8.4 ms 5.0 ms closest-camera, Zoom 1, Quality 1 corners 14 to 42 ms kifs 4.8 ms 5.7 ms 2.1 ms corners not searched mandelbulb 5.2 ms 5.7 ms 4.5 ms corners not searched pseudo_kleinian about 11.2 ms 14.8 ms 8.1 ms everything-max corner 27.7 ms apollonian 8.7 ms 27.3 ms 7.8 ms the earlier default 0.25 cost 15.5 ms; lowered to 0.08 for two-deck headroom

escape_time (library/sources/escape_time/escape_time.fs): 2D escape-time iteration z <- z^p + k (Julia, Burning Ship Julia with abs before the power, Mandelbrot with z0 = 0) or relaxed Newton on z^3 - 1. Iteration cap Detail 48 to 400 under a constant MAX_IT; escape radius 256 for smooth colouring n + 1 - log(log|z|)/log(p); Newton stops within 1e-5 of a root. Detail above 0.75 adds 2x2 supersampling. It supplies its own Zoom (0.3x to 3000x), CenterX/Y and Rotation; fp32 limits useful magnification to about 1e3 to 1e4. Measured on the RTX A2000 Laptop GPU at 1080p: Julia 0.4 ms, Newton 0.9 ms, Mandelbrot 1.5 ms at the default Detail, Julia at Detail 1 (with antialiasing) 1.2 ms; interior-heavy deep views cost far more because every pixel runs the full cap.

Defaults sit inside a 60 fps budget on one deck; two heavy decks plus a crossfade is the case to watch. Zooming in until every pixel hits, or an extreme parameter set, is what pushes a source toward 30 fps. The stock audit (StockGpuCostAuditTest) asserts all five carry LSD_COST 3; it does not measure frame time.

Volume and simulation generators (nebula_volume, reaction_diffusion, fluid_ink, lenia). nebula_volume is a raymarched emission/absorption volume (LSD_COST 3, is3D, own camera): domain-warped ridged value-noise fbm with a 0 to 4 tap light march, interleaved-gradient-noise jitter and empty-space leaping, caps 72 view steps, 4 light taps and 5 octaves (default about 28 steps, 2 taps, 2 octaves). The other three are the first stock generators to use PASSES: persistent FLOAT ping-pong grids of fixed size, so cost does not depend on output resolution. Each sim sub-step is its own pass with its own persistent target (rdA..rdD, lnA..lnD, prs1..prs4), because two passes sharing one target would share one slot and resizePassFBOs would allocate it twice. A persistent target reads the most recently written buffer, so chained targets see the same frame's output. Buffers are zeroed on allocation and on resize, so each sim re-seeds itself when its state is empty and never relies on FRAMEINDEX. reaction_diffusion is 512 x 512 with 4 sub-steps per frame (Gray-Scott, 9-point Laplacian, Du*dt capped at 1.2), fluid_ink is 384 x 384 with an RK2 semi-Lagrangian velocity pass, 4 Jacobi pressure passes (warm-started across frames) and a dye pass, and lenia is 256 x 256 with 4 steps per frame and a 27 x 27 tap window at most. Steps are per frame, not TIMEDELTA-scaled, so the simulations run faster at higher frame rates. The three sims are declared LSD_COST 2 and show no badge. Measured on the RTX A2000 Laptop GPU at 1080p, default settings: reaction_diffusion about 0.5 ms, fluid_ink about 0.7 ms, lenia about 2 ms, nebula_volume about 17 ms (Quality 1, Detail 4, Lighting 1 about 68 ms). Known limitation: lenia does not reproduce the published gliding creatures; it makes bubbles, rings and stripes.

Light generators (quasicrystal, thin_film, tunnel_scenes, video_feedback, hyperbolic_tiling). These target integrated graphics and carry no LSD_COST tag: the absence of the browser triangle is the signal. All are 2D, so the deck View zoom and rotate apply. Four are single pass with no texture reads and a constant-bound loop (quasicrystal 8 gratings, thin_film 4 octaves, tunnel_scenes 3 layers, hyperbolic_tiling 16 folds) with a Quality input that lowers the cap. video_feedback is the only multipass one: a persistent 512 x 512 RGBA8 state pass plus a bilinear display pass, re-seeding itself when the buffer is empty. Measured on an Intel UHD (TGL GT1) at 1080p, one deck, defaults: about 3 to 4 ms for the single-pass sources (thin_film about 6 ms, tunnel_scenes wormhole about 5 ms) and 2 to 4 ms for video_feedback. All five are also web sources (web/sync_manifest.json), transpiled to GLSL ES 3.00 by syncWeb. Time-driven phases come from host-integrated LSD_PHASES uniforms (section 6) and are wrapped (mod(SpeedPhase * k, period)) so they stay precise in long sessions.

More light generators (cyclic_ca, metaballs, wave_ripples, aurora_ribbons, isometric_voxels, halftone_matrix, kali_set, girih_stars, glitch_blocks, voronoi_cells). Same rules as above: no LSD_COST, web sources, a Quality input. Only cyclic_ca is multipass: four chained persistent 256 x 256 RGBA8 sub-step passes plus a display pass, reseeding when the grid is empty (never FRAMEINDEX), with the generation rate derived from TIMEDELTA and capped at 4 per frame. Measured at 1080p on the Intel UHD (TGL GT1) when the GPU was otherwise idle, roughly 2x the figures in the first batch because the machine was running slower: cyclic_ca 4 to 5 ms, voronoi_cells 7 to 9, glitch_blocks 6 to 9, kali_set 10, girih_stars 9 to 12, isometric_voxels 10 to 14, wave_ripples 10 to 16, aurora_ribbons 14 to 20, halftone_matrix 7 to 17; metaballs and harmonograph were 19 to 27 and 22 to 26 before optimisation. harmonograph now evaluates its 65 curve vertices once into a 65 x 2 float strip (pass 0; row 1 holds a bounding box per chunk of 8 segments) and the display pass skips chunks outside the glow radius (about 7 ms average). metaballs uses a monotonic dome height with a flat-top attenuation for its shading and a default Quality of 0.3 (single sample, about 11 ms); Quality of 0.5 or more turns on 2 x 2 antialiasing, which quadruples the field evaluations.

Stock registration touchpoints for a new stock source: VisualSourceRegistry.DEFAULT_SOURCE_IDS, a shipped default src/main/resources/stock_defaults/sources/<id>.json (knobs and audio response) + GeneratorDefaultsTest.stockInputNames, SourceDocRegistry (description plus "<id>/<Param>" tooltips), the StockGpuCostAuditTest heavy allowlist, Source3DModeTest, the licence and provenance rows, and the user-guide pages. Both .fs trees must be identical (diff -rq library/sources src/main/resources/default_sources).

docs.title: Video Recording & Deterministic Offline Studio
docs.text: Liquid LSD includes both a zero-lag live capture pipeline and a sample-accurate offline rendering studio in the llm.slop.liquidlsd.export package.

docs.title: 1. Zero-Copy DMA Readback (PboReadbackPipeline)
docs.text:
• Ping-Pong PBO Ring Buffer: Uses two GL_PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER objects. While PBO $A$ is mapped into CPU memory via glMapBufferRange(GL_READ_ONLY), PBO $B$ executes an asynchronous GPU DMA transfer via glReadPixels(..., 0).
  • Direct Memory Copy: Frame transfers use direct C-pointer block copies (MemoryUtil.memCopy) to eliminate CPU overhead on Thread 0. Vertical flipping is delegated to the FFmpeg filter graph (-vf vflip).

docs.title: 2. Live Session Recording (RealtimeRecorder)
docs.text:
• Background Frame Queue: Bounded ArrayBlockingQueue<ByteBuffer>(10) prevents frame capture from stalling the main OpenGL render loop. If disk I/O stalls, frames are cleanly dropped with a live HUD counter and percentage indicator.
  • Lock-Free Zero-Allocation Audio Tapping: Live audio blocks from AudioEngine.processAudio are captured into a pre-allocated pool of AudioBlock instances via a lock-free, wait-free Single-Producer Single-Consumer (SpscQueue) ring buffer without heap allocations or mutex acquisitions on the real-time audio thread. Audio is written to a temporary PCM WAV file on a background worker thread and losslessly remuxed with FFmpeg (-c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 320k) upon stopping.
  • Live REC Tally Badge: Pulsing red record badge overlaid directly on the master preview monitor with elapsed timer (REC MM:SS).

docs.title: 3. Deterministic Time Virtualization (TimeSource)
docs.text:
• Central Time Authority: All shaders (uTime), CVRegistry evaluators, DynamicSpiral, and Mixer query TimeSource.getTimeSec() and TimeSource.getTimeNanos().
  • Offline Simulation Clock: During OfflineRenderStudio passes, TimeSource.setSimulatedTime(subFrameTimeSec, subFrameDt) is set before stepping DSP analysis and deck rendering, guaranteeing sample-accurate synchronization between audio frequencies and visual animations regardless of rendering speed.

docs.title: 4. Offline Render Studio (OfflineRenderStudio)
docs.text:
• Frame-Accurate Stepping: Iterates frame-by-frame on Thread 0 while yielding to GLFW events.
  • Multi-Pass Motion Blur (AccumulationBuffer): Supports up to 8x temporal super-sampling, blending sub-frame passes to generate cinematic motion blur.
  • Automatic Encoder Prioritization & Fallback: Automatically probes and prioritizes hardware encoders (h264_nvenc, h264_qsv) with transparent fallback to software encoders (libx264, libx265, prores_ks).

docs.title: Desktop-to-Web Shader & Asset Synchronization
docs.text: To ensure continuous parity between desktop visual sources and the browser-based WebGL2 visualizer (web/), an automated synchronization subsystem tracks file changes and translates shader dialects.

docs.title: 1. Dialect Conversion
docs.text:
• GLSL 3.30 Core $\rightarrow$ WebGL2 (GLSL ES 3.00):
  • Desktop shaders in src/main/resources/shaders/ and library/sources/*/shader.frag use #version 330 core.
  • The synchronization tool transpiles #version 330 core into #version 300 es\nprecision highp float; for web/shaders/.
  • Sole Source of Truth: Shaders and visual sources should always be authored in desktop directories; running ./scripts/sync_web.py --apply or ./gradlew syncWeb mechanically updates the web client.

docs.title: 2. Algorithmic Drift Tracking
docs.text:
• For procedural geometry and math modules (Evaluators.kt $\rightarrow$ web/evaluator.js), web/sync_manifest.json tracks SHA-256 hashes.
  • Whenever a desktop Kotlin algorithm is modified, running ./scripts/sync_web.py --check or ./gradlew checkWebSync alerts the developer to review and update the JavaScript equivalent. Once verified, ./scripts/sync_web.py --mark-synced <target> records the updated hash.

docs.title: Flexible ISF Directory Architecture, Role Auto-Detection & Asset Resolution
docs.text: Liquid LSD scans arbitrary user-specified directories for Interactive Shader Format (ISF) assets without forcing files into rigid Generators/, Filters/, or Transitions/ folders.

docs.title: 1. Role Auto-Detection via JSON INPUTS
docs.text: Shaders are classified dynamically by parsing their ISF JSON header and inspecting image inputs: - 0 Image Inputs: Auto-detected as Generator (ISFAssetType.GENERATOR), loaded into VisualSourceRegistry. - 1 Image Input: Auto-detected as Filter (ISFAssetType.FILTER), loaded into ISFFilterRegistry. - 2+ Image Inputs (or 1 image input with explicit progress transition parameter): Auto-detected as Transition (ISFAssetType.TRANSITION), loaded into ISFTransitionRegistry.

docs.title: 2. Folder Hierarchy Preservation
docs.text:
• Relative subfolder structures (e.g., PackName/Subfolder/shader.fs) are captured in ISFAsset.folderPath and mirrored into categories tags.
  • The unified browser (BrowserPane) shows these folders as tree entries under each section and searches the folder names and custom tags along with the shader name.

docs.title: 3. Respecting Relative Assets (IMPORTED)
docs.text:
• Shaders remain in their original directories during execution.
  • Shaders declaring static lookup tables, noise textures, or auxiliary assets in IMPORTED (using either JSON Object or JSON Array syntax) have their paths resolved relative to the shader's parent folder (baseDir).
  • ISFParser.buildGLSLFragmentShader automatically injects uniform sampler2D <name>; declarations for all declared imported textures.
  • ISFTextureLoader decodes image files into OpenGL 2D textures on Thread 0 via STBImage (stbi_load). During execution, pre-resolved texture units are bound with zero allocations per frame on the render thread.

docs.title: 4. Discrete (stepped) inputs
docs.text: A parameter can declare a step set (ModulatableParameter.steps / labels); evaluate() snaps its result to the nearest step while baseValue stays continuous, so knobs, LFOs, audio, macros, MIDI and OSC all land on a valid value. - long / int inputs: steps come from VALUES (or the whole-number MIN..MAX span), labels from LABELS when there is one per step. bool has 2 steps. - float inputs that are really discrete take the optional Liquid LSD key "STEP" (for example "MIN": 2, "MAX": 24, "STEP": 1). The shader still receives a float uniform; other ISF hosts ignore the key. (MAX-MIN)/STEP must be a whole number, otherwise STEP is ignored and a warning is logged. - Integer uniforms are rounded, not truncated, before they reach the shader.

docs.title: 5. GPU cost tag (LSD_COST)
docs.text: ISFHeader.LSD_COST (optional Liquid LSD key, 1-3) is the author's declaration of how heavy a shader is; ISFHeader.gpuCost clamps it to 0-3 (0 = undeclared). The stock browser catalogs (BrowseCatalogs) copy it into AssetItem.gpuCost for stock generators and filters, and PresetListPanel.drawCostBadge draws a warning triangle for cost 3 (GPU_COST_HEAVY), with GPU_COST_TIP in the tooltip. It is static metadata, not a measurement. Bundled sources live in library/sources/ (the build copies them over default_sources), so tag both copies. StockGpuCostAuditTest checks range and the heavy set.

docs.title: 6. Integrated phases (LSD_PHASES)
docs.text:
A shader must never compute motion as TIME * Speed: when Speed changes, that product moves by TIME times the change, and TIME is the seconds since the app started, so an hour into a set even a small wobble of Speed (an LFO, audio, a knob, a morph) jumps the picture, and a modulated speed jumps it every frame. Instead the ISF header declares phases the host integrates, "LSD_PHASES": { "FlightPhase": ["FlightSpeed"], "ShearPhase": ["Speed", "Shear"] }: each key becomes a uniform float (declared by ISFParser) whose value is the running sum of the product of the listed inputs times the frame time. The shader uses FlightPhase * 1.5 where it had TIME * FlightSpeed_ (the input's scale factor moves across unchanged; an affine rate such as 0.5 + Rate * 23.5 becomes 0.5 * TIME + 23.5 * RatePhase). A rate change then changes the slope, never the position. - PhaseIntegrators (one per ISFVisualSource instance and per ISFFilter, so per deck and per FX slot) advances in setupUniforms / render from TimeSource, so offline export is deterministic. The first frame starts each phase at rate * TIME, where TIME * rate would have put it, so a freshly loaded source looks as it always did. A step longer than MAX_STEP_SEC (0.25 s), such as a deck that was not rendered for a while, counts as 0.25 s. - Products cover a rate that another input scales (dynamic_spiral integrates Speed, Speed x WaveAmp and Speed x Shear). An input inside a non-linear function of the phase (cos(WaveFreq * n) * phase) can still jump; no stock preset modulates one. - Every stock source and filter with a rate input is converted. cyclic_ca keeps floor(TIME * rate) - floor((TIME - dt) * rate): both terms use the current rate, so it only counts generations and never jumps. A fixed rate (TIME * 0.3) is fine. - The rate uniform itself is often no longer referenced, so the GLSL compiler drops it and Shader logs one "Uniform not found" warning for it; harmless. - web/isf.js mirrors this (advancePhases, state in ISFState.phases, reset when the program changes). The web rotation gate (web/tools/reactivity.test.mjs) lets presets modulate a rate input only when its shader integrates it.

LFOs and sequencers clocked in seconds or frames had the same bug (clock / period); see ClockAnchors in modulation.md.

docs.title: Concept Proposal: Automated Screen Capture, UI Testing & Responsive Lab
docs.text: Status: Implemented (CliArgs.kt, ScreenshotCapture.kt, UiLabPanel.kt, ./gradlew captureResponsiveApp, ./gradlew captureUiLab). Target Area: Main.kt, cli/CliArgs.kt, export/ScreenshotCapture.kt, ui/UiLabPanel.kt, ui/UIManager.kt, build.gradle.kts Origins: Adapted from PR #22 concept by Lawrence Norton (@lnorton89)

docs.title: 1. Motivation & Value Proposition
docs.text: As Liquid LSD matures with complex modular UI panels (Parameters, Properties accordions, Library drawer, Live Deck Monitors, and Custom CSD Titlebar), visual regression testing and up-to-date documentation imagery become essential.

docs.title: Core Objectives
docs.text:
1. Automated Documentation & Web Assets: Generate crisp, deterministic UI screenshots for user guides (docs/user_guide/) and web broadcasting pages on demand or during release builds.
  2. Visual Regression & Layout Auditing: Verify that UI layouts, column widths, text clipping, and responsive breakpoints remain functional across different window resolutions (1920x1080, 1440x900, 1280x720, 2560x1440, maximized) without manual testing.
  3. Isolated UI Lab Component Gallery: Provide an isolated sandbox environment to preview themes, custom icons, sliders, meters, and modal popups without requiring active audio hardware or heavyweight GLSL shader compilation.

docs.title: 2. Proposed CLI Flags & Launch Options
docs.text:
To support automated capture in CI or local developer workflows, Main.kt would parse optional startup arguments:

# Capture full app screenshot at 1080p after 5 frames and exit cleanly
./gradlew run --args="--screenshot-ui=docs/assets/main-1080p.png --window=1920x1080 --screenshot-after-frames=5 --no-audio"

# Launch isolated UI Lab gallery in compact window
./gradlew run --args="--ui-lab --window=1280x720 --no-audio"
Flag Argument Description --screenshot-ui <filepath.png> Path where the captured PNG framebuffer should be saved. Liquid LSD automatically triggers exit after capturing. --screenshot-after-frames <int> (default: 5) Number of frames to render before capturing, ensuring ImGui font atlases, layout metrics, and dynamic splitters have fully settled. --window <W>x<H> or maximized Overrides saved window dimensions for deterministic capture resolutions. --no-audio (flag) Bypasses JACK and JavaSound audio initialization to allow execution on headless CI nodes or systems without sound cards. --ui-lab (flag) Renders an isolated UI component gallery (icons, swatches, custom widgets, meters) instead of the main performance mixer.

docs.title: 3.1 Frame Capture Mechanism
docs.text:
Liquid LSD already contains high-performance readback infrastructure in export/PboReadbackPipeline.kt and STB bindings in LWJGL:

object ScreenshotCapture {
    fun captureFramebufferToPng(file: File, width: Int, height: Int): Boolean {
        file.parentFile?.mkdirs()
        val stride = width * 3 // RGB
        val source = BufferUtils.createByteBuffer(stride * height)
        val flipped = BufferUtils.createByteBuffer(stride * height)

        val previousPackAlignment = glGetInteger(GL_PACK_ALIGNMENT)
        glPixelStorei(GL_PACK_ALIGNMENT, 1)
        glReadPixels(0, 0, width, height, GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, source)
        glPixelStorei(GL_PACK_ALIGNMENT, previousPackAlignment)

        // Vertical flip (OpenGL lower-left origin to PNG top-left origin)
        for (y in 0 until height) {
            val sourceRow = (height - 1 - y) * stride
            val targetRow = y * stride
            for (x in 0 until stride) {
                flipped.put(targetRow + x, source.get(sourceRow + x))
            }
        }

        return STBImageWrite.stbi_write_png(file.absolutePath, width, height, 3, flipped, stride)
    }
}

docs.title: 3.2 Settle Counter & Clean Exit
docs.text: Because Dear ImGui dynamically calculates widget coordinates and auto-sizes windows across initial frames: 1. Render $N$ frames (e.g. 5 frames) to let ImGui layout passes, splitters, and font atlases converge. 2. On frame $N$, execute captureFramebufferToPng(). 3. Signal glfwSetWindowShouldClose(window, true) to trigger a graceful shutdown.

docs.title: 5. Summary & Next Steps
docs.text: This proposal provides a blueprint for when we decide to implement automated visual capture and headless UI verification. When ready to implement: 1. Wire CLI argument parsing into Main.kt / AppSettings.kt. 2. Add ScreenshotCapture.kt utility under export/ or utils/. 3. docs.title: Tour renderer (--tour)
docs.text:
A deterministic, scripted render of the real UI for the walkthrough video, chapter clips and the interactive tour page. The app runs on a fixed 60 fps simulated clock at 1920x1080, a synthetic cursor drives the UI, and every frame of FBO 0 is read back and piped to ffmpeg (libx264). Same script + same library + same machine/GPU = bit-identical frames.

./gradlew run --args="--tour=scripts/tour_phase3_test.json --tour-out=/tmp/t/raw.mp4 --no-audio [--tour-hidden] [--tour-dump=<dir>:70,81]"
scripts/render_tour.sh --draft tours/overview.json tours/draft/overview --tour-hidden   # while writing: a few minutes for the 5 min overview
scripts/render_tour.sh [--webm] tours/overview.json tours/out/overview --tour-hidden     # final: hero.mp4 (+ .webm), poster, .vtt, captions.json, chapters.json, clips/ (whole chapters, 1080p30), loops/ (landing cards); cuts made by scripts/tour_cuts.py
scripts/render_tour.sh [--draft] --all tours/out --tour-hidden                           # every tours/*.json into tours/out/<name>/
scripts/tour_determinism_check.sh <script.json> --tour-hidden [--tour-draft]   # renders twice, compares per-frame SHA-256

Render settings come from the command line, not the script (the website's renders use --tour-fps=30 --tour-encoder=nvenc --tour-no-hashes: the site plays 30 fps, NVENC output is reproducible on the same machine, and hashes are only for determinism checks; about 10 minutes for all seven videos instead of 1.5 hours): --tour-fps=<n> (default 60), --tour-scale=<f> (the UI is always laid out at 1920x1080; the frame is shrunk on the GPU before readback, so targets never move), --tour-encoder=x264|nvenc (default x264), --tour-hashes (per-frame SHA-256, about 5 ms a frame at 1080p). --tour-draft = 30 fps, scale 0.5, NVENC, no hashes. On the dev laptop (RTX A2000) a final frame costs about 20 ms (app and UI about 6, hash 5, x264 4, readback 3) and a draft frame about 11 ms, at half the frame count. Drafts are deterministic too (raw and NVENC-encoded frames, checked on this machine). TOUR_GL names the GPU the app rendered on and TOUR_TIMING gives the per-frame breakdown. VP9 has no hardware encoder here, so --webm is opt-in and slow.

Tour mode isolates itself: preferences are not read or written, MIDI/OSC/Link/watchers/live audio are off (a script with audio still shows the AUD column), imgui.ini is not used, real GLFW input is ignored, randomness comes from DeterministicRandom(seed). Library contents are part of the input: pin a small curated library for the final render.

docs.title: Script format (tour/TourScript.kt)
docs.text:
Top level: durationSec (optional: defaults to the last step's end plus tailSec), seed, audio (file fed to the analyzer by frame clock and muxed), bpm (manual beat clock), burnCaptions (draw captions into the video; the .vtt is always written; the tour page shows captions as text under the player, so only overview.json, whose full video is published, should burn them in, and its chapter clips will carry them until the render pipeline can make clips from a caption-free pass), captionStyle (cursor, the default, or bottom), tooltips (ImGui hover tooltips, off by default so they never collide with the caption box), chapters ({t, id, title, endSec?, clipSec?}, or use chapter steps), steps.

Timing: a step starts at absolute t seconds, or dt seconds after the previous step (dt alone is the easiest to edit: inserting a step shifts everything after it). Captions: caption on any step becomes a cue lasting until the next captioned step ("" clears). {ch:<id>} in a caption becomes "Ch. N at m:ss". With captionStyle: cursor the caption is an opaque box beside the last move target, below it by default; captionPos (above, left, right) on the captioned step keeps it clear of what the step shows. The box stays put during drags and clicks.

Checks printed as TOUR_WARN: a caption shown for less than its reading time (14 characters per second, at least 2.5 s), a chapter's last caption shown less than 5 s (or its reading time) before the chapter or video ends (the tour page autoplays the next chapter; lengthen the gap before the next chapter step, or tailSec for the last, rather than freezing: the app keeps running live meanwhile), a target that was not drawn in the previous frame (wrong page or view, or a move on the same frame as a page switch: wait about 0.4 s), unknown ids.

Action Fields move target (widget key) or x,y; durationSec; ox,oy offset from the target's centre. Also draws a highlight ring on the target. An open combo's items sit about 17 px apart starting 16 px below the combo's centre (oy 16, 33, 50, ...) click / rclick / drag click (or right-click) at the cursor; drag presses, travels dx,dy (or onto target / absolute x,y, with ox,oy) over durationSec, releases (aim with a move first). Before a second drag on the same control, move back onto it: a drag ends where the cursor stopped hold caption only type / key / scroll type: target = text; selects the focused field's text (Ctrl+A), types it, presses Enter (click the field first). key: target = [ctrl+][shift+] enter, escape, tab, space, backspace or a letter, e.g. q, shift+q, ctrl+z (app shortcuts fire; Escape in Edit also collapses the rack). scroll: value wheel notches at the cursor chapter target = id, title, clipSec tooltips value 0 or 1 set_page target = ab, bgpv, mixer library_mode, theme, preferences, preferences_close, output_view, randomization FULL/HALF; light/dark; category name; value 1 = Output View on (the F key), 0 = off; value 1/0 = randomization on/off (shows the Clock row's randomize buttons) open_params, open_params_pair, focus_pair, close_focus module id / pair tag load_source, load_preset deck A/B/BG/PV, target = source id / .lsd path set_param, bind_modulator deck, param, value; modulator target = CV source id, unit BEAT/TIME fx_filter, fx_enable, fx_link, fx_param, meta_knob deck (A/B/BG/PV/MASTER), slot 0-2, target/value/param fx_chain_enable deck, value 0 or 1: the chain's FX ON switch (0 = bypassed) fx_swap deck, slot, slot2 (a real drag of one slot cell onto another does the same through the UI) fx_chain, fx_clear, fx_dry_wet, super_knob deck, .lsdfxchain path / value (fx_clear = the chain menu's Clear All Slots: empty slots, named Untitled). super_knob and meta_knob set the FX row's macro knob, as a hand would; soft takeover still applies transition, transition_preset, crossfade stock id, .lsdtrans path, value -1..1 trans_param param (ISF NAME), value: turns the Transitions row knob bound to it (knobs 2-4 drive the first three float parameters every tick), else sets it deck_level deck A/B/BG/PV, value 0..1: as a hand on the deck's level fader (Mixer.setLevelByUser) pipe target show (opaque backdrop, empty diagram), hide, reveal (the diagram shrinks into the mini-map over durationSec while the UI fades in) pipe_add target = comma list of groups decks, fx, trans, bg, master, pv; fade and slide in over durationSec pipe_focus target = node, chain (A.fx .. PV.fx, master) or all; the camera eases there over durationSec and dims the rest pipe_params target = node, params = list of ISF NAMEs: boxes with the parameter's label and live value bar, wired into the node (empty list clears) pipe_controls target = a shown parameter: the fan of control icons (knob, audio, LFO, sequencer, MIDI/OSC) wired into it; value 0 hides, 2 flashes the wires pipe_tag target = node, title = chip text beside its title; value 0 removes pipe_minimap target = comma list of nodes or groups to light (all, a group, a node, A.fx for a chain); durationSec (default 2.5); x,y moves the corner (default bottom-left)

set_param, fx_param, trans_param, crossfade and meta_knob take durationSec to ease from the current value. fx_param warns when the slot's Metaknob owns the parameter (its value would be overwritten); turn meta_knob instead. A chapter step's minimap shows the pipeline mini-map at the chapter start with those nodes lit; every chapter of every video has one, so a clip watched on its own still shows where it sits in the pipeline.

Unknown targets print TOUR_WARN and are skipped; treat any warning as a script bug.

docs.title: Pipeline diagram (tour/PipelineDiagram.kt)
docs.text: A live schematic drawn on the foreground draw list, under the cursor and caption, in a 1920x1080 design space. Nodes: decks A, B, BG, PV; FX slots A.fx1 .. PV.fx3 and master.fx1 .. master.fx3; trans, behind (the A/B mix over BG) and out. Each box shows the real texture at that point: deck source (cleanFBO), each FX slot's output (rendering/FxSlotTaps: a 384x216 copy per rendered slot, made only while the diagram is up; an empty or bypassed slot shows its input), the transition (blendFBO), the composite (masterCompositeFBO) and the output (masterFBO), over a checkerboard so transparency shows. A camera (screen = p * s + o) eases between the overview, a focused node and the mini-map. move targets: pipe:<node>, pipe:A.fx / pipe:master (a chain), pipe:param:<NAME>, pipe:control:<0-4>; they resolve where the camera is heading, so move after a focus has settled. The intro using it is the first chapter of tours/overview.json (pipeline); plan and storyboard in .planning/pipeline-intro-plan.md.

docs.title: Widget keys (tour/WidgetRegistry.kt)
docs.text: Call sites do WidgetRegistry.note { key } right after the ImGui item (free outside tour mode). Keys: perf_tab_<page>, perf_<page>_r<row>_c<col> (knobs), perf_gen_badge_<tag>, perf_src_more_/save_/eject_/rand_<tag>, rack_chevron_<id>, crossfader_track, fxcell_<bank>_<slot>, fxbypass_/fxlink_<bank>_<slot>, fxchain_name_<bank>, fxpill_<bank>_<slot>, fxchainlink_<bank>, fxchain_on_<A|B|BG|PV|MST> (chain FX ON), fxchain_save_<bank>, fxchain_more_<bank> (chain Save and menu), focus mode fxwet_<bank> (Wet slider), fxpage_prev_/next_<bank>, fxfocus_name_<bank>, Transitions row perf_trans_picker, perf_snap_A/B, perf_autofade, perf_fade_time, perf_trans_rand (only with randomization on), browser_tab_<mode>, browser_search, browser_row_<src|fx|trans>_<stock id or file name without extension> (list rows; only rows scrolled into view are clickable), deck_fader_<A|B|BG|PV> (preview faders), prefs_cat_<category>, ui_theme, edit_side_<tab>, macro_name_<bank>_<label>. Edit grid: cv_<param path>_<label|val|midi|lfo|seq|audio> (param path as in <out>.keys, e.g. cv_Deck A/View/Zoom_lfo), grid_cols_kebab, grid_col_<midi|lfo|seq|audio>. Modulator panel: mod_power_<n>, mod_op_<n>, wave_lfo1_<sine|tri|square|random|left|center|right>, lfo_unit, aud_band, aud_profile, seq_unit, seq_bars_<row> (one key per row of up to 16 step bars; aim inside it with ox/oy or drag), range_<label>_<min|max> and slider_<label>_<value|min|max|track> (by the slider's label), and btn_<visible label> for every ButtonChrome.button (last drawn wins when labels repeat), plus btnid_<id after ##> when the label has an id (stays put when the text changes, e.g. btnid_perf_clock_tap, btnid_perf_q_next_B, btnid_cancelSavePreset). <out>.keys lists every key seen during a render, handy when authoring. Custom-drawn items without an ImGui item (deck title badges, knob strip labels) need x,y or a new explicit rect. Do not key on ##title_badge_*_x_y (coordinates in the id).

docs.title: Outputs next to --tour-out
docs.text:
.hashes (per frame), .vtt, .captions.json (index/start/end/chapter/text for the web page and transcript), .chapters.json, .ffmeta (ffmpeg chapters). render_tour.sh derives the rest.

Known leftovers: wall-clock use in FileSystemManager, DeckOps autosave names, PlaylistManager, PerformanceStats, TouchConsoleController (no pixel effect so far); other GPUs/compositors unverified.

docs.title: The walkthrough videos
docs.text: One script per video in tours/: overview.json (seven chapters, about 8 minutes, opening with the pipeline diagram), modulation.json (grid, LFO, audio, step sequencer, muting; about 4 minutes), and first drafts of fx_chains.json (about 4.8 minutes), mixing.json (3.8), library.json (2.8), hardware.json (2), output.json (2), each to be embedded on its user-guide page. A UI change re-renders only the videos it touches. In a deck's bound Browse (click the source name) a single click on a row loads it, so scripts show loads with move + click on browser_row_* keys instead of load_source. Things tour mode cannot show: MIDI and OSC are off, so their Preferences panels show the disabled state and nothing arrives (the learn ring and panels are what the Hardware video shows); a menu or modal opened by a click is real (avoid items that open windows or write files, close Save dialogs with btnid_cancelSavePreset); Output View is output_view, not the F key (GLFW key callbacks are ignored). Their soundtrack tours/beat.wav is a generated placeholder (scripts/make_tour_beat.sh, not committed) until the licensed track arrives; the script only names the file, so swapping it changes nothing else.

docs.title: The website tour page
docs.text: scripts/build_website.py generates /tour/ from the rendered videos (--tours DIR; default tours/out if it holds a render, else tours/draft). Video order, titles, summaries and the docs page each video links to live in website/data/tour.json. For every chapter it copies clips/<id>.mp4 (the whole chapter, silent) to tour/media/<video>/ and loops/<id>.mp4 (its first clipSec, at most 20 s) to tour/media/<video>/loops/ for the chapters landing.json features, and reads chapters.json + captions.json. It writes the chapter list and the full "Every caption" transcript as static HTML (readable without JS, indexable) and embeds the data as JSON for website/assets/js/tour.js: looping clip with YouTube-style overlay controls (play, prev, next bottom-left; Autoplay next, speed 0.5x-2x and fullscreen bottom-right; a draggable seek line above them; hidden 5 s after the cursor stops moving and at once when it leaves, back on any movement), NN / total counter and chapter title below the video with the current caption under it, keys arrows/space/k/f, Autoplay next on by default (a clip plays once and the next chapter starts), captions synced to the clip, click a transcript line to seek, deep links #<video>/<chapter>. The site header (site.js) fades out 3 s after scrolling stops when the page is not at the top, and any scroll brings it back; it stays while hovered, focused or with the mobile menu open. Hero videos are not published; re-render a video and rebuild the site and the page follows. Videos with no render are skipped. The same build inserts each video's chapter clips (click-to-play, linked back to the tour) after the intro paragraph of the user-guide page named in tour.json (inject_clips); the repo's docs/ and the in-app copy stay free of media, so they never show broken video. docs/user_guide/hardware.md is the Hardware video's page; it links into the existing MIDI/Twister/OSC sections of performance_controls.md rather than repeating them.

docs.title: Publishing the site
docs.text:
Videos and their posters are not on GitHub Pages: the build links them at MEDIA_URL (build_website.py, https://www.spaz.org/~gj/liquid-lsd-files, Apache with range requests) and writes them to <build>/tour/media/, which publish_site.sh copies to the server first with rsync -c over SSH (MEDIA_SSH; key login), so only changed videos upload. Captions (tour/captions/*.vtt) stay on the site, since browsers refuse cross-origin caption tracks. --media-url file://... previews a build locally. scripts/publish_site.sh builds the site and pushes it to greenjon/liquid-lsd-site (cloned next to this repo on first run); that repo's Actions workflow (website/deploy/pages.yml) deploys it to GitHub Pages at liquid-lsd.greenjon.com (SITE_HOST in build_website.py; the build writes CNAME and .nojekyll). The site repo holds no media since 2026-10-20 (its history was squashed then); --squash still resets its history to one commit. Pass --tours tours/out (or leave the default) to choose which render is published; check that you are not publishing draft renders.

Each chapter also gets a .jpg thumbnail (a frame a few seconds into its clip, made with ffmpeg at site build time), used as the poster on the tour page and the docs clips.

docs.title: Landing page and the overview video
docs.text: website/data/landing.json names the hero video (overview) and the four featured chapters shown as "See it in action" cards on the landing page (slug = <video>/<chapter>, plus a one-line blurb). The cards are muted loops that play only while on screen; phones, reduced motion and data saver get thumbnails only. The hero video is the only full-length file published: the build re-encodes its hero.mp4 to 1080p30 H.264 (CRF 30, slow preset, cached in the gitignored tours/web-cache/, about 28 MB for the 6-minute draft) and copies it with its poster and .vtt captions to tour/media/<video>/. It loads on click (.video-facade) on both the landing page and the tour page.

docs.title: Which videos are stale
docs.text: scripts/render_tour.sh stamps <out>/<tour>/rendered_at.json (commit, dirty-tree and draft flags). scripts/tour_staleness.py compares each stamp with HEAD and lists the tours to re-render: it maps the widget keys a script aims at (target fields) to the Kotlin files that register them, then reports commits since the render that touched those files, the script itself or the tour renderer (tour/). Other commits under ui/, rendering/, shaders or defaults/ are counted as "maybe" because colors and layout change a video without touching a key. -v lists the commits and any keys it could not map (dynamic or very generic labels such as btn_Randomize are not tracked); --names prints only the stale tour names; --out points at a different render root. Videos rendered before stamping existed fall back to the video file's date. Weekly: run it, then render_tour.sh on the names it prints.

docs.title: UI Architecture & ImGui Systems
docs.text: The ui/ package manages the immediate-mode desktop interface using ImGui (imgui-java), LWJGL 3, and GLFW. This document maps component ownership, memory safety patterns, popup scheduling, and the NoteEditorModal architecture. For an evaluation of workflow boundaries, loading interactions, and macro/library coordination, see UI Interaction Architecture Review.

docs.text:

    PerformanceMatrixPanel --> PerformanceClockControls[PerformanceClockControls.kt - Clock row tempo bar]
    PerformanceMatrixPanel --> PerformanceMasterControls[PerformanceMasterControls.kt - Master row: MIX/levels badge, FX pill, Master FX chain]
    PerformanceMatrixPanel --> PerformanceDeckControls[PerformanceDeckControls.kt - Deck rows left/right controls + DeckRowMetrics]

    PerformanceMatrixPanel --> PerformanceDeepEditBay[PerformanceDeepEditBay.kt - Edit bay accordion & 3-column layout]

    PerformanceDeepEditBay --> ParameterGridHeaders[ParameterGridHeaders.kt - Edit column headers]
    PerformanceDeepEditBay --> ParametersTabs[ParametersTabs.kt - Edit side rail & parameter rows]
    PerformanceDeepEditBay --> PropertiesPanel[PropertiesPanel.kt - Edit Properties column]
    PerformanceDeepEditBay --> DeckSourcePicker[DeckSourcePicker.kt - source picker & empty-deck launchpad]

    PropertiesPanel --> AudioModulatorSection[AudioModulatorSection.kt - Audio Followers & Controls]
    PropertiesPanel --> MidiModulatorSection[MidiModulatorSection.kt - MIDI CC Modulator Controls]

Most panel draw(...) methods (like PerformanceMatrixPanel) receive session: SessionContext, the current Mixer reference, and parametersState: ParametersState at frame render time. Other panels like MixerPanel and DeckControlPanel receive state via dependency injection in their constructors. Panels access subsystems (AudioEngine, CVRegistry, PresetManager, PlayQueueManager, NotesManager) via session rather than direct global singletons.

Deck preview monitors (Deck A, Deck B, Deck BG, Deck PV) in MixerPanel and DeckControlPanel render clean video monitors maximizing active preview area without non-image toolbar clutter. Former toolbar rows above the images (Save, Eject, and preset name box) and the crossfader transition button have been removed from the Mixer strip; saving presets is handled via keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+S/Cmd+S) or Gen Browse, deck loading is handled via Browser drag-drop, and transition selection is configured via Edit or Browser drag-drop onto the crossfader slider. MixerLayoutCalculator dedicates full vertical space to video monitor rendering.

Each deck preview monitor (DeckControlPanel.drawDeckControls) carries the same small overlay on all four decks: - Level fader (left edge): the channel Level (mixer.levelA, levelB, levelBG, levelPV) from the top margin down to just above the badge. Drag, scroll wheel, middle-click reset (100%). The fill shows the live level, the handle the base value. - Deck badge (lower-left corner, [A], [B], [BG], [PV]): click browses that deck's source in the Library below (focusDeckPair: the deck's rows come over it when the page does not show them). - Die button (right of the badge): randomizes the deck's modulators and base values, with undo. - The image: click does the same as the badge; drag routes (copy, move, swap) to another deck; dropping a preset file loads it into the deck. The per-deck FX Wet/Dry fader and [FX] kill button that used to sit in a right column are gone (FX on/off is on the deck's FX row).

MixerLayoutCalculator calculates exact aspect preview sizes against available pane height and comprehensive vertical chrome (master controls, preset bars, separator bands, and safety margins). It utilizes the full pane width without reserving unconditional scrollbars, automatically scaling monitor previews to fit vertically without scrolling on standard screens, and displaying scrollbars only on extremely small display heights. It also calculates the exact maximum allowed window width (calculateMaxAllowedWindowWidth) to lock the Mixer panel to its ideal aspect-ratio width, preventing wasted letterbox blank space and ensuring the Performance panel / Library column absorbs all remaining display space. The Mixer is also capped so the Performance panel keeps PerformanceMatrixPanel.calculateMinWidth() (Edit side rail + grid + a 450px Properties allowance).

docs.title: 1. UIManager.kt & Global Hotkey Routing (Main.kt)
docs.text:
• Main Loop Integration: Invoked once per frame (render(mixer, width, height)). Initialises and disposes ImGuiImplGlfw and ImGuiImplGl3. Zeroes io.mouseWheelH per frame to globally disable unintended horizontal scroll wheel panning from trackpads or trackpoints.
  • Global Key Routing (Main.kt & UIManager.kt): Chained GLFW key callback intercepts F (Output View toggle), F11 (WindowFrameController.toggleFullscreen, main window fullscreen via glfwSetWindowMonitor), B (background video toggle), and Ctrl-/Ctrl= (Library preset name font scaling) whenever !io.wantTextInput or when Output View is enabled. Spacebar (LibraryPanel.cycleMode) toggles the Library HALF $\leftrightarrow$ FULL when not typing; from Edit view it calls LibraryPanel.show instead (cancel Learn, collapse Edit), as do Ctrl+F and /.
  • Three views (UIManager.drawAssetManagementLayout, LibraryPanel.isEditView): UITheme.LibraryMode is only FULL / HALF (a saved legacy HIDE loads as HALF). Perform = HALF with no module in Edit; Edit = any module in Edit and not FULL, where the Library window isn't drawn at all and the Performance panel gets the whole column height; Library = FULL. ParametersState.setDisclosure drops FULL to HALF when it opens a Edit so the Edit view is actually visible. Edit is solo-only (no rackSoloMode); the only exception is a Learn-pinned module. On load, at most one persisted expanded module is restored.
  • Workspace Layout Orchestration: Lays out the Performance panel (top left, above the Library dock) and the Mixer (right, fitted to aspect preview height). Panels strictly enforce ImGuiWindowFlags.NoScrollbar with exact width calculation to prevent layout drifting. Vertical positioning below the 50% expanded top title bar uses titleBarH + TITLE_BAR_PANEL_GAP (2.0f), preserving an exact 2 px visual divider without hardcoded minimum bounds.
  • Title Bar Drag-to-Resize: Supports vertical resizing of the docked Library by click-dragging empty areas of the Library menu bar.
  • Deferred Font Atlas Rebuilding: Adjusting preset name scale sets pendingFontRebuild. Rebuilding the font atlas and OpenGL textures occurs at the top of the next frame (before ImGui.newFrame()) to prevent mid-frame atlas corruption.
  • Deferred Popup Triggering: Modal popups set a pendingOpen* flag and execute ImGui.openPopup(id) at the root ID stack level outside child windows.
  • Modal Rendering Pipeline: Invokes NoteEditorModal.draw(), SavePresetModal.draw(), and PopupManager's specific draw methods (e.g. drawExitPopup(), drawDeckConfirmPopups(), drawSourceChangeConfirmPopup(), drawMidiWarningPopup()) at root scope.
  • Single workspace (Perform view): PerformanceMatrixPanel.kt (4×4 macro knob matrix + Edit — see docs/user_guide/macros_and_rack.md) is the primary live editing view, orchestrating dedicated sub-controllers for clean separation of concerns:
  • PerformanceUiContext.kt: Shared styling colors (PerformanceColors), the Edit bay's SRC/FX and MIX/FX predicates (isDeckBayFx, isMasterBayFx, which read the deck / Mixer sub-tab in ParametersState to pick the row an open module shows), and label/module resolution helpers.
  • PerformanceTransitionsControls.kt: Transitions row controls: Line 1 transition picker (active shader/preset name with dirty marker) and TransitionQueue stepping (< [N/Total] >); Line 2 crossfader (Deck A/B snap badges, bipolar slider track, [AUTO]/[FADING] button, fade speed widget); right wing: randomize die button on Line 1 matching deck rows.
  • PerformanceClockControls.kt: Clock row's two control lines on the MIXER page (a 3 x 2 grid of equal CELL_W buttons, MAN/AUDIO/LINK over TAP (MIDI Learn on Global/tapTempo)/SNAP/the ± nudge pair, then the BPM readout with the 4-beat dots under it; right of them PerformanceClockTriggers: the QUEUE block (captions on line 1, prev / next on line 2, play-pause beside the caption on line 1; the FX queues' Mixer/fx*Queue* parameters have no play-pause) and, with randomization on, the RAND block at the right edge, each bound to the CTRL tab's ModulatableParameter and key, dropped whole when the row is too narrow), reusing AudioEngine/TapTempoController actions like TempoSyncPanel.
