docs.title: 4. Hardware Controller & User Mapping Workflow
docs.text: Inspired by Mixxx's mapping system, Liquid LSD can implement a tiered mapping system:

docs.title: 4.1 Global Mapping Manager & Table GUI
docs.text:
• A unified Mapping Settings Panel presenting the complete action inventory in a searchable, filterable table.
  • Each row lists:
  • Action Name & Description
  • Keyboard Binding (e.g. Ctrl + Shift + A, Space, Up Arrow)
  • MIDI Binding (e.g. Ch 1 - CC 14, Ch 1 - Note C3)
  • CV Source Binding (e.g. JACK In 1, LFO 1)
  • Mode (Momentary, Toggle, Continuous, Stutter)

docs.title: 4.2 Interactive "Learn" Overlay & Context Menus
docs.text:
• Right-clicking any button, slider, or grid pad in the GUI reveals:
  • MIDI Learn: Listens for the next incoming MIDI CC or Note event and binds it immediately.
  • Assign Key: Prompts for a keypress (with automatic capture of Ctrl, Shift, Alt).
  • Bind CV: Drops down available internal CV modulators and external JACK CV ports.

docs.title: 4.3 Hardware Controller Preset Files (JSON / YAML)
docs.text: Community and out-of-the-box hardware profiles stored under library/mappings/: - library/mappings/controllers/novation_launchpad_mini.json (Grid matrix mapping) - library/mappings/controllers/akai_apc40_mk2.json (Faders, knobs, crossfader, clip launch) - library/mappings/controllers/pioneer_ddj_400.json (DJ style transport, jog/rotary, crossfader) - library/mappings/keyboard/qwerty_default.json (Standard keyboard layout with stutter keys)

docs.title: 5. Implementation Phasing Strategy
docs.text:
1. Phase 1: Core Action Registry (CommandRegistry):
  2. Refactor existing parameter paths and button callbacks into registered Command instances with metadata (ID, category, input type, description).
  3. Phase 2: Keyboard Shortcut Engine:
  4. Intercept GLFW key events with modifier state (GLFW_MOD_CONTROL, GLFW_MOD_SHIFT, GLFW_MOD_ALT).
  5. Dispatch to CommandRegistry for triggers, toggles, and momentary hold/release states (e.g., crossfader stutter).
  6. Phase 3: Unified MIDI Mapping & MIDI Learn:
  7. Generalize MidiMappingManager to bind to any registered Command (not just continuous float parameters).
  8. Support Note On/Off, relative encoders, and momentary buttons.
  9. Phase 4: Mapping Configuration UI & Profile Exporter:
  10. Build the GUI mapping table and right-click "Learn" modals in ImGui.
  11. Support loading/saving controller presets to library/mappings/.

docs.title: 6. Implemented So Far (2026-10-01)
docs.text: Package llm.slop.liquidlsd.control; tests in src/test/kotlin/.../control/ and midi/GlobalCommandDispatchTest.kt.

docs.title: 6.1 Command registry
docs.text:
• CommandRegistry holds Command(id, kind, category, description, handler). Kinds: TRIGGER, TOGGLE (both fire on the rising edge only), MOMENTARY (both edges), SCALAR (0..1), RELATIVE (signed steps). Inputs are CommandInput.Press/Value/Delta; an input that doesn't fit the command's kind is rejected.
  • Edge detection lives in the registry (per command id), not in each caller.
  • Aliases map legacy identifiers to command ids. The ten Global/* mapping paths are aliases of the commands in GlobalCommands (mixer.queue_next, mixer.queue_prev, mixer.bg_queue_next/prev, mixer.trans_queue_next/prev, clock.tap_tempo, mixer.auto_crossfade_trigger, mixer.crossfade_snap_a/b). The four fx.* queue commands (fx.queue_next/prev, fx.bg_queue_next/prev) have no legacy path and are not bound in the built-in Twister profile (no free input); bind them in a user profile. Existing library/midi/*.json profiles load unchanged.
  • MidiMappingManager.processGlobalMidiEvents runs Global/* mappings through MidiMappingManager.commands. Handlers get a CommandContext (mixer, tap callback, queue deltas) and run on the render thread only; the registry is not thread-safe.
  • Parameter and Macro/... bindings are not on the registry yet.

docs.title: 6.2 Device tagging
docs.text: MidiEvent.deviceId is the javax.sound.midi device name of the port that produced the event ("" for synthetic events). On connect, MidiEngine logs which controller profile (if any) matches the device.

docs.title: 6.3 Controller profiles
docs.text:
• A profile is JSON: id, name, description, match (case-insensitive substrings of the device name), banks, inputs, bindings, bankBindings.
  • Built-ins live in src/main/resources/controllers/ and are listed in ControllerProfileStore.BUILT_IN_NAMES; user profiles in library/controllers/*.json. A user profile with the same id replaces the built-in, and user profiles win when two match one device. Profiles that fail to parse or validate are skipped with an error in the log.
  • banks.pages lists the app page to show when each hardware bank becomes active (index = 0-based bank; perform.<page id>: the built-ins are decks, master, ab, bgpv, mixer, plus any page in library/perform_pages/; the shipped Twister profile uses ab, bgpv, mixer, master). inputs: each entry is one input or a group. Group members come from ccs or cc until cc + count and are named <id>.<n> (1-based). bankStride adds bank * bankStride to the CC so a logical input keeps one id on every hardware bank. An ENCODER can carry press: {channel} (same CCs on another channel), exposed as <id>.<n>.press. kind is ENCODER, BUTTON, FADER or MODIFIER (a held button that selects alternate bindings). Encoders also take mode (ABSOLUTE, RELATIVE_BINARY_OFFSET, RELATIVE_SIGNED_BIT, RELATIVE_TWOS_COMP), step (fraction of a control's range per tick, default 1/127) and accel (maximum speed-up, 1 disables).
  • banks.switch describes the device's bank buttons (CC = cc + bankIndex; a non-zero value means that bank is now active).
  • Binding keys are an input id with optional held-modifier prefixes (shift+knob.3.press); bankBindings (1-based bank) override bindings. In the last part of a key * matches a group index and {n} in the value is replaced by it ("knob.*": "knob.{n}"). CompiledController.bindingFor(inputId, held, bank) picks the most specific binding: more modifiers beat fewer, then a bank binding beats a global one.
  • ControllerProfile.compile() builds a (type, channel, cc) -> ResolvedInput(inputId, kind, bank, mode) table and a list of structural problems (CC collisions, out-of-range values, duplicate ids, bindings naming unknown inputs or non-modifier prefixes). unknownCommands(registry) lists binding targets that aren't registered.
  • Bindings, modifiers, banks and encoder handling are live (6.5). Navigation/browse commands are live (6.7). Not implemented yet: response curves. See .planning/midi-controller-plan.md.

docs.title: 6.4 Built-in profile
docs.text: Banks select Perform pages (banks.pages: perform.ab, perform.bgpv, perform.mixer; the stock Twister profile has 4 banks, and bank 4 leaves the page alone). Side buttons side.1..3 (CC 8, 11, 13 on bank 1; +6 per bank) are the context-dependent navigation buttons; shift is CC 10. midi-fighter-twister: 64 encoders (CC 0..63 on ch1 = knob + 16 * bank), encoder switches on ch2 with the same CCs, 6 side buttons per bank on ch4 (CC 8+6n..13+6n: left-top, left-middle = chain link, left-bottom = shift, right-top, right-middle = bank step, right-bottom), all CC Hold; the app steps banks and sends the bank change (ch4 CC 0..3). The matching Utility settings ship as resources/controllers/midi-fighter-twister.mfs; the profile's optional utilityFile names it and Preferences > MIDI Controls > Controller Profiles saves a copy anywhere (ControllerProfileStore.utilityFileBytes; the last folder is the utilitySettingsDirectory preference). Measured on hardware.

docs.title: 6.5 Controller runtime and the Perform grid (phase 2)
docs.text:
• ControllerManager creates one ControllerRuntime per device the first time it sends a message and its name matches a profile. MidiMappingManager.processGlobalMidiEvents offers each event to it before the legacy Global/* and parameter bindings; a runtime consumes an event only if the profile binds that input, and a learned mapping on the exact channel/CC takes precedence over the profile, except while NavSurface.browsing is true (the profile then gets the event first).
  • The runtime tracks the active bank (from the bank buttons, or any bank-aware input), held modifiers, and per-encoder state. Encoder messages become signed ticks (relative modes decode directly; ABSOLUTE is the change since the last value, so the first message only locates the knob), scaled by step and a speed-based boost (accel, full at <= 8 ms between ticks, none at >= 60 ms), then sent as CommandInput.Delta. A button's release goes to the command that received its press.
  • KnobCommands registers knob.1..16 (RELATIVE), knob.<n>.press and knob.<n>.press_alt (MOMENTARY). It tracks which switches are held (the Twister sends the same turn messages either way): turning while held is fine (x0.1) and cancels the tap; a tap runs KnobSurface.primary (press) or secondary (press_alt).
  • KnobSurface (render thread) is implemented by ui/PerformSurface. Its page is PerformPages.resolve: PerfRows.visibleRowsForTab (the same rows PerformanceMatrixPanel draws, now in a shared object) through PerfKnobResolver, flattened row-major into 16 slots. Actions: turn adds to MacroControl.value; primary on an FX slot cell = FxOps.setSlotEnabled, on a parameter = reset to default, on a label knob = reset to 0.5; secondary on a slot cell = FxMacroSync.focusSlot (or leave focus when it is knob 1 of a focused row), on a parameter = FxMacroSync.stepParamPage; showPage sets the matrix tab.

docs.title: 6.6 Ring and LED feedback (phase 4)
docs.text:
• Profile output.knobs: input (the encoder group, e.g. knob), ringChannel (default: the encoder's channel), colorChannel (null = no LEDs) and color, a HueWheel (min/max value range, off, white, hueAtMin, degreesPerStep; defaults are the Twister's wheel: blue = 1, hue decreasing 2.88 degrees per step). The ring is set by sending the encoder's own CC on ringChannel; the LED by sending the same CC number on colorChannel.
  • KnobLightSource.knobLights() (implemented by ui/PerformSurface) returns 16 KnobLights: ring value, LED colour (PerformPages.ledColor: the row accent; Master is Scarlet and Global Butter, which LED_MASTER/LED_GLOBAL alias), lit. ControllerFeedback.update(lights, activeBank, nowMs) expands them to the encoder CCs of the group and writes only changed values, for the active bank only (all banks while it is unknown; the whole new bank when it changes, since the Twister showed its stored colours on banks that were not on screen). resync() forces a full rewrite. Each bank's own CC numbers are used (CC = knob + stride * bank; verified with amidi on the Twister: CC 16 is live on bank 2, CC 0 is not). output.trace (or env LSD_MIDI_TRACE=1) logs every feedback message (TracingSink), bank change and encoder message at INFO.
  • MidiOutputPorts.openFor(name, minIntervalMs) writes through a CcQueue (one pending value per channel/CC, so a slow device never accumulates stale values) from a daemon thread that keeps at least output.minIntervalMs (default 2) between messages, because the Twister drops bursts. It logs send time and backlog every 5 s (INFO when a send takes over 5 ms or the backlog exceeds 40).
  • ControllerManager.updateFeedback runs once per frame from UIManager.processInput, right after the MIDI drain. Once a second it scans MidiEngine.getConnectedDeviceNames(): matching devices get a ControllerFeedback over MidiOutputPorts.openFor(name) (an output port with the same device name, written from a daemon thread); devices that left or whose sink is unhealthy are dropped, and a failed open is retried after 10 s.

docs.title: 6.7 Navigation (phase 3)
docs.text:
NavSurface (on CommandContext, like KnobSurface) gets nav.button.1..3 / .alt from NavCommands and the knob 16 cursor (KnobCommands.BROWSE_KNOB) from KnobCommands while browsing; with browseLiveKnobs (a bound dock: the pair view's two rows, or the page's first two rows while the Perform dock is bound in place; knobs 1-8) those leading knobs also pass through to KnobSurface, and PerformSurface.knobLights darkens everything else. In the Library, a tap on a send knob (SendTarget: knobs 9-12 = A/B/BG/PV, knob 13 = master FX) calls NavSurface.browseSend (Library or picker) when it is in NavSurface.sendTargets (a function of the cursor item's type: LibraryNavigation.sendTargets/send), and from a bound dock LibraryNavigation.send then moves the binding to the target (openGenBrowse / openFxChainBrowse: in place when its row is on the page, else its pair view), so its rows are live through browseLiveKnobs; knobLights shows live send knobs in the target's colour. The UI implementation is ui/NavigationSurface.kt; it dispatches on the current view (Library FULL vs Perform/Edit) and calls LibraryNavigation (tab, list, cursor, accept, enqueue) and BackNavigation (the Esc stack). The user-facing layout (which button does what in the Perform, picker and Library contexts, and a worked "load an effect on Deck A" example) is in the user guide, performance_controls.md, section "Controller Profiles: Midi Fighter Twister".

The picker context: NavigationSurface.inPicker = a bound dock is up (ViewState.pair || ViewState.bound); side 1 = back, side 2 = stepTab (shift: previous), side 3 = stepPane (shift: the target's clear), knob 16 tap = accept, shift + tap = enqueue, as in the Library. BrowserPane.hosted() != null (the target the dock was last drawn bound to) decides whether accept applies to the row and whether shift + side 3 clears it. PairKnobTouch.sync runs every frame outside Edit and retargets a bound dock to the touched row's slot with openBrowse(..., retab = false), so a touch never changes the tab unless the target changed. Cursor API: LibraryNavigation.step/stepPane/accept (the same functions the Library uses, following LibraryPanel.navMode) and the hosted ApplyTarget.clear. Opening uses PerformSurface.lastTouchedKnob to find the row.

docs.title: 6.8 Profile store writes and the profile UI (phase 5, slice 1)
docs.text: ControllerProfileStore can write: copyBuiltInToUser(id) (refuses when a user file with that id exists), saveUser(profile) (returns compile().problems and writes nothing when invalid), deleteUser(id) (locates the file by profile id). sourceOf(id) reports BUILT_IN / USER / USER_OVERRIDE and rejected() lists user files that failed to parse or validate, with the reasons. Schema version: ControllerProfile.version (default 1; a missing field means 1; CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION is what this build reads and writes, and every write stamps it). version < current runs ControllerProfile.migrate (identity today; add one step per bump). version > current loads best-effort (unknown keys are ignored), appears in warnings(), and saveUser refuses to overwrite that file so unknown fields are never silently dropped. Bump the version only for changes an older build would misread; additive optional fields do not need a bump. The cache is one immutable snapshot, dropped by reload(); after any change call ControllerManager.reset() so runtimes pick up the new profile. The UI is MidiPreferencesPanel.drawControllerProfiles. Open: in-app binding editor, learn-into-profile, see .planning/midi-phase5-profile-ui-plan.md.

docs.title: 6.9 Binding editor (phase 5, slice 2)
docs.text: ProfileBindingEdit holds the pure edits (set, remove, key, fits, commandFits); CompiledController.inputKinds lists every bindable input id with its kind. MidiPreferencesPanel.drawBindingEditor writes through ControllerProfileStore.saveUser and schedules ControllerManager.reset() 600 ms after the last successful edit. Only global bindings are editable; bankBindings and learn-into-profile (MidiLearnTarget.ProfileCommand) are open.

docs.title: 6.10 Learn into a profile (phase 5, slice 3)
docs.text: MidiLearnTarget.ProfileCommand(profileId, commandId, modifiers) is handled by MidiMappingManager.learnIntoProfile, which calls ProfileBindingEdit.learn(compiled, event, commandId, modifiers): a resolved input gets a key (modifiers sorted + input id), an unresolved one gets a new InputDef (<type>-<channel>-<index>, kind guessed from the message). Result text goes to profileLearnMessage. Open: per-bank bindings.

docs.title: 6.11 Native mode (host-driven devices, Twister XT firmware)
docs.text:
• A profile with output.native is driven by the host: ControllerManager calls ControllerFeedback.enterNativeMode() when the output port opens and leaveNativeMode() (switch LEDs black, then the leave message) on disconnect, reset() and shutdown(); a JVM shutdown hook, installed once, calls shutdown() so quitting releases the device. A crash leaves the device in native mode until it is replugged.
  • NativeSysex builds F0 <header> ... messages: enter/leave (00 01/00 00), indicator config (01 00 knob type detent detentColor, type 0 dot / 1 bar) and switch colour (01 01 knob r g b, 7 bits each). One setting per message: hardware showed that concatenated configs are misparsed. Blended types look identical to plain ones and are not offered. The header and the ring style per MeterType live in the profile (output.native), so a tweak is a JSON edit.
  • Messages: knob turn ch0 CC = knob (64 + delta), knob press ch1, side buttons ch2 CC 0-5 (left top/middle/bottom, right top/middle/bottom), ring position ch0 CC = knob. Hardware banks, ring brightness and animations do not exist.
  • MidiSink.sendSysex has a no-op default. CcQueue keeps SysEx in a separate FIFO that is never coalesced and is drained before control changes, so the mode switch always precedes the writes that depend on it; DeviceSink.close waits (up to 300 ms) for it to empty.
  • ControllerFeedback in native mode has one target per knob and sends the style when KnobLight.meterType changes and the colour when the RGB changes, both ahead of the ring CC; resync() forgets both. banks.virtual means the profile's banks.pages are the app's own pages: inputs need bankStride 0, there is no banks.switch, and ControllerRuntime.stepBank finds its position from KnobSurface.currentPageId because activeBank stays null.
  • Two profiles can fit one device name (stock and XT). ControllerProfileStore.matchFor(deviceName, preferredId) takes the user's per-device choice (controllerProfileChoices preference, keyed by the device name without its [hw:...] port suffix) and falls back to the first match; the choice is made in the Controller Profiles section of the MIDI preferences, never automatically.
  • The firmware licence (DJTT) forbids redistributing modified builds: the app never bundles the firmware, and the guide only describes the mode.

docs.title: Web Subsystem & Broadcast Protocol
docs.text: This document provides a technical specification for Liquid LSD's browser-based WebGL2 visualizer, live WebSocket broadcast relay, and desktop-to-web synchronization architecture.

docs.title: 1. System Topology & Architecture
docs.text:
Liquid LSD's web subsystem enables zero-latency live visual streaming without video transcoding by transmitting lightweight mathematical state representations over WebSockets to client-side WebGL2 renderers.

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ DESKTOP APPLICATION                                          │
│                                                              │
│  Mixer / Deck Engine ──► WebPresetSerializer (JSON)          │
│                               │                              │
│                               ▼ (throttled, 5-60 Hz)         │
│  BroadcastEngine-IO Thread ──► java.net.http.WebSocket       │
└───────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                │ WSS: ?role=broadcast&key=<token>
                                ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ NODE.JS RELAY SERVER (server/server.js)                      │
│                                                              │
│  - Authentication & Role Verification                        │
│  - Active Broadcaster Arbitration                            │
│  - Merged State Cache (late joiners get current state)       │
│  - Low-Latency Fan-Out Distribution                          │
└───────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                │ WSS: ?role=viewer
                                ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ BROWSER CLIENT (web/)                                        │
│                                                              │
│  - Autopilot Playlist Manager (autopilot.js)                 │
│  - Web Audio DSP Graph & Beat Tracker (dsp.js)               │
│  - Beat-Clock Extrapolation (renderer.js)                    │
│  - WebGL2 Multi-Pass Pipeline & CRT Post-Processing          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 2. WebSocket Wire Protocol (v2)
docs.text: The relay server and browser clients exchange compact JSON messages. Every state_full carries "v": 2; a client that speaks another version ignores it (and the deltas that follow, until a full snapshot of its version arrives). Values on the wire are the desktop's evaluated parameter values, rounded to 4 decimals, so the browser runs no modulators in live mode and matches the desktop exactly.

docs.title: 1. Full State Snapshot (state_full)
docs.text:
Sent when the broadcaster connects, when a preset or setlist changes, and by the relay to a viewer joining mid-session (built from the relay's merged state, not the broadcaster's last snapshot).

{
  "type": "state_full",
  "v": 2,
  "clock": { "beats": 812.4, "bpm": 126.0 },
  "preset": {
    "deckA": {
      "source": "dynamic_spiral",
      "params": { "MaxPoints": 500.0, "Scale": 0.5, "HueOffset": 0.2 },
      "viewZoom": 1.0, "viewRotateZ": 0.0, "globalAlpha": 1.0,
      "fx": {
        "0": { "id": "feedback", "dryWet": 1.0, "params": { "fbDecay": 0.65, "fbGain": 0.48 } },
        "1": null,
        "2": null
      },
      "fxDryWet": 1.0
    },
    "deckB": { "empty": true },
    "deckBG": { "empty": true },
    "mixer": {
      "balance": 0.0, "alpha": 1.0, "levelA": 1.0, "levelB": 1.0, "levelBG": 1.0,
      "transition": "linear_crossfade", "transitionParams": {},
      "fx": { "0": null, "1": null, "2": null }, "fxDryWet": 1.0
    }
  }
}
  • params is keyed by the exact parameter name: the ISF input NAME the shader uniform uses (Mandala uses its own names, e.g. Hue Offset). The browser looks the name up in the source's ISF header.
  • fx is an object keyed "0".."2", not an array, so a delta can address one slot parameter. An empty slot is null. dryWet is the effective wet amount (zero for a disabled slot, scaled by the desktop's FX dip). fxDryWet is the effective chain wet. The master chain is mixer.fx / mixer.fxDryWet.
  • balance is the crossfader mapped to 0..1 (the transition's progress). transition is a transition id from web/catalog.json; unknown ids fall back to linear_crossfade.
  • mandala (Mandala decks only) holds the shader-ready uniforms (uL1..uL4 already normalised, uA..uD from the selected recipe, uThickness, uHueOffset, uHueSweep, uDepth, uMaxR), because the browser has no recipe table.
  • broadcaster (optional string, at most 40 characters) is the broadcaster's name from BroadcastPreferences.broadcasterName, for the web TV's LIVE title card. It rides inside preset so the relay's merged state and the deltas carry it with no relay change (a delta's null clears it); clients that do not know it ignore it, so the protocol stays v2.
  • empty: true marks an empty deck; a source the web cannot draw (external video) is sent with an id the catalog does not know and renders as nothing.

docs.title: 2. Throttled Delta Update (state_delta)
docs.text:
Streamed at BroadcastPreferences.targetFps (5-60 Hz). patch is a recursive diff against the last state sent: only changed keys appear, and null means the key was removed or the slot emptied. An empty patch is a once-a-second heartbeat that only carries the clock.

{
  "type": "state_delta",
  "clock": { "beats": 812.9, "bpm": 126.0 },
  "patch": {
    "mixer": { "balance": 0.52 },
    "deckA": { "fx": { "0": { "params": { "fbDecay": 0.7 } } } }
  }
}

docs.title: 3. Broadcaster Handshake (broadcaster_online / broadcaster_offline)
docs.text: Dispatched by the relay server to all connected viewers when the desktop broadcaster connects or disconnects: - broadcaster_online: Viewers smoothly transition from Autopilot mode to the live broadcaster state, and the TV station badge flips to SPAZ RADIO • LIVE. - broadcaster_offline: Viewers smoothly fade back to local autonomous Autopilot playlist cycles.

docs.title: Relay state (server/state.js)
docs.text: The relay keeps the broadcast state merged: each state_full replaces it, each state_delta is applied to it (a null deletes the key). A viewer that joins mid-session is sent a state_full built from it, with clock.beats advanced by the time since it was recorded, so it starts on the right beat. Messages of another protocol version are relayed but never cached. Tests: cd server && npm test (no ws needed).

docs.title: 3. Beat Clock
docs.text:
Every message carries clock: {beats, bpm}, the desktop's synchronised beat count and tempo at the moment of sending. The browser stores it with the local performance.now() at arrival and extrapolates (beats + elapsed * bpm / 60) for every lfo/beatSine modulator and any web-side evaluation, so in live mode it needs no beat detection of its own. Network latency (tens of milliseconds) is not compensated; the once-a-second heartbeat keeps drift from accumulating. Outside a live broadcast the client tracks the radio stream's own beat (below), so beat-synced modulators land on the music's beats there too.

Standalone beat tracking (web/onset-worklet.js, web/beattrack.js). An AudioWorklet computes an onset envelope at audio rate, one value per 10 ms (rise in log energy of the bass below 150 Hz, weighted double, plus the full signal), so its timing does not depend on the frame rate. Each value is stamped with the performance.now() time it is heard (AudioContext.getOutputTimestamp), so output latency is compensated. BeatTracker keeps 8 s of envelope and, every 250 ms: estimates the tempo by autocorrelation (70-180 BPM, plus the second harmonic, under a log-Gaussian prior centred on 120 BPM so it does not lock to double or half time; a fast track such as 174 BPM drum and bass is followed at half time, every kick still on a whole or half beat), fine-tunes the period by +-2% to the one whose comb peaks highest, and finds the phase with a comb filter. Confidence is how far the best phase stands above the average, and is zero unless the older and newer halves of the window agree on the grid (random onsets line up across the whole window, a real beat lines up in both halves). Tempo changes need three agreeing estimates. BeatClock turns confident estimates into anchors for a BeatFlywheel (the live-mode flywheel): two readings in a row must agree on the phase, a small backward error is absorbed by coasting and a large one jumps forward to the next beat, so the beat count never runs backward. With no audio or no clear beat it coasts at the last tempo (120 BPM to start). cvState.beatLocked is true while a confident estimate arrived in the last 4 s. Without AudioWorklet support the per-frame onset strength feeds the same tracker. Checks: node --test web/tools/beattrack.test.mjs (synthetic envelopes: tempos, off-beat hats, missing kicks, tempo changes, noise, clock lock) and node web/checks/beat_check.mjs [bpm ...] (a synthetic track through the real worklet in headless Firefox; fails unless every kick lands within 30 ms of a beat).

The autopilot runs on this clock. settings.json holds are in bars (fgHoldBars 16, bgHoldBars 32) and fades in beats (fgFadeBeats 4, bgFadeBeats 8). A change starts FadeBeats before the first bar line after the hold and finishes on it, so a new look arrives on the bar. The next preset (with its chain and transition) is built during the hold, so the change is not delayed by fetching. Bar lines are every 4 beats of the clock's own count; the clock does not know where the music's bar starts (downbeat detection is not done).

Song sections (web/energy.js). EnergyWatch follows the low end (0.7 bass + 0.3 amp): a 1.5 s level against a 20 s reference. A breakdown is the level under 45% of the reference for 3 s (not during the first 20 s, and not in silence); the reference freezes during it, so a drop is the level back above 85% of the pre-breakdown reference after at least 4 s (a shorter dip just ends the breakdown, and a calm look it brought in leaves again at the next bar line). A breakdown longer than 60 s becomes the new normal. dsp.js publishes cvState.section and cvState.drops (and cvState.energy, the watcher itself, for tuning); on a breakdown the autopilot brings in a look tagged ambient or build (from either playlist) at the next bar line and builds a hard / bass-gated look, which cuts in on the drop with a half-beat crossfade through settings.json dropTransition (laser_drop_flash, kept out of the regular transitions rotation). HOLD overrides both. node --test web/tools/energy.test.mjs; ui_check.mjs drives a breakdown and a drop through the real page.

docs.title: 4. Browser-Side Web Audio DSP Graph (dsp.js)
docs.text:
In standalone web mode or Autopilot mode, the client performs real-time audio analysis on the Icecast stream (https://radio.spaz.org:8060/radio.ogg) via the Web Audio API:

Audio Element (Icecast stream)
     │
     ▼
createMediaElementSource() ──► GainNode (Rotary Volume Dial: V²) ──► AudioDestination
     │
     ├─► BiquadFilter (Lowpass 150Hz)  ─► AnalyserNode ─► RMS (audio_bass, audio_flux_bass)
     ├─► BiquadFilter (Bandpass ~1kHz) ─► AnalyserNode ─► RMS (audio_mid, audio_flux_mid)
     ├─► BiquadFilter (Highpass 5kHz)  ─► AnalyserNode ─► RMS (audio_high, audio_flux_high)
     ├─► Broadband AnalyserNode ──────────────────────► RMS (audio_amp, audio_flux_amp)
     └─► AudioWorklet lsd-onset (10 ms onset envelope) ─► BeatTracker ─► BeatClock
                                                          (tempo, phase)  (totalBeats, bpm, beatLocked)

The audio_* values feed the modulators (evaluator.js) each frame; totalBeats and bpm drive every lfo/seq/beatSine modulator and the autopilot.

docs.title: 5. Desktop-to-Web Synchronization & Drift Tracking
docs.text: To maintain 1:1 visual parity without manual dual-maintenance: - Authoritative Source: Desktop GLSL shaders (src/main/resources/shaders/, library/sources/) and algorithmic Kotlin math files (Evaluators.kt, WebPresetSerializer.kt) are the sole sources of truth. (icosa_h3 and dynamic_spiral are now pure ISF v2.0 shaders rather than Kotlin-backed generators — see DECISIONS.md's "Standardization on Pure ISF v2.0 Shaders" — so their web ports are tracked as shader files, not algorithm files.) - Sync Manifest (web/sync_manifest.json): Authoritative mapping of desktop files to WebGL2 / ES module equivalents with tracked SHA-256 hashes. - Sync CLI Tool (scripts/sync_web.py): - --check: Compares actual files against manifest hashes and transpiled sources; fails with exit code 1 if drift exists. - --apply: Automatically transpiles desktop #version 330 core GLSL shaders to WebGL2 #version 300 es (precision highp float;). - --mark-synced <target>: Updates recorded hashes for verified manual Kotlin-to-JS algorithm ports. - Evaluator parity (web/evaluator.js): a port of ModulatableParameter.evaluate(), Evaluators.kt and WaveformMath.kt. It is checked by value, not by hash: WebEvaluatorVectorsTest runs the real desktop evaluator under simulated time and writes web/tools/evaluator_vectors.json (and fails when that file is stale, so a desktop change cannot go unnoticed); node --test web/tools/evaluator.test.mjs replays the vectors through the JS port. After changing desktop modulation, regenerate with UPDATE_WEB_VECTORS=1 ./gradlew test --tests '*WebEvaluatorVectorsTest*', then fix the port until the node test passes. beatPhase and sampleAndHold are no longer registered in CVRegistry, so the desktop skips them and the web does not implement them. - ISF assets and the catalog: sync_web.py --apply also copies default_filters and default_transitions into web/shaders/fx/ and web/shaders/transitions/ (same transpile: ES 3.00 header, uniform initialisers dropped) and regenerates web/catalog.json, the list of sources, filters and transitions the client can load. Ids are file stems, the same ids the desktop registries use. --check fails if the catalog is stale. - Content formats (web/preset.js, web/mandala.js): the autopilot reads the desktop's own formats. web/presets/*.lsd are DeckPresetDto files (a preset carries no FX); parseDeckPreset keeps each ParameterDto for evaluator.js and resolves randomizeBase once at load. FX come from .lsdfxchain (FXChainDto) files in web/content/fxchains/ (copied from defaults/fx_chains) and web/fxchains/ (web-authored, web-*; the desktop's stock chains have no modulation, so the rotation uses reactive web-* versions of them, generated in batch 7 of gen_web_presets.py; no web chain strobes, for photosensitive viewers); transitions from .lsdtrans in web/content/transitions/. web/catalog.json lists all of them. A playlist line is preset or preset | fxchain; with no pin, settings.json fxChains rotates (empty = no FX) and transitions picks each crossfade's transition. Mandala is evaluated by mandala.js, a port of Mandala.kt's recipe selection and uniforms over web/mandala_recipes.json (generated from MandalaLibrary.kt); web/tools/mandala_vectors.json pins the selection to the desktop. Validate authored content with node --test web/tools/content.test.mjs (validate_content.mjs checks ids, parameter names against the shader headers, ParameterDto fields and modulators; this includes the desktop's stock chains and transitions copied into web/content/, so a stock chain naming a parameter its effect no longer has fails the test, where the desktop would silently ignore it). node web/checks/gpu_bench.mjs [WxH ...] times every source on this machine's GPU (gl.finish() per frame, so the throttled headless frame timer does not matter). - REACT and the desktop Audio Response: both scale the audio CV signals before any modulator reads them (web: renderer.js multiplies evalCtx.cv by viewerState.react; desktop: AudioEngine.response after auto gain), so web/evaluator.js has no reactivity input of its own. The desktop auto gain (AudioAgc) is not ported: web/dsp.js still normalises bands by the fixed 0.25 / 0.05 / 0.1 scales. - Stock looks (scripts/gen_stock_web_presets.py): web/presets/stock-<source>.lsd are generated from the desktop's stock_defaults/sources/<id>.json. The sparse file is completed into full ParameterDtos (baseValue from the shader's DEFAULT, or the middle of the range; randomizeBase rolls it at every load), modulators (including bypassed alternates) are copied as they are, and tags come from the active modulators (bass, kick, mid, amp, high, bar) plus fullframe / sparse. Sources with no active modulator (Fluid Ink) or not in the catalog (Fractal Flame) are skipped. Re-run it after a stock default changes; the rotation gate and content.test.mjs guard the result. - Authoring web presets (scripts/gen_web_presets.py): the web-* presets and chains are generated from short definitions (the generated files are the source of truth once committed; hand edits are fine). Recipes: pulse(beats, depth) is an envelope that peaks on the beat; lfo(beats, depth, wave) is a beat-synced LFO (period in beats; 16 = four bars); kick/hat follow audio_flux_bass/audio_flux_high; bass/mid/high/amp follow the band levels with attack/decay smoothing; gate(source, threshold, depth) stays silent until the signal passes the threshold. A gate only works on a parameter whose base is its minimum (0 = "off"): below the threshold the amount goes negative and clamps at the minimum, so on any other base the silent value dips below base. Parameters in the shaders are normalised 0..1 or -1..1, so ADD depths are fractions of the range (half the range on bipolar parameters); lfo on a unipolar parameter sweeps base..base+depth. Tag a preset with the behaviours it promises (beat, bar, bass, kick, mid, high, amp, bass-gated); node --test web/tools/reactivity.test.mjs verifies each tag is backed by a parameter that moves. The same test is the rotation gate: every preset in a playlist and every chain in settings.json fxChains or a playlist pin must move with some audio signal or with the beat (a beat-synced LFO counts), so nothing deaf reaches the web TV. It also fails on any modulator on a rate parameter (a name ending in Speed, Spin or Rate) that the shader does not integrate: TIME * Speed moves the phase by TIME times the change, so after a few minutes on air even a small wobble jumps the picture every frame. Every stock source and filter now integrates its rates (LSD_PHASES, see rendering.md), so the check only bites on a new shader that multiplies by TIME. Each source has a groove, a hard and an ambient preset (ambient ones go in the BG playlist). Presets of sources that fill the frame with colour are tagged fullframe (FULL_FRAME_SOURCES in the generator); web/pairing.js makes the autopilot skip chains with a feedback or bloom slot for them, since those wash a full frame out to one flat colour, and presets of sources drawn as fine dots or thin lines (SPARSE_SOURCES: dynamic_spiral, harmonograph) are tagged sparse and skip chains with pixelate, halftone, polar_tunnel, luma_displace or directional_blur, which average or smear them away to black; and render_check picks chains the same way; content.test.mjs validates names and ranges, and node web/checks/render_check.mjs renders every preset (look at the PNGs: sources differ in how much they show at default settings; hyper_slice blows out under strong feedback, gyroid_hyperspace is black unless Brightness/Zoom are raised, a solid gyroid surface is mostly black). RC_EXTRA=specs.json RC_ONLY=name renders ad-hoc looks, and RC_LOUD=1 adds a <name>_loud frame per preset with the audio signals held high, to compare against the silent frame. - Render graph (web/isf.js, web/graph.js): isf.js wraps ISF source into GLSL ES 3.00 (a port of ISFParser.buildGLSLFragmentShader) and runs multi-pass shaders (PASSES, TARGET, PERSISTENT ping-pong, FLOAT, $WIDTH/$HEIGHT expressions). graph.js is Renderer.renderDeck/renderMixer: deck source, 3-slot FX chain, transition, composite over BG, master FX chain. Assets compile lazily on first use (Library), and a not-yet-loaded effect is skipped for those frames. Mandala is the only source drawn outside the graph. IMPORTED assets and audio/audioFFT inputs are not supported (nothing bundled uses them). - No signal (web/dsp.js, shaders/crt_post.frag): with the TV on, a stream that failed, stalled or stayed under 0.004 amp for 4 s sets cvState.noSignal; the CRT pass fades to snow (uNoSignal), the OSD says NO SIGNAL, and the stream is reloaded with a fresh URL every 10 s until it plays. Not during a live broadcast. ?nostatic turns it off for the headless checks, which have no audio. - GPU tier (web/renderer.js, settings.json heavySources / gpuProbe): at the first power-on the renderer draws gpuProbe.source (pseudo_kleinian, the heaviest) at 960x540 with gl.finish() after each frame: two untimed warm-up frames, then up to four timed ones, stopping after one if it is over twice maxMs. Only if the average is at most maxMs (12 ms) does autopilot.setHeavyAllowed(true) let presets of the heavySources into the rotation (playlist picks, CH up, breakdown and drop picks); otherwise they are skipped. Until the probe has run, heavy sources are off. ?heavy=1 / ?heavy=0 override it; window.LSD.gpu shows {state, ms, heavy}. The list comes from node web/checks/gpu_bench.mjs on an Intel UHD Tiger Lake GT1 (sources over ~15 ms at 768x432, plus Lenia and Reaction-Diffusion, whose fixed-size grids cost ~17-19 ms at any resolution); the probe measured 52 ms there. - Render resolution and prewarm (web/renderer.js): decks and the mixer render at a fraction of the canvas, capped at 1920x1080 worth of pixels, and the CRT pass scales up. The fraction steps through 1.0 / 0.85 / 0.7 / 0.55 / 0.4: down after 2 s of frames averaging over ~22 ms, up after 15 s under ~17.5 ms, at most every 3 s; a step up that has to be undone becomes the ceiling, so it never oscillates (each step reallocates the targets, which resets feedback). window.LSD.renderSize() reports [w, h, scale]. autopilot.setPrewarm gets a function that starts loading and compiling a queued look's source, FX and transition (Library.get), called when the next look is built during the hold. - Wake lock (web/ui.js): a screen wake lock is held while powered on, taken again on visibilitychange (browsers drop it when the page is hidden) and released at power off; viewerState.awake reports it. - Media Session (web/ui.js): metadata = Icecast title, artist Spaz Radio, album Liquid LSD · <look> (or LIVE), icons as artwork; updated on power, look and title changes. play/pause/stop press the power switch, nexttrack/previoustrack are CH up/down (locked while live like the buttons). - App and kiosk (web/manifest.webmanifest, web/sw.js, web/ui.js): the manifest makes the TV installable (fullscreen, the 192/512 icons). sw.js is network first for every same-origin GET (updates always land when online) with the cached copy as the offline fallback; the app shell is cached at install one file at a time, and other origins (stream, Icecast status, relay) are never intercepted. Bump CACHE to drop old copies. It is not registered under ?nolive (the headless checks). ?kiosk adds body.kiosk (no TV body, picture fills the window, cursor hidden after 3 s idle) and presses power after load; when the browser blocks audio, the OSD asks for a click or key and the first one starts the sound. - Service menu (web/menu.js, web/ui.js): createMenu(screen, rows) draws rows {label, value(), step?(dir), run?(), locked?()} over the picture; while open it owns the keyboard (the CH arrows do nothing) and the OSD is hidden. ui.js rows: SYNC (viewerState.syncMs, -100..+400 ms, 10 ms steps), TAP SYNC, Announce looks (viewerState.announce, off by default: a new look is named only when the viewer pressed CH/FX in the last 4 s, or on I / a picture click), REACT (25-400%, default 200%) and TIME (drive the dials), Reduced motion and Big GPU looks (viewerState.reducedMode / heavyMode: auto / on / off; heavy on/off overrides the GPU probe, which only applies itself in auto), Reset, Exit. Each row's help is its hover tooltip and the menu's bottom line while selected. Stored in localStorage (lsd.sync, lsd.announce, lsd.reduced, lsd.heavy). - SYNC (web/sync.js): heardBeats(now, syncMs) is the beat the viewer hears (live: clock.read(now - sync); standalone: totalBeats extrapolated from cvState.beatsAtMs, minus sync); the renderer evaluates modulators on it and on the audio signals read syncMs late from a DelayLine (a negative SYNC advances the beat only). The beat LED uses it too. TAP SYNC: 8 taps, errors folded into [-100 ms, beat - 100 ms) so a long delay is not read as early, median = SYNC (rounded to 10 ms), refused if the middle taps spread over 150 ms or the beat is not locked. node --test web/tools/sync.test.mjs. - Reduced motion (viewerState.reducedNow, autopilot.setReducedMotion): auto follows prefers-reduced-motion (live, via its change event). When on: the renderer caps REACT at 1.2 (the default is 2.0); the autopilot skips looks tagged hard, chains tagged strobe / glitch and the luminous_flash / cyber_datamosh / film_burn transitions, makes no drop cut, and doubles crossfade length; turning it on rebuilds the queued look. - Tempo-aware picks (autopilot.tempoWeight, weightedPick): with a locked beat and random order, the next foreground look is a weighted random pick among playable lines: < 95 BPM ambient/groove/mid x3, hard x0.3; 95-125 groove x2; > 125 hard/kick/hat x2.5, ambient x0.5; everything else x1. Unlocked or sequential order: unchanged. Tested in tools/autopilot.test.mjs. - Answering chains (pairing.js dominantBand, bands, chainAnswers): audio modulators are grouped into bands (low = bass + kick, mid, high). A chain whose modulation follows only the look's dominant band is skipped for it (the autopilot's pickChain falls back to any fitting chain if none answers). With today's content 18 of 35 chains answer a low-end look. reactivity.test.mjs checks every rotation look has an answering chain and at least a third of the chains answer low-end looks; render_check picks the same way. - LIVE title card (web/ui.js, index.html #title-card): on lsd-broadcast-status live, a 4.5 s CSS ident (scanline roll-in) shows LIVE and autopilotState.broadcaster; the OSD keeps the name while live. The name comes from preset.broadcaster (see the wire protocol). - Branding (index.html, tv.css, ui.js): #nameplate (link, excluded from the click-to-power area, hidden in kiosk); #ident at the first power-on of a page load (logo icon-512.png, 3.6 s); #about (MENU › ABOUT; the QR code for the site is inline SVG, made with segno); #osd-brand on I / picture clicks only; #bumper every 30 min while on and not live (BUMPER_EVERY_MS, timer restarts at power-on); the LIVE card's "from Liquid LSD". While a card is up the OSD steps aside (.card-up). Open Graph / Twitter tags point at og-tv.jpg (1200x630 screenshot of the TV). - Viewer controls (web/ui.js): CH up/down, FX, HOLD, TIME (bars per look) and REACT (a factor on every audio_* signal in renderer.js, so gates and depths respond as if the music were louder or quieter) call advanceForeground / previousForeground / nextFxChain / setHold / setHoldBars in autopilot.js. Both are changeChannel(±1): the next playable playlist line up or down from the one on air (or the one a quick earlier press is still building), whatever the autopilot's own order; a line in the on-air history comes back with its deck, chain and transition. The OSD listens for lsd-now-showing (fired when a crossfade starts) and lsd-broadcast-status (fired when the relay goes live or offline; the controls lock while live). Now playing comes from the Icecast status-json.xsl every 30 s. node web/checks/ui_check.mjs drives every control in the real page in headless Firefox, including the live lock. - Headless checks (web/checks/): node web/checks/shader_check.mjs compiles every catalog shader in headless Firefox; node web/checks/render_check.mjs [outDir] drives the real app through every source, filter, transition and bundled preset, writes PNGs, and fails on blank frames, console errors or GL errors. Both need only firefox and node; software GL is fine. - Beat and audio parity (web/beatclock.js, web/dsp.js): live mode runs BeatFlywheel on the wire clock (getSynchronizedTotalBeats semantics plus blending of each anchor against network jitter); standalone runs BeatClock on the stream's tracked beat (section 3). dsp.js publishes audio_* and audio_flux_* with the desktop's scaling (AudioEngine: RMS / 0.25, band flux / 0.05, amp flux = (2 bass + 0.8 mid + 0.3 high flux) / 0.1). Beat tracking only runs from the radio stream, so it only matters standalone. - Continuous Integration: Gradle task ./gradlew checkWebSync and JVM unit test WebSyncTest.kt guard against drift on every build.

docs.title: 6. Publishing the Web TV
docs.text: The web TV is served at https://spaz.org/tv/: Apache on spaz.org has Alias /tv /www/spaz/htdocs/lsd-relay/public, a folder gj can write over SSH (key login). scripts/publish_web_tv.sh rsyncs web/ there (checksums, so only changed files go; web/checks/ and web/tools/ stay behind). --dry-run shows the changes, --delete also removes server files that are no longer in web/ (older deployments left prototype shaders and desktop presets there). The relay's code lives next to it in /www/spaz/htdocs/lsd-relay/ and is deployed separately (section 7).

docs.title: 6b. Embed Mode (?embed)
docs.text:
index.html?embed is the web TV as a component, built for Spaz Radio's Android WebView (plan: .planning/spazradio-embed-plan.md). embedmode.js exports the flag; it implies the kiosk layout and adds body.embed (tv.css: chrome hidden, pointer-events: none everywhere, so the host's panels own all touches).

  • Audio in: dsp.js skips the <audio> element and builds the same analysis graph from a feed-worklet.js node (lsd-feed, no inputs) whose output goes to analysisIn; the analysers also hang off a muted gain to the destination so the graph keeps being pulled. feedring.js is the worklet's mono ring buffer with a linear resampler (stream rate to context rate), a 40 ms prefill, and a skip-ahead to 80 ms when more than 300 ms is queued, so the picture stays close to the sound. feedPCM(data, rate) accepts Int16Array, Float32Array, ArrayBuffer (little-endian int16) or base64 and posts to the worklet (transferring buffers it decoded itself). It returns false until the graph exists (LSD.feedReady(); lsd-embed-ready event).
  • Silence is not "no signal": updateSignal pins cvState.noSignal false in embed mode; there is no reconnect logic.
  • What is off: microphone (micAvailable() false), service worker, status-json polling, media session, wake lock, bumper, ident, and the relay (autopilot.setRelayEnabled, off until the live option).
  • Host API (embed.js, installed on window.LSD by renderer.js): feed, feedReady, setOption(name, value) (quality, reactivity, reducedMotion, live, sync), pause, resume, next, prev, hold. quality: 'low' turns heavy looks off and floors the render scale at the third step (adapt.ceiling); pause stops the render loop and suspends the AudioContext, resume restarts both and resets the frame clock.
  • Frame rate over sharpness: in embed mode renderer.js uses a 1280x720-pixel budget, seven scale steps down to 25%, steps down after 1 s above 19 ms (not 2 s above 22 ms) with 1.5 s between steps, and forces gpu.heavy false (the probe's gl.finish() returned in 0.4 ms on a Pixel 7a, so it can't tell). ?embed&debug shows fps, render size, scale and heavy state in a corner and logs a status line every 2 s.
  • Sync: the host's sound reaches the speaker after the audio sink's buffer, so the feed leads what is heard; set the sync option to delay the picture to match.
  • Checks: node --test web/tools/feedring.test.mjs; node web/checks/embed_check.mjs (headless Firefox: loads the page with ?embed, pushes a synthetic 124 BPM kick track in real time, expects the signals, the beat lock, no snow in silence, options, pause/resume and a non-black picture).

docs.title: 6c. Content Updates for the Spaz Radio App
docs.text:
scripts/publish_web_tv.sh also publishes a signed manifest to https://spaz.org/tv/update/ so the app can fetch new presets and playlists without an app release. scripts/make_content_manifest.py lists the data files of web/ (presets, playlists, shaders, FX chains, transitions, catalog.json, settings.json, mandala_recipes.json, autopilot.json) with sha256 and size; JS/HTML/CSS are never listed (the engine ships with the app). manifest.json.sig is an ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 signature over the exact manifest bytes. The private key is ~/.config/liquid-lsd/content-signing.pem (not in the repo; back it up, losing it means an app release to change the key); the public key is scripts/content_signing_pub.pem.

Publishing validates content first (web/tools/content.test.mjs) and uploads the manifest last. CONTENT_ENGINE in the script is the engine level the content needs: bump it when new content depends on a web feature old apps lack, so those apps skip the update. rsync --delete leaves update/ alone.

docs.title: 7. Relay Server Operations (server/server.js)
docs.text: The relay server is a zero-dependency Node.js service using ws.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
• LSD_PORT: Port to listen on (default: 9004).
  • LSD_HOST: Host interface to bind to (default: 0.0.0.0).
  • LSD_TOKEN: Broadcaster authorization secret. Required: the relay exits at startup without it, so no shared default can let a stranger broadcast.

docs.title: CLI Management
docs.text:
# Run standalone
./server/lsd_relay start

# Or deploy via PM2
cd server
npm install
pm2 start server.js --name lsd-relay
pm2 save && pm2 startup

docs.title: Health & Monitoring Endpoint
docs.text:
GET /health returns live telemetry JSON:

{
  "status": "ok",
  "viewers": 42,
  "broadcasterConnected": true,
  "uptime": 128450
}
  • Fullscreen and microphone (web/ui.js, web/dsp.js): S / MENU › Fullscreen / double-click all run toggleFullscreen on #tv-screen-area. A / MENU › Input run toggleMic → dsp.setMic: every analyser and the onset worklet hang off one analysisIn gain that the radio's element source and the getUserMedia stream (echo cancellation, noise suppression and AGC off) both feed; only the radio also goes to the volume gain, so the mic never plays back. The radio element is paused while the mic is in, reconnect() is skipped, silence still shows NO SIGNAL, stopAudio releases the mic, and the lsd-mic event refreshes the menu (also when the browser revokes the mic). The headless check only verifies the menu rows; the mic itself needs a real browser.

docs.title: Shaders License Audit Log
docs.text: This document tracks the licensing, authorship, and commercial distribution rights for all Interactive Shader Format (ISF) visual shaders, filters, and generators bundled with Liquid LSD.

docs.title: Licensing Policy
docs.text: To preserve the right to commercially distribute or monetize Liquid LSD: 1. Permissive Licenses Only: All bundled shaders must use permissive licenses (MIT, BSD-2/3-Clause, Apache 2.0, CC0 / Public Domain) or be original cleanroom implementations. 2. Strictly Prohibited: No shaders under copyleft (GPL/LGPL/AGPL), non-commercial licenses (CC-BY-NC), or all-rights-reserved copyright may be bundled. 3. Attribution Preservation: Copyright notices and original author attributions are preserved in the shader header metadata (CREDIT).

Tunnel Scenes library/sources/tunnel_scenes/tunnel_scenes.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved Analytic ray-plane and ray-cylinder tunnel scenes (grid, Truchet, polygonal wormhole) with no ray marching. Video Feedback library/sources/video_feedback/video_feedback.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved Video-feedback loop on a persistent 512 x 512 frame with zoom, rotation, drift, decay and seed shapes. Hyperbolic Tiling library/sources/hyperbolic_tiling/hyperbolic_tiling.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved Poincare-disk {P,Q} tiling by Coxeter-triangle mirror folds and circle inversion. Cyclic CA library/sources/cyclic_ca/cyclic_ca.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved Cyclic cellular automaton on a persistent 256 x 256 grid (Moore, von Neumann and extended neighbourhoods). Metaballs library/sources/metaballs/metaballs.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved 2D metaball field from 4 to 12 orbiting balls with shaded, contour, neon and two-tone styles. Wave Ripples library/sources/wave_ripples/wave_ripples.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved Interference of 2 to 8 travelling circular waves from orbiting sources. Aurora Ribbons library/sources/aurora_ribbons/aurora_ribbons.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved Layered aurora curtains over a starfield, with mountain and water-reflection options. Isometric Voxels library/sources/isometric_voxels/isometric_voxels.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved Isometric cube field with analytic per-layer occlusion. Halftone Matrix library/sources/halftone_matrix/halftone_matrix.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved Procedural halftone, LED-matrix, line-screen and CMYK-screen dot generator. Kali Set library/sources/kali_set/kali_set.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved 2D inversion-fold (Kali family) fractal with orbit-trap colouring. Girih Stars library/sources/girih_stars/girih_stars.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved Girih / Hankin strapwork on square, hexagonal and 4.8.8 lattices via wallpaper-group folding. Glitch Blocks library/sources/glitch_blocks/glitch_blocks.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved Procedural glitch generator (block displacement, tearing, RGB split, posterise). Voronoi Cells library/sources/voronoi_cells/voronoi_cells.fs Liquid LSD Engine (Cleanroom) MIT Approved Animated Worley / Voronoi cells with F1 and F2 shading styles.

docs.title: Algorithm Credits
docs.text:
• Mandelbox (mandelbox): the construction (box fold, sphere fold and scale applied to a point and iterated) was introduced by Tom Lowe (known as Tglad), around 2010. Only the published definition is used; the shader was written from the mathematics and no code of his or anyone else's was used.
  • Mandelbulb (mandelbulb): the triplex power map in spherical coordinates is due to Daniel White and Paul Nylander (2009). Only the published formulas are used; no shader code was copied.
  • Orbit traps (escape_time, mandelbox, mandelbulb, kifs, pseudo_kleinian, apollonian): the colouring idea of recording an orbit's closest approach to a chosen set is due to J. C. Hart.
  • Apollonian and Kleinian structures (apollonian, pseudo_kleinian): the sphere packings of Apollonius of Perga and F. Soddy, and the reflection and inversion groups of Poincare and Klein, are textbook mathematics; the shaders were derived from them directly.
  • KIFS (kifs): iterated function systems (Menger sponge, Sierpinski tetrahedron) are textbook mathematics; no third-party shader code was used.
  • Reaction Diffusion (reaction_diffusion): the Gray-Scott model is due to P. Gray and S. K. Scott, and the pattern map to John E. Pearson (1993). Only the published equations and the commonly published (feed, kill) regimes are used; no shader code was copied.
  • Fluid Ink (fluid_ink): the stable-fluids method is due to Jos Stam (1999); vorticity confinement to Fedkiw, Stam and Jensen (2001). Only the published method is used; no shader code was copied.
  • Lenia (lenia): the continuous cellular automaton is due to Bert Wang-Chak Chan (2019). Only the published kernel and growth formulas are used; no code was copied.
  • Quasicrystals (quasicrystal): the sum of cosine plane waves with 5-fold or higher rotational symmetry as a model of quasi-periodic order is due to de Bruijn (1981) and the physics of quasicrystals (Shechtman 1984). Only the mathematics is used.
  • Thin-film interference (thin_film): the optical path difference 2 n d cos(theta) is textbook optics.
  • Hyperbolic tilings (hyperbolic_tiling): Coxeter reflection groups and the Poincare disk model are textbook mathematics; no code was copied.
  • Cyclic cellular automata (cyclic_ca): the cyclic CA is due to David Griffeath and colleagues (1990s), and the Hodgepodge machine to Gerhardt and Schuster (1989). Only the published rules are used.
  • Metaballs (metaballs): the blobby-objects field model is due to Jim Blinn (1982).
  • Cellular noise (voronoi_cells): Steven Worley (1996). Only the published definition is used.
  • Kali set (kali_set): named after the Kali (Kaliset) inversion-fold iteration of the demoscene; only the mathematical definition z -> |z|/(z.z) - c was used.
  • Girih and Hankin strapwork (girih_stars): Hankin's polygons-in-contact method (described by Kaplan and others); only the geometric construction is used.
  • Fractal Flame (fractal_flame): implemented from the published description in Scott Draves and Erik Reckase, "The Fractal Flame Algorithm" (2003, revised 2008): the iterated function system with non-linear variations, the log-density tone mapping and the 49 variation formulas of its Appendix A. The 46 further variations (ids 49-97 apart from the four not built) were implemented from a written mathematical specification (.planning/flame-variations-spec.md), not from any flame renderer's source. How that specification was produced is recorded, with its open items, in docs/developer/clean_room_provenance.md; check it before relying on this paragraph for a release. No source code of flam3, Apophysis, Electric Sheep or any other flame renderer was read or copied (clean-room, the same approach as the beat tracker). No genome archive is bundled. Verify the exact authors, year and revision against the paper before citing it in a commercial release; a trademark search for the user-facing names is also still open.

docs.title: Command Line Usage & Startup Options
docs.text: Liquid LSD supports command-line startup options for headless automated capture, window resolution overrides, audio engine bypassing, and launching the isolated UI Lab sandbox.

docs.title: Quick Syntax
docs.text:
./gradlew run --args="[OPTIONS]"

Or when launching packaged executables:

./liquid-lsd [OPTIONS]

docs.title: 1. Automated UI Screenshot Capture
docs.text:
Capture a crisp PNG screenshot of the application window and exit automatically:

./gradlew run --args="--screenshot-ui=docs/assets/app-1080p.png --window=1920x1080 --screenshot-after-frames=5 --no-audio"
  • --screenshot-ui=<file.png>: Sets the target PNG image path.
  • --screenshot-after-frames=<N>: Sets the frame delay before capture (default: 5 frames) to allow UI layouts and font metrics to settle.

docs.title: 2. Window Resolution Override
docs.text:
Override startup window dimensions:

./gradlew run --args="--window=1280x720"

Or start in maximized mode:

./gradlew run --args="--window=maximized"

docs.title: 3. Audio Engine Bypass
docs.text:
Bypass JACK and JavaSound audio engine initialization for environments without physical or virtual sound cards:

./gradlew run --args="--no-audio"

docs.title: 4. UI Lab Component Sandbox
docs.text:
Launch an isolated UI component gallery sandbox to preview theme colors, Lucide icons, custom sliders, and status meters:

./gradlew run --args="--ui-lab --window=1280x720 --no-audio"

docs.title: 5. Headless Smoke Test
docs.text:
Run a headless multi-component smoke test and exit with a status code (0 on success), without opening a window:

./gradlew run --args="--smoke-test"

docs.title: 6. Help & Version
docs.text:
./gradlew run --args="--help"
./gradlew run --args="--version"
  • --help / -h: Prints all available startup options and exits.
  • --version / -v: Prints the application version and exits.

docs.title: 7. Automated Gradle Tasks
docs.text: Liquid LSD includes pre-configured Gradle tasks for automated asset generation: - ./gradlew captureResponsiveApp: Captures 1080p main workspace screenshot. - ./gradlew captureUiLab: Captures UI Lab gallery screenshot.

docs.title: Hardware Control
docs.text:
Liquid LSD can be played from a hardware controller, a tablet or a phone. There are three ways in; pick the one that matches what you own, and mix them freely.

You have Use Setup A DJ TechTools Midi Fighter Twister The built-in Twister profile Plug it in. Optional one-time settings file for the Midi Fighter Utility Any other MIDI controller (knobs, faders, pads, keyboard) MIDI Learn Enable MIDI, right-click a control, move a knob TouchOSC or another OSC app on a phone or tablet OSC Learn Enable the OSC server, point the app at your computer

MIDI and OSC are both off by default. Turn them on in Preferences (Ctrl+,) under MIDI Controls and OSC Controls. Each tab has a live monitor that shows every incoming message, which is the quickest way to check that a device is talking to the app.

docs.title: The Midi Fighter Twister
docs.text:
The Twister is the controller the app is built around. Its 16 encoders are the 16 knobs of the Performance Matrix: the 4×4 grid on the hardware mirrors the 4×4 grid on screen, and whatever a row is showing is what its encoders control.

  • Pages. The hardware banks (or, in native mode, the top-right side button) step through the Perform pages: A/B, BG/PV and MIXER. The screen follows the hardware, and clicking a tab on screen moves the encoders to match.
  • Effects. On an FX row the first knob is the chain's Super Knob and the other three are the slots' Metaknobs. A tap on a knob's switch bypasses a slot, and Shift + tap focuses it so the whole row becomes that effect's parameters.
  • Chain view. Shift + tap a deck's source knob and the whole Twister becomes that deck: its source row on top, then one row per FX slot, so all three effects are under your hands. The bottom-right side button turns Load on, which swaps the top row for loading: knob 4 scrolls the effect list and knobs 1-3 load the highlighted effect into slot 1, 2 or 3.
  • Browsing. The side buttons open the Library and the source and effect pickers, so you can load a source or effect without touching the mouse.
  • Lights. Rings show each knob's value. Knob 13 on the MIXER page pulses on the beat, shows the tempo and taps tempo when pushed. In Pickup mode, an FX slot waiting for the Super Knob blinks amber.
  • Native mode. With the optional XT firmware, rings change style to suit each parameter and the switch LEDs show the row colour.

Setup, every gesture, a worked example and troubleshooting are in Controller Profiles: Midi Fighter Twister. Jump straight to one-time setup, gestures, side buttons or the XT firmware mode. To change what a page controls, see Perform Pages.

docs.title: Other MIDI controllers
docs.text:
1. Connect the controller and enable Preferences → MIDI Controls → Enable MIDI Subsystem. New devices are picked up without restarting.
  2. Right-click the on-screen knob, slider or button you want to control. Choose Learn MIDI. It pulses while it waits.
  3. Move a knob or fader, or press a pad, on the controller. The two are now linked.
  4. Right-click again to cancel, or choose Clear MIDI Mapping to remove a link.

The app recognises what the control is (a continuous knob, a button, an endless encoder, pitch bend). Min and max, invert, smoothing and soft takeover (so a knob does not make a value jump after a preset change) are set per mapping in the MIDI tab. Mappings live in a profile you can save and switch, so a home setup and a gig setup can differ.

Buttons learn the same way: right-click A, B, AUTO or TAP, then press a pad. In Edit, any slider can be learned. Details: MIDI Hardware & Control Mappings.

docs.title: OSC and TouchOSC
docs.text:
1. Enable Preferences → OSC Controls → Enable OSC Server. It listens on UDP port 8000 and sends feedback on 9000; both can be changed.
  2. In your app, set the target to this computer's IP address and the same ports.
  3. Right-click a control in Liquid LSD, choose Learn OSC, then move a control in the app.

Macro knobs also answer /macro/<bank>/knob/1 to /8 with no mapping, and report their values back so a tablet layout stays in sync. OSC mappings are saved in profiles, one per app or layout. Details: OSC / TouchOSC Control Surfaces.

docs.title: Macro Controls & the Perform View
docs.text: Macro Controls give you a small number of physical-style knobs that each drive several parameters at once — the fast, tactile layer you reach for live instead of hunting through parameter grids. The Perform view builds on the same macro system to give you a 4×4 knob matrix purpose-built for live performance, with Edit underneath for everything else.

docs.title: Macro Controls
docs.text:
Macro knobs live in the Perform view 4×4 matrix, and they are edited in place. The right-hand column shows only the Mixer; there is no separate MACROS tab.

In the Edit view, select a macro knob in an expanded row. That row's left side switches to the target strip:

  • Line 1 — the knob's name (double-click to rename), its live value, Add Target / Cancel, one chip per target (1–4), a kebab menu (⋮), and a close button.
  • Line 2 — the selected target's settings (name, Min/Max, Curve, Link, Invert, Enabled).

FX rows show a read-only strip instead: FX knobs have a fixed role per mode (Super Knob + 3 Metaknobs, or Metaknob + 3 parameters when a slot is focused), so the strip names the role rather than offering targets.

docs.title: Adding targets to a knob
docs.text:
1. Click Add Target on a macro knob. It starts pulsing to show it's armed, and a banner appears: "ADD TARGET: Click any parameter slider or modulator property."
  2. Click the target:
  3. A parameter slider in a Edit parameter grid becomes a target through that parameter's base value.
  4. A modulator control in Edit's Modulation column — e.g. an LFO's Subdivision or Morph slider, or an envelope's Attack/Decay — becomes a target directly. This lets a macro knob speed up an LFO or shorten an envelope's decay, not just move a value.
  5. A toast confirms the target (e.g. "Added target: Knob 3 → Zoom [LFO 1 Morph]") and Add Target turns itself off.

A knob can only target parameters in its own deck and section:

  • Deck A SRC knobs target Deck A's SRC parameters only.
  • FX knobs (each deck's and Master's) follow their FX chain automatically and take no manual targets; the editors show them as "Driven by the FX chain".
  • Master and Transition knobs take Mixer parameters only, and FX Send knobs take the per-deck FX send only.
  • Global knobs can target anything.

If you click a parameter outside that section, the banner says "Cannot add target…" and Add Target stays armed, so you can click the right one. If you move to another section while Add Target is armed, it is cancelled. That includes Edit's SRC/FX tabs and the side rail. Master knobs aren't limited this way, and Transitions knobs can't be learned (they follow the active transition).

Each knob can hold up to 4 targets, so one knob can drive several parameters (or modulator properties) simultaneously — with independent settings per target.

docs.title: Editing a target
docs.text:
Selecting a knob shows its targets in the target strip (Edit view) and in the Modulation editor of the open Edit. For each target you can set:

  • Min / Max — the travel range the target maps onto, independent of the target's own range.
  • Curve — Linear, Exponential, Logarithmic, S-Curve, or Step (quantized into a fixed number of positions).
  • Link — which zone of the knob's travel this target responds to (Mixxx-style parameter linking). Instead of a plain dropdown, this is controlled via an intuitive vector transfer curve button displaying the exact response curve on the button face, with an adjacent [±] invert toggle:
  • Full (0-100%) [ / ] — tracks the entire knob travel.
  • 1st Half (0-50%) [ / ‾ ] — sweeps 0→1 across the first half of the turn, then holds at 1.0 for the rest of the travel.
  • 2nd Half (50-100%) [ _ / ] — holds at 0.0 for the first half, then sweeps 0→1 across the second.
  • Triangle (Peak) [ /\ ] — sweeps 0→1 up to center, then back down to 0 — useful for a target that should peak mid-turn and fall off at either extreme.
  • Bipolar (Center-0) [ \/ ] — 0.0 at center, rising to 1.0 at either end — useful for a target that should stay neutral at rest and react to turning the knob in either direction.
  • Invert Toggle [±] — dynamically flips the direction and mirrors the vector glyph geometry.

Left-click the link button to cycle through the modes; right-click to open a context menu and select directly. A common pattern: give one knob two targets, one on 1st Half and one on 2nd Half, to crossfade or choreograph between them from a single knob turn. - Live Value Meter Knob — on the second row of each target (to the left of Min/Max, Zone, and Curve), a rotary meter knob (the same crisp knob widget used in the parameter grid) displays the live evaluated output value in relation to the macro knob position. If you use a Triangle ramp (peak) curve or a half-turn zone, moving the macro knob from 0 to 1 lets you see the binding sweep (e.g. 0 → 1 → 0) in real time. Hovering over the knob displays exact numerical readouts. - Enabled — toggling a target off immediately hands the target field back to normal manual/mouse editing; toggling it back on resumes macro control.

The target name (e.g. Deck A/Mandala/L1) is a clickable link. Clicking it opens the corresponding deck's (or the Mixer's) Edit on the right sub-tab with the parameter selected, so you can immediately reach the parameter being controlled without hunting for it manually.

docs.title: Locked fields & Visual Indicators
docs.text:
Any parameter base value or modulator property that is the target of an enabled macro knob receives distinct visual cues in Edit:

  • Parameter grid:
  • The row displays an Electric Cyan left-accent border and a subtle cyan background tint.
  • An inline badge such as [K1] appears beside the parameter name, and the name is tinted Electric Cyan.
  • The "VAL" meter cell is outlined with a cyan border.
  • Hovering over the row or value cell shows a contextual tooltip identifying the controlling macro (e.g. Locked: Driven by Knob 1 (WARP) [K1]).

  • Clicking the row label, badge, or VAL cell selects that macro control and shows its target strip.

  • Modulation & Sliders:

  • An Electric Cyan bounding box and background highlight frames the entire slider row.
  • The variable label displays the [K1] badge in cyan.
  • The slider track and dynamic indicator dot glow Electric Cyan instead of their default color.
  • Numeric input text boxes are outlined in cyan and set to read-only to prevent fighting the engine.
  • Hovering over the slider track, handle, or text box displays a tooltip indicating the controlling macro knob.
  • Clicking the variable label or badge selects the controlling macro and shows its target strip.

docs.title: Saving your knob layout
docs.text: Macro banks are bundled directly into .lsd / .lsdplay preset files — they load and save with the preset automatically, with no extra file to manage. If you want to reuse a favorite knob layout across unrelated presets, use the kebab menu (⋮) on the target strip: Export Macro Bank... saves the whole bank (all 4 knobs) as a standalone .knobpreset.json (default folder library/knobpresets), and Import Macro Bank... loads one into the bank you're editing. Targets that don't exist on the deck it lands on are skipped and counted in the status message. Importing onto a deck bank points its targets at that deck to that deck, like a preset load; the Master bank keeps targets as saved. The same menu has Rename (double-clicking the name also works). FX banks have no menu.

docs.title: Hardware control
docs.text:
Macro Knobs sit at the top of the MIDI/OSC input hierarchy:

  • Right-click any knob in the Perform view 4×4 matrix (see below) to arm hardware MIDI Learn for it — the next CC your controller sends is mapped to that knob. Hardware MIDI Learn is Performance-Mode-only; the target strip's Add Target button chooses what a knob controls, not which controller moves it.
  • Turn on the OSC server in Preferences → OSC Controls, and /macro/knob/1–/macro/knob/8 send and receive live updates.

docs.title: FX chains in Edit
docs.text:
Each deck and Master has its own independent FX chain. A deck's FX tab in Edit (and OUT > FX for Master) starts with the chain's Dry/Wet row and its ⋮ chain menu (the same menu as on the FX row), then the SUPER KNOB & METAKNOBS block: the chain's Super Knob, then one row per slot Metaknob with its Super Knob Link checkbox. These are full parameter rows, so they take modulators and right-click MIDI / OSC Learn like any other. Below it, each slot has its parameters, its Metaknob targets and its Knobs order.

Edit and the macro strip always point at the same deck and section:

  • Opening a deck's Edit anywhere (its row's [EDIT], the side rail, the SRC / FX tabs) focuses that deck and section.

The same applies to the other decks and Master (the Master MST row opens Edit's MST side tab, the Transitions and Master FX rows its OUT side tab).

docs.title: Who wins when several things drive the same value
docs.text:
A parameter's base value can be driven from several places. From strongest to weakest:

  1. A macro knob target locks the value against direct writes, but the Value and the knob are linked both ways: dragging, scrolling or typing in Initial Range moves the knob (and so every other target of that knob), and the Value follows. Stepped and S-curve targets land on the nearest position, and a typed value outside the target's range stops at the knob's end. A randomize (the deck die, Rand, or the Initial Range dice) moves the knob the same way, so a rolled value sticks. Any MIDI or OSC mapping on it is suspended (its row in Preferences shows "Suspended: driven by ...") and works again when you release the target.
  2. An effect Metaknob target (including through the Super Knob, which moves linked Metaknobs) owns the effect parameter it is aimed at. A macro knob can't be added to that parameter ("driven by its Metaknob"), and an existing macro target on it is ignored while the Metaknob target is enabled. The parameter's row shows the same cyan highlight as a macro target, with a [K1] badge when the Metaknob sits on a macro knob. As with a macro target, editing the Value in Edit moves the Metaknob instead (and the macro knob above it, if it has one). Uncheck the Metaknob target (in the slot's Metaknob targets block or on the Edit-row strip) to use a macro knob there instead. A Metaknob aimed at Dry/Wet owns the slot's Dry/Wet the same way: the focus header's Wet slider then moves the Metaknob. MIDI and OSC mappings on it are suspended as well.
  3. Direct edits, MIDI and OSC mappings on an unlocked value: the last one to move wins.
  4. Modulators (LFO, sequencer, audio) never compete. They are always added on top of whatever value results from 1-3.

docs.title: Chain Super Knob & effect Metaknobs
docs.text:
• Super Knob — one knob that sweeps every linked slot's own Metaknob together.
  • Metaknob (one per slot) — the effect's single macro control. For a hand-curated effect (the bundled filters) it's tuned to feel right out of the box. For any other ISF shader — including the thousands available from third-party shader packs — it's auto-mapped the first time the shader loads, using the shader's own declared IDENTITY/parameter metadata, or a Dry/Wet fallback if nothing better is found. If you remove every target, the Metaknob drives nothing, and stays that way when the slot is saved. A target that names a parameter the effect doesn't have (renamed, or copied from another effect) drives nothing and shows (missing). When a slot loads or resets, the Metaknob starts where its targets come closest to their current values: exactly for one target, and the best compromise when several targets can't all be matched by one position.
  • Slot cells — on a Performance row in FX mode, each Metaknob has no caption; the slot cell right under it names the effect in that slot. Only the Super Knob keeps its SUPER caption.
  • Link (per slot) — toggles whether that slot's Metaknob follows the Super Knob. Linking never snaps a Metaknob to wherever the Super Knob sits. A linked slot's own knob still works: turning it (or editing the Metaknob any other way) moves just that Metaknob.
  • Super Knob response (Preferences) — how linked slots follow:
  • Relative (default): every linked slot moves as soon as you turn the Super Knob, and keeps its own position: a slot at 20% and one at 90% both rise, stay apart, and both reach 100% at the top and 0% at the bottom. Bring the Super Knob back and they return to where they were. Moving a slot by hand just gives it a new starting point.
  • Pickup: a slot waits until the Super Knob reaches its Metaknob (soft pickup, as for MIDI/OSC takeover), then follows it exactly, so linked slots end up moving together. Turning a slot's own knob lets go of the Super Knob until it reaches the slot again. While a slot waits, its link button is amber and the Edit-row strip says "waiting for pickup".
