  • Focus Mode (per slot) — hands the chain's knobs to one effect slot. Focusing from the Perform row, the Twister or the Metaknob row's menu in Edit is the same thing: the knobs follow, and Edit's SUPER KNOB & METAKNOBS block shows which parameters knobs 2-4 hold, with page arrows and Group Mode to leave.
  • Knob 1: The focused slot's Metaknob, linked or not. The slot's Dry/Wet is the Wet slider in the chain header (middle-click resets to 100%).
  • Knobs 2–4: Retargeted to the focused effect's top parameters on the active page, with parameter paging ([◀ P1/N ▶]) when more than 3 parameters exist. A parameter the Metaknob already drives is left out, since knob 1 moves it, unless you set the slot's own knob order (see Editing a Metaknob's targets and knob order below). Time-like parameters (names with a word such as rate, speed, frequency, decay or feedback, e.g. fbDecay) respond exponentially, so the slow end gets more of the knob's travel.
  • Parameter Cells (FxParamCell): Display parameter values with a reset-to-default button (counter-clockwise arrow).
  • Hardware MIDI: Physical controllers mapped to Macro/<bankId>/knob_1..4 keep their paths; in Focus Mode they control the focused slot's Metaknob and parameters. The layout is fixed per mode (Mixxx-style), so a mapped CC changes meaning when you toggle focus.
  • Click the active slot pill in the header (or Group Mode in Edit) to return to standard Group Mode.
  • Right-click a Metaknob row in Edit to focus that slot, Save as Default for the effect, or Remove Saved Default (see Explicit ISF FX Defaults below).

docs.title: Editing a Metaknob's targets and knob order
docs.text:
A Metaknob can drive several parameters at once, each with its own response.

  • In the Edit view, select a slot's Metaknob. The row strip shows one numbered chip per target, Add Target (pick from the parameters that aren't targets yet, or Dry/Wet) and the selected target's controls: the enable checkbox, knob zone (full range, first half, second half, triangle, bipolar, invert), response curve (linear, exponential, logarithmic, S-curve, step with a step count), a range bar with draggable handles, Min and Max, and delete. Right-click the zone button for the full list.
  • In the Edit bay, each slot has a Metaknob targets block with the same controls for every target and an Add Target menu. A parameter's own row menu also has a Metaknob Target check to add or remove it quickly.
  • Words used here: a Metaknob's targets are the parameters it drives; Link only ever means a slot following the Super Knob.
  • Knobs (also in the Edit bay) lists the parameters on focus-mode knobs 2-4, three per page. Move a parameter up or down, take it off the knobs, bring it back from Hidden, or Reset order. A lock beside a parameter means the Metaknob drives it, so its knob does nothing while that target is enabled.
  • Targets and knob order are saved with the slot and chain. Changing them in one chain never changes another chain or the stock effect; Save as Default makes your targets and order the starting point for new copies of that effect. Ctrl+Z undoes a change, and a drag on a range handle is a single step.

docs.title: Hardware control note
docs.text: Map hardware to the Perform knobs (right-click a knob, or use a controller profile such as the Twister's): their paths (Macro/<bankId>/knob_1..4) stay fixed and their meaning follows the mode, so the same physical knob is the Super Knob in group mode and the focused Metaknob in Focus Mode, Mixxx-style. Learn on a Super Knob or Metaknob row in Edit maps that one control instead, and is locked (locked by K#) while a Perform knob already drives it.

docs.title: The Perform View (4×4 Matrix)
docs.text:
The Perform view is the app's main view: a 4×4 Macro Knob Matrix — 16 knobs arranged in 4 rows across 4 columns, color-coded by deck — on the left, with the Mixer column and Library dock alongside. (Earlier versions also had a "Classic" Parameters/Properties view, toggled with F4; everything it did now lives in Edit, below.)

The active page is remembered between sessions in application preferences.

docs.title: The Perform pages
docs.text:
Each page shows 4 rows of 4 knobs, mapped to different banks:

Page Row 1 Row 2 Row 3 Row 4 A/B Deck A source Deck A FX Deck B source Deck B FX BG/PV Deck BG source Deck BG FX Deck PV source Deck PV FX MIXER Transitions Master FX Master MST Clock (knob 13)

Every deck and Master row shows one half (source or FX), so a knob never changes meaning under you. Opening a deck in Edit shows the row for the Edit tab you are on (SRC or FX).

  • Per-Deck Insert FX & Flexible Routing: Every deck (A, B, BG, PV) now owns its own dedicated 3-slot FxChain running post-generator and pre-crossfader, completely decoupled from other decks.
  • Deck Rows Are Split into a Source Row and an FX Row: Each deck has a source row ([ SRC ] pill, kebab, generator/preset badge, Save, queue navigation, eject; its knobs are the source's macros) and an FX row ([ FX ] pill, kebab, chain name, Save, queue navigation, slot pills 1 2 3; its knobs are the chain's Super Knob and three Metaknobs). The right wing of the FX row has the [ FX ON ] button. The source row's right wing has the randomize die (Source and FX).
  • Master Rows Are Split Too: The Master MST row ([ MST ] pill) has the deck-levels badge, with the four knobs on the deck levels and the master level. The Master FX row ([ FX ] pill) has the Master FX chain header (the chain name, then [⋮] [Save] [1] [2] [3]) and its [ FX ON ] button, with the knobs on the Master FX Super Knob + 3 Metaknobs. The crossfader sits on the Transitions row.
  • The Transitions row has the transition picker on line 1 (click it to pick from the Library below — see below; the Edit gear sits at its end), and line 2 is laid out like an FX row: [⋮] menu, [Save] (saves the transition as a preset), queue [◀] [▶], then the crossfader cells below. Its four knobs are fixed: knob 1 is the crossfader (it follows auto-fades and the slider, and turning it takes over like the slider does), and knobs 2-4 are the active transition's first three sliders, relabelled whenever you change transition. Transitions with fewer than three sliders leave the spare knobs blank. Line 2 ends with A / B snap buttons, AUTO and the fade time; there is no crossfader slider on the row (use knob 1 or the Mixer panel's slider). These knobs cannot be re-learned; Dry/Wet stays in the Edit bay.

Each row is color-coded to its deck or target (orange for Deck A, blue for Deck B, green for Deck BG, plum for Deck PV, cyan for Transitions, light grey for Master) and starts with a title badge spanning both control lines: a large A, B, BG or PV on deck rows (its caption strip, SRC or FX, shows which half the knobs control), a large M captioned TRAN, FX or MST on the MIXER page's Transitions and Master rows, and CLK on the Clock row. No row has a header bar over its knobs, so MIXER-page knobs are the same size as deck knobs.

docs.title: Performance Controls & Side-Wing Layout
docs.text:
To maximize vertical space in the matrix and keep the knobs comfortably clustered together: - Row Titles & Side-Wing Controls: Row group titles (e.g. DECK A, DECK A (FX)) sit at the top-left of the row, level with the top of the knobs. The left- and right-wing controls sit below the title, with their bottom edge lined up with the bottom of the knobs, so short rows never push the controls up into the title. Every wing control (buttons, badges, generator/preset badge) is the same height. - Row Height: Every row has the same fixed height, whatever the window size, so knobs never resize and nothing scrolls. The Library fills the window height below the rows. - Deck Rows (Deck A, B, BG, PV): - Left Wing (Info & Deck Controls): - Row 1 (SRC): - [ SRC ] Pill: Labels the source row, whose 4 on-screen macro knobs drive the deck's source. - Source / Preset Badge: One control, not two -- a preset is just a source with its parameter values saved under a name. With a preset loaded it shows the preset's name (with * when changed) followed by the source it plays, dimmed (curated-0001 · Fractal flame); with a bare source, the source's name. Click it and the Library below lists stock sources and saved presets together, applying to this deck (click again to stop); right-click for source defaults. Clicking the stock source of the preset you're playing loads that source's defaults; clicking the source a deck already plays bare does nothing. - Eject Button (⏏): Empties the deck (with the unsaved-changes guard). The deck's FX chain is left as it is. Ctrl+Z can't undo it. - Queue Navigation: Deck A and Deck B connect to PlayQueueManager (< N/Total >), Deck BG connects to BgQueueManager (< N/Total >), and Deck PV features a quick Preview focus button. - Save Button: Saves the deck's source and parameters as a preset, back to the file it was loaded from (a new name goes to presets/). Greyed out for external video, which can't be saved. - Kebab Menu (⋮): Source operations (Browse, Save As, defaults). - Row 2 (FX): - [ FX ] Knob Pill: Assigns the row's 4 on-screen macro knobs to the deck's insert FX chain (Super Knob + 3 Metaknobs). - Dedicated Chain Controls: Step through chains (◀ / ▶), active chain name with dirty dot (•) — click it to pick a whole chain from the Library below — [Save] button, and kebab menu ([⋮]) for Save As, Revert, Copy/Paste, and Resync. - Knob Columns: The 4 macro knobs are uniformly spaced across the center area between the control wings, sharing the exact same column pitch and horizontal alignment whether assigned to SRC or FX. When assigned to FX, each of knobs 2–4 gets two stacked buttons on its left: a link button (Icons.LINK/Icons.UNLINK) that links/unlinks its Metaknob to the Super Knob, and a power button that bypasses just that effect. Interactive FX slot cells showing the effect name appear beneath knobs 2–4; hover a cell to show its ◀ / ▶ shortlist arrows. - Macro Knob Ergonomics & Display Modes: - Dual-Axis Drag & Shift Fine-Tuning: Drag vertically or horizontally (up/right increases, down/left decreases). Holding Shift engages 6x fine-tuning resolution (1200px full sweep) for high-precision decimal tuning without cursor jumps on Shift toggle. Cursor locking (lockCursorOnKnobDrag) prevents the mouse from leaving the window on large sweeps. - Bipolar & Endless Modes: Knobs adapt their visual geometry to the underlying parameter's MeterType: - Monopolar (standard 7:30 to 4:30 sweep). - Bipolar (12 o'clock center detent, sweeping left for negative or right for positive; middle-click resets to 0.5 center). Focused FX and Deck parameters with negative ranges (e.g. shifts, pans, zooms) render in bipolar mode. - Endless (continuous 360° circle where 0 and 1 meet at 6 o'clock straight down, sweeping continuous angles for rotation and hue). - Double-Click Direct Numeric Entry: Double-click any macro knob face to open an inline text entry box. Type exact numerical values (e.g. 0.25, -1.5, 42) and press Enter to commit, or Escape to cancel. The typed value is what the parameter receives, so the knob's curve, invert and zone are taken into account (the readout shows the same value). For stepped or half-range bindings the knob snaps to the nearest position that gets closest. - In-Face Readouts: Hovering or dragging over a targetless or group-mode knob displays a subtle real-time value readout in the center of the knob face. - Right Wing: - Randomize Die Button (🎲): Randomizes the source's modulators and base values, its Gain, Deck Zoom / Deck Rotate, the FX chain's Dry/Wet and the inputs of the effects in its chain (parameters with randomization turned on), with undo of both the values and the knob positions (when randomization is enabled). Every stock source and most stock effects ship with random ranges on their look parameters (see Modulation, "Built-in random ranges"; an effect's Metaknob is never rolled), and the source knobs move with the roll. Positioned on Row 1 directly above the FX ON button. - [ FX ON ]: Turns the deck's FX chain on or off; lit while on. Positioned on Row 2 aligned with the FX row. - Drag-and-Drop: Dropping a deck preset (.patch, .lsd, .json) loads the visual preset; dropping a .lsdfxchain loads that FX chain onto the deck. - Whole-Rig Randomize ([ ALL 🎲 ]): Positioned at the top right of the performance matrix tab strip, pushing undo state and invoking mixer.randomizeAll() across all decks (their effects included), the Master parameters and FX, and the transition simultaneously. - Master FX row: Left wing: the FX-captioned M badge, the chain name box and the chain controls line, as on a deck FX row; right wing: Master FX [ FX ON ]. Dropping a .lsdfxchain onto the MASTER badge loads it into Master FX. - Level faders on the deck tiles (the thin strip beside each preview badge) share their value with the Master MST knobs: move the fader and the knob follows, turn the knob and the fader follows, last mover wins. A fader drag also mutes non-MIDI modulation on it and makes a Soft Takeover MIDI/OSC mapping on it pick up again instead of jumping. The handle line marks the fader's own value; the filled bar is the live level after modulation. - Master MST row: The M badge carries an MST caption. Line 1 is the Deck Levels & Master box (click to edit the levels, right-click for level resets) and a 100% reset button; its gear opens Edit on the MST side tab's LEVELS section (the master level, then each deck's level), which shows this row together with the Clock row; the knobs are the Deck A / B / BG and Master levels. The crossfader is not here: it lives on the Transitions row (knob 1) and the Mixer panel. - Transitions (Row 2 in MASTER): Left wing features a Transition Picker button displaying the active transition with modified indicator (*) — click it to pick from the transition list in the Library below — and Transition Queue stepping controls (<, N/Total, >); right wing hosts the transition randomize die button (🎲) on Row 1 (matching the deck rows): it rolls the transition's inputs that have a random range, inside that range, and moves the TRANS knobs with them; Ctrl+Z undoes it. Transition presets (.lsdtrans) and shaders (.fs/.isf) can be dropped directly onto the picker button. - Clock & Global (Row 4 in MASTER): The two lines beside the CLOCK badge have the tempo controls from Preferences > Tempo & Sync, placed here for use mid-set: - [ MAN ] / [ AUDIO ]: clock source (manual tempo or the audio beat tracker). - [ LINK n ]: the third button of the top line, with the peer count while Ableton Link is on and dim while it is off. Click it to open Tempo & Sync preferences. - BPM readout: click it to open Tempo & Sync preferences. The beat dots under it (one per beat of the bar, 4 by default) show the bar phase; the downbeat is cyan. Hover for the detector's confidence when Downbeat is on Auto. - [ TAP ]: tap tempo. Right-click for MIDI Learn. In Audio mode it nudges the detected tempo and phase. The first tap of a run also marks beat 1 of the bar. - [ SNAP ]: makes the beat nearest now beat 1 of the bar, snapping the beat phase and the bar line together. Press it on the one when the bar dots' cyan dot is in the wrong place. Preferences > Tempo & Sync > Bar & Downbeat sets the beats per bar and can let the app find beat 1 from the music (Downbeat: Auto); SNAP, or the first tap of a run, overrides it for 16 bars. - Twister clock knob: knob 13 on a Midi Fighter Twister pulses its LED on the beat (orange on the downbeat), shows the tempo on its ring and taps tempo when pushed. See Rings and LEDs. - [ - ][ + ]: nudge the tempo by 0.5 BPM. The pair takes the space of one button, so MAN, AUDIO, LINK, TAP, SNAP and the pair make a tidy 3 x 2 grid. - Queue triggers (QUEUE): right of the tempo controls, captions A/B, A/B FX, BG, BG FX and TRN over each queue's buttons: [◀] [▶], with a play / pause button beside the caption on the A/B, BG and TRN queues (it toggles that queue's auto-advance and is lit while it runs; the FX queues have none). They are the same triggers as the queue rows of Edit's MST › CTRL tab: right-click a button for MIDI or OSC Learn, and a mapping made there shows on the CTRL row and the other way round. - Randomize triggers (RAND): while randomization is enabled (Preferences), at the right edge, [A] [B] [ALL] over [BG] [PV] randomize that deck (or everything), with the same Learn menu and Ctrl+Z undo as the decks' dice. On a window too narrow for them, they are the first thing to go.

The BPM is deliberately not a knob, since one bump would shift the whole show. The row has no macro knobs; a configurable row of free "global" knobs that can target any parameter is planned for a later release.

docs.title: MIDI Learn in the Performance Matrix
docs.text:
Right-click any knob to arm it for MIDI Learn — a cyan pulsing ring appears around the knob, identical to the Learn ring on Parameter rows. Send a CC message from any connected controller to map it immediately. Right-click again while armed to cancel.

Interactive header controls in the Performance Matrix also support right-click MIDI & OSC Learn: - Deck A and Deck B Badges: Right-click to Learn MIDI (Global/snapDeckA, Global/snapDeckB) or Learn OSC (Mixer/snapDeckA, Mixer/snapDeckB) to instantly snap the crossfader left or right. - Auto-Fade Button [ AUTO ] & Fade Speed Badge: Right-click to Learn MIDI (Global/autoFade, Mixer/xfadeSpeed) or Learn OSC (Mixer/xfadeSpeed). - PlayQueue & BG Queue < and >: Right-click to Learn MIDI (Global/queuePrev, Global/queueNext, Global/bgQueuePrev, Global/bgQueueNext). - Transition Queue < and >: Right-click to Learn MIDI (Global/transQueuePrev, Global/transQueueNext) or Learn OSC (Mixer/transQueuePrev, Mixer/transQueueNext). Controls actively armed for MIDI learn display a pulsing cyan highlight border. Active MIDI assignments are shown in tooltips.

docs.title: Interacting with knobs
docs.text:
• Drag (up/down or left/right) to adjust the knob value. Dragging up or right increases the value; dragging down or left decreases it — the standard DAW/synth convention. Horizontal dragging makes it easy to adjust knobs located near the top edge of the screen or display boundary.
  • Mouse wheel to fine-adjust (Shift for finer, Ctrl+Shift for coarser).
  • Hover/drag highlight: the knob body tints toward the row's accent color on hover, and more strongly while you're dragging it, so the knob under your pointer is easy to spot.
  • Right-click arms hardware MIDI Learn for that knob — the knob pulses cyan while armed, and the next CC message from your controller is mapped to it. Right-click again to cancel.

Knobs in the 4×4 matrix, the target strip and the hardware controller all read from and write to the same underlying MacroEngine banks — changes in one are immediately visible in the others.

docs.title: The Modular Rack: Edit
docs.text:
Every deep-editable row group in the 4×4 matrix (Deck A/B/BG/PV, the FX row, Master, Transitions) has a small [EDIT] button in its top-right corner (the Clock row has no knobs and no button). Clicking it toggles that row between two disclosure tiers, without leaving the Perform view:

  1. Faceplate (collapsed, the default) — just the 4 knobs, exactly like the plain 4×4 matrix above. The [EDIT] button has a dark fill and off-white text. Clicking a knob selects it (electric cyan focus card, glowing rim, cyan label), shows its current value (Val: 0.00) beneath the label, and reveals a compact [Add Target] / [Cancel] button for adding a target on the spot.
  2. Edit — click [EDIT] to open the comprehensive Edit bay below the top macro row. The [EDIT] button turns green with black text while active. The bay is arranged into a 3-column layout:
  3. Side Rail on the left: color-coded buttons ([MST], [OUT], [A], [B], [BG], [PV]) allowing instant 1-click navigation between all major sections of the app without closing Edit. Selecting a side tab switches both the parameter editor below and the top macro row above.
  4. Parameter Grid in the center: displays the full VAL / MIDI / LFO / SEQ / AUD parameter grid with section subtabs across the top. Parameters show the shader's own label, or a readable form of the name (CellScale reads "Cell scale"). Above the grid sits the same header line as the pair view: Back, a Browse | Params switch (Browse shows the list for this deck and half in the pair view), the module's name and what the queue plays next. Each side tab has its own section tabs:
    • MST: [ LEVELS ] [ CTRL ] (the master level, then each deck's level; and the queue and randomize triggers, which are also on the Clock row)
    • OUT: [ FX ] [ TRANS ] (the Master FX chain's 3 ISF slots, and Transitions, led by crossfade and fade speed)
    • A, B, BG, PV: [ SRC ] [ FX ] (visual generator with Gain/Zoom/Rotate Z, and the insert FX chain) Edit shows the open unit's two rows above the editor, as the Pair view does: a deck's source and FX rows, Master's Transitions and Master FX rows (OUT side tab), or Master's MST and the Clock row (MST side tab): in each case the two rows that share a half of a Twister page. The rows stay put when you switch sections; the gear that is lit marks the row the editor is on, and clicking the other row's gear moves the editor there (click the lit one to close Edit). Both rows' macro knobs stay live.
  5. Modulation Editor on the right: side-by-side per-parameter CV detail editor (LFO period/phase/morph/hold/slew, MIDI, SEQ, AUD, curves, and modulators) of whichever cell is selected. Opening Edit or switching tabs selects the first knob-assigned parameter (or the first row), so it is never empty.

If the deck is empty, Edit shows the empty-deck card instead: Add Source (opens Browse, see below, including external video), Load Preset, and Open Library Panel.

docs.title: Browse: picking a generator, FX or transition
docs.text:
Clicking a generator/preset badge, an FX chain's name, an FX slot's name, or the active transition's name (or a preview monitor) points the Library below at that slot: nothing moves, the slot is outlined on its row, and its name shows on the Library's tab line with a ✕. Esc, the ✕, or clicking the slot again stops. When the current page doesn't show that row (say, the BG monitor from the A/B page), the pair view opens instead: that deck's SRC and FX rows (or Transitions and Master FX) stay on screen, every other row hides, and the Browse list fills the space below. Nothing covers the mixer or the deck/master monitors; you keep watching the show while you pick. The pair view's header line has Back (or Esc) to return to Perform and a Browse | Params switch that opens the full editor for the half you last touched.

  • Instant apply, list stays open: clicking an item in the list applies it immediately and the list doesn't close, so you can try several generators, effects, or chains back-to-back. Ctrl+Z undoes any one pick. A double-click applies and stops (back to the plain Library, or out of the pair view). Changing a deck's source while a named/dirty preset is loaded prompts once; the answer is reused for the next picks on that deck.
  • The half you touched picks the list: click a row's source badge, chain name, an effect cell or the transition name, or turn a knob on that row, and Browse applies to that target (a deck's source, a chain, one FX slot, the transition). the Master MST row and the Clock row have nothing to browse (they are not a pair); the Master pair (Transitions + Master FX) with nothing touched browses the Master FX chain. On Edit's MST side tab the Browse button is disabled.
  • Source Browse lists sources and presets together: stock sources and saved presets always appear in the same list — a preset is just a source with its parameter values saved under a name. Saved-preset rows get a "⋮" menu (also on right-click) that starts with Apply to , then Rename..., Clone..., Delete... and Reveal in File Manager, and a floppy-disk Save / Save As button sits beside the target's name — the same save flow as the Mixer's Save button and Ctrl+Shift+S — so managing presets no longer requires the Library view.
  • FX Browse applies to either a whole chain (the saved .lsdfxchain files) or one slot's effect (stock filters, ★ favorites, saved single-FX presets), each opening on its usual folder.
  • The same browser as the Library: it has the Library's own Sources / FX / Transitions / Queues / Macros tabs, folder tree and list. The target's name, such as "● Deck A · FX 1" (the slot, chain or transition you are editing), says what a click applies to: on that tab a click applies, the row that is applied (stock or saved) is tinted across the whole row, and the list shows only what the target can take. Pick another tab and the name greys out ("paused"): it is the plain Library again (double-click loads to the inactive deck). Each target remembers the folder you last used there. Search with Ctrl+F or /. Clear Slot / Clear Chain empties the target. The Sources tree also has an External video folder listing the live video streams running right now.

    • Keyboard shortcuts in Edit: Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V (copy/paste a cell or row), Delete / Backspace (clear the cell's modulators, or reset the parameter), and Ctrl+S / Shift+Ctrl+S (save / save-as the deck being edited) act on the open Edit. Copy/paste/clear only fire while the Perform view has focus, so Delete in the Library doesn't also reset a parameter. Ctrl+Z (undo) works anywhere in the Perform view, with or without Edit open.

    While in Edit, the top macro row renders the macro controls corresponding to the active channel and subtab, reserving the freed vertical space for the side rail and parameter bay. The row keeps the same knob size and control positions it has in the four-row view; it only grows by one line under each knob for the value readout (and the Add Target button under the selected knob). There's no separate title above the parameters, since the row says which deck and section you're editing. Collapsing back to Faceplate brings the rest of the 4×4 grid, and the Library, back. While Edit is open the Library is hidden completely (the Edit view — see Your Workspace).

    Click [EDIT] again (or press Esc) to fold back to the Faceplate.

    Opening Edit from Confidence Monitors: Clicking any preview monitor in the Mixer column (Deck A, Deck B, Deck BG, Deck PV, or Main Output Master) points the Library at that deck's source (or the Master FX chain), or opens the pair view when the page doesn't show those rows. For the full editor use the row's gear, or Params in the pair view's header.

    One Edit at a time: opening a row's Edit collapses any other open one. To move between decks, use the Edit side rail (MST / OUT / A / B / BG / PV) rather than opening rows side by side.

    Esc collapses every expanded row back to the Faceplate — unless a Learn is currently armed (Add Target, MIDI Learn or OSC Learn), in which case Esc cancels every armed Learn at once instead (a second Esc then collapses the rack). A row whose own knob has an armed Add Target is also exempt from the auto-collapse, so it can't be accidentally folded away mid-way; a "Adding target: ‹name› — Esc to cancel" indicator stays visible in the toolbar the whole time Add Target is armed, even if you've expanded a different row. View → Close Edit does the same as the row's [EDIT] button.

    Expanding or collapsing a row is purely a display change — it never re-syncs the Super Knob/Metaknob mapping.

docs.title: Setting up knob labels and targets
docs.text:
Targets are edited in the Edit view, in the target strip described above (rename, target chips, Min/Max/Curve/Invert/Link/Enabled) and in the Modulation editor of the open Edit. Clicking a target's name opens that deck's (or the Mixer's) Edit on the right sub-tab with the parameter selected.

  • From the 4×4 matrix: click a knob to select it, then click Add Target (on the target strip, or the inline button in the Perform view). This arms Add Target and opens that row's Edit Params — click a target parameter and set Min/Max/Curve as desired. The target must be in the knob's own deck and section (see Adding targets to a knob above).

The change is live immediately everywhere, since all views share the same MacroEngine banks.

docs.title: Macro Banks
docs.text:
There are 12 always-resident canonical macro banks (4 knobs each, conforming to the 4-column performance grid):

Scope Bank Knobs Canonical ID Smart Defaults Deck Generators Deck A 4 deckA Blank Deck B 4 deckB Blank Deck BG 4 deckBG Blank Deck PV 4 deckPV Blank Per-Deck Insert FX Deck A FX 4 deckA_fx Super Knob + 3 Metaknobs Deck B FX 4 deckB_fx Super Knob + 3 Metaknobs Deck BG FX 4 deckBG_fx Super Knob + 3 Metaknobs Deck PV FX 4 deckPV_fx Super Knob + 3 Metaknobs Mixer & Transitions Transitions 4 trans Crossfade, Type, Speed, Next Master 4 master Level A, Level B, Master Level, Crossfader Master FX 4 masterFx Super Knob + 3 Metaknobs

Deck generator banks initialize from their generator's default preset. Master, Transitions, and FX banks initialize with pre-mapped smart defaults. The five FX banks target their chain's Deck A/FX/... … Master/FX/... parameters and re-sync automatically whenever that chain's contents change (loading a chain, swapping a slot, restoring a session) — FX knobs are fixed (Super + 3 Metaknobs, or Metaknob + 3 parameters when focused) and can't be retargeted per knob; change what a Metaknob controls with its Retarget menu. Sessions saved with hand-retargeted FX knobs lose those targets on load. All 12 canonical banks are preserved in last_session.json and session files.

Banks are saved in last_session.json and bundled into preset files automatically.

docs.title: Generator & FX Defaults ("Save as Default")
docs.text: Similar to Ableton's default presets, you can configure your favorite parameter starting points and 4-knob macro layouts for any visual generator or ISF FX filter, and save them as that device's permanent default.

docs.title: Visual Generator Defaults
docs.text:
When swapping sources on any deck (via the source badge or the empty-deck card), the incoming source's default configuration is resolved across three tiers: 1. User Default: Custom parameter baselines, globalAlpha, and 4-knob macro layout saved in library/generator_defaults/<sourceId>.json. 2. Stock Default: the default shipped with each bundled generator: its 4-knob macro targets and its built-in audio and beat responses (mandala, dynamic_spiral, icosa_h3, domain_warp_fluid, gyroid_hyperspace, celestial_engine, hyper_slice, chladni_cymatics, mandelbox, kifs, mandelbulb, pseudo_kleinian, apollonian, escape_time, nebula_volume, reaction_diffusion, fluid_ink, lenia, quasicrystal, thin_film, tunnel_scenes, video_feedback, hyperbolic_tiling, cyclic_ca, metaballs, wave_ripples, aurora_ribbons, isometric_voxels, halftone_matrix, kali_set, girih_stars, glitch_blocks, voronoi_cells). 3. Automated Heuristic Fallback: For third-party ISF shaders (nothing is written to disk; it is worked out again on every load until you save a default yourself), continuous floats (e.g. speed, rate, zoom, scale, morph, depth, detail) are prioritized, discrete stepped selectors are filtered out, and speed/frequency parameters are shaped with exponential response curves.

Bank Replacement Behavior: Applying a default replaces the resident 4-knob deck bank wholesale, identical to preset loading. Stored Deck/* targets are dynamically remapped to the target deck slot (e.g., Deck A, Deck B). Knobs are positioned via inverse-curve mapping so parameter values do not jump on load. Hardware MIDI mappings are stripped on save to avoid duplicate hardware CC collisions across decks.

How to Save or Reset Generator Defaults: - Right-click the generator badge on any deck row in the Perform view to open the context menu: - Save as Default for <Generator>: Saves current parameters, Gain, and 4-knob macro layout as the generator default. - Apply Default Now: Reapplies the default layout and parameters to the current deck. - Reset to Factory Default: Deletes the user default file and restores the stock (or heuristic) default. - Alternatively, open the Save menu in Edit's monitor toolbar and select Save as Default for <Generator>.

docs.title: Explicit ISF FX Defaults
docs.text: A slot's Metaknob targets, knob order and parameter values can be saved as the effect's own default: - Tweaking parameters or targets during performance is purely temporary and does not silently overwrite defaults on disk. - Right-click a Metaknob row in Edit's SUPER KNOB & METAKNOBS block: - Save as Default for <Filter> saves this slot's Metaknob targets, knob order, parameter values and modulators (not MIDI mappings) into library/isf_overrides/<contentHash>.json. New copies of the effect start from it; slots already in chains keep their own. - When a saved default exists, Remove Saved Default for <Filter> deletes it, so new copies go back to the stock (or auto-mapped) default, and resets this slot to it too. - Targets themselves are edited in the slot's Metaknob targets block or on the Edit-row strip.

docs.title: Transition Defaults
docs.text: The transition's ⋮ menu (on the Transitions row, and the kebab beside the transition picker in the Mixer TRANS tab) has Save as Default for <Transition>: it saves the running transition's parameter values and modulators (not MIDI mappings) the same way, keyed by shader content. Picking that transition from then on starts from it; saved .lsdtrans presets keep their own values. Remove Saved Default for <Transition> deletes it and resets the running transition to the built-in values and audio response.

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text: Key What it does Esc Cancel every armed Learn (Add Target, MIDI, OSC), or (if none is armed) stop browsing a slot, or collapse every expanded Rack row back to Faceplate

docs.title: Modulation
docs.text: Modulation is how you make your visuals react to music, touch, MIDI, oscillators, or a sequencer. Instead of just setting parameters to fixed values, you connect them to live signals — audio energy, LFOs, step patterns, or MIDI knobs — and let those signals drive what's happening on screen.

docs.title: The CV Grid
docs.text:
The CV grid is the middle column of Edit (click a row's gear in the Perform view). It's a matrix:

  • Rows = visual parameters (Lobes, Zoom, Hue, Feedback Decay, etc.)
  • Columns = modulation sources (manual value, MIDI, LFO, Sequencer, Audio)

Click any cell at the intersection of a parameter and a source type to configure that connection. Active cells show an animated readout knob so you can see the live signal at a glance.

The side rail on the left ([MST] [OUT] [A] [B] [BG] [PV]) switches between the master levels and clock controls, the output stage and the decks; the section tabs above the grid switch between a deck's source (SRC) and its FX chain, the output stage's FX / TRANS, or the MST tab's LEVELS / CTRL. The selected cell's details appear in the Modulation column on the right.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Each column is colour-coded:

  • VAL (mint cyan) — The manual base value, plus range limits and a reset button.
  • MIDI (violet) — Hardware MIDI controller assignments.
  • LFO (sky blue) — Low-frequency oscillators.
  • SEQ (lime green) — Step sequencer.
  • AUD (amber) — Audio modulation.

You can hide columns you're not using via the ⋮ kebab menu, positioned just left of the VAL column header and aligned with the row action buttons below it. That menu also shows warnings if a loaded preset uses modulators that are currently hidden or offline, with a one-click Turn On Needed Columns button to sort it out.

docs.title: Audio Modulation
docs.text:
Clicking an AUD cell opens the audio modulator config. Each parameter supports two independent audio connections (Audio 1 and Audio 2).

Auto Gain: audio signals are normalized against each band's own recent peak (Preferences > Audio Hardware > Auto Gain, on by default), so a modulator behaves the same whether the feed is quiet or hot. Switch it off for a fixed scale. Because of this, turning Input Gain down does not calm the picture for long; use Audio Response (below) for that.

Built-in responses: most stock sources, every stock effect and every stock transition but Linear Crossfade ship with audio and beat modulators already wired on their key parameters: one running, and one or two alternates sitting bypassed in the same row, so you switch an alternate on (and the running one off) by clicking its AUD or LFO cell. They are ordinary modulators, so edit or delete them freely. To make everything that follows the music move more or less, use Preferences > Audio Hardware > Audio Response (0% = nothing follows the music, 100% = as tuned, up to 200%); it scales the audio signals themselves, so it applies to built-in and hand-made audio modulators alike, and leaves LFOs and the beat alone. A default you saved yourself replaces the built-in response, and a preset that stores its own parameters replaces it too. On an effect, a response on the parameter its main knob (Metaknob) drives multiplies rather than adds (MUL), so an effect turned down to zero stays off and turning it up makes the hits bigger too. The stock FX chains carry the built-in effect responses; a chain you saved yourself keeps the parameters it stored. A transition's response only plays during a fade (with the crossfader fully on A or B the visible deck is shown as is), and the stock transition presets carry the same responses. Luminous Flash's Spread and Film Burn's Burn Spread have none on purpose: pushed above about 45% they make the picture pop the moment a fade starts.

Built-in random ranges: every stock shader source also ships with a random range (the Initial Range slider with its dice on) on the parameters that change its look: types, colour modes and palettes, twists, folds, sizes, glow, hue and saturation. The deck die rolls new values inside them, and the deck's Rand control fades from one roll to the next. Controls that decide whether the picture is watchable at all (Brightness, Quality, reseed triggers) have none. Each range stops short of the parameter's limit by the reach of its running audio or LFO response, so a roll never leaves the response pressed against a limit. Stepped parameters (types, modes, palettes, side counts) give every step an equal chance and switch halfway through a Rand fade rather than stepping through the values in between. A parameter a macro knob drives takes part too: the roll moves the knob. Ctrl+Z after a roll puts the values and knob positions back. Like the audio responses, a default you saved yourself or a preset that stores its own parameters replaces the ranges.

Stock effects and transitions ship random ranges the same way. The deck die and Rand roll the effects in that deck's chain along with its source (the whole-rig die and Rand All also roll the Master FX chain). An effect's main knob, its Metaknob, is never rolled: it says how much of the effect you get, so the roll changes the effect's look (angle, segments, centre, palette, mode) and leaves the amount to you. Invert and Luma Key have nothing else to roll. The transition die on the Transitions row rolls only the transition's ranged inputs, inside their ranges, and its TRANS knobs move with it; Rand All rolls the transition too. Every transition range is kept low enough that nothing shows with the crossfader at rest. The stock FX chains carry the ranges too; a chain you saved yourself keeps what it stored.

docs.title: Frequency bands
docs.text: Band What it tracks AMP Full-spectrum energy BASS Low end — kick drums, sub-bass (below ~150 Hz) MID Midrange — vocals, snares, lead synths (~1 kHz) HIGH Top end — hi-hats, cymbals, texture (above ~5 kHz)

docs.title: Detection modes
docs.text:
• Continuous — Tracks the ongoing energy level of the band. Good for sustained movement, breathing dynamics, amplitude-following effects.
  • Transient — Fires on attacks and hits. Detects the moment energy increases in the band, making it sharp and percussive. Great for triggering flashes, jumps, or snaps on drum hits.

docs.title: Response profiles
docs.text:
These control how quickly the signal rises and falls:

Profile Character Instant (Raw Jitter) No smoothing — raw and jittery. Snap Immediate attack, fast release. Good for fast percussive tracks. Punchy Slight attack, medium release. Captures rhythm cleanly. Smooth Swell Slower attack, long release. Peaks become gentle pulses. Slow Pulse Gradual rise, lingering tail. Ambient Drift Long, fluid swells. Ideal for ambient or drone music. Custom Set your own attack and decay times.

Selecting Custom inherits the timings from whatever profile was active before, so you can fine-tune from a sensible starting point.

docs.title: The oscilloscope
docs.text: The oscilloscope shows two traces: the raw audio energy (faint ghost trace) and the smoothed follower output (solid line). This makes it easy to see how the profile is shaping the signal before it reaches your parameter.

docs.title: Range (Min / Max)
docs.text:
The dual-handled range slider at the bottom sets the floor and ceiling of the modulation output. For example, if you want bass energy to push Lobes between 3 and 8, set Min to 3 and Max to 8.

Min and Max are measured from the parameter's set value, and moving one never moves the other. Audio sources only push upward from silence, so Min is the resting offset and Max is the loudest peak.

Enabling randomization adds independent drift sliders for the Min and Max bounds, so the range itself wanders gently over time.

docs.title: LFO Modulation
docs.text: Clicking an LFO cell opens the LFO config. Each cell has a primary oscillator and an optional secondary modulator.

docs.title: Primary LFO (LFO 1)
docs.text:
Waveforms:

  • Sine — Smooth, rounded oscillation.
  • Triangle — Linear rise and fall, adjustable asymmetry.
  • Square — Snaps between two values. Adjust pulse width with the Hold control.
  • Random (Sample & Hold) — Holds a random value for each cycle, then jumps to a new one.

Clock mode:

  • Time — Set the period in seconds. Use Fast / Medium / Slow sliders. Changing the period (by hand, from a controller, a macro or a preset morph) only changes how fast the LFO runs; it never jumps.
  • Beat — Synced to the beat clock. Subdivisions from 1/8 beat to 8 bars.

Waveshaping:

  • Slope — Makes the waveform asymmetric. At 0.5 it's symmetric; at 1.0 you get a slow rise and a fast drop.
  • Morph — Softens sharp corners. At 0.0 you get a pure triangle; at 1.0 you get a smooth sine-like curve.
  • Hold — Compresses the transition into a shorter moment and adds a plateau at the peak.

Range (Min / Max): Sets the output range directly. No need to think in terms of depth and offset — just say "I want this to move between 2.0 and 6.0" and set those values. Min and Max are the lowest and highest the LFO reaches, whatever the parameter's own range, and moving one leaves the other where it is. (The LFO swings evenly either side of the midpoint, so on a 0-to-1 parameter a Min below the set value pulls the parameter down as well as up; the result is clamped at the parameter's limits.)

docs.title: Secondary Modulator (LFO 2)
docs.text:
LFO 2 modulates LFO 1 to add movement and complexity:

  • AM (Amplitude Modulation) — LFO 2 scales LFO 1's depth up and down, making the oscillation breathe.
  • PM (Phase Modulation) — LFO 2 shifts LFO 1's phase, making it wobble in time.
  • Add — LFO 2's output is added directly to LFO 1's output.

docs.title: Step Sequencer
docs.text:
The sequencer outputs a stepped voltage pattern that advances with each beat or at a set interval — good for geometric shifts, colour steps, and rhythmic stutter effects.

Note: The sequencer is on by default. If you don't use it, turn it off in Preferences → General (under Features, "Enable Step Sequencer"), or from the ⋮ kebab menu left of Edit's VAL column header, to hide its column and tab.

docs.title: The step editor
docs.text:
Each step is a bar. Bars sit in rows of up to 16, so a 32-step pattern is two rows. The step playing now is outlined, and every fourth step is numbered. A white line traces the output as it will actually move: flat steps when Step Hold is 100%, slides when it is lower. A dot rides the line at the current position.

  • Paint — click and drag across the bars to draw a pattern. Values snap to the Snap grid (5% by default; pick Off, 10%, 12.5% or 25% in the toolbar), and holding Shift paints freely. A fast drag fills the steps in between.
  • Nudge — hover a bar and scroll, by one Snap step per notch (Shift for 1%, Ctrl for 20%).
  • Keyboard — clicking a bar selects it (thin outline). While the pointer is over the bars, Left / Right move the selection, Up / Down nudge it (Shift for 1%), Delete or Backspace resets it, and Enter opens the number box.
  • Type a value — double-click a bar, type a number (0 to 100, or -100 to 100 for a bipolar parameter) and press Enter.
  • Reset — right-click or middle-click a bar to set it to 0.

Length is a 1 to 32 slider, so odd lengths such as 5 or 7 work. Steps past the end are kept and shown ghosted after the last playing step, so lengthening again brings them back. Phase starts the pattern part-way through, and Sync to Step 1 restarts it now.

docs.title: Pattern tools
docs.text:
The row above the bars edits the active steps:

  • Randomize — random values. Auto (when randomization is enabled) — also re-roll the pattern whenever a preset or deck is randomized; the deck morph then slides between patterns. Invert — flip every step.
  • Shift < / Shift > — rotate the pattern one step earlier or later.
  • Copy / Paste — copy a pattern (with its length) from one sequencer to another.
  • Fill... — Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Triangle, Alternate, Pulse or All On.
  • Euclid... — spread N hits evenly across the pattern, the classic euclidean rhythm, with a Rotate control and a preview before you apply.
  • Clear — reset all 32 steps to 0.
  • Snap — the grid painting and nudging snap to.

docs.title: Timing
docs.text:
• Beat — Syncs to the beat clock. Pick a subdivision from 1/16 to 4 beats per step.
  • Time — Wall clock seconds per step (0.01s to 5.0s).
  • Frame — Advances every N render frames (1 to 120).

Changing the clock unit keeps the same step duration where it can. Changing a Time or Frame interval while it plays keeps the current step and only changes the speed.

docs.title: Glide
docs.text:
• Step Hold slider — At 100% the value jumps instantly and holds flat for the full step. At 0% it glides smoothly from one step to the next over the whole duration. In between you get a hold then glide. It has a dice to randomize within a range, like the other sliders.
  • Glide Curve — Linear is a straight ramp; Smooth is an S-curve with gentle acceleration and deceleration. Greyed out while Step Hold is 100%, since nothing glides.

docs.title: Depth and Offset
docs.text: Depth scales the pattern and Offset shifts it up or down before it is applied to the parameter. Both can be randomized.

docs.title: Modulation Operators
docs.text:
When you set up a modulator, you also choose how it combines with the base value:

  • ADD — The modulation signal is added on top of the base value. Most common.
  • MUL — The signal multiplies the base value. Quiet when the base is low, loud when it's high. Like ring modulation.
  • SCALE — Attenuates the base value based on the signal. At zero signal you get full base value; at full signal the base is scaled down. Useful for "duck" effects.

All outputs are clamped to the parameter's valid range automatically.

docs.title: How values are shown
docs.text: Parameters, LFO and sequencer fields, and macro knobs whose range is 0 to 1 (or -1 to 1) display as 0 to 100 (or -100 to 100), with a decimal only when the value needs one (37, 37.4). Type either form. Angles stay in degrees, and parameters with their own units (counts, Hz, seconds, BPM) keep them. This is display only: presets, MIDI and OSC still use the underlying 0 to 1 values.

docs.title: Stepped parameters
docs.text: Some parameters are really a list of choices (a mode, a palette, a segment count). Their knobs show a tick mark for each choice (none when there are more than 16), and the value always lands exactly on a choice: a knob, LFO, audio source, macro, MIDI or OSC sweep passes through the choices instead of between them. In an FX row's focus mode the knob shows the choice's name when it has one (for example a 3D mode), otherwise its number. Hover a stepped value for the number of choices. In the VAL panel a stepped parameter with up to 16 choices gets a drop-down list of them (for example the 3D mode), and its live and starting values read as the choice name.

docs.title: Adjusting values without clicking
docs.text:
Hover over any slider or number and scroll the mouse wheel:

  • Scroll — fine step
  • Shift + scroll — medium step
  • Ctrl+Shift + scroll — coarse step

Middle-click any slider to reset to factory default.

docs.title: Edit shortcuts
docs.text:
These act on the selected cell in Edit (see Macros & the Rack for which Edit receives them when several are open).

Action Shortcut Save active preset Ctrl+S Save preset as... Shift+Ctrl+S Undo Ctrl+Z Copy cell Ctrl+C (with a CV cell selected) Paste cell Ctrl+V (onto another cell) Copy full parameter row Ctrl+C (with the VALUE cell selected) Clear / reset selected cell Delete or Backspace Toggle cell mute Middle-click the modulation cell Toggle row mute (all modulators) Right-click or middle-click the VAL cell

Muted cells still show the live oscilloscope but don't affect the parameter — useful for previewing what a connection would do without committing to it.

Toggle all modulators: Right-clicking or middle-clicking the VAL cell toggles mute for all active modulators assigned to that parameter. If the parameter has no modulators, middle-clicking the VAL cell resets the base value to default.

Copying cells: Copy an LFO, audio, or MIDI cell and paste it onto any compatible cell — the modulator follows automatically. Copy a full parameter row (from the VALUE cell) and paste it onto another parameter to clone all settings, rescaled to the new parameter's range.

Right-click any parameter row label or kebab button for a context menu with randomize, copy, paste, reset, mute/unmute all modulators, and note-editing options.

See Preferences → Keyboard Shortcuts for a full grouped list of all shortcuts in the app.

docs.title: Output & Recording
docs.text: This page covers everything about where your visuals go: sending them to projectors and other apps, recording your live set, and exporting a polished high-res render afterwards.

docs.title: Fullscreen & Projector Output
docs.text:
The simplest way to output: press F for Output View. The UI disappears and the master output fills the screen. Press Esc to come back.

To make the whole window fullscreen with the normal UI still showing, press F11 (again to restore the previous size and position). The two combine: F11 for a fullscreen window, then F for Output View on top of it.

For a second display or projector, use Preferences → Video & Display to configure a secondary output window you can drag to the projector screen and go fullscreen there independently.

Choosing the output screen: the Output → Secondary Output Window item fills one monitor. By default (Output → Output Monitor → Automatic) that is the first monitor that is not the system's primary one. If the video lands on the wrong screen, which can happen on Wayland where there is no true primary monitor, pick your projector under Output → Output Monitor. The choice is remembered by monitor name.

Output scaling: - If your shaders are demanding and your GPU is struggling (especially on a laptop), lower the internal render resolution in Preferences → Video & Display. Dropping from 1080p to 720p or 540p cuts GPU load significantly while the output still fills the screen. - Use Fit / Fill / Stretch to handle non-standard aspect ratios — useful for LED walls or vintage 4:3 projectors.

docs.title: Sending Video to Other Apps (Spout / Syphon / PipeWire)
docs.text:
Liquid LSD can share its video feeds live to other VJ apps, media servers, and streaming tools — without any encoding overhead or latency.

Go to Preferences → Video & Display → Live Video Sharing and toggle which feeds you want to share:

  • Deck A, Deck B, Deck BG, Deck PV (Preview), Master Output — enable any combination.
  • Set a custom stream name for each (e.g. LiquidLSD-Master, MainStage-Feed).
  • Choose a resolution for the shared stream, or keep it synced to the master.
  • Pick how the image is scaled if the resolutions don't match (Fit, Fill, or Stretch).

The sharing method depends on your platform:

  • Windows: Spout2
  • macOS: Syphon
  • Linux: PipeWire (DMA-BUF GPU sharing, with a memory fallback if the GPU doesn't support it)

On Linux with OBS: Add a PipeWire Screen Capture source and select the Liquid LSD video node. Use qpwgraph or Helvum to inspect and route video nodes.

Status: Check the Preferences → Video & Display panel for a live status indicator next to each shared feed showing which sharing method is active and whether it's working.

docs.title: Recording Your Set (REC)
docs.text:
Press Ctrl+R (or go to Output → Record Output) to start recording. A red REC mm:ss badge appears on the title bar while recording is active, along with a dropped-frame counter.

Press the same shortcut again, or click Stop Recording, to finish. The output file lands in the recordings/ folder as an MP4, named with the date and time (e.g. liquid_lsd_2026-09-01_20-15-00.mp4).

What you get: H.264 video at your current render resolution and frame rate, with synchronized audio from your input. On capable hardware, NVENC, QuickSync, or VAAPI hardware encoding is used automatically.

You can also map the REC toggle to a MIDI controller button so you never have to touch the keyboard during a performance.

docs.title: Offline Render Studio
docs.text:
The Offline Render Studio is for making video content — music videos, promotional visuals, or anything where quality matters more than real-time speed. It renders frame by frame at whatever resolution and frame rate you like, fully decoupled from the clock.

Open it via Output → Render Video (Offline)....

docs.title: What you can set
docs.text:
• Audio file — A .wav, .flac, .mp3, or .ogg file that drives the visual modulation.
  • Preset source — The current active deck, or any saved preset.
  • Resolution — 1080p, 1440p, 4K UHD (3840×2160), or custom.
  • Frame rate — Typically 60fps, but configurable.
  • Motion blur — 2×, 4×, or 8× temporal oversampling. Each frame is blended from multiple sub-frame renders, producing smooth cinematic motion on fast-rotating mandalas and feedback loops. More samples = more render time.
  • Output destination — Where to save the file.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
The audio file is decoded up front and the audio analysis runs mathematically per frame — so the beat tracking, frequency bands, and envelope followers all behave exactly as they would in real time, just calculated offline. You get a frame-accurate render even on complex shaders.

A progress bar shows render percentage, elapsed time, estimated time remaining, and output file size estimate. There's also a live thumbnail so you can confirm it looks right before committing an hour to a 4K render.

docs.title: Hardware Preferences & Persistence
docs.text: Your audio routing, MIDI mappings, display preferences, and broadcast preferences all save automatically to lsd-preferences.properties in the app folder (with automatic backward compatibility for existing lsd-settings.properties files). You don't need to reconfigure anything between sessions.

docs.title: Performance Controls
docs.text: This page covers two things that are especially useful during a live show: the trackpad performance surface, and the notes system for keeping reminders attached to your presets and parameters.

docs.title: Trackpad Performance Surface
docs.text:
If you're performing on a laptop, you can turn your trackpad into a hardware-style performance controller — a bit like the classic Stanton SCS.3m DJ mixer. Hold CapsLock to activate it.

While CapsLock is held: - The trackpad stops moving the mouse cursor - It becomes an absolute-position performance surface with three faders and a crossfader

Release CapsLock to return to normal mouse control.

docs.title: Surface layout
docs.text:
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  [Deck A Level]  [Deck BG Level]  [Deck B Level]   │  ← Top 55% of trackpad
│                                                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                   (dead zone)                      │  ← Middle buffer zone
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              Crossfader  (A ←——→ B)                │  ← Bottom 28%
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Bottom zone (crossfader): Drag left for Deck A, right for Deck B. The full width maps to the crossfader range. Touch the centre and it snaps to 50/50.

Top zone (level faders): Three vertical strips — left third controls Deck A level, middle controls Deck BG, right controls Deck B. Touch anywhere in a strip to jump the level to that position instantly.

Dead zone (middle): A buffer between the two zones that prevents accidental switches when you're moving fast.

docs.title: Multi-finger stutters
docs.text:
The real power comes from using two fingers at once. Each zone tracks fingers independently, using a last-in-first-out stack:

Crossfader cut stutters: 1. Hold one finger down on the Deck A side. 2. Tap repeatedly with a second finger on the Deck B side. 3. Each tap snaps the crossfader to B; lifting the tap snaps it back to A.

This gives you machine-gun visual cuts synchronized to your tapping rhythm.

Video strobes: 1. Hold a finger at the bottom of a deck's level strip (level = 0%, blackout). 2. Tap with a second finger at the top of the same strip (level = 100%, full brightness). 3. Releasing the tap drops the deck back to blackout.

This creates rhythmic video flashes and stroboscopic accents.

When all fingers lift from a strip, the level stays frozen where you left it.

docs.title: Setup on Linux
docs.text:
On Linux, the trackpad surface reads raw multi-touch input directly. This requires read/write permission on the input device.

If the permission isn't set up, you'll see a Touchpad Status: Read/Write Permission Required message in Preferences → General, next to the Enable CapsLock Trackpad Console checkbox, with an Install Permissions (Polkit) button. Clicking it installs the necessary udev rule using pkexec — no reboot required. If you ran the desktop installer script (./install-desktop.sh) when you first unzipped the app, this was done automatically.

On macOS, native trackpad support works without any extra setup.

Focus safety: If Liquid LSD loses window focus (e.g. via Alt+Tab), the trackpad grab releases immediately, so you're never locked out of your mouse.

docs.title: Hover tooltips
docs.text:
Hovering over almost any parameter in the app shows a tooltip with: 1. The parameter name, valid range, and factory default value. 2. A plain-English description of what the parameter does. 3. Any personal note you've attached to the parameter (in amber text).

Macro knob tooltips show the value in the target parameter's real units, with the knob position as a percentage: ZOOM: 5.00 (100%). The same real value is shown on the knob face (always while a row is in Edit, otherwise on hover).

Tooltips appear after a short delay (~250ms) so they don't flash annoyingly as you move the mouse.

docs.title: The three-tier notes system
docs.text:
You can attach notes at three different scopes:

Scope What it's for Where it's stored When it appears Source Note Notes about a visual generator (e.g. "Gyroid works best with low gain feedback") ~/.liquid-lsd/source-notes.json Stays with you globally, across all presets Preset Note Notes about a specific preset Inside the .lsd file Shows when hovering the preset name label on the deck monitor Parameter Note A reminder about a specific parameter in a preset Inside the .lsd file Shows in the parameter's hover tooltip

Source Notes are global and persist no matter which preset you load — good for tips about generators that are always true. Preset and Parameter Notes travel with the preset file when you share it.

docs.title: Adding and editing notes
docs.text:
Parameter notes: Hover over any parameter row in Edit's parameter grid and click ⋮ (or right-click the parameter name), then choose Add/Edit Parameter Note...

Preset notes: Right-click the preset name label below the deck monitor preview and choose Add/Edit Preset Note...

Source notes: Open the Deck Menu popup and choose Add/Edit Source Note...

All three open the same note editor: a multi-line text box up to 2048 characters. Press Ctrl+Enter to save, or Escape to cancel.

docs.title: The preset name label
docs.text:
Below each deck's monitor preview you'll see the name of the currently loaded preset. Hovering it shows the full file path, the last save time, and the preset note if one exists. A * next to the name means there are unsaved changes.

If no preset is loaded yet (the deck is in an unsaved state), the label shows Untitled in grey. You can't attach a preset note until the preset has been saved at least once.

docs.title: FX Chain & Slot Management
docs.text:
Every deck and the master bus each own one FX chain of 3 serial ISF filter slots: a deck's chain is its FX sub-tab, and Master FX (the Mixer's FX sub-tab in Edit) is applied to the final output after the crossfader. All five chains work the same way. Each chain has a Chain Super Knob and each slot its own Metaknob — see Macro Controls & the Perform View for how they work and where to edit them.

  • Deck row layout: the deck badge (A, B, BG, PV) carries a caption, slate SRC or cyan FX, naming the half the row shows. Line 1 is the long name box (click to Browse) and the Edit gear; line 2 holds ⋮, Save, queue ◀ ▶ and the slot pills on an FX row, or ⋮, Save, ◀ ▶ and a right-aligned Eject on a source row (same button sizes on both).
  • Chain menu (⋮): the same menu on the FX row and on the chain's Edit tab.
  • Focus Slot… / Exit Focus Mode.
  • Save As…: Saves the chain's 3 slots, Dry/Wet, Super Knob and links into an .lsdfxchain file, in the folder the chain came from (library/fx_chains/ for a new chain).
  • Revert to Saved: Puts the chain back the way its file has it.
  • Clear All Slots: Empties all 3 slots and starts a new Untitled chain.
  • Copy Chain / Paste Chain: Copies or pastes one chain between any decks and Master FX.
  • Revert, Clear and Paste can be undone with Ctrl+Z.
  • Per-Slot Kebab (⋮):
  • Save Slot Preset As...: Saves the slot's filter ID, dry/wet, Metaknob position/target, and parameters into an .lsdfx file in library/fx/.
  • Copy Slot / Paste Slot: Copies or pastes individual slot configurations across slots or chains.
  • Clear Slot: Clears the slot filter and resets parameters.
  • Drag-and-Drop Targets: Drag .lsdfxchain onto a chain header, or .lsdfx onto a slot, to instantly load/swap effects. A .lsdfxchain dropped onto a slot replaces the whole chain. Ctrl+Z undoes a drop.
  • Library Browser: The [ FX ] Library view's right-click menus can load stock filters, saved singles, and saved chains into any deck or Master FX.
  • FX is separate from presets: Loading or saving a deck preset (.lsd) never touches that deck's FX chain. FX chains are saved with your session and restored on the next launch.
  • Performance Matrix FX Controls:
  • Shared Chain Header (Name • on line 1, [⋮] [Save] [◀] [▶] [1] [2] [3] on line 2, [FX ON] on the right):
    • ◀ / ▶ (Decks A, B, BG): On Decks A, B, and BG, steps through the respective live FX queue (A/B or BG) directly on that deck, advancing the queue while targeting the clicked deck. Rendered disabled when the FX queue is empty. Omitted on Deck PV and Master FX, allowing the chain name button to expand while keeping row width perfectly aligned.
    • Chain Name Button: Displays current chain name with • when it differs from its file: a slot, parameter, Dry/Wet, link or Metaknob target changed. Turning the Super Knob or a Metaknob (and what the Metaknobs drive) is performing, not editing, so it doesn't count. When the chain's own Dry/Wet (set on its Edit tab) is below 100% the name shows it, e.g. Wet 40%, and at 0% the name is dimmed: the effects are not visible. Clicking binds the Library dock below to this chain (the Chain list: no row is expanded, and the name gets a coloured outline; ✕ or Esc lets go), with live text search over saved .lsdfxchain files. Accepts .lsdfxchain drag-and-drop.
    • [Save]: Overwrites the loaded chain file with current state, or triggers Save As if untitled.
    • [⋮] Menu: the chain menu above (Focus, Save As, Revert to Saved, Clear All Slots, Copy/Paste Chain).
    • [FX ON]: Turns the whole chain on or off at once. Lit while the chain is on, dark while it is bypassed, like each slot's power button. Saved with your session, not in chain files.
  • FX Slot Cells (Effect Name):
    • Drawn under each of knobs 2–4 on Deck rows in [FX] mode and the Master row in [FX] mode. The cell is just the effect name, so names get the full cell width.
    • ◀ / ▶ (on hover), Ctrl + Mouse Wheel, or Right-Click → Previous/Next in Shortlist: Steps to previous/next effect in the FX Shortlist. From a favorited ★ effect (or an empty slot) it walks your favorites; from any other effect it walks that effect's category alphabetically, and stepping off either end of the category lands in your favorites. The effect name's tooltip shows which list you are in and where, e.g. ★ 3/8 or Blur 4/12. The arrows only appear at the cell's edges while the mouse is over it. A plain mouse wheel scrolls as usual and never swaps a live effect.
  • Slot Side Buttons (left of each slot knob): two stacked buttons.
    • Link (top): links/unlinks that slot's Metaknob to the Super Knob. A linked slot's knob still moves its Metaknob; the Super Knob picks the slot up again when it reaches it.
  • Link All (left of the Super Knob, knob 1): links or unlinks all three slots at once. Click links all unless they are all linked already, in which case it unlinks all; the icon shows a chain when every filled slot is linked, a dimmer chain when only some are, and a broken chain when none are. The Edit tab has the same toggle by the SUPER KNOB & METAKNOBS title. Where a new chain starts (linked or unlinked) is the Default FX chain linking preference; how linked slots follow is Super Knob response (Relative or Pickup, see Macro Controls). In Pickup mode a slot still waiting for the Super Knob shows an amber link button, and on the Twister its LED blinks amber.
    • Bypass (bottom, power icon): turns just that effect on or off. Row-coloured when on, red when bypassed, dim when the slot is empty. In Focus Mode, only the focused slot's bypass is shown, next to knob 1.
    • Effect Name: Truncated caption showing loaded filter. Click points the Library below at that slot (Stock filters, ★ Favorites, and Saved .lsdfx presets); click it again to stop. This happens a moment after you release the click, so a double-click (Focus Mode) or a drag doesn't trigger it.
    • Drag & Drop: Drag an effect name onto another slot's name to swap/reorder (hold Ctrl while dropping to duplicate). Only the effects move: each slot keeps its own Super Knob link setting. Accepts stock ISF filters and .lsdfx single presets from Library; a .lsdfxchain replaces the whole chain.
    • Right-Click Context Menu: Focus Mode, Previous/Next in Shortlist, Replace..., Save as FX Preset..., Copy/Paste Slot, Reset Parameters, Clear Slot, Add/Remove from FX Shortlist (★), and Edit in Edit.
    • Undo: Ctrl+Z undoes a drag swap or copy, a drop, Paste Slot, Reset Parameters and Clear Slot. Stepping through the shortlist is not undone step by step.
  • Swap Gain Dip:
    • Replacing an effect or loading a chain applies a smooth audio/visual gain dip (fade out -> swap -> fade in) instead of a hard cut.
    • Duration is customizable in Preferences (FX Swap Fade (ms), 0–1000 ms, default 150 ms; 0 = immediate hard cut).
  • Knob Labeling:
    • Knob 1 controls the chain's SUPER knob. Middle-clicking it does nothing (centring it would move every linked slot at once).
    • Knobs 2–4 display META, while the effect name itself is clearly displayed in the slot cell below. A slot whose Metaknob has no targets shows NO TARGET, since turning that knob does nothing; add a target on the slot's Edit tab.
  • Focus Mode (Traktor / Mixxx style):
    • Entering Focus Mode:
    • Click any slot pill ([1], [2], or [3]) in the FX row header.
    • Or double-click any slot cell's effect name.
    • Or right-click a slot cell and select Focus Mode (Edit Parameters).
    • Header Controls in Focus Mode:
    • [⋮]: Chain kebab menu remains accessible for Save As, Clear, etc.
    • [Focused Effect Name ▾]: Displays the name of the focused effect; clicking points the Library's FX list at that slot to audition or swap shaders.
    • [◀ P1/N ▶]: Parameter page stepper; appears automatically whenever the focused shader exposes more than 3 parameters.
    • [1] [2] [3]: Slot focus pills with clean styling. The active slot pill is highlighted in blue accent. Click another slot pill to switch focus instantly, or click the active focused slot pill a second time (or press Escape) to exit Focus Mode back to the 3-slot chain view.
    • 4 Knobs in Focus Mode:
    • Knob 1 (META): The focused slot's Metaknob ($chainLabel/FX/FX<slot>/Meta). Its Dry/Wet is the Wet slider in the chain header. The focused slot's FxSlotCell is drawn underneath so shortlist stepping (hover ◀ ▶ or Ctrl + mouse wheel) and picker access remain directly below the knob, with the slot's bypass button to its left.
    • Knobs 2–4 (Top Parameters): Dynamically retargeted to the focused shader's parameters on the active page, in the slot's knob order (set in the Edit bay's Knobs list; the effect's own order by default) (e.g. SPEED, INTENSITY, COLOR).
    • Parameter Cells (FxParamCell): Drawn under Knobs 2–4 with the parameter's name and a modulation indicator dot. The current value is shown inside the knob face, and a [⟲] reset button (restores the authored default) sits to the left of the knob. Middle-clicking the knob does the same. Replacing the effect with one that has fewer parameter pages moves the page back to the last one.
  • Stable Layout: Knobs stay the same size and in the same place whichever mode a row is in (source, FX group, or Focus Mode), and switching one row never resizes the others. Knob names and effect/parameter names share the same line under each knob. Names too long for it end in …; hover the knob for the full name.
    • Seamless Hardware MIDI Retargeting:
    • Physical MIDI controllers mapped to the row's standard macro paths (Macro/<bankId>/knob_1..4) immediately control the focused slot's Metaknob and parameters without requiring any MIDI remapping or controller mode switching.
    • Exiting Focus Mode restores Knob 1 to SUPER and Knobs 2–4 to META.
  • Chain View:
    • Shows one deck's source row and one row per FX slot, so all three effects are playable at once, with the Browse list underneath. Open it from Chain View in any FX chain's [⋮] menu, or with the Chain button on the pair view's Browse header. Master has one too, with the Transitions row on top.
    • Rows 2-4 are FX1, FX2 and FX3. Each always shows its own slot, whatever the deck's FX row was doing: knob 1 is the slot's Metaknob (tap to bypass), knobs 2-4 its parameters on that slot's page. Beside the knobs: the effect's name (click to point the Browse list at that slot), the chain's [⋮] menu, the slot's Wet slider and, when the effect has more than three parameters, [◀ P1/N ▶]. Touching a slot row's knob also points the Browse list at that slot. The deck's die and FX ON button are on the FX1 row.
    • Load (next to Chain on the Browse header) swaps row 1 for a load row: the effect highlighted in the list, and three targets, → FX1, → FX2, → FX3, that load it into that slot (Ctrl+Z undoes it). The slot rows don't move, so you can load an effect, play it, and compare it with the other two. Press Load again to get the source row back.
    • Esc (or Back) leaves Chain view in one press, back to your Perform page. A page tab or opening Edit leaves it too.
  • Performance Matrix Tabs:
    • Deck FX chains are on each deck's FX row; Master FX is on the Master FX row, on the MIXER tab.
    • The Transitions row includes a [DICES] die button to randomize transition parameters with undo support.

docs.title: MIDI Hardware & Control Mappings
docs.text: Liquid LSD includes an intelligent, multi-type MIDI subsystem for connecting hardware controllers (DJ controllers, fader banks, rotary knobs, pads, foot switches, and keyboards).

docs.title: Quick Setup
docs.text:
1. Connect your USB or DIN MIDI interface.
  2. Open Preferences → MIDI Controls (or press Ctrl+,).
  3. Ensure Enable MIDI Subsystem is checked. The background watchdog automatically detects newly connected controllers without restarting the application.
  4. Check the Live MIDI Monitor (Sniffer) at the top of the panel: moving any knob or pressing any pad on your controller will immediately stream incoming packets (Channel, Message Type, Index, and Values).

docs.title: MIDI Learn & Modulator Variables
docs.text:
You can map any parameter, internal modulator variable, matrix CV modulator, or global performance action:

  1. In-Situ Right-Click Learn (Fastest):
  2. Right-click any slider or variable label in the UI — including an LFO's Speed / Subdivision, Depth, Min/Max bounds, Asymmetry (Slope), Morph, Hold, or a parameter's Initial Range (Base Value).
  3. Select Learn MIDI Mapping (...) from the context menu. This is a controller mapping: it sets the value itself and is saved in your controller profile, not in the preset. The slider will pulse in cyan/blue while awaiting hardware input.
  4. Move a knob, fader, or press a pad on your MIDI controller. Liquid LSD immediately maps the control, preserves your configured min/max limits, and saves the mapping to the active profile.
  5. If a macro knob currently drives that value (its slider shows the cyan lock and a [K#] badge), Learn MIDI is greyed out as "locked by K#": the knob rewrites the value every frame, so a mapping would do nothing. Release the target first (uncheck it in the macro editor), or map a different value.

  6. Right-click again and select Cancel MIDI Learn if needed.

  7. Modulation Matrix Cells:

  8. Click any cell in the MIDI column of the Parameters matrix, then click Learn MIDI Modulator (or Re-Learn MIDI Modulator) in Modulation. This adds a MIDI modulator that is saved in the preset and adds on top of the parameter's value; Clear MIDI Modulator removes it.

  9. Global Performance Actions:

  10. In Preferences → MIDI Controls, click Learn next to Queue Advance A/B Next, Queue Step Back A/B Prev, BG Shader Advance, BG Step Back, or Tap Tempo.

  11. Modulator Variable Paths:

  12. Modulator variables use unified path syntax: <parameterPath>:mod/<modulatorId>/<propertyName>. Learn writes the modulator's stable id, so the mapping keeps following that modulator when others are added, removed or reordered. Older numeric paths such as Deck A/geometry/zoom:mod/0/subdivision (LFO 1 Speed), :mod/0/depth or :mod/1/morph still work and resolve by list position. Modulator mappings resolve dynamically each frame and display user-friendly labels (e.g. Deck A/geometry/zoom [LFO 1 Speed]) in the MIDI Preferences mapping table.

docs.title: Intelligent Signal Classification
docs.text:
When you turn a knob or tap a pad during Learn mode, Liquid LSD inspects the incoming stream and classifies it automatically: - Note On / Off: Identified as a discrete button (pads/keys), defaulting to Momentary mode. - Continuous CC: Identified as an absolute continuous pot or slider ($0 \dots 127$). - Relative Rotary Encoders: Endless rotaries sending delta step packets ($63/65$ or $1/127$) are auto-classified into relative decoding mode. - Pitch Bend: 14-bit bipolar inputs are mapped with center-spring return.

You can override any auto-detected mode at any time using the dropdowns in Preferences → MIDI Controls.

docs.title: Fine-Tuning Continuous Controls
docs.text: In the Parameter Mappings table of the MIDI tab: - Min / Max Bounds: Clamp physical travel to a specific sub-range of the parameter. - Invert: Flips the physical direction ($0 \leftrightarrow 127$). - Slew (Smoothing): Configurable smoothing filter ($0 \dots 250\,\text{ms}$) that eliminates 7-bit "zipper noise" or stepped visual jumps on sensitive shader uniforms. - Soft Takeover (Pickup): Toggle between Immediate jump and Soft Takeover. With Soft Takeover active, parameter values will not jump upon loading a new preset until your physical knob/fader crosses the stored software value. The UI indicates Awaiting Pickup along with physical knob telemetry until synced.

docs.title: Discrete Controls (Buttons & Pads)
docs.text: Hardware buttons and pads support four distinct trigger behaviors: - Momentary: Active only while held; snaps back to minimum/default on release (ideal for video strobes, momentary feedback bursts, and glitch triggers). - Toggle (Latched): Flips state on each press. - Step Increment: Each press increments the parameter value by a configurable step size. - Step Decrement: Each press decrements the parameter value by a configurable step size.

docs.title: Relative Rotary Encoders
docs.text: Liquid LSD supports the three industry-standard relative encoding formats used by hardware like the DJ TechTools MIDI Fighter Twister, Behringer X-Touch, and Arturia controllers: - Binary Offset (64-centric): $65 = +1, 63 = -1$. - Signed Bit (1-centric): $1 = +1, 65 = -1$. - Two's Complement (1-centric): $1 = +1, 127 = -1$. Each rotary mapping includes an editable Step multiplier to dial in coarse or fine rotational sensitivity.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: All assignments are stored in JSON profiles under library/midi/<profile_name>.json. You can create, save, switch, and delete mapping profiles in the MIDI tab, allowing you to quickly switch between different hardware setups (e.g. home studio controller vs live gig setup).

docs.title: Controller Profiles: Midi Fighter Twister
docs.text:
Some controllers are recognised automatically. When a device whose name contains Twister connects, the app loads the built-in Midi Fighter Twister profile and its 16 encoders drive the Performance Matrix with no learning at all. (The log line Controller profile 'midi-fighter-twister' matches MIDI device: ... confirms the match.)

This section is in the order you will need it: one-time setup, what the knobs control, gestures, a first walkthrough, the side buttons, lights, troubleshooting, the optional XT firmware mode, and your own profiles.

docs.title: One-time setup in the Midi Fighter Utility
docs.text:
Do this once, in DJ TechTools' Midi Fighter Utility. The app ships a ready-made settings file for it, midi-fighter-twister.mfs:

  1. In Preferences → MIDI Controls → Controller Profiles, press Save Utility Settings... on the Midi Fighter Twister profile and pick a folder (the app remembers it for next time). Open Folder then shows the saved file.
  2. In the Utility, load that file, then send the settings to the Twister.
  3. That is all.
