The file sets every encoder on all four banks to Relative (ENC 3FH/41H) (binary offset: clockwise sends 65, counter-clockwise 63; relative mode has no end stops, so a knob never gets stuck at 0 or 127), every knob switch and all six side buttons to CC Hold, and every LED black in both its on and off state, so a knob the app is not using stays dark instead of showing the factory blue.

Then start Liquid LSD with the Twister plugged in and check Preferences → MIDI Controls → Controller Profiles: the Twister profile should be listed with your device. The log reports Controller feedback on for ... when the output port is opened; if it says No MIDI output port found, the app can read the Twister but cannot light it. While the app runs it overrides the ring and LED colours set in the Utility.

The app owns the banks. The top and middle side buttons on the right are plain CC Hold buttons, not the firmware's Previous/Next Bank. Right-top steps to the next bank (wrapping), Shift + right-top goes back; the app shows the bank's page and sends the bank change to the Twister, so the screen and the hardware agree. Right-middle opens the Library (Shift + right-middle opens it on the FX tab). Left-middle toggles Link All on the FX chain of the row you touched last (Shift + left-middle taps tempo). Don't set the side buttons to Previous/Next Bank in the Utility: the side buttons send six CC numbers per bank and would misfire.

If you set the Twister up by hand instead, use those same settings in the Utility.

To use the factory absolute mode instead, copy the profile to library/controllers/ and set "mode": "ABSOLUTE" on the knob input (the app then tracks each change, and a knob can hit the end of its 0-127 range).

docs.title: What the knobs control
docs.text:
The 16 knobs are the 16 knobs on screen. Knobs 1-4 are the first visible row, 5-8 the second, and so on, so the Twister's 4×4 grid mirrors the matrix. Whatever a row is showing is what its encoders control: a deck's source knobs, its FX chain's Super Knob and Metaknobs, or the focused effect's parameters. Focus an FX slot, with the mouse or the Twister, and the same encoders follow. In Edit the Twister follows the open module: knobs 1-4 control that module's 4 macro knobs (reflecting its active sub-tab, e.g. SRC or FX), while knobs 5-16 are inert. Edit itself (the full 3-column parameter matrix) is opened and edited with the mouse; the controller only opens Browse for a row.

The Twister's hardware banks pick the page shown on screen (three pages: A/B, BG/PV, MIXER; the fourth bank leaves the page as it is). Press right-top (Shift + right-top goes back) and the matrix changes with it; clicking a tab on screen moves the encoders to that page too, so screen and hardware always agree.

Bank Page Knobs 1-4 Knobs 5-8 Knobs 9-12 Knobs 13-16 1 A/B Deck A source Deck A FX Deck B source Deck B FX 2 BG/PV Deck BG source Deck BG FX Deck PV source Deck PV FX 3 MIXER Transitions Master FX Master MST Clock (knob 13)

Each row shows one half (source or FX), so no SRC/FX switching is needed on the hardware. Which page each bank shows is the profile's banks.pages; you can point a bank at your own page (see Perform Pages).

An FX row has the chain's Super Knob on its first knob and the three slots' Metaknobs on the other three. Focusing a slot (shift + tap) hands the whole row to that effect: knob 1 becomes the slot's Metaknob and knobs 2-4 its parameters (more than three parameters make extra pages).

docs.title: Gestures
docs.text:
Gesture On a source / mix knob On an FX slot knob On a focused parameter Turn moves the knob moves the slot's Metaknob moves the parameter Tap the switch reset to centre bypass or un-bypass that slot reset to the parameter's default Hold the switch and turn fine adjustment (10× slower) same same Shift + tap - focus that slot next parameter page Shift + tap on knob 1 of a focused row - leave focus - Tap on knob 1 (Super Knob) of an FX row - nothing (so a stray tap never moves every linked slot) - Shift + tap on knob 1 (Super Knob) of an FX row - Link All: link or unlink all three slots - Shift + tap on a deck's SRC knob (Master: a Transitions knob) Chain view on or off for that deck - -
  • Shift is the bottom button on the Twister's left side (the same physical button on every bank).
  • Fast turns accelerate up to 4×; slow turns stay exact.
  • Your own mappings win. If you have learned a mapping on a specific Twister channel/CC, that mapping still runs and the profile ignores that input.

docs.title: Walkthrough: load an effect onto Deck A with only the Twister
docs.text:
1. Go to bank 1 (A/B). Deck A's FX row is knobs 5-8 (the second row of the grid): knob 5 is the chain's Super Knob, knobs 6-8 are slots 1-3.
  2. Touch the slot you want. Give knob 6 (slot 1) a small turn. Browse opens for the last knob you touched, so this step chooses the target. Don't tap it: a tap bypasses the slot.
  3. Press the right-bottom side button. The Library below now applies to that slot (its name shows on the Library's tab line) and lists stock filters, favourites and saved effects. Nothing else on screen moves.
  4. Browse. Turn knob 16 (the last knob of the grid, bottom right) to move the highlight. Nothing is applied while you move. Right-bottom moves between the folder tree and the list; right-middle steps the tab.
  5. Tap knob 16 to apply the highlighted effect to the slot. The item currently loaded is tinted in the list.
  6. Stop browsing with left-top. The effect is now in slot 1; turn knob 6 for its Metaknob and knob 5 for the Super Knob (knobs 1-8 stay live the whole time).
  7. Tune it. Hold Shift and tap knob 6 to focus the slot: its parameters spread over knobs 6-8 and knob 5 becomes the Metaknob. Shift + tap knob 5 leaves focus.

Variations:

  • Replace an effect: repeat steps 2-5 on the same slot. Clear a slot: while browsing, Shift + right-bottom.
  • Load a saved chain into all three slots: touch knob 5 (the Super Knob) before step 3. The list then shows your saved chains, and Shift + right-bottom clears the whole chain.
  • Change Deck A's source instead: touch any knob in the source row (knobs 1-4) and press right-bottom for the source list. While browsing, touching a knob of the other row (knobs 1-8) moves the target to it.
  • Switching decks: while browsing, Shift + tap knob 9-12 (A, B, BG, PV) or 13 (Master) moves the target to that deck. Or stop with left-top, touch a knob on the other deck (switching Twister banks if needed), and press right-bottom again.
  • Master FX or a transition: use bank 3 and touch a knob in Transitions (knobs 1-4) or Master FX (knobs 5-8).
  • If nothing happens when you press right-bottom, you haven't touched a knob since the app started: turn one first.
  • Picking from the Library view instead is described below.

docs.title: Side buttons
docs.text:
The side buttons change meaning with the view:

View Left-top Left-middle Right-top Right-middle Right-bottom Knob 16 Perform back (Esc); Shift + toggles Edit mode toggle Link All; Shift + tap tempo next bank / page (Shift + prev) open the Library; Shift + opens it on the FX tab browse the touched row's slot; Shift + toggles Pair view normal knob Browsing a slot (bound Library or Pair view) stop browsing toggle Link All; Shift + tap tempo next bank / page, which stops browsing (Shift + prev); in the Pair view, the next pair step the tab (Shift + prev) step the pane; Shift + clears the slot or chain cursor: turn to move; tap applies, Shift + tap queues Chain view, playing leave Chain view toggle Link All; Shift + tap tempo next deck (Shift + prev), staying in Chain view open the Library; Shift + opens it on the FX tab Load on (row 1 becomes the load row) normal knob (FX3's last parameter) Chain view, loading leave Chain view toggle Link All; Shift + tap tempo next deck (Shift + prev), staying in loading step the pane (Shift + the tab) Load off (the SRC row comes back); Shift + clears the targeted slot normal knob; knob 4 is the cursor Library leave Library toggle Link All; Shift + tap tempo next bank / page (Shift + prev) step the tab (Shift + prev) step pane (Shift + prev) cursor: turn to move, tap to load; Shift + tap queues it (after the queue knob's cursor, see below)
  • Send-knob rings: a send knob that can receive the highlighted item shows a full ring at half brightness in the target's colour; the others stay dark. Set the encoders' indicator to Bar in the Midi Fighter Utility to get a full ring (a Dot ring shows a single LED).
  • Knob 16 ring: while browsing a slot and in the Library the ring shows the cursor's place in its list (empty at the first row, full at the last); it is full when the list has no cursor yet or one row.
  • Left-middle button: Toggles Link All on the FX chain of the row you touched last. Shift + left-middle taps the BPM tempo (clock.tap_tempo).
  • Right-top button: Steps through hardware banks / Perform pages (Shift + right-top steps backward).
  • Unsaved-changes prompt: when loading would discard edits on a deck, the prompt takes over the controller: left-top = Cancel, right-middle or knob 16 tap = Save, right-bottom or Shift + tap = Discard. Nothing else navigates until you answer.
  • Browsing a slot: moving never applies anything; only a tap does. Touch a knob of the row first; with none touched yet the button does nothing. When the row is on the current page the Library below simply starts applying to its slot; otherwise the Pair view opens. Knob 16 is the cursor. Knobs 9-15 do nothing (apart from the sends) while browsing (knobs 9-13 send the highlighted item, see below); knobs 1-8 keep controlling the first two rows on screen (the page's, or the pair view's two rows; they light in their rows' colours), so you can tweak a freshly loaded source or chain without stopping. Touching one of them points the browser at that row's slot. Touching a knob does not change the tab unless it moves the target, so it won't pull you off Queues or Macros. To pick for another deck, send the item there with knobs 9-12, use the quick switch, or stop with left-top first.
  • Chain view: Shift + tap any of a deck's SRC knobs (Master: a Transitions knob) to show that deck as Chain view: its SRC row on top, then FX1, FX2 and FX3, all 16 knobs live. The same gesture on row 1 leaves again, as does left-top. Right-bottom turns Load on and off. While loading, row 1 is the load row: knob 4 is the cursor (turn to move through the FX list, tap to apply the highlighted effect to the targeted slot), and a tap on knob 1, 2 or 3 loads it into slot 1, 2 or 3 (Ctrl+Z undoes it); those three glow in their slot row's colour while the highlighted item can go in a slot. Knobs 5-16 stay on the slot rows the whole time, so you can play what you just loaded and compare it with the other two slots. There are no send knobs in Chain view. The bank buttons step to the next deck (A, B, BG, PV, Master) and keep you in Chain view.
  • Edit: Left-top closes Edit (collapsing the module bay back to the Faceplate, same as Esc); Shift + left-top toggles Edit mode for the touched row. Right-bottom opens the pair view for the last-touched knob's row.
  • Banks in the pair view: pressing a bank button walks the pairs instead of changing the page: a higher bank is the next pair (Deck A, B, BG, PV, Master, wrapping; the Master pair is Transitions + Master FX), a lower bank the previous one, so you can reach any deck's pair from the Twister alone. A pair is the two rows that share a half of a page, so the MIXER page's other half (Master MST + Clock) has no list to browse and no pair.
  • Quick switch: while browsing a slot, Shift + tap on knob 9-12 (A, B, BG, PV) or 13 (Master) moves to that deck without sending anything (in place when the page shows its rows, else its pair view).
  • Send knobs (Library and while browsing): tap a knob in row three to send the highlighted item to a deck: knob 9 = Deck A, knob 10 = Deck B, knob 11 = Deck BG, knob 12 = Deck PV; in the FX tab knob 13 = Master FX. A source or preset replaces the deck's content (with the usual unsaved-changes prompt), an FX chain replaces all three slots, and a single FX goes into the first empty slot (the last slot if all are full). From the Library the send only loads (you stay in the Library with your place kept, so you can send the next item straight away, and an FX send shows a toast with where it landed); Ctrl+Z undoes it. While browsing a slot the target follows the send (in place when its rows are on the page, else its pair view), so you can play what you just loaded while knob 16 keeps browsing; send again to move to another deck. A knob glows in its target's colour while the highlighted item can go there. They work on the Sources and FX lists only. Back returns to Perform.
  • Library view, knobs 1-8: the Library hides the page, so the first two rows of knobs play the source and FX rows of the deck you last sent to with knobs 9-13 (Master's Transitions and Master FX rows after a knob 13 send). Until you send anything they play Deck PV, where previews go, so you can audition an item and tweak it straight away. A coloured Knobs 1-8: Deck PV label on the Library's tab line says which deck it is, and the knobs light in its colours.
  • Library view, queue knobs 14 and 15: with the queues under the browser (the Library maximized, Sources, FX or Transitions tab), knob 14 is the tab's main queue (A/B, A/B FX or Transitions) and knob 15 its BG queue (BG or BG FX; dark on Transitions). Their columns are outlined on screen in the knobs' colours (mint and rose). Turn moves that queue's highlight (the first turn lands on the playing item); hold the knob down and turn to carry the highlighted item up or down, one row per click; tap uses it now (as a double-click does); Shift + tap removes it (a toast says what went, and Ctrl+Z puts it back). The ring shows the highlight's place in the queue and fills for a moment when items arrive. Hide the queues and the two knobs go dark.
  • Queueing at a place: Shift + tap knob 16 puts the highlighted browser item (or the playlist under the tree cursor) after the highlight of the queue knob you touched last, and moves that highlight onto it, so a second item goes after the first. With the highlight on the playing item, the new item plays next. If you haven't touched a queue knob since opening the Library, it goes to the end of the main queue as before.
  • Auto-preview: Shift + tap knob 12 (the PV send) turns it on: PV loads whatever the cursor rests on for 0.4 s, on the Sources and FX tabs, and knob 12 blinks. Tap again, or leave the Library, to stop. It pauses with a message while PV has unsaved changes (rather than asking mid-scroll), and an effect previews on whatever PV is playing, so send PV a source first.
  • Library: a preset or generator loads onto the deck the crossfader is moving away from, a BG queue item onto Deck BG, a transition onto the mixer. In the FX tab, a tap applies the item to the live deck (a single effect goes into the first empty slot, the last slot if all are full; a chain replaces the deck's chain) and Shift + tap adds it to the FX queue. Holding Shift, the side buttons add to the BG queue and step the tab and list backwards.
  • Unified browser: a fresh tab starts in the list. Right-bottom moves on to the queues and Shift + it goes back to the folder tree. In the tree, turning moves a cursor (an outline) over the visible folders and playlists without changing the list; a tap selects the folder or playlist under it, which fills the list and clears the list's selection. A playlist is just a tree entry, so there is no separate playlist pane.
  • The FX queue transport commands (fx.queue_next/prev, fx.bg_queue_next/prev) have no free button in the built-in profile; map them in your own profile.

docs.title: Rings and LEDs
docs.text:
The Twister mirrors the screen. Each encoder's ring shows its knob's value, and its LED takes the colour of the row it controls. A knob with nothing to control goes dark: an empty or bypassed FX slot, or a blank position on a focused effect's parameter page (its ring still shows the value).

  • LEDs can't show greys, so on the MIXER page the Master row is red (the screen keeps its greys) and Transitions stay cyan.
  • The clock knob (knob 13, the first knob of the Clock row on the MIXER page) is the beat light: its LED sits dim plum and flashes light plum on every beat and orange on beat 1 of the bar, and its ring shows the tempo across the beat tracker's BPM search range (Preferences → Tempo & Sync). Push it to tap tempo (the same as the TAP button); turning it does nothing. On the stock firmware the ring brightness pulses instead of the colour. While a Library or picker is browsing, the knob does its browse job instead.
  • On pages with a pinned FX row (A/B, BG/PV, MIXER) the FX row's LED is a shifted hue of its source row's, so the four LEDs of a bank differ.
  • Waiting for pickup (Super Knob response set to Pickup): a linked FX slot the Super Knob hasn't reached yet blinks its LED amber and dark twice a second, on both firmwares, until the Super Knob gets there. Its ring keeps showing the Metaknob; on the stock firmware the ring is also dimmed (native mode can't dim rings). In Relative mode slots never wait, so nothing blinks.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Nothing responds: check Enable MIDI Subsystem in Preferences → MIDI Controls, and that the log shows the matches MIDI device line. Watch the Live MIDI Monitor to confirm the Twister's messages arrive.
  • Knobs jump to the ends or stick: the encoders are not in Relative (ENC 3FH/41H) mode on every bank (see setup).
  • Wrong page, or rings and LEDs from the wrong bank, or a side button doing the wrong thing: the middle side buttons must be CC Hold (save and load the settings file, see setup); on the factory Previous/Next Bank setting the side buttons send different CC numbers.
  • Unused knobs glow blue: the LEDs' off colour in the Utility is not black. Save and load the settings file (see setup), or set every knob's on and off colours to black on all four banks.
  • No lights at all: the log says No MIDI output port found. Reconnect the device, or close other software holding the Twister's port.
  • Rings lag or drop: the app writes lights to the showing bank a few messages at a time (the Twister drops bursts), rewrites the whole bank just after you switch to it, and re-sends it shortly after you stop turning, because the Twister redraws its own stored colours after bank changes. If rings still lag, raise output.minIntervalMs (default 2) in a copy of the profile.
  • See exactly what is sent: set "trace": true in the profile's output section (or start the app with LSD_MIDI_TRACE=1). Every message sent to the device, every bank change and every encoder message is then logged.
  • A Twister knob drives something else, or the browse cursor won't move: a learned mapping on that knob's channel/CC wins over the controller profile in the Perform view (while browsing, the profile wins). Clear the learned binding in the Learned Mappings list.
  • The Twister profile isn't in the Learned Mappings bar: that bar holds your learned mappings. The controller profile is chosen automatically from the device name and is listed under Controller Profiles in MIDI Controls.

docs.title: Optional: XT firmware and native mode
docs.text:
If you have flashed your Twister with the custom XT firmware (the nativeMode build from the Midi Fighter Twister Open Source project; flashing is done with DJ TechTools' tools and is entirely your choice), Liquid LSD can drive it in native mode:

  • Each ring follows its parameter: a bar, a bar with a centre detent for -100..100 parameters, and a dot for endless and stepped parameters. The style changes live as you change pages, effects and sources.
  • The switch LEDs show the exact row colour.
  • There are no hardware banks. Right-top steps through the Perform pages (Shift + right-top goes back); the other side buttons work as before. No Utility settings file is needed.
  • The send knobs (9-13) in the Library and while browsing a slot leave the ring off and show the target in the switch LED colour, because native mode has no half-brightness.

To use it: open Preferences → MIDI Controls → Controller Profiles, and in Use profile under the Twister choose Midi Fighter Twister (XT firmware, native mode). Choose the stock profile again to go back. Both profiles fit the same device name, so the app never switches by itself, and a Twister on the stock firmware must keep using the stock profile.

When the app quits, unplugs the Twister or you change the profile, the app turns the switch LEDs black and returns the device to normal. If the app crashes the Twister stays in native mode until you unplug and replug it.

docs.title: Your own profiles
docs.text:
Profiles are JSON files: built-ins ship inside the app, and yours go in library/controllers/*.json. A file with the same id as a built-in replaces it, so copy a built-in's JSON and edit it. A file with a mistake is skipped; the reason is logged and shown in the Controller Profiles section of Preferences > MIDI Controls. That section lists each profile and the device using it, and has Copy to User File (for built-ins), Delete User File (reverts to the built-in) and Reload Profiles (after you edit a file by hand).

Each user profile also has a Mappings list:

  • Click a command to choose another (the list is filterable and dimmed where the command can't be driven by that input).
  • Use the trash button to remove a mapping, or add one with the row at the bottom (modifier, input, command). Invalid edits are not saved; the problems are listed.
  • To map by touch, choose a command and a modifier in the add row, press Learn and move the control on the device. A control the profile doesn't know becomes a new input. Modifier and bank buttons can't be learned.
  • Only global mappings can be edited there; per-bank mappings are still edited in the JSON.

See docs/developer/unified_control_mapping.md for the format.

docs.title: OSC / TouchOSC Control Surfaces
docs.text: Liquid LSD includes a native, zero-dependency OSC 1.0 server for wireless control from TouchOSC and other OSC-capable apps on phones and tablets — no external bridge software required.

docs.title: Quick Setup
docs.text:
1. Open Preferences → OSC Controls (or press Ctrl+,).
  2. Check Enable OSC Server. By default it listens on UDP port 8000 and sends feedback out on port 9000 — both are editable, with a Restart Server button to apply port changes.
  3. Point your TouchOSC layout at your computer's IP address, using the same inbound/outbound ports. Move any control on the layout — Liquid LSD automatically learns the client's IP from the first packet it receives, so there's nothing to configure on the desktop side beyond the ports.
  4. The Live Packet Sniffer in the OSC Controls tab streams recent inbound and outbound traffic (address, arguments, and remote host) so you can confirm packets are arriving.

docs.title: OSC Learn & Modulator Variables
docs.text:
You can map OSC controls either in-situ from the UI or manually from Preferences:

  1. In-Situ Right-Click Learn (Fastest):
  2. Right-click any slider or variable label in the UI — including an LFO's Speed / Subdivision, Depth, Min/Max bounds, Asymmetry, a parameter's Initial Range (Base Value), the crossfader, fade speed, or a deck/transition queue's </> buttons.
  3. Select Learn OSC (...) from the context menu. The control will pulse in amber while awaiting input.
  4. Move a fader, knob, or XY pad on your TouchOSC surface. Liquid LSD ignores the first packet from a new address (guarding against a controller's connect-time sync burst) and maps once a later packet actually moves the value, preserving your configured min/max limits and saving the mapping to the active profile.
  5. As with MIDI, Learn OSC is greyed out as "locked by K#" while an enabled macro knob target drives that value.

  6. Right-click again and select Cancel OSC Learn (or cancel from Preferences) if needed. Once mapped, the same context menu offers Clear OSC Mapping to remove it without leaving the performance view.

  7. Manual Learn from Preferences:

  8. Open Preferences → OSC Controls.
  9. Type or paste the target parameter or modulator path into the Learn OSC field:
    • Base parameters: Mixer/crossfade, Deck A/geometry/zoom, Master/FX1/speed.
    • Modulator variables: Deck A/geometry/zoom:mod/<modulatorId>/subdivision (a numeric :mod/0/... is a legacy list position and still works).

  10. Click Start Learn, then move the control on your OSC surface.

  11. TouchOSC XY Pads & Multi-Argument Vectors:

  12. Multi-argument messages (e.g. /2/xy) are automatically unpacked into per-axis sub-addresses (/2/xy/0 for X, /2/xy/1 for Y). Learning from an XY pad maps the active axis.

docs.title: Fine-Tuning & Shaping
docs.text:
The Address Mappings table in the OSC Controls tab offers comprehensive per-control shaping: - Min / Max Clamping: Scales the incoming controller range $[0.0, 1.0]$ to custom parameter boundaries (e.g., $0.1\,\text{s} \dots 8.0\,\text{s}$ for an LFO period). - Invert: Inverts incoming values ($1.0 - x$). - Slew Rate Smoothing: Exponential filter ($0 \dots 250\,\text{ms}$) to smooth out coarse touch faders or packet jitter without visual stepping. - Soft Takeover (Pickup): Prevents value jumping by waiting until the physical controller crosses the current software value before taking over control.

Macro Knobs also respond directly to /macro/<bankId>/knob/1–/macro/<bankId>/knob/8 (no manual mapping needed), and broadcast their values back out over OSC whenever they change — keeping tablet layouts in bidirectional sync. See Macro Controls & the Perform View.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: Like MIDI, OSC address mappings are stored in JSON profiles under library/osc/<profile_name>.json. Create, save, switch, and delete profiles from the OSC Controls tab to switch between different tablet layouts or venues.

docs.title: Perform Pages
docs.text:
You manage pages in Preferences > MIDI Controls > Perform Pages (it is there even with MIDI turned off).

The tab strip above the matrix (A/B, BG/PV, MIXER) lists pages: each is four rows. Clicking a tab closes Edit and the Pair view, stops browsing a slot, and shows that page's rows, including when you click the tab you are already on. You can add your own by putting a JSON file in library/perform_pages/ (press Reload Pages in Preferences > MIDI Controls, or restart the app, to pick it up):

{
  "id": "mine",
  "name": "MINE",
  "tooltip": "Deck A source, Deck A FX, Transitions and Clock & Global",
  "rows": [
    { "row": "deck.A.src" }, { "row": "deck.A.fx" }, { "row": "trans" }, { "row": "global" }
  ]
}

A page needs exactly 4 rows. Row names: deck.A.src and deck.A.fx (likewise B, BG, PV) for a deck's source row and FX row, master.mix and master.fx for Master's levels and Master FX, trans, global. Each FX slot also has a row of its own: deck.A.fx1, deck.A.fx2, deck.A.fx3 (likewise for the other decks) and master.fx1 to master.fx3. A slot row always shows its slot, whatever the chain's FX row is doing: knob 1 is the slot's Metaknob (tap to bypass), knobs 2-4 its parameters on the slot's own page (Shift + tap a parameter knob for the next page). A page of deck.A.src, deck.A.fx, deck.B.src, deck.B.fx shows both halves of both decks at once. A file whose id is ab, bgpv, mixer or master replaces that built-in page. Pages saved by an earlier version that name deck.<tag>.srcfx or master are skipped (the log says why): replace those rows with the split ones above. You can also manage pages in Preferences > MIDI Controls > Perform Pages: copy a built-in page to edit it, create a new page, rename it and pick each of its four rows from a list, or delete it again. Edits are saved at once. Each page shows its controller name (perform.<id>), the name a controller profile uses; it does not change when you rename the page. To get a different name, type one into Name for a copy and press Copy As New Page, then hide the original if you like. Untick Show in tab strip to hide a page's tab (a Twister bank that selects it still shows it, with a temporary tab while it is active); with more than five tabs they narrow to fit. Files with mistakes are skipped; the log says why. A controller profile can select your page with perform.mine.

docs.title: Presets & Library
docs.text: Presets are the core unit of work in Liquid LSD. A preset captures the complete state of a deck — every parameter, every modulation connection, every note you've added — into a single .lsd file. The library and playlist tools are built around organizing and performing with those files.

docs.title: What a preset contains
docs.text:
• All visual parameter values (geometry, colour, view, feedback)
  • Every modulation setup (LFOs, audio connections, sequencer patterns, MIDI assignments)
  • Preset notes and per-parameter notes (if you've added any)

docs.title: Saving a preset
docs.text:
• Ctrl+S — Saves the active deck's preset to disk immediately. If the deck doesn't have a saved file yet, it opens a Save As dialog instead.
  • Shift+Ctrl+S — Always opens the Save As dialog, even for already-saved presets. The suggested name gets _copy appended so you don't accidentally overwrite the original.
  • Which folder — The Save As dialog has a Folder dropdown. It starts in the folder of the preset the deck was loaded from, so a variation lands next to its original. For a deck with no saved file, it starts in the folder selected in the Library tree, or else at the top level. Saving FX, chains and transitions works the same way.

When you modify a loaded preset, a * appears next to the deck name to show there are unsaved changes. A generator you picked without loading a preset is tracked the same way: tweak it and the deck shows *. Editing a knob's label or its targets counts as a change; turning a knob does not.

docs.title: Loading onto a deck with unsaved changes
docs.text:
Loading a preset, picking a generator, ejecting, or using Copy / Move / Swap onto a deck that has unsaved changes asks first: Save, Discard or Cancel. Tick Don't ask again on the prompt to always discard from then on (Ctrl+Z still undoes preset and generator loads). You can change this in Preferences → General → Manual Load Dirty Behavior:

  • Prompt (default) — Ask each time.
  • Discard — Overwrite without asking.
  • Auto-Save — Save the deck's preset first, then load.

Press Ctrl+Z after loading a preset or changing a generator to put back the previous deck, its knobs and its preset name. FX changes undo the same way wherever you make them (Perform rows, Edit, the Library): picking, clearing, pasting, dropping, swapping, resetting and reverting slots and chains. Shortlist stepping and FX queue steps don't. Picking or clearing the mixer transition from a bound list (after clicking it on its row) can be undone too. Eject, Copy / Move / Swap and Library loads of transitions can't be undone yet. Drag one monitor onto another and pick from the menu: Move, Copy or Swap, each for Source, FX or Source + FX. Copy, Move and Swap carry the knobs along with the source, so the knobs on the target deck control the copied parameters. A preset saved without knobs gets the generator's default knobs.

docs.title: The .lsd format
docs.text: Presets are plain JSON files stored in library/presets/ (and subfolders). You can open them in any text editor, back them up, share them, or paste them as JSON using Copy Preset JSON / Paste Preset JSON from the right-click context menu.

docs.title: Copying settings between decks
docs.text: Right-clicking in the VALUE column (or in Deck Controls) gives you copy and paste options to clone parameters from one deck to another. You can also copy individual modulator cells and paste them onto other parameters — see the Modulation page for details. You can also use the keyboard shortcuts CTRL-c and CTRL-v to copy and paste (or Command-c and -v on Macs)

docs.title: Unsaved changes & the Auto-VJ queue
docs.text:
The prompt above is for loads you start yourself. If Auto-VJ switches presets while a deck has unsaved changes, you can control what happens in Preferences → General:

  • Skip — Don't load the next preset until changes are saved or discarded.
  • Auto-Save — Automatically save the current state before switching.
  • Auto-Discard — Discard changes and switch immediately.

docs.title: The Library Panel
docs.text:
The Library panel spans the left and middle columns. That column has four views:

  • Perform — The Performance rows sit above the Library, which fills the rest of the window. This is the everyday view for playing a set.
  • Edit — Click a row's gear and the Library goes away completely. That row's pair of rows and its parameters fill the column, so you have room to fine-tune presets and FX. Press Esc, Back or the lit gear to get back to Perform.
  • Pair view — When you pick something for a deck whose rows are not on the current page (for example clicking the BG monitor while the A/B page is up), the Library goes away too: that deck's SRC and FX rows (or, for Transitions and Master FX, the Master pair's two rows) stay on screen with the same browser below. Press Esc or Back to return to Perform.
  • Library — The Library fills the whole column and the Performance rows are hidden. Use this when you're building or editing playlists and queues.

Press Space (when the cursor isn't in a text field) or the button at the right of the Library's title bar to switch between Perform and Library. From Edit or the pair view, Space, Ctrl+F or / closes them (cancelling any armed Add Target or Learn) and brings the Library back; Esc from there returns to the Edit or pair view you left, with the same slot.

The Performance rows have a fixed height, so the Library gets whatever window height they leave: a taller window means a taller Library.

docs.title: Picking for a slot: the Library applies in place
docs.text:
Click a source name, an FX chain name, an FX slot or the transition name on a Perform row, and the Library below starts applying to that slot. Nothing moves. The slot is outlined on its row, the list's border takes the row's colour, and the Library's tab line shows the slot's name (for example "● Deck A · FX 1") with its buttons (Save, Clear Slot / Clear Chain) and a ✕. A deck monitor, the main output monitor or the Master M badge does the same for a deck's source or the Master FX chain.

  • Click a row to apply it; the list stays, so you can try several in a row. Ctrl+Z undoes each pick.
  • Double-click applies the row and goes back to the plain Library.
  • Esc, the ✕, or clicking the slot on its row again stop without applying. Changing page stops too.
  • Only rows the slot can take are listed, and the row that is applied is tinted.
  • Pick another tab and the name greys out ("paused"): that tab is the plain Library. Going back to the slot's tab, or clicking the slot again, picks up where you were.
  • Space (or maximizing the Library) pauses the binding while the Library fills the column; Space again or Esc brings it back. Ctrl+F or / keeps it and just jumps to the search box.
  • On a deck with unsaved changes the first pick asks Save / Discard / Cancel; your answer is reused while that deck stays bound.

The pair view works the same way, with its header line instead of the tab line: Back, a Browse | Params switch (Params opens the full editor for the half you last touched; Edit's own header has the same switch to come back), the target and its buttons, and what the queue plays next. Edit and the pair view keep this line in the same place, so switching between them moves nothing. The Master pair (Transitions + Master FX) starts on the Master FX chain, or on the transition if you touched that last.

docs.title: Library View Mode ([ Sources ] / [ FX ] / [ Transitions ] / [ Macros ])
docs.text:
Toggle between sources, FX, transitions and banks (macro banks and Perform pages) using the segmented mode button in the top-left of the Library menu bar. Sources, FX and Trans share one three-part browser:

  • Folder tree (left) — All, Recent (the last 20 items you loaded or applied, newest first, kept across restarts), Favorites, the kind's sections (Sources: stock sources, saved presets and live external video; FX: stock filters, saved single FX and saved chains; Trans: stock transitions and saved transitions), and a Playlists group with one entry per playlist. Arrows fold a group open or shut. Each entry shows how many items it holds (none when empty). Click one to list it. A playlist is just another tree entry: select it to see and edit its rows. The list-plus button above the tree makes a new, empty playlist.
  • Tags — Tags work like crates: an item can have any number, and the Tags group in the tree (folded at first) lists every tag of the tab with a count. Pick a tag to list everything that has it. Right-click any saved row (or a multi-selection) for Add Tag... (type new tags or click existing ones) and Remove Tag, or drag rows onto a tag in the tree. Right-click a tag for Rename Tag... and Delete Tag... (which removes it from every item; the items stay). Tags are stored in each file, so they travel with it; stock items have categories instead and don't appear under Tags.
  • Folders — The saved sections (Saved presets, Saved single FX, Saved chains, Saved transitions) can hold folders, nested as deep as you like; stock sections can't. The folder-plus button above the tree makes a new folder in the selected saved section or folder. Right-click a saved section or folder for New Folder..., Rename Folder..., Delete Folder... and Reveal in File Manager. To move items, drag rows (or a multi-selection) onto a folder, or use Move to in the row menu; drag a folder onto another folder (or its section) to move it. Moving an item somewhere that already has one by that name asks whether to Keep both (the moved one gets _2) or Skip it. Moving and renaming keep every playlist, queue, Favorite and Recent entry pointing at the item, and a deck or chain loaded from it still saves back to it.
  • List (middle) — The rows of the selected tree entry, with a search box on top (Ctrl+F or / focuses it, or just start typing a letter while the list has the keyboard) and a button for the kind's "new" action: New preset for Sources, a save icon for FX and Transitions (save what is playing). On Sources, the ⋮ beside it has Restore Factory Presets and Import Flame.
  • Queues tab — All five queues side by side: A/B, A/B FX, BG, BG FX and Transition, in that order (which the crossfader advances through automatically). Items get in from the other tabs (Q, Shift+Q, the row menu or drag-and-drop); this tab is where you watch, reorder and play them. An empty queue says how to fill it, and every column has the same button strip. While you drag something a queue can't take (a source over an FX queue, a stock source, another queue's row), that column dims and won't accept it; a drop that mixes kinds keeps only the right ones and says how many it skipped. When items arrive in a queue, by drag or by Q / Shift+Q, its border flashes briefly. Dragging near the top or bottom edge of a long queue scrolls it.
  • Queues under the browser — In the Library view (the Library maximized), the Sources, FX and Transitions tabs show the five queues under the browser, so you can audition a source, effect or chain and drag it straight to the place in a queue it should go, instead of adding it at the bottom and reordering on the Queues tab. Drag the line between the two halves to give either more height (double-click it for half and half); the rows-icon button left of Restore hides or shows the queues. The arrow keys and the controller's cursor step from the browser on into the queues. The Perform view's Library is too short to split, so it stays as it is.

Loaded markers. Rows in the Sources, FX and Transitions lists carry one coloured chip per deck holding the item, to the left of the name: A / B / BG / PV for a source, preset or external stream, and M for Master FX or the current transition. When they don't fit they shrink to colour bars, and a count shows only for many slots; hover them for the full list (stock effects list deck and slot, such as A2). Saved single effects and saved transitions are not marked.

Row names. Long names end in "..." (hover for the full name), and saved file names are shown readably (hyperspace_crash_zoom reads "Hyperspace crash zoom"; the file keeps its name). A muted gauge marks a heavy shader that may run slowly on integrated graphics.

Keyboard. Enter runs the highlighted row's default action on every tab (what a double-click does, or apply while a slot is bound). Delete (set in Preferences → Shortcuts; Backspace works too) deletes the selected saved items after a confirmation, which names the playlists and queues they're in. Deleted items and folders go to the system trash where there is one (macOS, Windows, and Linux desktops with gio), so you can get them back from there; otherwise deleting can't be undone. The Rename, Delete, New Playlist and Export dialogs put the cursor in their text field; Enter confirms and Esc cancels.

The mode buttons pick what the three parts show:

  • [ Sources ]: stock sources and saved full deck presets (.lsd, in library/presets/); setlists (.lsdplay) live in library/playlists/.
  • [ FX ]: stock ISF filters, saved single-slot FX presets (.lsdfx, in library/fx/) and saved 3-slot FX chains (.lsdfxchain, in library/fx_chains/); curated FX playlists (.lsdfxplay) live in library/fx_playlists/.
  • [ Transitions ]: stock ISF transition shaders and saved transition presets (.lsdtrans, in library/transitions/); setlists (.lsdtransplay) live in library/transition_playlists/.

The same browser applies to a slot when you click one on a row (see above); then a click applies to that deck's source, slot, chain or the mixer transition.

docs.title: The Unified Sources Browser
docs.text:
The [ Sources ] list shows two kinds of row side by side, each marked with its own icon:

  • Stock Sources — The bundled generators (see Visual Sources for the list), plus external video streams and any custom sources dropped into your configured shader directories. They load straight to a deck's source stage with their shader's default parameters; they can't be added to a playlist or queue.
  • Saved Presets (.lsd) — A full deck preset: the source plus every parameter value, modulation connection, and note. Its row shows the source it plays before its tags; a preset whose source isn't installed (or failed to compile) shows ⚠ and won't load.
  • External Video — Live Spout, Syphon or PipeWire streams running right now, one row each in the External video folder (empty when none is active). Load one like a stock source (double-click, the menu, or drag it onto a deck); it appears and disappears as the stream starts and stops. Streams are not files, so they have no favorites, playlists or queues and cannot be saved as presets.

Pick a section in the folder tree to show only stock sources, saved presets or live streams. Use the New preset button above the list to eject a deck to blank so you can build a new preset on it (see Saving a preset above).

  • Search — Type to filter by name, tag, or (for stock sources) category. Ctrl+F or / jumps focus to the search box of the open tab (Sources, FX or Transitions) from anywhere in the app.
  • Multi-Selection (Shift-Click & Ctrl/Cmd-Click) — works the same in the Sources, FX and Transitions lists:
  • Click — Selects a single row, clearing existing selections.
  • Ctrl+Click (or Cmd+Click on macOS) — Toggles selection of an individual item without affecting others.
  • Shift+Click — Selects every visible row from the last clicked row to this one. Ctrl+Shift+Click adds that range to the existing selection.
  • Ctrl+A (Cmd+A) — Selects every row the list is showing (after search and the folder pick), while the list has the keyboard.
  • Batch Queueing — When multiple rows are selected, pressing Q (or the row menu's Add N … to A/B Queue) enqueues them all in list order into the A/B Queue. Pressing Shift+Q (or Add to BG Queue) enqueues them into the BG Queue. The hotkeys and row menu act on the tab you picked the items on: in the FX tab they feed the FX queues, and in the Transitions tab Q feeds the transition queue (there is no background queue for transitions).
  • Batch Context Menu — Right-clicking a row inside the selection shows the count and the actions that make sense for several items: Add N to A/B Queue, Add N to BG Queue, Add N to '' and Delete N.... Right-clicking a row outside the selection selects just that row. Stock rows that can't be queued (stock sources, stock FX filters) or deleted (any stock row) are skipped and not counted.
  • Multi-Item Drag & Drop — Dragging any row from a multi-selection carries all selected saved items into a playlist or queue at once. A deck, FX slot or the crossfader takes one item, so drag a single row there.
  • Batch Deletion — Pressing Delete or choosing Delete N... opens a confirmation listing exactly what will be deleted. Inside a playlist, Delete removes the selected rows from the playlist instead.
  • While the list is bound to a target (opened from a deck, slot or transition to pick for it), a click applies the row, so selection stays single there.
  • Double-click — Loads the item into whichever deck is currently inactive on the crossfader. For a stock source this replaces only the deck's source, leaving its FX chain untouched; for a saved preset it loads the full deck state.
  • Alt+click — Previews the source or preset on Deck PV.
  • Right-click or ⋮ (saved presets) — Load to a specific deck, add to a queue or to the selected playlist (Add to ''), Rename... (also edits tags), Clone..., Delete..., or Reveal in File Manager.
  • Renaming and deleting keep everything in step — Renaming a saved preset, FX or transition updates every playlist, queue, Favorites and Recent entry that points at it, and a deck or FX chain loaded from it keeps saving back to the renamed file. Deleting one removes it from all of those too.
  • Right-click or ⋮ (stock sources) — Load to Deck A/B/BG or Preview on Deck PV only. Stock sources have no persisted parameter state, and their bundled defaults and Metaknob auto-mappings haven't all been individually audited yet, so they're intentionally left out of playlists and the live/background queues — an unattended queue firing an unverified default has no performer there to catch it. Loading straight to a deck is fine, since you're present to dial it in.
  • Drag-and-drop — Drag any row (or multi-selection) onto a deck's monitor in the Mixer panel or onto its row in the Performance Matrix to load it (source-only for stock rows, full preset for saved rows). Saved presets can also be dragged into the playlist in the tree or a queue; stock sources can't, for the same reason the context menu omits those options.
  • [!] before the name — Appears when a saved preset has modulators that are inactive or hidden right now (for example MIDI or audio is turned off). The preset still loads fine; hover the row to see what's missing.

docs.title: The Unified FX Browser
docs.text:
The [ FX ] list shows three kinds of row side by side, each marked with its own icon:

  • Stock ISF Filters — Built-in filters with no saved parameters. A deck or Master has several FX chain slots, so a bare stock filter is ambiguous without knowing which slot it targets — double-click and drag-and-drop resolve this by loading into the first vacant slot, and the right-click menu lets you pick a specific slot explicitly (Load to Deck/Master > Slot 1–3). That same ambiguity is why stock filters can't be added to a playlist or live queue: there's no interactive slot-picker available when a queued item gets applied automatically later.
  • Favorites — Right-click a stock filter, saved single or saved chain and choose Add to Favorites (or Remove from Favorites) to star it. Starred rows show a ★ in the list, and the Favorites folder in the tree lists only them. Starred stock filters are also the slot shortlist that a slot's ◀ / ▶ steps through; saved FX are not, since stepping changes the effect, not a saved setup.
  • Saved Single FX Presets (.lsdfx) — One FX slot's full parameter state, captured from a deck.
  • Saved FX Chains (.lsdfxchain) — A complete 3-slot FX pipeline, captured from a deck's or Master's FX chain. Loading a chain replaces all 3 slots on the target chain.

Pick a section in the folder tree to show only stock filters, singles or chains. Use the save button above the list to save the current FX state of any deck or Master FX slot (or all 3 slots as a chain) into a new preset.

  • Multi-select: Ctrl/Cmd+click, Shift+click and Ctrl+A select several rows, as in the Sources list; the row menu, Q/Shift+Q, drag and Delete then act on all the saved singles and chains among them (stock filters load one at a time).
  • Drag-and-Drop: Drag a saved single or chain onto Slot 1–3 in a deck's Edit FX subtab, onto an FX playlist in the tree, or onto a A/B FX Queue.
  • Double-click: Loads into the dominant deck's first vacant slot (singles) or overwrites all 3 slots (chains). If all 3 slots are full, a single effect asks which slot to overwrite. FX always goes to the deck the crossfader is on (it is audible now); presets and generators go to the other deck (the next look). At exactly the middle of the crossfader, FX goes to Deck A and presets to Deck B.
  • Right-click or ⋮ menu: Load to > Deck [A|B|BG|PV] / Master FX > Slot [1|2|3] (stock filters and singles) or Load to Deck [A|B|BG|PV] / Master FX (chains), plus Add to A/B FX Queue, Add to BG FX Queue, Add to '', Rename..., Clone, Delete... and Reveal in File Manager. Deleting a saved effect also removes it from the queues and playlists.

docs.title: Bundled Stock FX Chains
docs.text:
Liquid LSD includes 16 pre-calibrated 3-slot FX chains in library/fx_chains/ designed for live club and festival VJ performance:

  1. Hyperspace Trip (hyperspace_trip.lsdfxchain):
  2. Slots: kaleidoscope → feedback → gradient_map
  3. Vibe: Classic psychedelic trance / festival tunnel breakdown with multi-axis kaleidoscopic folding, dithered zoom burst, and filmic Oklab contrast roll-off.
  4. The Drop Weapon (the_drop_weapon.lsdfxchain):
  5. Slots: radial_blur → video_strobe → rgb_split
  6. Vibe: High-intensity EDM/bass music drop impact with directional motion streaks, rhythmic beat flash gating, and chromatic aberration impact.
  7. Cyberpunk 1984 (cyberpunk_1984.lsdfxchain):
  8. Slots: pixelate → retro_crt → rgb_split
  9. Vibe: Retro-futuristic dystopian terminal aesthetic with honeycomb pixel lattice, curved CRT phosphor scanlines, and duotone cyberpunk neon grading.
  10. Liquid Mercury (liquid_mercury.lsdfxchain):
  11. Slots: luma_displace → fluid_smear → bloom
  12. Vibe: Viscous organic fluid and metallic chrome distortion with concentric liquid ripples, curl advection smearing, and surface normal refraction.
  13. Neon Wireframe (neon_wireframe.lsdfxchain):
  14. Slots: neon_edge → directional_blur → feedback
  15. Vibe: Glowing electric neon vector graphics with orientation-to-hue Sobel edge glow, spherical optical lens bulging, and soft high-pass bloom.
  16. Wormhole Flight (wormhole_flight.lsdfxchain):
  17. Slots: polar_tunnel → pinch_bulge → bloom
  18. Vibe: Deep space infinite warp portal with aspect-preserving log-polar vortex, zoom burst trails, and recursive feedback rotation.
  19. FLIR Predator Vision (flir_predator_vision.lsdfxchain):
  20. Slots: thermal_scanner → retro_crt → video_strobe
  21. Vibe: Military reconnaissance and sci-fi tactical optics with FLIR Ironbow heat mapping, sensor noise grain, horizontal smear, and quantized block mosaic.
  22. Liquid Chrome Dimension (liquid_chrome_dimension.lsdfxchain):
  23. Slots: wave_displace → mirror_sphere → color_levels
  24. Vibe: 3D raytraced floating chrome orb reflecting the scene with liquid surface turbulence and punchy high-contrast color grading.
  25. 2D to 3D Elevation with Feedback (2d_to_3d_elevation_with_feedback.lsdfxchain):
  26. Slots: 3d_elevation → feedback → bloom
  27. Vibe: The iconic Liquid LSD topological displacement chain featuring heightmap mesh rendering, recursive rotation feedback, and ACES filmic grading.
  28. Laser Concert Anamorphic (laser_concert_anamorphic.lsdfxchain):
    • Slots: anamorphic_streak → bloom → color_levels
    • Vibe: Ultra-widescreen concert stage lighting with horizontal laser glare, soft volumetric bloom, and high-contrast filmic punch.
  29. Pop-Art Comic Print (pop_art_comic_print.lsdfxchain):
    • Slots: neon_edge → halftone → gradient_map
    • Vibe: Authentic Roy Lichtenstein / vintage comic book print with black ink contours, 4-plate CMYK dot rosettes, and duotone pop grading.
  30. Grindhouse VHS Bootleg (grindhouse_vhs_bootleg.lsdfxchain):
    • Slots: vhs_glitch → retro_crt → color_levels
    • Vibe: Gritty 80s horror / VHS bootleg tape with magnetic tracking jitter, head-switching bars, phosphor scanlines, and tape saturation.
  31. Prismatic Crystal Kaleidoscope (prismatic_crystal_kaleidoscope.lsdfxchain):
    • Slots: faceted_glass → kaleidoscope → rgb_split
    • Vibe: Shattered diamond prism reflection with polyhedral symmetry and spectral dispersion.
  32. Cosmic Black Hole Vortex (cosmic_black_hole_vortex.lsdfxchain):
    • Slots: vortex_swirl → luma_displace → polar_tunnel
    • Vibe: Gravitational accretion singularity with logarithmic space swirl, surface normal marbling, and infinite log-polar warp.
  33. Subtle Optical Warmth (subtle_optical_warmth.lsdfxchain — the default Master FX):
    • Slots: color_levels → retro_crt → bloom
    • Vibe: Gentle tape/phosphor warming with contrast roll-off, subtle enough to leave on the master all night.
  34. Digital Bitcrush Mosaic (digital_bitcrush_mosaic.lsdfxchain):
    • Slots: pixelate → rgb_split → video_strobe
    • Vibe: Lattice quantization and spectral glitch.

On a fresh install, Master FX starts with Subtle Optical Warmth, Deck A with Liquid Mercury, Deck B with Liquid Chrome Dimension, Deck BG with Hyperspace Trip, and Deck PV with Prismatic Crystal Kaleidoscope.

docs.title: FX Playlists (.lsdfxplay)
docs.text: FX playlists are entries under Playlists in the FX tree. Select one to edit it like a preset playlist: drag singles/chains in from the list to insert them, drag rows to reorder, and double-click an entry to apply it. Entries whose file is gone are listed below the playlist's rows instead, with Find, Locate... and Remove (see Playlists).

docs.title: A/B FX Queues (A/B and BG)
docs.text:
On the Queues tab the two FX columns are independent live FX queues — volatile, RAM-only sequences of FX singles/chains you can improvise with mid-set:

  • < / > — Step to the previous/next queued FX item and apply it.
  • 🔁 Repeat — Cycle back to the start when the bottom of the queue is reached.
  • 🔀 Shuffle — Play items in random order.
  • ⋮ menu (right of the column caption) — Export as playlist... saves the current live queue as a new .lsdfxplay playlist; Clear queue empties it.
  • Drag-and-drop — Reorder items within a queue, or drag a preset/chain from the list to append or insert it.
  • No Auto button on the FX queues: they have no timer of their own and step with < / >, the controller, or their deck's preset queue.
  • Double-click an item to jump straight to it. Pressing the MIDI controller's accept on a queue item does the same: it moves the queue position, fades to the loaded deck and advances the transition queue.

The A/B queue applies to whichever of Deck A/B is currently dominant on the crossfader; the BG queue always applies to Deck BG.

docs.title: Playlists (Setlists)
docs.text:
Playlists are where you build your setlist; they appear under Playlists in the Sources folder tree. Playlists are .lsdplay files — simple ordered lists of presets.

  • Switch between playlists — Click another playlist in the tree.
  • Reorder — Drag and drop presets within the list. Changes save automatically.
  • Playlist actions (right-click the playlist in the tree), for the A/B Queue and again for the BG Queue:
  • Play now — Replaces the queue with this playlist and starts playback.
  • Insert after current — Slides the playlist into the queue right after the currently playing preset.
  • Add to the bottom — Appends it to the end of the queue.

The same menu has Rename..., Clone, Delete... and Reveal in File Manager.

Missing items. If a playlist refers to a file that was moved or renamed outside the app, or deleted, that item is listed under the playlist's rows with a ⚠. Find lists files of the same name elsewhere in the library; pick one to use it. Locate... lets you pick the file yourself, and Remove takes the item out of the playlist. Find all fixes every missing item that has exactly one same-named file. A found file is fixed everywhere the old path was used, in every playlist and queue, not only this one. (Moves and renames made inside the app never leave items missing.)

Playlist folders. Right-click Playlists in the tree for New Folder...; right-click a playlist folder to rename or delete it. Drag a playlist onto a folder (or onto Playlists for the top level) to move it, and drag folders onto each other to nest them. Playlist folders work the same on the Sources, FX and Transitions tabs.

docs.title: The A/B Queue (Auto-VJ)
docs.text:
The play queue drives the main crossfader automatically, sequencing through presets with transitions between Deck A and Deck B.

  • Transport controls — < (previous), ▶/⏸ (play/pause), > (next).
  • Loop / Shuffle — 🔁 for continuous looping, 🔀 for random order.
  • Add to queue — Select a preset in the browser and press Q, or right-click and choose Add to A/B Queue.
  • Export / Clear — The ⋮ menu at the right of the queue's caption has Export as playlist... (saves an improvised live queue as a permanent playlist file) and Clear queue. Every queue column has the same header: a caption naming the queue with the menu, then one row of icon buttons (hover for a tooltip).

When the queue is playing, the crossfader moves automatically between decks as presets transition. Grabbing the crossfader manually immediately pauses Auto-VJ so you have direct control.

docs.title: BG Queue (Deck BG)
docs.text: The BG Queue works the same way as the main queue but drives Deck BG independently. Add presets with Shift+Q. Background transitions use dip-to-black fades — double-click or right-click a queued item to choose between an instant cut or a fade.

docs.title: Curated Transitions Suite & Transition Presets
docs.text:
Liquid LSD features a curated suite of 8 club-grade ISF transition shaders designed for high-impact live mixing between Deck A and Deck B:

  1. Linear Crossfade (linear_crossfade.fs) — Pristine, transparent dissolve with Perceptual Cosine S-curve, Linear, or Equal Power curve modes.
  2. Luminous Flash (luminous_flash.fs) — Midpoint exposure flare and Gaussian bloom overdrive with tunable color temperature (-1.0 icy strobe to +1.0 warm amber) and spread, designed for high-energy beat drops.
  3. Film Burn (film_burn.fs) — 35mm celluloid burn with multi-octave procedural fractal noise erosion and glowing chromatic combustion contours (Fiery Ember, Electric Violet, Acid Green).
  4. Noise Dissolve (noise_dissolve.fs) — Multi-octave domain-warped fractal noise erosion with soft feathered contours and chromatic fringing.
  5. Liquid Displacement (liquid_displacement.fs) — Interactive cross-deck vector morphing where Deck A and Deck B dynamically displace each other's UV coordinates based on luminance gradient fields.
  6. Kinetic Zoom (kinetic_zoom.fs) — High-speed camera crash zoom with multi-tap radial velocity streak blur, edge chromatic dispersion, and exponential acceleration curves.
  7. Vortex Swirl (vortex_swirl.fs) — Gravitational singularity twisting Deck A into a spiraling vortex at the frame center, peaking at midpoint, and unwinding into Deck B with chromatic flare.
  8. Cyber Datamosh (cyber_datamosh.fs) — Digital video compression breakdown emulating I-frame/P-frame corruption, macroblock displacement, horizontal sync tear, and chromatic shear.

docs.title: The Unified Transition Browser
docs.text:
The [ Transitions ] list shows two kinds of row side by side, each marked with its own icon:

  • Stock ISF Transition Shaders — The curated suite above, plus any custom .fs transitions found in your configured shader directories. Unlike FX, there's only ever one active transition — no chain of slots to disambiguate — so a bare stock transition id is a complete, unambiguous instruction. Combined with sane bundled defaults, that makes them safe to apply, queue, or add to a playlist just like saved presets.
  • Saved Transition Presets (.lsdtrans) — A dialed-in transition configuration (parameters, dry/wet, modulators) captured from the mixer.

Pick a section in the folder tree to show only stock shaders or only saved presets. Use the save button above the list to save the mixer's current transition as a new preset.

  • Multi-select: Ctrl/Cmd+click, Shift+click and Ctrl+A select several rows, as in the Sources list; the row menu, Q, drag and Delete then act on all of them (stock shaders queue and go into playlists too; only saved presets can be deleted).
  • Double-click: Applies the transition to the mixer immediately.
  • Keyboard: Enter applies the selected transition (as on every tab); the Add to A/B Queue shortcut (Q by default, rebindable in Preferences → Shortcuts) adds it to the transition queue.
  • Failures: a transition or FX file that can't be loaded or applied now shows a toast instead of failing silently.
  • Right-click or ⋮ menu: Apply to Mixer, Add to A/B Queue, Add to '', plus Rename..., Clone, Delete... and Reveal in File Manager for saved presets (stock shaders have no file). Deleting a saved transition also removes it from the queue and playlists.

docs.title: The Macros Tab (Macro Banks and Perform Pages)
docs.text:
The [ Macros ] tab has two lists, switched with the Banks / Pages radio buttons. It has no playlists or queues, so it uses the whole Library width.

  • Banks lists the saved macro banks (.knobpreset.json files in library/knobpresets). Save bank from... saves the knobs of a deck, Master or Transition row under a name you choose. Right-click a bank to Apply to one of those rows (deck banks retarget to the deck they land on; targets that row can't take are dropped, and a toast says if parameters were missing) or Delete it. FX banks are rewritten from the FX chain, so they can't be saved or applied here. This is the same as the bank kebab menu in the Edit row, without the file browser.
  • Pages lists the Perform pages with where each comes from (built-in, user, or user override). Click a page to show it in Perform. Right-click for Hide from / Show in tab strip, Copy to user file (built-ins) or Delete user file. Editing a page's rows stays in Preferences → MIDI Controls.

docs.title: Transition Presets (.lsdtrans) & Playlists (.lsdtransplay)
docs.text:
• Transition Presets (.lsdtrans): Stored in library/transitions/. Save dialed-in transition configurations (including parameter values, dry/wet, and modulators) from the Transitions row's Save or its ⋮ > Save As, from the save button above the Trans list, or by right-clicking in the Mixer panel.
  • Transition Playlists (.lsdtransplay): Stored in library/transition_playlists/. Group transitions into ordered setlists for the Transition Queue. A factory playlist, festival_elite.lsdtransplay, is bundled out of the box.
  • AutoVJ Integration: The Transition Queue automatically advances to the next staged transition preset or stock transition shader each time the crossfader cycles between decks.

docs.title: Drag & Drop
docs.text:
From To Result Sources list (saved preset) Playlist (between items) Inserts at that position Sources list (saved preset) Empty space at playlist bottom Appends to the end Playlist item Up / down in the same playlist Reorders Sources list (saved preset) or Playlist A/B or BG Queue (between items, or below the last) Inserts at that position, or appends Sources list row (stock, saved or external video) Deck monitor (Mixer) or deck row (Performance Matrix) Loads source (stock, external) or full preset (saved) to that deck FX Preset (.lsdfx) FX Slot 1–3 in Edit's FX tab Loads into target slot Stock FX filter FX Slot in Edit or on a Perform row Loads into that slot FX Preset (.lsdfx) Deck badge in the Performance Matrix Loads into the first vacant slot (a toast says so if all 3 are full; drop on a slot instead) FX Chain (.lsdfxchain) FX Slot / Chain in Edit, or the deck badge Overwrites 3-slot chain FX list row FX playlist in the tree Inserts/appends to playlist FX list row A/B FX Queue (A/B or BG) Inserts at that position, or appends A/B FX Queue item Up / down in the same queue Reorders Transition list row Transition playlist in the tree Inserts/appends to playlist Transition list row Transition Queue Inserts at that position, or appends

A deck's monitor takes presets and sources only, not FX. Each queue takes only its own kind: while you drag, a queue that can't take the item dims. With the Library maximized, the queues sit under the browser, so every row in this table can go from the list to a queue position in one drag.

docs.title: MIDI Mapping
docs.text:
MIDI is disabled by default. Enable it in Preferences → MIDI Controls ("Enable MIDI Subsystem") or via the ⋮ kebab menu next to Edit's column headers ("MIDI Column").

Liquid LSD keeps hardware controller maps separate from visual presets, so you can swap physical controllers without touching your preset files.

There are two levels of MIDI mapping:

  1. Hardware Profile (stored in library/midi/default.json) — Maps physical knobs and faders to global controls like the master crossfader, deck gain, and level faders. These mappings follow you regardless of which preset is loaded.

  2. Grid Cell Modulators (stored inside each .lsd file) — Maps MIDI CC numbers to specific parameters as dynamic modulation sources in the CV grid. These travel with the preset.

docs.title: MIDI Learn
docs.text:
1. Click the MIDI Learn button in the Parameters header or next to any parameter slider.
  2. Move a knob, fader, or button on your controller.
  3. Liquid LSD captures the CC and confirms the mapping automatically.
  4. To remove a mapping, right-click the mapped control and choose Clear MIDI Mapping.

docs.title: Visual Sources
docs.text: Each deck runs one source at a time. Sources range from the built-in procedural generators to ISF shaders you drop in from the internet or write yourself, and live video from other apps. On top of the source, each deck has a chain of three effect slots.

docs.title: Picking a Source
docs.text:
Click a deck's source badge and the Library below lists sources for that deck (see Your Workspace / Macros & the Modular Rack). You can search by name, tag, or author. Browse automatically filters to show only sources appropriate for what you're assigning — generators for the main source slot, effects for the FX slots, and transitions for the mixer. Picks apply immediately and the list stays open, so you can try several in a row.

To empty a deck, click Eject on its row (its FX chain stays). A preset whose generator isn't installed, or failed to compile, won't load: you get a message naming the missing source, and the deck keeps what it was playing.

docs.title: Live Video Input
docs.text:
Besides generating its own video, a deck can show live video from another app or device. Liquid LSD receives the same GPU-sharing protocols it sends:

  • Windows: Spout senders
  • macOS: Syphon servers
  • Linux: PipeWire video streams

Every stream running right now is listed in Browse under External video (see Presets & Library). The list refreshes every couple of seconds, so a stream appears shortly after its app starts sending and disappears when it stops. Load one like any other source. A live stream has a single Gain parameter in place of a generator's parameter list, and the deck's FX chain, levels and transitions work on it exactly as they do on a generator.

Streams are not files, so they cannot be saved as presets, added to playlists or queued.

docs.title: Built-In Generators
docs.text:
Liquid LSD includes a curated suite of 34 built-in procedural generators spanning harmonic geometry, 3D raymarching, 3D fractals, volumetric gas, 4D polytopes, organic fluid dynamics, living simulations, acoustic wavefields, and a set of light generators that run comfortably on integrated graphics.

The raymarchers (Icosa-H3, Gyroid Hyperspace, 4D Hyper-Slice, Nebula Volume and the fractals below) show a gauge mark in the browser: they are GPU-intensive and can run slowly on integrated graphics. The fractals are tuned for a mid-range discrete GPU (an RTX A2000 or better); every one has a Quality knob, and lowering it is the first thing to try if a deck stutters.

Decks off air cost less. Deck PV only feeds its monitor, so it renders at half the output size (full size when you send it out over Spout / Syphon / PipeWire). With Off-air decks at half frame rate on (Preferences > General, on by default), a deck the output can't show at the moment (A or B faded fully across, a deck or the master at level 0, and PV) renders every other frame, leaving the GPU to the decks on air. Its monitor runs at half rate, and simulations and feedback trails on it advance at half speed until it comes on air. A deck you stream always renders every frame.

Black is transparent. Generators let the BG deck (or any layer beneath them) show through wherever they are black: a source's alpha follows its brightest colour channel, so bright areas cover what is behind and dark areas reveal it. Over a black BG nothing changes.

Updates. When you install a new version, bundled generator files you haven't changed are updated to the new version; a file you edited is kept as it is (the log says so).

docs.title: Mandala (mandala)
docs.text:
The signature parametric harmonic curve engine. Mandala generates intricate symmetrical geometry using over 300 curated harmonic ratios. Built-in size normalization guarantees the outer boundary stays stable and fills your frame cleanly no matter how aggressively you modulate parameters.

  • Lobes: Selects the petal-count harmonic group (3 to 26 lobes).
  • Recipe Select: Browses individual frequency ratios within the active Lobes group.
  • Arm Lengths (L1–L4): Sets harmonic amplitude from primary outer petals down to inner detail loops.
  • 3D Elevation: Pair with the 3d_elevation filter in any FX slot to wrap Mandala into a spherical gyro, cube cage, 6-plane intersection, or 24-chamber kaleidoscope.

docs.title: Dynamic Spiral (dynamic_spiral)
docs.text:
A high-performance particle dynamics system where particles spiral outward under radial wave, shear, and velocity damping forces.

  • Max Points: Particle density across the visible spiral.
  • Wave Freq & Wave Amp: Modulates particle trajectories into undulating ripple formations.
  • Shear: Applies tangential twisting to particle velocity, creating spiral vortices.
  • Trail Decay: Governs the longevity of particle streaks. Low decay produces luminous, silky light trails.

docs.title: Icosa-H3 (icosa_h3)
docs.text:
A native 3D Coxeter $H_3$ raymarcher combining a continuous Icosahedron/Dodecahedron duality morph with an independent spike-and-blocker stellation CSG.

  • Morph: Continuous 4-stage cyclic Coxeter morph:
  • 0.00 – 0.25: Icosahedron (20 triangular faces) $\to$ Dodecahedron (12 pentagonal faces).
  • 0.25 – 0.50: Dodecahedron $\to$ Great Stellated Dodecahedron.
  • 0.50 – 0.75: Great Stellated Dodecahedron $\to$ Great Icosahedron.
  • 0.75 – 1.00: Great Icosahedron $\to$ Icosahedron.
  • Support H: Wythoff facet cutting: negative values truncate vertices (e.g. $-0.15$ yields the truncated icosahedron / Buckyball), while positive values bevel edges.
  • Opacity: Translucency control ($0.6 \dots 0.8$ reveals internal self-intersecting facets).
  • Camera Controls: Native 3D pitch (RotateX), yaw (RotateY), roll (RotateZ), and Zoom exposed in the View tab.

docs.title: Domain Warp Fluid (domain_warp_fluid)
docs.text:
A multi-scale domain-warped fluid simulation with fractional Brownian motion (fBm) curl noise, dynamic vorticity, surface specular normals, and iridescent liquid marbling. Evokes 1960s liquid light overheads, oil-on-water marbling, and liquid metal.

  • Warp Strength & Swirl: Dial from gentle chromatic ripples to turbulent psychedelic marbling.
  • Specular Gloss: Computes finite-difference surface normals and specular highlights for a wet, embossed liquid look.
  • Palette Modes:
  • 0: Psychedelic Neon (Cyan / Magenta / Gold / Emerald)
  • 1: Liquid Chrome / Mercury
  • 2: Oil Slick / Prismatic Iridescence
  • 3: Opal Sunset / Warm Fire & Dusk
  • 4: Deep Ocean Bioluminescence

docs.title: Gyroid Hyperspace (gyroid_hyperspace)
docs.text:
A native 3D raymarcher rendering Triply Periodic Minimal Surfaces (TPMS) with continuous morphing between Gyroid, Schwarz P, and Neovius minimal surfaces, volumetric internal radiance, and camera flight.

  • Surface Type: Smoothly morphs the minimal surface geometry between Gyroid (0.0), Schwarz P (1.0), and Neovius (2.0).
  • Wall Thickness & Hole Scale: Transitions from delicate skeletal lattices to dense porous bio-sponges.
  • Wireframe Mode: Carves open coordinate lattice struts to reveal an architectural cage.
  • Flight Speed: Camera flight forward through the infinite labyrinth.
  • Core Glow: Volumetric radiance accumulating inside internal chambers.

docs.title: Celestial Engine (celestial_engine)
docs.text:
A multi-symmetry sacred geometry and op-art generator combining Flower of Life overlapping circles, concentric harmonic rings, phase twisting, and moiré fringes.

  • Symmetries: Discrete rotational symmetry fold count from 3 to 24.
  • Ring Density & Moiré Strength: Cross-modulates radial harmonic rings to produce shimmering optical interference fringes.
  • Flower Fold: Folds the coordinate space into intersecting Flower of Life geometry.
  • Pulse Wave: Expanding radial shockwave ring, ideal for kick/snare CV modulation.

docs.title: 4D Hyper-Slice (hyper_slice)
docs.text:
A raymarched 3D cross-section (MRI scan) through 4-dimensional 120-cell (600 vertices) and 600-cell (120 vertices) polytopes using the $H_4$ Coxeter reflection group (order 14,400).

  • Slice Offset W: Sweeps the 3D cutting hyperplane along the 4th dimension ($W$ axis), revealing shifting geometric cross-sections.
  • 4D Hyper-Rotations (RotateXW, RotateYW, RotateZW): Rotates the polytope through 4-space, turning geometry inside-out in 3D.
  • Polychoron Morph: Smoothly interpolates the facet normals between the 600-cell and 120-cell.
  • Support H: Adjusts Wythoff facet cutting distance.
  • Face Opacity & Edge Highlight: Crystal interior reveal with glowing ridge boundaries.

docs.title: Chladni Cymatics (chladni_cymatics)
docs.text:
A physical 2D acoustic plate resonance simulation computing standing wave nodal harmonics across square and circular boundaries, complete with particle accumulation physics.

  • Frequency M, N, L: Acoustic modal frequencies governing standing wave harmonic interference patterns.
  • Plate Shape: Blends smoothly from square plate resonance (0.0) to circular Bessel vibration (1.0).
  • Sand Accumulation & Node Sharpness: Simulates sand grains migrating away from kinetic antinodes and gathering along quiet nodal lines.
  • Invert Mode: Swaps behavior from quiet nodal sand gathering (0.0) to kinetic fluid pooling in energetic antinodes (1.0).
  • Palette Modes: Obsidian & Gold Sand, Electric Cymatic Blue, Prismatic Spectrum, and Bioluminescent Emerald.

docs.title: Mandelbox (mandelbox)
docs.text:
A raymarched Mandelbox: space is repeatedly folded into a box, inverted in a sphere and scaled, producing cathedral-like chambers. The camera glides in and out and stays outside the solid. The light is camera-relative, so the lit side always faces you as the view turns.

  • Scale: The fold scale. Right of centre gives the classic box, left of centre the inverted variants. It jumps at the centre, so avoid automating across it.
  • Fold Limit, Min Radius, Max Radius: Box-fold size and the two sphere-fold radii; they reshape the chambers.
  • Quality: Ray-march steps, fold iterations and ambient-occlusion taps together.
  • Flight Speed, Glow: Signed in-and-out camera motion, and a halo from near-miss rays.
  • Color Mode: Orbit trap (origin), orbit trap (planes), sphere-fold fraction, normal spectrum, depth.

docs.title: KIFS (kifs)
docs.text:
A kaleidoscopic iterated-function-system fractal: repeated folds, a scale and an offset toward a fixed vertex, with a rotation added at every iteration. The light is camera-relative, so the lit side always faces you as the view turns.

  • Fractal Type: Menger-like, Sierpinski tetrahedron, octahedral, or a mixed construction.
  • Scale, Offset: Look controls on the construction; away from the centre it stops tiling exactly.
  • Twist X/Y/Z, Morph Speed: Rotation applied to each nested level of the fractal except the outermost, so the object stays in place while its inner geometry twists (safe to modulate with an LFO). Morph Speed adds a time-driven rotation to the same twist. Morph Speed defaults to 0, so nothing moves until you raise it.
  • Flight Speed: Endless self-similar dolly toward the fixed vertex; negative flies outward. Defaults to 0 (holds still).
  • Rotate X/Y/Z: Turn the camera rig around the whole object; these never animate on their own.
  • Quality, Glow, Color Mode: Detail versus speed, a grazing-ray halo, and five colourings.
  • Color Spread: Folding makes every copy of a detail identical, so this shifts hue by fold depth, position in space and facing direction to bring in more colours. 0 is the plain ramp; the gold ramp ignores it.

docs.title: Mandelbulb (mandelbulb)
docs.text:
A raymarched Mandelbulb, the 3D analogue of the Mandelbrot set built on a power map in spherical coordinates, with a turntable camera. The light is camera-relative, so the lit side always faces you as the view turns.

  • Power: Exponent from 2 to 16 (default 8). Non-integer values show a cut seam.
  • Power Swing: A slow automatic oscillation of the power; 0 keeps it fixed.
  • Julia Mix: Blends toward a Julia set.
  • Bailout: Escape radius; higher keeps more of the set at higher cost.
  • Quality, Flight Speed, Glow, Color Mode: Detail versus speed, turntable speed (signed), halo, five colourings.

docs.title: Pseudo Kleinian (pseudo_kleinian)
docs.text:
A fly-through of a Kleinian-style structure: a periodic mirror fold followed by repeated sphere inversion, with the camera travelling down an open channel.

  • Slab Size, Inversion Radius, Inversion Strength: Spacing of the repeating structure, and how the inversion carves and magnifies it.
  • Offset X/Y/Z: Shifts that reshape the channels and walls.
  • Core Size: Wall thickness. Near the maximum the channel can fill in and the frame goes flat.
  • Quality, Flight Speed, Color Mode: Detail versus speed, signed fly-through speed, four colourings.

docs.title: Apollonian (apollonian)
docs.text:
A fly-through of an Apollonian-style sphere gasket: space is tiled into cells and inverted in a sphere, packing smaller and smaller spheres into the gaps.
